facts.action: Use scroll of enchant armor on green dragon scales to upgrade to scale mail.

facts.fact: Uncontrolled polymorph while wearing green dragon scales will turn the wearer into a green dragon.
facts.detect: Message: 'You feel a strange tingling sensation.'
facts.action: Avoid uncontrolled polymorph while wearing green dragon scales.

facts.fact: Green dragon scales are not randomly generated, but can be wished for or found in bones.
facts.detect: Item name: green dragon scales, bones level
facts.action: Wish for green dragon scales if needed.

facts.fact: Gremlins are chaotic humanoids that are intelligent and inediate, and attack using claws and bites.
facts.detect: Encountering a gremlin, gargoyle, or winged gargoyle on the map.
facts.action: Avoid engaging chaotic gremlins if possible, as they may be part of a larger chaotic group or have allies nearby. If combat is necessary, be prepared for intelligent tactics and multiple attacks.

facts.fact: Griefing involves leaving malicious bones files for other players to encounter, which can lead to their immediate death or debilitation.
facts.detect: Encountering a bones level with unusually dangerous traps or monsters.
facts.action: Avoid bones levels or use bones files from trusted players only.

facts.fact: Players can convert altars in temples, causing the aligned priest to attack any players who attempt to chat with them.
facts.detect: Encountering a hostile priest in a temple.
facts.action: Avoid chatting with priests in temples or convert altars only when necessary.

facts.fact: Cockatrice corpses left around magic traps can blind players, who must then feel objects on the floor.
facts.detect: Finding a cockatrice corpse near a magic trap.
facts.action: Avoid touching magic traps near cockatrice corpses or use gloves to protect against blindness.

facts.fact: Invisible and frustrating monsters like rust monsters and blue jellies can be left on levels to harass players.
facts.detect: Encountering invisible monsters or noticing rusting of metal items.
facts.action: Use a magic whistle to summon help or avoid areas with invisible monsters.

facts.fact: Levels can be filled with holes in the floor, making traversal impossible depending on the player's items and capabilities.
facts.detect: Encountering a level with numerous holes in the floor.
facts.action: Avoid such levels or find a way to fill the holes.

facts.fact: A 'large' group consists of 2-11 monsters and a 'small' group of 1-4.
facts.detect: Encountering multiple monsters of the same type at once.
facts.action: Lure the group into a corridor or doorway to fight one monster at a time.

facts.fact: Monsters in groups are more common than their monster frequency would imply.
facts.detect: Frequent encounters with the same type of monster.
facts.action: Be prepared for group encounters and use tactics to handle multiple monsters.

facts.fact: A common strategy for killing monster groups is to lure them into a corridor or doorway.
facts.detect: Encountering a group of monsters.
facts.action: Lure the group into a narrow space to fight one monster at a time.

facts.fact: Monsters that appear in small groups have a 2 in 3 chance of appearing in groups of 2-4.
facts.detect: Encountering 2-4 of the same type of monster.
facts.action: Prepare for group encounters and use tactics to handle multiple monsters.

facts.fact: Monsters that appear in large groups have a 2 in 3 chance of appearing in groups of 2-11, otherwise 2-4.
facts.detect: Encountering 2-11 of the same type of monster.
facts.action: Lure the group into a narrow space to fight one monster at a time.

facts.fact: A monster's maximum and current HP will both increase if it kills another monster.
facts.detect: Monster HP increase message
facts.action: Avoid killing monsters that are close to reaching their next level to prevent them from gaining HP and potentially becoming stronger.

facts.fact: Monsters can gain a level and increase their HP by drinking a potion of gain level or eating a wraith corpse.
facts.detect: Monster drinking potion of gain level or eating wraith corpse
facts.action: Avoid letting monsters consume potions of gain level or wraith corpses to prevent them from gaining levels and HP.

facts.fact: Monsters can change form when they reach a certain level, such as a little dog becoming a dog at level 4.
facts.detect: Monster form change message (e.g., 'The kitten grows up into a housecat')
facts.action: Avoid allowing monsters to reach levels that would cause them to change into more dangerous forms.

facts.fact: There is a limit to the maximum level a monster can attain via natural growth, which is 3/2 of the base level for the current monster type, but no less than 5 and normally no greater than 49.
facts.detect: Monster reaching level 30 or higher
facts.action: Prevent monsters from reaching high levels to avoid them becoming too powerful.

facts.fact: Growing up is a one-way process, and level draining a grown-up monster will not cause it to revert to a lesser form.
facts.detect: Monster form change message
facts.action: Avoid letting monsters grow up into forms that are harder to deal with or revert.

facts.fact: The player will be greeted with the message 'It is pitch black. You are likely to be eaten by a grue.' when entering an unlit area.
facts.detect: It is pitch black. You are likely to be eaten by a grue.
facts.action: Immediately light a source or use a light spell to avoid being eaten by a grue.

facts.fact: An instadeath occurs if the player attempts to do anything while in an unlit area three times.
facts.detect: Eaten by a Grue
facts.action: Avoid any actions in darkness after receiving the grue warning message twice.

facts.fact: The sinister device, once identified, is called the 'Frobozz Company Inter-Dimensional Portal Generator (TM)' and applying it will allow the player to escape the room.
facts.detect: Frobozz Company Inter-Dimensional Portal Generator (TM)
facts.action: Identify and apply the sinister device to escape the room.

facts.fact: Multi-step movement commands do not count entering darkness or the message appearing as cause to interrupt those commands.
facts.detect: Attempting multi-step movement in darkness
facts.action: Break multi-step movement commands into single steps to avoid repeated grue warnings.

facts.fact: Checking inventory for a light source can trigger the grue warning message.
facts.detect: Checking inventory in darkness
facts.action: Avoid checking inventory in darkness to prevent triggering the grue warning.

facts.fact: Elbereth engraving can cause most monsters to not attack you hand-to-hand.
facts.detect: Message 'You engrave Elbereth.' or seeing monsters hesitate to attack.
facts.action: Engrave 'Elbereth' on the ground to avoid melee attacks from most monsters.

facts.fact: Pets follow you through staircases if they are close enough.
facts.detect: Pet moves with the player when going up or down stairs.
facts.action: Use pets to scout ahead or to help in combat by moving them close to stairs.

facts.fact: Praying to your god can help with starvation.
facts.detect: Feeling hungry and having no food.
facts.action: Use the #pray command to ask your god for help with starvation.

facts.fact: Liquids like water, fruit juice, and booze provide nutrition without breaking foodless conduct.
facts.detect: Having liquids and feeling hungry.
facts.action: Drink liquids to quench hunger without breaking foodless conduct.

facts.fact: Pets can be trained by throwing food (treats) at them.
facts.detect: Pet following player and not aggressive.
facts.action: Train pets to be more helpful by throwing food (treats) at them.

facts.fact: Half physical damage protects against ordinary physical damage from a monster attack.
facts.detect: Monster attack message
facts.action: Carry The Master Key of Thievery or The Orb of Fate to reduce damage from monster attacks.

facts.fact: Half physical damage protects against contact damage dealt by a monster.
facts.detect: Monster contact damage message
facts.action: Carry The Master Key of Thievery or The Orb of Fate to reduce damage from monster contact.

facts.fact: Half physical damage protects against explosion of a gas spore.
facts.detect: Gas spore explosion message
facts.action: Carry The Master Key of Thievery or The Orb of Fate to reduce damage from gas spore explosions.

facts.fact: Half physical damage protects against rust damage from exposure to water if polymorphed into an iron golem.
facts.detect: Polymorph into iron golem and water exposure
facts.action: Carry The Master Key of Thievery or The Orb of Fate to reduce rust damage if polymorphed into an iron golem.

facts.fact: Half physical damage does not protect against damage from an arrow trap or dart trap.
facts.detect: Arrow trap or dart trap damage message
facts.action: Avoid or disarm traps that deal damage not covered by half physical damage.

facts.fact: Half spell damage reduces damage from many monster spells, ray attacks (but not breath attacks), other magical attacks, and a few magical effects that are not attacks.
facts.detect: Carrying Orb of Detection, Platinum Yendorian Express Card, Orb of Fate, or Eye of the Aethiopica
facts.action: Carry one of these items to reduce damage from magical attacks and effects

facts.fact: Half spell damage halves the duration of stun, confuse, paralyze, and blind effects from monster spells.
facts.detect: Monster spell effects such as 'stunned', 'confused', 'paralyzed', or 'blinded'
facts.action: Carry one of the items to reduce the duration of these effects

facts.fact: Half spell damage halves the strength reduction from drain strength monster spells.
facts.detect: Message 'You feel your strength draining away.'
facts.action: Carry one of the items to reduce the strength reduction

facts.fact: Half spell damage halves the damage from lightning and fire pillar clerical spells.
facts.detect: Messages 'A bolt of lightning strikes you!' or 'A fire pillar engulfs you!'
facts.action: Carry one of the items to reduce the damage

facts.fact: Half spell damage does not reduce damage from magic missile monster spells, the geyser monster spell, or breath weapons.
facts.detect: Messages 'A magic missile strikes you!' or 'A geyser erupts from the ground!'
facts.action: Do not rely on half spell damage for these specific attacks

facts.fact: The war hammer is the only weapon to use the hammer skill.
facts.detect: war hammer
facts.action: Prioritize finding and using a war hammer as it is the only weapon that benefits from the hammer skill.

facts.fact: There are two artifacts that use the hammer skill: Mjollnir and Ogresmasher.
facts.detect: Mjollnir or Ogresmasher
facts.action: If you find Mjollnir or Ogresmasher, use them as they are powerful artifacts that enhance your hammer skill.

facts.fact: Harrower of Zariel can summon between 2 and 6 (2d3) Zarielite shades once per seven turns.
facts.detect: Appearance of Zarielite shades around the Harrower.
facts.action: Prepare to deal with summoned shades by having blessed or cursed weapons ready, depending on the shade type.

facts.fact: Zarielite shades can only be damaged by weapons with the opposite beatitude.
facts.detect: Zarielite zealot or heretic shade.
facts.action: Switch to blessed weapons for zealots and cursed weapons for heretics.

facts.fact: Zarielite shades have heavily enchanted weapons, swing twice per move, and get 1.5 turns per move.
facts.detect: Observing the shade's attack pattern.
facts.action: Focus on attacking the shade quickly before it can attack back.

facts.fact: Zarielite shades wear enchanted armor.
facts.detect: Shade's armor resistance.
facts.action: Use appropriate weapons to penetrate the armor.

facts.fact: A circle of Acheron ward is suggested to avoid being overwhelmed by summoned shades.
facts.detect: Presence of summoned shades.
facts.action: Cast Acheron ward to protect against shades.

facts.fact: Haste self is a non-directed spell that can be used by any monster of at least level 3 with the ability to cast mage spells.
facts.detect: Encountering a level 3 or higher monster with mage spellcasting ability.
facts.action: Be cautious and prepare for increased combat speed from the monster.

facts.fact: When cast, the haste self monster spell increases the caster's speed, similar to the spell of haste self for the hero: a monster at normal speed will become fast, and a slowed monster will return to normal speed.
facts.detect: Observing a monster's speed increase during combat.
facts.action: Use speed-boosting items or spells to match the monster's speed.

facts.fact: Monsters will cast the spell when the hero is close to them regardless of their hostility, and will not cast it if they are already at fast speed.
facts.detect: Noticing a monster casting haste self when approaching it.
facts.action: Maintain distance or use speed-boosting items to avoid being overwhelmed.

facts.fact: Hats do not protect against damage from falling objects such as rocks and boulders.
facts.detect: Encounter with falling objects or boulders.
facts.action: Avoid wearing hats when in areas with falling hazards or switch to a hard helm.

facts.fact: Wearing a hat reduces ceiling damage from a cursed potion of levitation from d10 to d6.
facts.detect: Quaffing a cursed potion of levitation.
facts.action: Continue wearing a hat to reduce ceiling damage.

facts.fact: Certain helms are referred to as hats in messages: cornuthaum, dunce cap, elven leather helm (known as a 'leather hat' when unidentified), and fedora.
facts.detect: Message references to these items as 'hat'.
facts.action: Identify these items as hats to understand their properties.

facts.fact: Dwarvish iron helm appears as a 'hard hat' when unidentified but is referred to as a 'helm' in messages.
facts.detect: Message references to 'hard hat' or 'helm'.
facts.action: Identify the dwarvish iron helm as a hard helm for better protection.

facts.fact: A headbutt attack can turn the attacker to stone if they headbutt a cockatrice or chickatrice without a worn helm.
facts.detect: Encountering a cockatrice or chickatrice
facts.action: Wear a helm before approaching cockatrices or chickatrices

facts.fact: Monsters will avoid headbutting a cockatrice or chickatrice if they can see the target and have a helm.
facts.detect: A monster lunges wildly and misses when near a cockatrice or chickatrice
facts.action: Ensure the cockatrice or chickatrice is not visible to monsters to avoid them attempting a headbutt

facts.fact: A minotaur is the only monster form a hero can take that allows them to wear helms.
facts.detect: Polymorphing into a minotaur
facts.action: Wear a helm when polymorphed into a minotaur to avoid headbutt damage

facts.fact: Headbutting a shade with a blessed or silver helm can hypothetically hit the shade.
facts.detect: Encountering a shade while wearing a blessed or silver helm
facts.action: Headbutt a shade if wearing a blessed or silver helm

facts.fact: Headstones have a 20% chance of appearing in a graveyard per floor tile.
facts.detect: Encounter a vertical bar (|) symbol in a graveyard.
facts.action: Be cautious around headstones in graveyards due to the risk of summoning undead monsters.

facts.fact: A randomly-generated headstone has a 30% chance of containing a pile of gold pieces.
facts.detect: See a headstone with a pile of gold pieces next to it.
facts.action: Carefully dig or kick the headstone to retrieve the gold, being prepared for potential undead summoning.

facts.fact: Kicking a headstone has a 12.5% chance of summoning a ghoul.
facts.detect: Kicking a headstone and seeing the message 'The grave's owner is very upset!' or 'Dude! The living dead!'.
facts.action: Avoid kicking headstones unless necessary, especially in areas with high monster density.

facts.fact: Digging up a headstone may produce a zombie, mummy, or very old corpse.
facts.detect: Digging a headstone and seeing messages like 'You unearth a corpse.', 'You've disturbed a tomb!', or 'The grave's owner is very upset!'.
facts.action: Only dig up headstones if the potential rewards outweigh the risk of summoning dangerous monsters.

facts.fact: Engraving on a headstone abuses wisdom and may summon a ghoul.
facts.detect: Attempting to engrave on a headstone and seeing the message 'You disturb the undead!'.
facts.action: Avoid engraving on headstones unless absolutely necessary.

facts.fact: Healers start with 4 non-cursed potions of healing and 4 non-cursed potions of extra healing.
facts.detect: Item name: potion of healing, potion of extra healing
facts.action: Use these potions to heal and maintain health during the early game.

facts.fact: Healers start with a blessed spellbook of healing, a blessed spellbook of extra healing, and a blessed spellbook of stone to flesh.
facts.detect: Item name: spellbook of healing, spellbook of extra healing, spellbook of stone to flesh
facts.action: Learn and use these spells to heal, restore health, and convert boulders into meat for food.

facts.fact: Healers gain poison resistance at level 1.
facts.detect: Message: You are immune to poison.
facts.action: No specific action needed, but be aware of this intrinsic to avoid certain dangers.

facts.fact: Healers can identify the wand of undead turning by zapping a corpse with it.
facts.detect: Item name: wand of undead turning, corpse
facts.action: Use this ability to identify wands of undead turning without needing to guess.

facts.fact: Healers do not suffer damage or attribute loss from quaffing a potion of sickness.
facts.detect: Item name: potion of sickness
facts.action: Drink these potions to cure hallucination without fear of damage or attribute loss.

facts.fact: The spell 'sleep' is raised to level 3, making it more difficult to cast.
facts.detect: Spell level information or difficulty in casting 'sleep'.
facts.action: Avoid using 'sleep' spell unless absolutely necessary.

facts.fact: The spell 'confuse monster' is lowered to level 1, making it a useful utility spell option.
facts.detect: Spell level information or availability of 'confuse monster'.
facts.action: Use 'confuse monster' spell when dealing with groups of monsters.

facts.fact: The Staff of Aesculapius provides a small boost to spellcasting.
facts.detect: Possession of the Staff of Aesculapius.
facts.action: Use the Staff of Aesculapius as a weapon to enhance spellcasting.

facts.fact: A silver saber or other silver weapon is preferred for traversing Gehennom to avoid the Staff of Aesculapius becoming cursed.
facts.detect: Presence of the Staff of Aesculapius and the need to traverse Gehennom.
facts.action: Carry a silver weapon as a backup in Gehennom.

facts.fact: Healers can wear metal boots and cast reliably or wear a metal helm with a ~3% failure rate.
facts.detect: Possession of metal boots or helm.
facts.action: Wear metal boots or helm to enhance spellcasting.

facts.fact: The Healer quest involves navigating through levels with undiggable walls and floors, and teleportation is restricted on some levels.
facts.detect: Undiggable walls and floors, inability to teleport.
facts.action: Use wands of fire to evaporate pools or luring red dragons to breathe fire to create passable paths.

facts.fact: Random monsters on the quest include giant rats, snakes, and various dangerous creatures like sharks and electric eels.
facts.detect: Monster names like 'giant rat', 'snake', 'shark', 'electric eel'.
facts.action: Be cautious and prepared to fight or avoid these monsters.

facts.fact: The quest nemesis, the Cyclops, is generated with the Bell of Opening and the Staff of Aesculapius.
facts.detect: Encounter with the Cyclops.
facts.action: Prepare to fight the Cyclops and retrieve the Staff of Aesculapius.

facts.fact: The home level of the Healer quest is the Temple of Epidaurus, which has a specific layout with attendants, chests, and various traps.
facts.detect: Entering the Temple of Epidaurus.
facts.action: Explore the temple carefully, avoiding traps and dealing with attendants.

facts.fact: The Isle of the Cyclops is the goal level where the Cyclops is located.
facts.detect: Arriving at the Isle of the Cyclops.
facts.action: Prepare to fight the Cyclops and retrieve the Staff of Aesculapius.

facts.fact: Potion of full healing restores up to 400 HP regardless of BUC status.
facts.detect: Item name: potion of full healing
facts.action: Use potion of full healing to restore HP when critically low.

facts.fact: Prayer restores HP to maximum if you have less than 6 HP or less than or equal to 1/7 of your max HP.
facts.detect: Player HP is less than 6 or less than 1/7 of max HP
facts.action: Pray to restore HP to maximum when critically low.

facts.fact: Invoking The Staff of Aesculapius heals half the HP you would need to return to full health.
facts.detect: Item name: The Staff of Aesculapius
facts.action: Invoke The Staff of Aesculapius to heal when critically low, but avoid overuse due to timeout.

facts.fact: Eating a nurse corpse or tin of nurse meat fully restores HP.
facts.detect: Item name: nurse corpse or tin of nurse meat
facts.action: Eat nurse corpse or tin of nurse meat to fully restore HP when critically low.

facts.fact: Being hit by a nurse heals you if you are wearing no armor and wielding no weapon.
facts.detect: Monster name: nurse
facts.action: Allow a nurse to hit you to heal when critically low and no armor or weapon equipped.

facts.fact: Entering Hell without fire resistance leads to instadeath.
facts.detect: You burn to a crisp.
facts.action: Ensure fire resistance before entering Hell.

facts.fact: Hell begins at dungeon level 30 in versions up to NetHack 2.3e, and on the level after the Castle in NetHack 3.0.0 and later.
facts.detect: Arrival at Hell level.
facts.action: Prepare for fire resistance and teleport to Hell level.

facts.fact: All levels in Hell have only up-stairs, and the mazes between Medusa and Hell also have only up-stairs in versions up to NetHack 2.3e.
facts.detect: Presence of only up-stairs.
facts.action: Use level teleportation to proceed.

facts.fact: Starting in NetHack 3.0.0, ascent by up-stairs in Hell no longer places you on the next up-stairs, but rather on a random spot in the next level.
facts.detect: Random location on next level.
facts.action: Find stairs on all levels and zap back down to fight the Wizard.

facts.fact: The mysterious force makes its debut in NetHack 3.0.0, harder on lawful adventurers and easier on chaotic ones.
facts.detect: Teleportation failure or success.
facts.action: Use teleportation wisely, especially if chaotic.

facts.fact: Metallic helms raise spell failure rate by 4 unless the hero is a Knight casting clerical spells.
facts.detect: Checking hero's armor inventory and spellcasting status.
facts.action: Avoid wearing metallic helms if not a Knight casting clerical spells.

facts.fact: A hard helm reduces falling object damage from d10 to d3, while a hat reduces it to d6.
facts.detect: Hero polymorphing into a form that takes falling damage or encountering falling objects.
facts.action: Wear a hard helm to reduce falling object damage.

facts.fact: A greased helm blocks intelligence-draining tentacle attacks of mind flayers and master mind flayers.
facts.detect: Encountering a mind flayer or master mind flayer.
facts.action: Wear a greased helm to block intelligence-draining attacks.

facts.fact: Unidentified helms with randomized appearances are dangerous to wear as two types are autocursing.
facts.detect: Encountering unidentified helms with randomized appearances.
facts.action: Avoid wearing unidentified helms with randomized appearances.

facts.fact: A helm of telepathy detects hostile monsters, useful for ascension.
facts.detect: Finding a helm of telepathy.
facts.action: Equip a helm of telepathy for detecting hostile monsters.

facts.fact: The helm of caution grants 1 base AC and warning.
facts.detect: Wearing the helm and encountering a hostile monster.
facts.action: Wear the helm to gain AC and warning benefits.

facts.fact: The helm of caution interferes with spellcasting.
facts.detect: Attempting to cast a spell while wearing the helm.
facts.action: Avoid wearing the helm when spellcasting is necessary.

facts.fact: Helms of caution make up 0.6% of all randomly generated armor.
facts.detect: Finding a helm of caution in a random location.
facts.action: Pick up and use the helm of caution for its benefits.

facts.fact: Player monsters have a 7.95% chance of generating with a helm of caution.
facts.detect: Encountering a player monster with a helm of caution.
facts.action: Be cautious as player monsters may be well-equipped.

facts.fact: Helms of caution are advantageous over helms of telepathy for detecting mindless monsters.
facts.detect: Encountering mindless monsters like air elementals or green slimes.
facts.action: Use the helm of caution for detecting these specific monsters.

facts.fact: A herbivore prefers to eat vegetable matter such as fruit, vegetables, fungi, and other plants. Apples and carrots are considered treats.
facts.detect: Item names such as 'apple', 'carrot', 'fruit', 'vegetable', 'fungus', 'lichen', 'mold', 'shrieker', 'blob', 'jelly', 'melon', 'orange', 'pear', 'wolfsbane', 'garlic', 'kelp frond'.
facts.action: Feed the herbivorous pet with these items when it is hungry or starving.

facts.fact: Herbivorous pets will eat melons, oranges, pears, wolfsbane, garlic, kelp fronds, and other plants only when hungry.
facts.detect: Item names such as 'melon', 'orange', 'pear', 'wolfsbane', 'garlic', 'kelp frond'.
facts.action: Save these items for when the pet is hungry and not just as treats.

facts.fact: Herbivorous pets will eat food rations, pancakes, and lembas when starving.
facts.detect: Messages indicating the pet is 'confused from hunger'.
facts.action: Feed the pet food rations, pancakes, or lembas when it is starving.

facts.fact: Herbivorous pets will not eat meat products, meaty corpses, eggs, or tins.
facts.detect: Item names such as 'meat', 'egg', 'tin'.
facts.action: Avoid feeding these items to the pet.

facts.fact: When riding a herbivorous pet, it won't eat vegetables other than apples and carrots.
facts.detect: Message indicating the pet is hungry while riding it.
facts.action: Dismount the pet to feed it other vegetables when it is hungry.

facts.fact: Some monsters can hide, such as trappers, lurkers above, piercers, cave spiders, snakes, and mimics.
facts.detect: Monster names like 'trapper', 'lurker above', 'piercer', 'cave spider', 'snake', and 'mimic'.
facts.action: Be cautious when moving next to objects or tiles where these monsters might be hiding. Use ranged attacks or throw gold to detect them.

facts.fact: Moving next to a hidden monster produces 'Wait! There's a foo hiding under !'.
facts.detect: Exact message 'Wait! There's a foo hiding under !'.
facts.action: Do not move onto the tile where the message appears. Use ranged attacks or throw objects to detect and attack the hidden monster.

facts.fact: Attacking a hiding monster in melee will cause it to stop hiding.
facts.detect: Adjacent to a hidden monster and using melee attack commands like 'F'.
facts.action: Attack the hidden monster with melee to force it to reveal itself.

facts.fact: Searching a tile will reveal hidden monsters and cause them to stick to you.
facts.detect: Using the 's' command to search a tile.
facts.action: Search the tile to reveal hidden monsters and prevent them from hiding again.

facts.fact: Applying a stethoscope or wand of probing at a hiding monster's square will reveal its presence.
facts.detect: Using a stethoscope or wand of probing on a tile.
facts.action: Use a stethoscope or wand of probing to detect hidden monsters without provoking an attack.

facts.fact: High clerics have fire resistance, shock resistance, sleep resistance, and poison resistance.
facts.detect: The bot will encounter a high cleric with these resistances when it attacks or approaches one.
facts.action: The bot should prepare for encounters with high clerics by ensuring it has items or intrinsics that can counter these resistances, such as shock resistance and fire resistance.

facts.fact: The high cleric of Moloch is initially peaceful but will become hostile once the hero enters the temple they reside in.
facts.detect: The bot will see a peaceful high cleric in the temple of Moloch.
facts.action: The bot should avoid entering the temple until it is fully prepared to fight the high cleric of Moloch.

facts.fact: The high cleric of Moloch will have the Amulet of Yendor in their possession.
facts.detect: The bot will see the high cleric of Moloch with the Amulet of Yendor.
facts.action: The bot should be cautious and prepared to fight the high cleric of Moloch to obtain the Amulet of Yendor.

facts.fact: High clerics can see invisible and can be seen via infravision.
facts.detect: The bot will encounter a high cleric that can see invisible and can be seen via infravision.
facts.action: The bot should avoid being invisible when near high clerics and ensure it has infravision to see them.

facts.fact: High clerics can cast paralyze, curse items, and geyser spells.
facts.detect: The bot will be affected by paralyze, curse items, or geyser spells when near a high cleric.
facts.action: The bot should have a means to counter these spells, such as a source of magic resistance or half spell damage.

facts.fact: In NetHack 3.6.1, monsters get an action for each 12 points of speed they have, plus a possible extra action with probability proportional to any extra movement they have beyond that.
facts.detect: Monster speed and player speed comparison
facts.action: Assume monsters' speed is rounded up to a multiple of 12 and plan accordingly.

facts.fact: Hit and run is still possible but less reliable in NetHack 3.6.1, especially if you are not very fast or riding.
facts.detect: Monster speed and player speed comparison
facts.action: Only attempt hit and run if you are very fast or riding, as it is less reliable otherwise.

facts.fact: If your movement rate is at least double the monster's movement rate, you can hit and run effectively.
facts.detect: Monster speed and player speed comparison
facts.action: Calculate the optimal rhythm based on the speed ratio and hit the monster accordingly.

facts.fact: Hit and run is most likely to be successful if the monster in question is the only monster nearby.
facts.detect: Number of monsters in the vicinity
facts.action: Close doors or block off other exits to avoid having other foes intrude.

facts.fact: Hit and run is less useful when facing a creature that can attack you at range.
facts.detect: Monster's ability to attack at range
facts.action: Avoid hit and run tactics against ranged attackers.

facts.fact: A hero or monster whose hit points reach zero will usually die, with exceptions for amulet of life saving, shapeshifted vampires, and polymorphed heroes.
facts.detect: Checking inventory for amulet of life saving, observing monster behavior for shapeshifting, and noticing polymorph status.
facts.action: Carry an amulet of life saving, be cautious around shapeshifting monsters, and avoid situations that could reduce HP to zero while polymorphed.

facts.fact: Quaffing healing potions can increase maximum hit points if doing so would heal more than the difference between current and maximum HP.
facts.detect: Checking inventory for healing potions and current HP status.
facts.action: Use healing potions to increase maximum HP when possible.

facts.fact: A hero gains hit points when leveling up, with the amount determined by race, role, and constitution.
facts.detect: Leveling up and checking HP gain.
facts.action: Level up to increase HP, especially if constitution is high.

facts.fact: Natural HP-healing rate varies by experience level and constitution, with slower recovery for higher levels and worse encumbrance.
facts.detect: Checking experience level, constitution, and encumbrance status.
facts.action: Manage encumbrance and wait for natural HP recovery when necessary.

facts.fact: Certain monsters, like adult dragons and player monsters, have specific HP generation rules.
facts.detect: Encountering adult dragons or player monsters.
facts.action: Be prepared for high HP encounters with these monsters.

facts.fact: A grabbing attack prevents the player from moving away from a monster, with messages like 'grabs you!' or 'You are being crushed.'
facts.detect: Messages like 'grabs you!' or 'You are being crushed.'
facts.action: Use a wand of teleportation to teleport away or engrave Elbereth if possible.

facts.fact: A non-cursed oilskin cloak or greased outermost item prevents the initial grabbing attack.
facts.detect: Having an oilskin cloak or greased outermost item.
facts.action: Wear an oilskin cloak or grease outermost item before encountering monsters with grabbing attacks.

facts.fact: Drowning attack is a two-stage instadeath that occurs when a monster first holds you and then pulls you into water.
facts.detect: Messages like 'brushes against your leg' or 'swings itself around you!'
facts.action: Wear an amulet of magical breathing or teleport away with a wand of teleportation.

facts.fact: Stopping levitation on dry land releases the monster's hold.
facts.detect: Being held by a monster on dry land.
facts.action: Stop levitating to release the monster's hold.

facts.fact: A sticky attack is preventable by high magic cancellation and can occur when stumbling upon mimics.
facts.detect: Stumbling upon mimics or being stuck to a mimic.
facts.action: Increase magic cancellation or polymorph into a monster that does not breathe.

facts.fact: Holes are much less likely to be randomly generated than other eligible types. Only 1 in 7 attempts to randomly place a hole will succeed.
facts.detect: There's a gaping hole under you!
facts.action: Explore other areas of the level to find holes, as they are less common.

facts.fact: If you step on a hole, there is a chance you escape its effects. This chance is normally 20%, but 0% if fumbling or in Sokoban, and 100% if outside Sokoban and levitating, flying, being held, polymorphed into a huge monster etc.
facts.detect: There's a gaping hole under you!
facts.action: If levitating or flying, step on the hole to safely descend.

facts.fact: If you or a monster step on to a hole and fail to escape it, or an item is thrown onto the same square as a hole, it will fall a random number of dungeon levels, with increasingly less chance of higher numbers of levels.
facts.detect: You fall down a shaft!
facts.action: Avoid stepping on holes unless you are certain you can escape or are levitating/flying.

facts.fact: Holes in Sokoban, only possible on levels 2, 3 or 4, are special. These holes have air currents that will pull you into them even if you are flying, jumping or levitating over them.
facts.detect: Sokoban level 2, 3, or 4
facts.action: Avoid holes in Sokoban levels by filling them with boulders or using heavy iron balls.

facts.fact: A hole can be removed by pushing a boulder onto it.
facts.detect: There's a gaping hole under you!
facts.action: Push a boulder onto the hole to remove it.

facts.fact: Killing humans generated peaceful is murder, no matter what your starting race.
facts.detect: Peaceful human monster name (e.g., 'shopkeeper', 'guard')
facts.action: Avoid killing peaceful human monsters to prevent alignment penalties.

facts.fact: Human monsters cannot be tamed.
facts.detect: Attempting to tame a human monster (e.g., 'shopkeeper', 'guard')
facts.action: Do not attempt to tame human monsters.

facts.fact: Figurines of human monsters are very rarely generated.
facts.detect: Finding a figurine in the game
facts.action: Do not rely on finding figurines of human monsters.

facts.fact: Humans do not respect Elbereth or a scroll of scare monster when you are not standing on it.
facts.detect: Human monster name (e.g., 'Keystone Kop', 'shopkeeper')
facts.action: Do not rely on Elbereth or scare monster scrolls to protect against human monsters.

facts.fact: Genociding human monsters reduces the alignment record of lawful adventurers, and increases that of chaotic ones.
facts.detect: Genocide message for human monsters
facts.action: Avoid genocide of human monsters if you are lawful to prevent alignment penalties.

facts.fact: Humans lack infravision.
facts.detect: Dark areas in the dungeon
facts.action: Carry a light source or use telepathy to navigate dark areas.

facts.fact: Hostile gnomes and dwarves will attack humans of non-lawful alignments.
facts.detect: Gnomes or dwarves with hostile alignment
facts.action: Avoid or neutralize hostile gnomes and dwarves to prevent combat.

facts.fact: Eating nurse meat from tins is considered cannibalism for humans.
facts.detect: Tin containing nurse meat
facts.action: Use potions of full healing instead of nurse meat to avoid cannibalism penalties.

facts.fact: Human heroes have the second-best HP gains overall when gaining experience levels.
facts.detect: Level up messages
facts.action: Focus on gaining experience to improve health and energy.

facts.fact: Human heroes start with default equipment for each role.
facts.detect: Starting inventory
facts.action: Adapt strategy based on the default equipment provided for the chosen role.

facts.fact: Genocide of the human or elf monster class from reading a blessed scroll of genocide will always kill the hero, regardless of their own race.
facts.detect: Reading a blessed scroll of genocide
facts.action: Avoid reading a blessed scroll of genocide if you are a human or elf character.

facts.fact: Heroes polymorphed into the form of any vampire are warned of any human or elf monsters on the current level.
facts.detect: Message: 'You feel uneasy around humans and elves.'
facts.action: Avoid human or elf monsters if you are a vampire.

facts.fact: Mind flayers and master mind flayers are often nasty enough as hostile monsters that they warrant elimination of the entire monster class using a blessed scroll of genocide.
facts.detect: Mind flayer or master mind flayer name
facts.action: Use a blessed scroll of genocide to eliminate all mind flayers and master mind flayers

facts.fact: Using a blessed scroll of genocide will remove all {{mcsl|h}} from the current game including dwarves, serving as a particularly aggravating form of YASD for dwarvish characters.
facts.detect: Mind flayer or master mind flayer name
facts.action: Avoid using blessed scroll of genocide if playing as a dwarf

facts.fact: I represents the detected position of a monster that is invisible or otherwise cannot be seen by you
facts.detect: I on the map
facts.action: Be cautious and prepare for combat, as there is an invisible monster nearby

facts.fact: i represents an imp or minor demon (manes, homunculus, imp, lemure, quasit, tengu)
facts.detect: i on the map
facts.action: Prepare to fight or avoid these minor demons

facts.fact: Ice is slippery, and walking on it often causes you to stumble.
facts.detect: You feel the ice shift beneath you!
facts.action: Wear snow boots or polymorph into a monster with cold resistance to prevent slipping.

facts.fact: Ice created by a spell or breath attack has a chance of melting on its own after between 50–2000 turns.
facts.detect: The ice seems very soft and slushy.
facts.action: Avoid standing on ice that is about to melt, especially near fire traps or fire-breathing monsters.

facts.fact: Flames from a fire-breathing monster, a wand of fire, fire traps, and other sources of fire can melt ice and cause you to fall into the newly created moat.
facts.detect: Some ice melts away.
facts.action: Carry a source of levitation or water walking boots to prevent drowning if you fall into water.

facts.fact: Ice created on level generation will always be permanent, and newly created ice has a chance of becoming permanent as well.
facts.detect: The ice seems very solid and sturdy.
facts.action: Explore areas with permanent ice cautiously, as it may still be dangerous due to melting from fire sources.

facts.fact: Slipping on ice may, with 1/(10+Dex) chance, cause you to slip and move an extra space in a random direction.
facts.detect: You feel the ice shift beneath you!
facts.action: Increase your dexterity or wear snow boots to reduce the chance of slipping further.

facts.fact: The Great Ring of Ice level contains five frosters, two peaceful white dragons, and a peaceful baby white dragon.
facts.detect: Encountering peaceful frosters, white dragons, and a baby white dragon.
facts.action: Avoid combat with peaceful monsters and try to pass through the level quickly.

facts.fact: The Great Ring of Ice level has six falling rock traps and two magic traps.
facts.detect: Stepping on a falling rock or triggering a magic trap.
facts.action: Be cautious and use telepathy or a magic whistle to detect traps.

facts.fact: The Earth Mage's Cave level contains ten earth elementals and four xorn.
facts.detect: Encountering earth elementals and xorn.
facts.action: Prepare for combat and be cautious of their abilities.

facts.fact: The Lair of the Earth Mage level contains eight earth elementals and five xorn.
facts.detect: Encountering earth elementals and xorn.
facts.action: Prepare for combat and be cautious of their abilities.

facts.fact: The Lair of the Earth Mage level has four falling rock traps and two random traps.
facts.detect: Stepping on a falling rock or triggering a random trap.
facts.action: Be cautious and use telepathy or a magic whistle to detect traps.

facts.fact: Items that you start with are automatically identified for you.
facts.detect: Starting inventory items
facts.action: Use identified items from the start inventory

facts.fact: When reading a scroll of identify, you will be allowed to ID one or more of your possessions depending on the scroll's beatitude.
facts.detect: Scroll of identify
facts.action: Read scroll of identify to identify items

facts.fact: Selling or buying an item in a shop will cause the shopkeeper to tell you the appearance of the item.
facts.detect: Shopkeeper's description of item appearance
facts.action: Sell or buy items to get identification

facts.fact: Formal type identification causes a type of item to be called by its proper name, overriding its appearance and anything you may have called the type.
facts.detect: Item name changes to proper name
facts.action: Wait for auto-identification or use methods to trigger it

facts.fact: Some items are identified instantly when you wear, quaff, or otherwise use them.
facts.detect: Immediate item effect
facts.action: Use items to identify them

facts.fact: A hero with immunity to sickness is completely immune to both food poisoning from tainted corpses and disease attacks from monsters like Juiblex.
facts.detect: You feel a slight illness. (disease attack) or It doesn't seem at all sickening though... (tainted corpse)
facts.action: Seek to polymorph into a ghoul or any type of fungus or mold to gain immunity to sickness.

facts.fact: Green dragon scale mail and green dragon scales provide immunity to sickness while worn.
facts.detect: Green dragon scale mail or green dragon scales
facts.action: Equip green dragon scale mail or green dragon scales to gain immunity to sickness.

facts.fact: There are no items or corpses that confer immunity to sickness.
facts.detect: No items or corpses provide immunity to sickness.
facts.action: Do not rely on items or corpses for immunity to sickness, focus on polymorphing or equipping green dragon scale mail/scales.

facts.fact: Monsters cannot obtain immunity to sickness, but disease attacks cannot sicken or deal damage to other monsters.
facts.detect: Encounter with monsters like Juiblex or Pestilence.
facts.action: Be aware that monsters cannot be sickened or damaged by disease attacks.

facts.fact: The property is highly useful for specific cases such as dealing with Pestilence and Demogorgon.
facts.detect: Encounter with Pestilence or Demogorgon.
facts.action: Ensure immunity to sickness before facing Pestilence or Demogorgon.

facts.fact: All monsters in the class except the tengu are vulnerable to silver, taking an extra +d20 damage when hit with a silver item.
facts.detect: Monsters such as manes, homunculus, imp, lemure, quasit (excluding tengu)
facts.action: Use silver weapons or silver-coated weapons to deal extra damage.

facts.fact: Minor demons do not resist death magic or take damage from holy water.
facts.detect: Monsters such as manes, homunculus, imp, lemure, quasit (excluding tengu)
facts.action: Use death magic or holy water to deal additional damage or effects.

facts.fact: Imps and minor demons are the first quest monster class for Knights.
facts.detect: Knight quest levels
facts.action: Be prepared for imps and minor demons as the first type of monster encountered in the Knight quest.

facts.fact: Random imps and minor demons are generated on some levels of the Knight quest and all levels of the Wizard quest.
facts.detect: Knight quest levels and Wizard quest levels
facts.action: Expect imps and minor demons to appear on these quest levels.

facts.fact: A confused monster will move randomly and may blunder into and attack a player it might not otherwise, unless the player is protected by Elbereth, a scroll of scare monster or sanctuary.
facts.detect: Monster name and 'confused' status message
facts.action: Use Elbereth, a scroll of scare monster, or sanctuary to protect against confused monsters.

facts.fact: Scared monsters generally run away from the player and may use ranged attacks they would not otherwise use.
facts.detect: Monster name and 'scared' status message
facts.action: Avoid provoking monsters into a scared state and be prepared for ranged attacks.

facts.fact: Blind monsters with eyes move randomly and do not respect Elbereth.
facts.detect: Monster name and 'blind' status message
facts.action: Be cautious around blind monsters as they may move unpredictably and ignore Elbereth.

facts.fact: Invisible players are assumed to be on a square within 1 square of their current location by monsters, making melee hits less likely but ranged attacks possible.
facts.detect: Player status 'invisible'
facts.action: Use invisibility to avoid melee combat and be cautious of ranged attacks from monsters.

facts.fact: Displacement makes monsters assume the player is on a square within 2 squares of their current location, making melee hits less likely but ranged attacks possible.
facts.detect: Player status 'displacement'
facts.action: Use displacement to avoid melee combat and be cautious of ranged attacks from monsters.

facts.fact: Star-elves and their grown-up forms can be found very rarely in crystal skulls (1/24 for Star-elves, 1/48 for Star-emperors and Star-empresses, 1/12 chance for any).
facts.detect: Finding a crystal skull and checking its contents.
facts.action: If a crystal skull is found, check its contents for a Star-elf or its grown-up form to obtain imperial elven gear.

facts.fact: Elven heroes in a role other than Madperson finding the Stranger in bones can spawn a dream-leech Star-elf with its inventory.
facts.detect: Encountering the Stranger in bones and observing the spawned yellow nasties.
facts.action: If the Stranger is encountered in bones, check the spawned yellow nasties for a dream-leech Star-elf.

facts.fact: There is a ~45% chance of finding a crystal skull containing a set of imperial elven armor, but only a ~25% chance of finding one that is useful and can be upgraded.
facts.detect: Finding a crystal skull and checking its contents.
facts.action: If a crystal skull is found, check its contents for a set of imperial elven armor and assess if it can be upgraded.

facts.fact: Mithril imperial elven armor is likely the best choice, offering 9/9 base AC/DR compared to 6/6 from wood.
facts.detect: Finding imperial elven armor and checking its material.
facts.action: If imperial elven armor is found, check if it is made of mithril.

facts.fact: Upgrading imperial elven armor requires having Dantalion bound or prolonged eye contact with the summoned monster from the skull for Tourists.
facts.detect: Having Dantalion bound or prolonged eye contact with the summoned monster from the skull.
facts.action: Ensure Dantalion is bound or prolonged eye contact is made with the summoned monster from the skull to upgrade the armor.

facts.fact: An inediate player completes the game without eating to achieve the foodless conduct.
facts.detect: The player notices they have not eaten any food throughout the game.
facts.action: The bot should avoid eating any food to achieve the foodless conduct.

facts.fact: Monsters classified as inediate do not need to eat to stay alive.
facts.detect: The bot encounters monsters like undead, demonic, angelic beings, or magical creatures.
facts.action: The bot should be cautious as these monsters do not need to eat and can persist indefinitely.

facts.fact: Polymorphing into an inediate form suppresses the standard one point per turn of nutrition consumption.
facts.detect: The bot polymorphs into an inediate form such as a vampire.
facts.action: The bot should polymorph into an inediate form to temporarily avoid nutrition loss.

facts.fact: Killer bees and queen bees are inediate.
facts.detect: The bot encounters killer bees or queen bees.
facts.action: The bot should be aware that these bees do not need to eat and can be persistent enemies.

facts.fact: Acid blobs and quivering blobs are inediate.
facts.detect: The bot encounters acid blobs or quivering blobs.
facts.action: The bot should be aware that these blobs do not need to eat and can be persistent enemies.

facts.fact: Infravision is an intrinsic property possessed by dwarves, elves, gnomes, and orcs.
facts.detect: The bot's character is a lawful dwarvish Valkyrie.
facts.action: No action needed as the bot already has infravision.

facts.fact: Infravision allows a character to detect warm-blooded or fire-based monsters in their line of sight, even if that location is unlit.
facts.detect: Warm-blooded or fire-based monsters in unlit areas.
facts.action: Use infravision to navigate dark areas and detect potential threats.

facts.fact: Infravision does not detect invisible creatures unless you can also see invisible.
facts.detect: Invisible monsters.
facts.action: Be cautious around invisible monsters as infravision does not help in detecting them.

facts.fact: Turning to stone (unless stoning resistant) can occur by touching, eating, kicking, sacrificing, tinning, falling into a pit while wielding, falling down stairs while burdened and wielding, or attacking a cockatrice or chickatrice without gloves or while polymorphed.
facts.detect: Touching, eating, kicking, sacrificing, tinning, falling into a pit, falling down stairs, or attacking a cockatrice or chickatrice corpse.
facts.action: Avoid touching, eating, kicking, sacrificing, tinning, falling into a pit, falling down stairs, or attacking a cockatrice or chickatrice corpse without gloves or while polymorphed.

facts.fact: Being hit by a death ray without magic resistance will instantly kill the player.
facts.detect: Zapping a wand of death or finger of death, or being hit by a monster's wand of death.
facts.action: Avoid zapping a wand of death or finger of death, and avoid monsters with wands of death.

facts.fact: Being fatally poisoned by a monster attack, a poisoned weapon, or a spiked pit will instantly kill the player unless they have poison resistance.
facts.detect: Attacked by a poisonous monster, hit by a poisoned weapon, or falling into a spiked pit.
facts.action: Avoid poisonous monsters, poisoned weapons, and spiked pits unless you have poison resistance.

facts.fact: Falling into lava without fire resistance will instantly kill the player.
facts.detect: Falling into lava.
facts.action: Avoid falling into lava unless you have fire resistance.

facts.fact: Intentionally level teleporting yourself to level 0 or any negative-numbered level will instantly kill the player.
facts.detect: Attempting to level teleport to level 0 or negative-numbered levels.
facts.action: Avoid level teleporting to level 0 or negative-numbered levels.

facts.fact: Intelligence is the spellcasting stat for the following roles: Archeologist, Barbarian, Caveman, Ranger, Rogue, Samurai, Tourist, and Wizard.
facts.detect: Hero's role is one of the listed spellcasting roles.
facts.action: Prioritize raising intelligence to improve spellcasting abilities.

facts.fact: A hero with higher intelligence has a better chance of successfully reading a spellbook.
facts.detect: Hero attempts to read a spellbook and fails.
facts.action: Increase intelligence to improve spellbook reading success rate.

facts.fact: Wizards with high intelligence benefit from reduced-hunger casting or even hungerless casting of spells.
facts.detect: Hero is a Wizard and is casting spells while hungry.
facts.action: Increase intelligence to reduce or eliminate hunger from spellcasting.

facts.fact: Eating the corpse or tin of a mind flayer or master mind flayer has a 1/2 chance of increasing the hero's intelligence by 1.
facts.detect: Hero encounters a mind flayer or master mind flayer corpse or tin.
facts.action: Eat the corpse or tin to potentially increase intelligence.

facts.fact: Intelligence can be decreased by the attribute-decreasing effect of quaffing a non-blessed potion of sickness.
facts.detect: Hero drinks a non-blessed potion of sickness.
facts.action: Avoid drinking non-blessed potions of sickness to prevent intelligence loss.

facts.fact: Mind flayers and master mind flayers use intelligence drain for their tentacle attacks.
facts.detect: Encountering a mind flayer or master mind flayer
facts.action: Avoid melee combat with mind flayers and master mind flayers

facts.fact: A worn helm, especially a greased one, can block intelligence drain attacks.
facts.detect: Wearing a helm, especially a greased helm
facts.action: Wear a greased helm when facing mind flayers

facts.fact: Intelligence drain attacks can cause instant death if the hero's base intelligence is 3.
facts.detect: Base intelligence is 3
facts.action: Avoid situations where intelligence can be drained when base intelligence is 3

facts.fact: Intelligence drain attacks cause amnesia, removing 1/4 of known level maps and discovered objects.
facts.detect: Message 'Your brain is eaten!'
facts.action: Have means to re-identify items and maps after an attack

facts.fact: A hero polymorphed into a monster immune to intelligence drain is not affected by the attack.
facts.detect: Polymorphed into a monster immune to intelligence drain
facts.action: Polymorph into a monster immune to intelligence drain if threatened

facts.fact: Certain monsters are intelligent and can use dungeon features such as stairs and polymorph traps, even if they lack hands.
facts.detect: Monster names like 'floating eye', 'dragon', 'salamander', etc.
facts.action: Avoid or prepare for intelligent monsters that can use dungeon features to escape or trap the player.

facts.fact: Intelligent monsters include those in the classes & (demons), A (angels), C (constructs), D (dragons), G (giants), H (humanoids), K (kobolds), L (lich), N (nagas), O (orcs), Q (queeleen), T (tengu), U (unicorns), V (vampires), W (wraiths), X (xorn), g (golems), h (human), i (ice demons), k (kittens), l (lich), n (nymph), o (orc), and others.
facts.detect: Monster names or classes mentioned.
facts.action: Be cautious around these monsters as they can use dungeon features and items.

facts.fact: Monsters like couatl, ki-rin, and unicorns are intelligent but have no hands.
facts.detect: Monster names 'couatl', 'ki-rin', 'white unicorn', 'gray unicorn', 'black unicorn'.
facts.action: Treat these monsters as potentially dangerous due to their intelligence and ability to use dungeon features.

facts.fact: A hero hit by an attack that causes intense pain will lose 6 movement points for their next action and be unable to spellcast, chat, or read scrolls or spellbooks for two turns if they scream.
facts.detect: Screaming in pain message
facts.action: Avoid or block attacks that cause intense pain, especially when near stairs or important items.

facts.fact: A hero has an 8/8 chance of the poison triggering, dealing 6-15 extra damage and a 6/8 chance of decreasing strength by 3-6 points, and a 30/8 chance of decreasing constitution by 3-6 points.
facts.detect: Intense pain damage message
facts.action: Equip poison resistance or magic cancellation to mitigate the effects.

facts.fact: Monsters with attacks that cause intense pain include ancient of thought, jellyfish, chorister jelly, desert seer, tongue-puppet monsters, and parasitology research path undead hunters.
facts.detect: Monster names or descriptions
facts.action: Avoid or prepare to fight these monsters with appropriate resistance or cancellation.

facts.fact: Poison resistance blocks the attribute-draining effects of the attack and halves the poison damage taken.
facts.detect: Poison resistance status
facts.action: Equip poison resistance to mitigate damage and attribute loss.

facts.fact: Magic cancellation can block the poison of melee attack types that inflict intense pain.
facts.detect: Magic cancellation status
facts.action: Equip magic cancellation to block intense pain attacks.

facts.fact: You can gain intrinsic protection by donating to a peaceful aligned priest in a temple, up to 9 points guaranteed, unlikely after that. In NetHack 3.6.7 and before, donate at least 400 but less than 600 times your XL.
facts.detect: Approaching a peaceful aligned priest in a temple, having gold in inventory.
facts.action: Donate to the priest to gain intrinsic protection.

facts.fact: You can gain intrinsic protection as a favor from prayer if luck is at least 6.
facts.detect: Having a luck score of at least 6, praying to god.
facts.action: Pray to god to gain intrinsic protection as a favor.

facts.fact: Eating a ring of protection can gain intrinsic protection equal to the ring's bonus if successful.
facts.detect: Eating a ring of protection, seeing 'magic spreads through your body'.
facts.action: Eat a ring of protection to gain intrinsic protection.

facts.fact: All intrinsic protection is lost if you incite any god to smite you, including praying when it is unsafe to pray, sacrificing a former pet, sacrificing a coaligned unicorn, sacrificing any unicorn on an altar of the same alignment, sacrificing a member of your own race, offering an identified cheap plastic imitation of the Amulet of Yendor on your own high altar in the Astral plane, killing a coaligned priest, putting on or removing a helm of opposite alignment, attempting to put on a helm of opposite alignment in the quest, converting yourself to another alignment through sacrifice, having your protection stolen by a gremlin's intrinsic theft, praying for unholy water at a cross aligned altar.
facts.detect: Messages indicating divine displeasure or specific actions that lead to divine smiting.
facts.action: Avoid actions that lead to divine smiting to prevent losing intrinsic protection.

facts.fact: If you donate the right amount of gold to a priest (between 2*baseline and 3*baseline), you can execute the code that gives you protection. If you previously had protection but lost it to a gremlin, one donation restores all previous protection.
facts.detect: Donating to a priest, seeing messages indicating successful donation.
facts.action: Donate to a priest to restore lost intrinsic protection.

facts.fact: The only monster with the intrinsic theft ability in NetHack is the gremlin, which can steal intrinsics only at night.
facts.detect: Night-time and encountering a gremlin
facts.action: Avoid or prepare for intrinsic theft by gremlins at night

facts.fact: If hit by a gremlin's intrinsic-stealing attack, there is a 1/10 chance of losing one of the listed intrinsic properties.
facts.detect: Message 'chuckles.' from a gremlin
facts.action: Be prepared to lose any of the listed intrinsics if attacked by a gremlin

facts.fact: A hero polymorphed into a clay golem form is instantly returned to normal form if hit by an intrinsic theft attack.
facts.detect: Message 'Some writing vanishes from your head!'
facts.action: Avoid polymorphing into a clay golem if gremlins are present

facts.fact: A monster hit by an intrinsic theft attack is cancelled, instantly destroying clay golems.
facts.detect: Message 'Some writing vanishes from head!' when seeing a gremlin attack
facts.action: Avoid letting gremlins attack other monsters, especially clay golems

facts.fact: Intrinsic theft is a rare but serious danger, and the only other forms of intrinsic loss are eating the corpse of a disenchanter.
facts.detect: Encountering a gremlin or disenchanter
facts.action: Keep backup sources of intrinsics and avoid risky situations

facts.fact: The inventory is limited to 52 stacks of objects, a quantity of gold, and a load stone if necessary.
facts.detect: Inventory letter limit reached when picking up an item.
facts.action: Prioritize dropping less essential items to make space for new ones.

facts.fact: The hero is assumed to be carrying a wallet or purse and a backpack or knapsack.
facts.detect: Wallet or purse can be examined with the '$' command, backpack or knapsack cannot be dropped.
facts.action: Use the wallet or purse to store gold and the backpack or knapsack to store items.

facts.fact: The backpack or knapsack can hold 52 distinct stacks of items.
facts.detect: Backpack or knapsack cannot accommodate more items.
facts.action: Organize inventory to maximize the use of the backpack or knapsack capacity.

facts.fact: The wallet and backpack/knapsack are impervious to fire, shock damage, rotting, and cursing.
facts.detect: Wallet or backpack/knapsack cannot be damaged by fire or shock.
facts.action: Store valuable items in the wallet or backpack/knapsack for protection.

facts.fact: Nethack characters have a source of fire to light lamps and candles.
facts.detect: Characters can light lamps and candles without carrying a torch.
facts.action: Use the source of fire to light items as needed.

facts.fact: Quaffing a blessed potion of invisibility grants permanent invisibility with a 1/30 chance, increased to 1/15 if already invisible.
facts.detect: Quaffing a blessed potion of invisibility.
facts.action: Quaff a blessed potion of invisibility to attempt to gain permanent invisibility.

facts.fact: Wearing a cloak of invisibility grants temporary invisibility while worn.
facts.detect: Wearing a cloak of invisibility.
facts.action: Wear a cloak of invisibility to become invisible.

facts.fact: Zapping a wand of make invisible at oneself grants permanent invisibility unless wearing a mummy wrapping.
facts.detect: Zapping a wand of make invisible at oneself.
facts.action: Zap a wand of make invisible at oneself to become permanently invisible.

facts.fact: Eating a stalker corpse or tin grants permanent invisibility if not already invisible.
facts.detect: Eating a stalker corpse or tin.
facts.action: Eat a stalker corpse or tin to gain permanent invisibility.

facts.fact: Invoking The Orb of Detection toggles a hero's invisibility on or off.
facts.detect: Using The Orb of Detection.
facts.action: Use The Orb of Detection to toggle invisibility.

facts.fact: A monster can become invisible by quaffing a potion of invisibility.
facts.detect: Suddenly you cannot see [monster name].
facts.action: Be cautious and use a scroll of remove curse or a blessed scroll of remove curse to remove the potion of invisibility from the monster if you have one.

facts.fact: You can see invisible monsters if you have the 'see invisible' intrinsic.
facts.detect: Your body takes on a transparency.
facts.action: Gain the 'see invisible' intrinsic to detect invisible monsters.

facts.fact: You are invisible to others if you have intrinsic invisibility and can see invisible.
facts.detect: You are invisible to others.
facts.action: Maintain intrinsic invisibility if you can see invisible to remain undetected.

facts.fact: Wearing a mummy wrapping makes you visible.
facts.detect: You are visible.
facts.action: Remove the mummy wrapping if you are trying to remain invisible.

facts.fact: Losing intrinsic invisibility while having see invisible intrinsic changes your visibility status.
facts.detect: You can't see through yourself anymore!
facts.action: Be aware of your visibility status changes and adjust your tactics accordingly.

facts.fact: The Candelabrum of Invocation must have 7 candles placed in it to be lit.
facts.detect: Candelabrum with 7 candles
facts.action: Ensure the Candelabrum has 7 candles before attempting to light it.

facts.fact: The Bell of Opening must be charged and non-cursed to be rung.
facts.detect: Bell of Opening with a charge
facts.action: Ensure the Bell of Opening is charged and non-cursed before ringing it.

facts.fact: The Book of the Dead must be non-cursed and read last.
facts.detect: Non-cursed Book of the Dead
facts.action: Ensure the Book of the Dead is non-cursed and read it last.

facts.fact: Performing the ritual creates a ring of fire traps and a moat around the player.
facts.detect: Fire traps and moat around the player
facts.action: Be prepared to deal with fire traps and moat after the ritual.

facts.fact: The correct order for the ritual is Candelabrum, Bell, Book.
facts.detect: Order of items used
facts.action: Use the items in the correct order: Candelabrum, Bell, Book.

facts.fact: Artifacts tire after you invoke them, and you cannot do so again for rnz(100) turns (averages 100; can be up to 2000, but 95% of the time it is less than 400).
facts.detect: The bot can notice the cooldown period by attempting to invoke an artifact and receiving the message 'You feel that the is ignoring you'.
facts.action: The bot should wait the appropriate number of turns before invoking an artifact again to avoid extending the cooldown period.

facts.fact: The optimum strategy is waiting 82;81;68;81;88;67;54;96;78;62;88;81;65;63;81;65 turns after consecutive failed #invokes and restarting the list after successes.
facts.detect: The bot can detect consecutive failed invocations and track the number of failed attempts.
facts.action: The bot should follow the optimal waiting schedule after failed invocations to maximize the expected rate of success per turn.

facts.fact: The Staff of Aesculapius heals half HP damage, cures sickness, unblinds, unslimes.
facts.detect: The bot can detect when it is sick, blinded, or slimed, or when it has half HP damage.
facts.action: The bot should invoke the Staff of Aesculapius when it is in a state that can be healed or cured by the staff.

facts.fact: The Platinum Yendorian Express Card charges objects like a scroll of charging with the same blessed/cursed status.
facts.detect: The bot can detect when it has a Platinum Yendorian Express Card and objects that need charging.
facts.action: The bot should use the Platinum Yendorian Express Card to charge objects, especially wands, to maximize their use.

facts.fact: The Orb of Fate allows for level teleportation.
facts.detect: The bot can detect when it needs to move to a different level.
facts.action: The bot should invoke the Orb of Fate to teleport to a different level when necessary.

facts.fact: Monsters pull back from making melee attacks against you, and grabbing monsters loosen their grip.
facts.detect: Observing monsters backing away or loosening grip when attacking.
facts.action: Pray to gain invulnerability before engaging in melee combat with dangerous monsters.

facts.fact: Poison clouds do not affect you.
facts.detect: Entering a room or area with poison clouds.
facts.action: Pray to gain invulnerability before entering areas with poison clouds.

facts.fact: You do not burn nutrition.
facts.detect: Checking nutrition levels while hungry.
facts.action: Pray to gain invulnerability when hungry to prevent nutrition loss.

facts.fact: Timeouts other than for Luck do not operate—in particular, stoning, sliming, strangulation, vomiting, and sickness freeze at the point where the prayer began.
facts.detect: Experiencing stoning, sliming, strangulation, vomiting, or sickness.
facts.action: Pray to gain invulnerability to halt these conditions.

facts.fact: If trapped in lava, you will not sink further.
facts.detect: Being in lava and sinking.
facts.action: Pray to gain invulnerability if trapped in lava.

facts.fact: Wearing iron armor increases spellcasting failure rates.
facts.detect: Wearing iron armor (plate mail, splint mail, banded mail, chain mail, orcish chain mail, scale mail, ring mail, orcish ring mail)
facts.action: Avoid wearing iron armor if you plan to cast spells.

facts.fact: Iron helms protect against falling objects and reduce damage from falling piercers and rocks.
facts.detect: Equipped iron helm (orcish helm, dwarvish iron helm, dented pot, helmet, helm of caution, helm of opposite alignment, helm of telepathy)
facts.action: Wear an iron helm to protect against falling objects and piercers.

facts.fact: Hitting a brown or black pudding with iron weapons or items causes them to divide and corrodes iron items.
facts.detect: Encountering brown or black pudding
facts.action: Avoid using iron weapons or items against brown or black puddings.

facts.fact: Metallivores eat iron objects but avoid certain items like poisoned weapons, artifacts, amulet of strangulation, and ring of slow digestion.
facts.detect: Encountering metallivores (rust monsters, iron golems)
facts.action: Avoid letting metallivores eat certain items to prevent loss.

facts.fact: Iron golems take increased damage from water and rusting attacks.
facts.detect: Encountering iron golem
facts.action: Avoid using water or rusting attacks against iron golems.

facts.fact: Iron bars cannot be dug through and have a chance of stopping objects thrown through them.
facts.detect: Attempting to dig through iron bars or throwing objects at them.
facts.action: Avoid throwing large objects at iron bars and be cautious with smaller objects as they may be stopped.

facts.fact: Monsters can pass through iron bars if they are whirly, amorphous, phasing, tiny, or slithy and no bigger than medium-sized.
facts.detect: Observing monsters passing through iron bars.
facts.action: Be prepared for monsters to pass through iron bars and potentially attack from the other side.

facts.fact: Acid can dissolve iron bars, but only with a 1/5 chance for thrown potions.
facts.detect: Attempting to throw a potion of acid at iron bars.
facts.action: Use a force-fight with a potion of acid or a corrosive breath attack to reliably dissolve iron bars.

facts.fact: Iron bars in non-diggable regions cannot be dissolved by acid.
facts.detect: Attempting to dissolve iron bars in a non-diggable region.
facts.action: Avoid attempting to dissolve iron bars in non-diggable regions as it will not work.

facts.fact: Iron bars on Medusa's Island can cause petrification if you see Medusa through them.
facts.detect: Approaching Medusa's dwelling on Medusa's Island.
facts.action: Wear a blindfold or towel before approaching Medusa's dwelling to avoid petrification.

facts.fact: Items can be randomly found on the floor and in containers, with different probabilities depending on the dungeon level.
facts.detect: The bot can detect the probability changes by noting the dungeon level and the types of items found.
facts.action: The bot should prioritize picking up items based on the current dungeon level's item generation probabilities.

facts.fact: Comestibles have a high generation probability in normal dungeons (20%) and inside containers (15%).
facts.detect: The bot can detect comestibles by their symbol '%'.
facts.action: The bot should prioritize picking up comestibles to keep fed.

facts.fact: Potions and scrolls have a high generation probability in normal dungeons (16% each) and inside containers (18% each).
facts.detect: The bot can detect potions by their symbol '!' and scrolls by their symbol '?'.
facts.action: The bot should prioritize identifying potions and scrolls to avoid harmful effects.

facts.fact: Wands and rings have a lower generation probability in normal dungeons (4% and 3% respectively) but higher in Gehennom (8% and 8% respectively).
facts.detect: The bot can detect wands by their symbol '/' and rings by their symbol '='.
facts.action: The bot should prioritize finding and using wands and rings as it progresses deeper into the dungeon.

facts.fact: Gems have a 7% generation probability in normal dungeons and 18% inside containers.
facts.detect: The bot can detect gems by their symbol '*'.
facts.action: The bot should prioritize picking up gems as they can be sold for a good amount of gold.

facts.fact: The four monsters that have item theft attacks are the monkey, wood nymph, water nymph, and mountain nymph.
facts.detect: Encountering a monkey, wood nymph, water nymph, or mountain nymph
facts.action: Avoid or prepare to defend against these monsters if you have valuable items in your inventory.

facts.fact: Magic cancellation does not protect against item-stealing attacks.
facts.detect: Noticing that a monster with item theft attacks is targeting you
facts.action: Equip gloves or other protective items to prevent theft of worn items.

facts.fact: An animal stealing from the hero that is not cancelled will target and then attempt to steal a singular item.
facts.detect: A monkey or nymph targeting a specific item in your inventory
facts.action: Ensure that any critical items are not easily stolen (e.g., wear gloves over rings, ensure items are not cursed and welded)

facts.fact: A nymph stealing from the hero that is not cancelled will target and then attempt to steal a singular item.
facts.detect: A nymph targeting a specific item in your inventory
facts.action: Ensure that any critical items are not easily stolen (e.g., wear gloves over rings, ensure items are not cursed and welded)

facts.fact: Item theft attempts that 'miss' a mounted hero can fall upon their steed instead, and if the steed's saddle is stolen this way, then the hero will be dismounted without suffering any damage.
facts.detect: Being mounted and encountering a monster with item theft attacks
facts.action: Be cautious when mounted, especially if your steed has valuable items like saddles.

facts.fact: Many players consider it extremely poor form to kill Izchak, a special shopkeeper in Minetown.
facts.detect: Encounter with a shopkeeper named Izchak in Minetown.
facts.action: Avoid killing Izchak to maintain good form and avoid potential social repercussions.

facts.fact: In TNNT, completing the dev team's quest for the Really Cool Shirt is not possible if Izchak was previously killed.
facts.detect: Completion of the dev team's quest in TNNT.
facts.action: Ensure Izchak is alive to receive the Really Cool Shirt reward.

facts.fact: J represents a jelly monster (blue jelly, spotted jelly, ochre jelly)
facts.detect: monster name (blue jelly, spotted jelly, ochre jelly)
facts.action: Avoid or prepare to fight jellies, especially ochre jellies which are dangerous due to their high HP and acid attack.

facts.fact: J represents a jabberwock, a powerful monster in vanilla NetHack
facts.detect: monster name (jabberwock)
facts.action: Avoid or prepare to fight the jabberwock, which is a very dangerous monster with high stats and a vorpal blade.

facts.fact: Press j to move south if numpad movement is off
facts.detect: numpad movement setting
facts.action: Use j to move south if numpad movement is disabled.

facts.fact: Press j to jump if numpad movement is on
facts.detect: numpad movement setting
facts.action: Use j to jump if numpad movement is enabled.

facts.fact: Jabberwocks are represented by an uppercase J glyph ({{white|J}}).
facts.detect: Glyph J on the map
facts.action: Be cautious as Jabberwocks are dangerous and should be approached with a spear or other weapon with a +2 to-hit bonus.

facts.fact: Attacks with weapons using the spear skill gain a +2 to-hit bonus against Jabberwocks.
facts.detect: Equipping a spear or other weapon with the spear skill
facts.action: Use a spear or other weapon with the spear skill to attack Jabberwocks for increased effectiveness.

facts.fact: Jellies are neutral monsters that are amorphous, mindless and unbreathing, and their corpses are vegan and vegetarian-friendly.
facts.detect: Encountering a jelly monster on the map.
facts.action: Eat the corpse if vegan or vegetarian diet is preferred.

facts.fact: Each jelly has a passive attack that triggers in response to melee attacks.
facts.detect: Attacking a jelly with melee.
facts.action: Avoid melee attacks against jellies or use ranged attacks.

facts.fact: The ochre jelly is the only jelly that is not sessile and able to engulf other monsters.
facts.detect: Encountering an ochre jelly.
facts.action: Be cautious and avoid being engulfed by the ochre jelly.

facts.fact: Randomly-generated jellies are always created hostile.
facts.detect: Encountering a randomly generated jelly.
facts.action: Prepare for combat as the jelly will be hostile.

facts.fact: Jellies make up 6/175 of the monsters that are randomly generated on the Knight quest.
facts.detect: Being a Knight and exploring the Knight quest levels.
facts.action: Expect to encounter jellies frequently on the Knight quest.

facts.fact: Juiblex's swamp is located between the 4th and 7th levels of Gehennom (DL 29-36).
facts.detect: Level number or DL (Dungeon Level) in the game.
facts.action: Navigate to DL 29-36 to find Juiblex's swamp.

facts.fact: Juiblex, a slug-like demon lord, lurks at the exact center of the map.
facts.detect: Exact center of the map.
facts.action: Avoid the center of the map to avoid Juiblex.

facts.fact: Three lemures occupy the large island on the center-right of the map.
facts.detect: Three lemures on the large island.
facts.action: Be cautious around the large island with lemures.

facts.fact: All but one of the marked fountains are actually giant mimics.
facts.detect: Fountains on the map.
facts.action: Be cautious around fountains, treat them as potential mimics.

facts.fact: The level is no-teleport.
facts.detect: Cannot teleport on the level.
facts.action: Avoid teleporting on this level.

facts.fact: Jumping consumes d25 nutrition and you become immobile for the rest of the current turn after landing.
facts.detect: Nutrition level and turn counter.
facts.action: Use jumping sparingly to avoid excessive hunger and ensure you can take actions after landing.

facts.fact: You cannot jump over monsters and attempting to do so will anger them.
facts.detect: Monster name or symbol on the map.
facts.action: Avoid jumping over monsters to prevent angering them.

facts.fact: Jumping out of shops counts as direct theft.
facts.detect: Shop floor or item names.
facts.action: Avoid jumping out of shops to prevent theft.

facts.fact: Jumping can be used to escape from pits, lava, webs, and bear traps, but jumping out of a bear trap causes 1d10 damage and can inflict a long-lasting leg wound.
facts.detect: Pit, lava, web, or bear trap symbols on the map.
facts.action: Use jumping to escape dangerous situations but be cautious with bear traps.

facts.fact: Jumping is restricted in various situations such as being in water, levitating, or having wounded legs.
facts.detect: Water symbol, levitation status, or wounded leg message.
facts.action: Avoid jumping in restricted conditions to prevent penalties or damage.

facts.fact: Items in NetHack are generally persistent and do not spontaneously vanish.
facts.detect: Presence of items in the dungeon that do not disappear over time.
facts.action: Collect useful items and manage inventory to avoid clutter.
