facts.detect: A hostile disenchanter appears after casting summon nasties.
facts.action: Avoid casting summon nasties in Gehennom or areas with disenchanters.

facts.fact: Disenchanters can be scared off with instruments like a tooled horn or leather drum.
facts.detect: A tooled horn or leather drum is available.
facts.action: Use a tooled horn or leather drum to scare off a disenchanter.

facts.fact: Disenchanters can be useful for selectively reducing the enchantment of weapons or armor.
facts.detect: A disenchanter is present and a weapon or armor needs to be re-enchanted.
facts.action: Wield the item and hit the disenchanter to reduce its enchantment.

facts.fact: Dispater is a unique monster with a difficulty of 40 and appears in NetHack.
facts.detect: Dispater
facts.action: Avoid or prepare for a high-level encounter if you see or hear about Dispater.

facts.fact: Dispater can bribe the hero if wielding Excalibur, otherwise becomes hostile.
facts.detect: Excalibur in inventory
facts.action: Avoid wielding Excalibur if you know Dispater is nearby.

facts.fact: Dispater is generated with a wand of striking and will use it when possible.
facts.detect: Wand of striking in inventory
facts.action: Ensure you have magic resistance to avoid being hit by the wand.

facts.fact: Dispater is a dangerous spellcaster with access to spells like curse items and summon nasties.
facts.detect: Dispater's spellcasting
facts.action: Prioritize dispelling or countering magic if you encounter Dispater.

facts.fact: Dispater does not leave a corpse upon death.
facts.detect: Dispater's death
facts.action: No action needed, but be aware that you won't get a corpse.

facts.fact: A djinni has a single weapon attack and possesses poison resistance and stoning resistance.
facts.detect: Monster name 'djinni' or message 'You disturbed me, fool!' or 'I am in your debt. I will grant one wish!' or 'Thank you for freeing me!' or 'You freed me!'
facts.action: Avoid melee combat if possible, use poison resistance or stoning resistance enhancing items if available.

facts.fact: Djinn are not randomly generated, and may be peaceful towards neutral heroes.
facts.detect: Message 'Thank you for freeing me!' or 'You freed me!'
facts.action: If peaceful, tame and use as a pet to collect items.

facts.fact: Rubbing a magic lamp or quaffing a smoky potion has a chance of producing a djinni.
facts.detect: Item 'magic lamp' or 'smoky potion'
facts.action: Ensure items are blessed before using to minimize hostile djinni generation.

facts.fact: A djinni does not leave a corpse upon death.
facts.detect: Monster 'djinni' dies
facts.action: Do not rely on corpses for nutrition or items.

facts.fact: Three hostile djinn are generated on the Plane of Air at level creation.
facts.detect: Entering Plane of Air
facts.action: Be prepared for combat upon entering the Plane of Air.

facts.fact: A dog can be tamed by throwing meat or rations at it.
facts.detect: The bot sees a dog on the map.
facts.action: Throw meat or rations at the dog to tame it.

facts.fact: During a full moon, dogs have a 5/6 chance of becoming peaceful instead of tame when thrown acceptable food.
facts.detect: The bot sees a full moon icon or message.
facts.action: Throw food at the dog to pacify it.

facts.fact: Eating a dog corpse or tin grants the aggravate monster intrinsic.
facts.detect: The bot sees a dog corpse or tin.
facts.action: Avoid eating dog corpses or tins unless necessary.

facts.fact: Chatting to a dog can provide information about its tameness and condition.
facts.detect: The bot sees a tame or peaceful dog.
facts.action: Chat with the dog to understand its condition.

facts.fact: Dogs can be polymorphed into other forms if tamed.
facts.detect: The bot sees a tamed dog.
facts.action: Use a wand of polymorph or magic whistle to change the dog's form.

facts.fact: A doppelganger has a 6/7 chance of changing form each turn, potentially becoming a powerful monster or a player monster.
facts.detect: The bot should notice changes in monster appearance or behavior, especially if it starts acting like a powerful monster.
facts.action: The bot should avoid engaging with monsters that suddenly change form or appear unusually powerful, and use cancellation or protection from shape changers to force them into base form.

facts.fact: Eating a doppelganger corpse or tin causes polymorph.
facts.detect: The bot should detect doppelganger corpses or tins.
facts.action: The bot should avoid eating doppelganger corpses or tins unless it is a human Caveman intending to polymorph.

facts.fact: Doppelgangers are a source of player monsters and powerful monsters in the main dungeon and other branches.
facts.detect: The bot should notice the appearance of player monsters or powerful monsters out of depth.
facts.action: The bot should be cautious and quickly deal with doppelgangers, using cancellation or protection from shape changers.

facts.fact: Doppelgangers cannot be permanently polymorphed or subjected to system shock unless they are locked in their base form by protection from shape changers.
facts.detect: The bot should notice doppelgangers that are not changing form despite attempts to polymorph them.
facts.action: The bot should use protection from shape changers to lock doppelgangers in their base form.

facts.fact: In NetHack brass, doppelgangers always imitate the hero, copying their inventory and attributes.
facts.detect: The bot should notice a duplicate of itself or its inventory.
facts.action: The bot should avoid engaging with such duplicates and use cancellation or protection from shape changers to force them into base form.

facts.fact: A dust vortex has an engulfing attack that deals no damage and instead blinds the target for a few turns.
facts.detect: You can't see in here!
facts.action: Carry a blindfold or towel to blind yourself before encountering a dust vortex to avoid being blinded.

facts.fact: Dust vortices possess sleep resistance, poison resistance and stoning resistance.
facts.detect: Not directly detectable, but can be inferred from monster attributes.
facts.action: Be prepared for dust vortices to resist sleep, poison, and stoning attacks.

facts.fact: Dust vortices are generated on the Plane of Earth and Plane of Fire at level creation.
facts.detect: Entering the Plane of Earth or Plane of Fire.
facts.action: Be cautious when entering these planes due to the presence of dust vortices.

facts.fact: Dust vortices are mindless and cannot be seen with telepathy.
facts.detect: Not directly detectable, but can be inferred from monster attributes.
facts.action: Avoid using telepathy to detect dust vortices.

facts.fact: Dust vortices do not leave a corpse upon death.
facts.detect: No corpse is left after killing a dust vortex.
facts.action: Do not rely on corpses for identification or experience.

facts.fact: Dwarves are generated within the Gnomish Mines and Minetown, and can collect items such as armor, weapons, food, gold, and gems.
facts.detect: Encountering dwarves in the Gnomish Mines or Minetown, seeing dwarves carrying or wearing items.
facts.action: Stealthily approach dwarves to loot their collected items, especially armor and weapons.

facts.fact: Dwarves have a single weapon attack and can have up to 10 points of AC from a mithril-coat, iron helm, and iron shoes.
facts.detect: Seeing a dwarf with a mithril-coat, iron helm, and iron shoes.
facts.action: Avoid direct confrontation unless well-prepared, as dwarves can deal significant damage.

facts.fact: Dwarves can be generated with a dwarvish short sword, dwarvish iron helm, and dwarvish mithril-coat.
facts.detect: Encountering a dwarf with a dwarvish short sword, dwarvish iron helm, and dwarvish mithril-coat.
facts.action: Attempt to negotiate or charm the dwarf to obtain the valuable items.

facts.fact: Dwarves are peaceful towards dwarven and gnomish heroes and mostly peaceful towards other lawful heroes.
facts.detect: Encountering a peaceful dwarf.
facts.action: Negotiate or charm the dwarf to obtain items or avoid conflict.

facts.fact: Dwarves can anger other peaceful monsters if attacked, leading to alignment penalties.
facts.detect: Witnessing a dwarf being attacked and seeing other peaceful monsters become hostile.
facts.action: Avoid attacking peaceful dwarves to prevent angering other peaceful monsters.

facts.fact: Dwarf mummies have a 6/7 chance of being generated with a mummy wrapping.
facts.detect: mummy wrapping
facts.action: Pick up mummy wrapping if found, as it is valuable and can be used for bandages or to wrap up items.

facts.fact: A dwarf mummy leaves behind an aged dwarf corpse upon death.
facts.detect: aged dwarf corpse
facts.action: Eat aged dwarf corpse to gain nutrition and experience points.

facts.fact: Dwarf mummies are always hostile.
facts.detect: Hostile dwarf mummy on the map
facts.action: Avoid or prepare to fight hostile dwarf mummies to prevent damage.

facts.fact: Dwarf mummies have resistance to cold, sleep, and poison.
facts.detect: Dwarf mummy resisting cold, sleep, or poison effects
facts.action: Use fire or non-poisonous attacks when fighting dwarf mummies.

facts.fact: Dwarf mummies have a single claw attack.
facts.detect: Dwarf mummy attacking with claw
facts.action: Defend against claw attacks and retaliate with appropriate weapons or spells.

facts.fact: Dwarf zombies have a single claw attack dealing 1d6 damage.
facts.detect: Dwarf zombie icon or name
facts.action: Attack dwarf zombies with melee or ranged weapons, or use spells/scrolls to avoid close combat.

facts.fact: Dwarf zombies can appear in groups of 2 to 4 and are always hostile.
facts.detect: Multiple dwarf zombie icons or names
facts.action: Use area-effect spells or fireballs to clear groups of dwarf zombies.

facts.fact: Dwarf zombies leave an aged dwarf corpse upon death.
facts.detect: Aged dwarf corpse icon or name
facts.action: Eat aged dwarf corpse for nutrition (150) and possible useful items.

facts.fact: Dwarf zombies have resistances to cold, sleep, and poison.
facts.detect: Monster description or resistance check
facts.action: Use fire or acid attacks to bypass resistances.

facts.fact: Dwarf zombies can follow the player to other levels if adjacent.
facts.detect: Dwarf zombie icon following the player
facts.action: Avoid leaving dwarf zombies adjacent when descending or ascending levels.

facts.fact: Earth elementals have a +2 to-hit bonus against weapons that use the pick-axe skill.
facts.detect: Using a pick-axe or dwarvish mattock
facts.action: Equip a pick-axe or dwarvish mattock when fighting earth elementals to gain a +2 to-hit bonus.

facts.fact: Earth elementals can phase through walls.
facts.detect: Monster symbol 'E' moving through walls
facts.action: Be cautious of earth elementals' ability to phase through walls and avoid being surrounded.

facts.fact: Earth elementals are generated when digging with a pick-axe or dwarvish mattock.
facts.detect: Message 'The debris from your digging comes to life!'
facts.action: Avoid digging with a pick-axe or dwarvish mattock in areas where earth elementals are likely to be dangerous.

facts.fact: Earth elementals are the first quest monster for Monks and appear frequently on the Monk quest.
facts.detect: Entering the Monk quest branch
facts.action: Be prepared for earth elementals on the Monk quest and consider strategies to deal with their phasing ability.

facts.fact: Earth elementals have poison resistance, fire resistance, cold resistance, and stoning resistance.
facts.detect: Earth elemental attacking
facts.action: Use weapons and spells that deal damage other than poison, fire, cold, or stoning to defeat earth elementals.

facts.fact: Electric eels have a shocking bite attack that can destroy wands and rings in the target's open inventory.
facts.detect: When an electric eel attacks, the bot will notice if its wands or rings are destroyed.
facts.action: Keep wands and rings in the main inventory and not in the open inventory when near electric eels.

facts.fact: Electric eels have a touch attack that causes it to wrap around the target, resulting in drowning if adjacent to a pool or moat.
facts.detect: The bot will notice if it is wrapped by an electric eel and adjacent to water.
facts.action: Avoid swimming in large bodies of water where electric eels are present and use ranged attacks or teleportation to avoid being wrapped.

facts.fact: Eating an electric eel corpse has a 46% chance of granting shock resistance.
facts.detect: The bot will notice the corpse of an electric eel.
facts.action: Retrieve and eat the corpse of an electric eel to potentially gain shock resistance, but be cautious of the 54% chance of not gaining resistance.

facts.fact: Electric eels are generated in the Plane of Water, making them particularly dangerous there.
facts.detect: The bot will notice when it enters the Plane of Water.
facts.action: Use blessed scroll of genocide to eliminate all electric eels upon entering the Plane of Water.

facts.fact: Electric eels are vulnerable to spells and wands since they lack an MR score, but their -3 AC makes this unreliable for dealing with one that is about to drown you.
facts.detect: The bot will notice the electric eel's AC and MR score.
facts.action: Use wands of teleportation or other reliable methods to keep electric eels at a distance.

facts.fact: An elf has sleep resistance.
facts.detect: elf
facts.action: Eat an elf corpse or tin to gain sleep resistance.

facts.fact: Eating an elf corpse or tin has a 2/3 chance of granting sleep resistance.
facts.detect: elf corpse or tin
facts.action: Eat an elf corpse or tin to potentially gain sleep resistance.

facts.fact: Standard elves are not randomly generated and are not valid polymorph forms or genocide targets.
facts.detect: elf
facts.action: Do not attempt to polymorph into or genocide elves.

facts.fact: An elf corpse left by undead poses a high risk of food poisoning.
facts.detect: elf corpse left by undead
facts.action: Use a tinning kit to safely eat an elf corpse left by undead.

facts.fact: An elf has infravision and can see invisible.
facts.detect: elf
facts.action: Be cautious around elves as they can see invisible and have infravision.

facts.fact: Elf mummies have a 6/7 chance of being generated with a mummy wrapping.
facts.detect: mummy wrapping
facts.action: Pick up and wear the mummy wrapping if it provides useful resistances or benefits.

facts.fact: An elf mummy leaves behind an aged elf corpse upon death.
facts.detect: aged elf corpse
facts.action: Eat the aged elf corpse to gain nutrition and possibly useful intrinsics.

facts.fact: An elf zombie has a single claw attack that deals 1d7 damage.
facts.detect: elf zombie
facts.action: Be prepared to deal with the damage output of an elf zombie, which can be significant for early-game characters.

facts.fact: Eating an elf zombie's corpse has a 2/3 chance of conveying sleep resistance.
facts.detect: aged elf corpse
facts.action: Eat the corpse if you have a tinning kit and a way to cure food poisoning, such as a non-cursed unicorn horn.

facts.fact: Elf zombies can follow the player to other levels if they are adjacent.
facts.detect: elf zombie adjacent to the player
facts.action: Avoid moving to new levels with elf zombies adjacent to prevent them from following.

facts.fact: Elf zombies are part of the first quest monster class for Priests and appear in undead-filled graveyards.
facts.detect: graveyard or Priest quest level
facts.action: Be prepared to encounter elf zombies in these areas and have strategies to deal with them.

facts.fact: Elf zombies are one of the monsters that can be used by player elves to convert cross-aligned altars or summon demons on co-aligned ones.
facts.detect: cross-aligned or co-aligned altar
facts.action: Use elf zombie corpses to convert altars or summon demons if you are an elf player.

facts.fact: An energy vortex has an engulfing attack that deals shock damage and a passive energy drain attack with a 3/4 chance during each of the vortex's turns.
facts.detect: The air around you crackles with electricity. You feel your magical energy drain away.
facts.action: Equip shock resistance and try to avoid being engulfed. Use ranged attacks or a wand of slow monster to weaken the vortex's assault.

facts.fact: Energy vortices possess shock resistance, sleep resistance, disintegration resistance, poison resistance, and stoning resistance.
facts.detect: The energy vortex is immune to certain types of attacks.
facts.action: Carry a source of shock resistance to nullify its attacks.

facts.fact: Energy vortices do not leave a corpse upon death.
facts.detect: No corpse is left after killing an energy vortex.
facts.action: Genocide energy vortices if possible to avoid future encounters.

facts.fact: A ranged attack is all but required to dispatch of an energy vortex quickly since it will not trigger the passive attacks.
facts.detect: The energy vortex is approaching.
facts.action: Use ranged attacks to defeat the vortex.

facts.fact: The energy vortex's MR score of 30 makes all these approaches somewhat risky.
facts.detect: The energy vortex is approaching with a high MR score.
facts.action: Use high magic cancellation to reduce the chances of shocks and energy drain.

facts.fact: Erinyes are lawful and always-female humanoid major demons that will follow the hero to other levels if adjacent.
facts.detect: Adjacent to the hero and following them.
facts.action: Avoid having erinyes adjacent to you and move away if they are.

facts.fact: Erinyes gain abilities based on the hero's alignment abuse, including seeing invisible, amphibious movement, flying, extra damage, regeneration, teleport control, and spellcasting.
facts.detect: Erinyes with abilities like flying, teleporting, or casting spells.
facts.action: Avoid alignment abuse and be prepared for erinyes with enhanced abilities.

facts.fact: Erinyes can be summoned by wearing a helm of opposite alignment, which increases alignment abuse and can summon erinyes adjacent to the hero.
facts.detect: Wearing a helm of opposite alignment.
facts.action: Avoid wearing a helm of opposite alignment or be prepared for erinyes.

facts.fact: Erinyes can see invisible and have poison resistance, making them difficult to avoid or fight.
facts.detect: Erinyes attacking while invisible or resisting poison.
facts.action: Gain poison resistance and invisibility detection.

facts.fact: Erinyes never leave a corpse upon death.
facts.detect: Erinyes dying without leaving a corpse.
facts.action: Do not rely on erinyes dropping useful items.

facts.fact: An ettin is always generated with a club.
facts.detect: Upon encountering an ettin, the bot will notice it is wielding a club.
facts.action: Steal or disarm the ettin's club before engaging in combat to reduce its damage output.

facts.fact: Ettins are strong and move as fast as an unhasted hero.
facts.detect: The bot will notice the ettin's speed and strength stats when it is generated.
facts.action: Avoid direct combat if possible, use ranged attacks or spells to keep distance.

facts.fact: An ettin's lack of MR score and their inability to utilize armor renders them quite vulnerable against wands, poison and spells.
facts.detect: The bot will notice the ettin's lack of armor and MR score.
facts.action: Use wands, poison, or spells to attack the ettin from a distance.

facts.fact: Ettins are randomly generated hostile.
facts.detect: Upon encountering an ettin, the bot will notice it is hostile.
facts.action: Prepare for combat or avoid the ettin if possible.

facts.fact: Ettins are capable of using other projectiles.
facts.detect: The bot will notice the ettin throwing a projectile.
facts.action: Dodge or block the projectile and maintain distance.

facts.fact: An ettin mummy has two claw attacks that deal 2d6 damage each.
facts.detect: Ettin mummy
facts.action: Avoid melee combat with ettin mummies if possible, use ranged attacks or magic.

facts.fact: Ettin mummies have a 6/7 chance of being generated with a mummy wrapping.
facts.detect: Mummy wrapping
facts.action: Steal or pick up mummy wrapping if encountered, as it can be useful for protection against magic.

facts.fact: An ettin mummy leaves behind an aged ettin corpse upon death.
facts.detect: Aged ettin corpse
facts.action: Eat the aged ettin corpse for nutrition if hungry and not poisoned.

facts.fact: Ettin mummies are always hostile.
facts.detect: Ettin mummy
facts.action: Prepare for combat if an ettin mummy is detected.

facts.fact: Ettin mummies have resistance to cold, sleep, and poison.
facts.detect: Ettin mummy
facts.action: Use fire-based attacks or items to combat ettin mummies.

facts.fact: An ettin zombie has two claw attacks.
facts.detect: ettin zombie
facts.action: Avoid melee combat with ettin zombies if not well-armored or prepared.

facts.fact: An ettin zombie will leave an aged ettin corpse upon death.
facts.detect: aged ettin corpse
facts.action: Eat the aged ettin corpse for nutrition if hungry and not allergic to corpses.

facts.fact: Ettin zombies are randomly generated within the main section of Orcus-town at level creation.
facts.detect: Orcus-town level
facts.action: Be cautious when exploring Orcus-town as ettin zombies are likely to be present.

facts.fact: Ettin zombies are part of the first quest monster class for Priests.
facts.detect: Priest quest level
facts.action: Expect ettin zombies among other undead on Priest quest levels.

facts.fact: Ettin zombies are tied for the fastest among zombies with the giant zombie.
facts.detect: ettin zombie
facts.action: Use ranged attacks or spells to avoid close combat with ettin zombies.

facts.fact: Famine is a unique monster with a difficulty level of 34 and appears on the Astral Plane.
facts.detect: Famine appears in the center of one of the three round rooms on the Astral Plane.
facts.action: Prepare for a high-damage encounter and ensure you have enough food to avoid fainting from hunger.

facts.fact: Famine's touch attack drains 40-80 nutrition points per hit and deals damage.
facts.detect: The message 'You feel a sudden pang of hunger!' or 'You feel a sudden pang of hunger and faint!' when attacked.
facts.action: Avoid melee combat and use ranged attacks or spells to defeat Famine.

facts.fact: Famine has teleport control and can revive from its corpse with a 1/3 chance each turn.
facts.detect: Famine teleports or a message indicating it has revived from its corpse.
facts.action: Ensure Famine's corpse is destroyed or teleported far away to prevent revival.

facts.fact: Eating Famine's corpse is instantly fatal and causes it to revive.
facts.detect: Attempting to eat Famine's corpse.
facts.action: Avoid eating Famine's corpse and ensure it is destroyed or teleported.

facts.fact: Famine possesses many resistances and can see invisible monsters.
facts.detect: Famine is unaffected by elemental attacks and can see invisible monsters.
facts.action: Use non-elemental attacks and avoid invisible monsters when fighting Famine.

facts.fact: Fire ants have two bite attacks, with the second bite dealing fire damage that can burn away sliming, instantly destroy paper golems and straw golems, and potentially destroy potions, scrolls, and spellbooks in the victim's inventory.
facts.detect: Messages indicating fire damage to inventory items or sliming removal.
facts.action: Carry extrinsic fire resistance sources like a dwarvish cloak to protect inventory. Bag flammable items before engaging fire ants.

facts.fact: Fire ants have a 10% MR score, making them vulnerable to magic.
facts.detect: Message indicating successful magic missile or sleep spell.
facts.action: Use wands of sleep, magic missile, or offensive spells to quickly dispatch fire ants.

facts.fact: Fire ants are the first quest monster for Valkyries and make up 96/175 of the monsters on the Valkyrie quest.
facts.detect: Appearance of fire ants on the Valkyrie quest levels.
facts.action: Eat fire ant corpses to gain fire resistance if not already intrinsic.

facts.fact: An anthole has a 1/3 chance of being populated entirely by fire ants.
facts.detect: Appearance of an anthole.
facts.action: Be cautious and prepared to deal with fire ants when approaching antholes.

facts.fact: Fire ants are vulnerable to cold damage.
facts.detect: Message indicating successful use of a wand of cold.
facts.action: Use wands of cold to efficiently kill fire ants.

facts.fact: A fire elemental has a fiery claw attack and a passive fire attack that can burn vulnerable items in a target's inventory.
facts.detect: When the bot is attacked by a fire elemental, it will notice the damage from the fiery claw and passive fire attacks.
facts.action: The bot should equip fire-resistant items and weapons to avoid damage from the fire elemental's attacks.

facts.fact: Fire elementals are resistant to fire, poison, and petrification.
facts.detect: When the bot encounters a fire elemental, it will notice the elemental's resistance to fire, poison, and petrification.
facts.action: The bot should avoid using fire-based attacks or weapons against fire elementals.

facts.fact: A fire elemental does not leave a corpse upon death.
facts.detect: When the bot kills a fire elemental, it will not see a corpse drop.
facts.action: The bot should not expect to gain any items or experience from a fire elemental's corpse.

facts.fact: Fire elementals generated on the Plane of Fire have three times as many hit points.
facts.detect: When the bot enters the Plane of Fire, it will encounter fire elementals with significantly higher hit points.
facts.action: The bot should be prepared for more challenging fights with fire elementals on the Plane of Fire.

facts.fact: Fire resistance nullifies both the damage from a fire elemental's attacks and most of the inventory damage it can cause.
facts.detect: When the bot equips fire-resistant items, it will notice a reduction in damage from fire elemental attacks.
facts.action: The bot should prioritize obtaining and equipping fire-resistant items to fight fire elementals effectively.

facts.fact: Fire giants have a 50% chance of being generated with a boulder or a club, and an independent chance of being generated with gems.
facts.detect: Upon encountering a fire giant, the bot should notice if the fire giant is carrying a boulder, club, or gems.
facts.action: If the fire giant is carrying a boulder, the bot should avoid it to prevent being hit by the boulder. If the fire giant is carrying a club or gems, the bot should attempt to take them.

facts.fact: Fire giants have fire resistance and can inflict knockback.
facts.detect: The bot should detect fire giants by their name and be aware of their fire resistance and knockback abilities.
facts.action: The bot should avoid engaging fire giants in close combat, especially near hazards like water or lava, and use ranged attacks or spells if available.

facts.fact: Fire giants can generate in small groups of two to four.
facts.detect: The bot should detect multiple fire giants appearing together.
facts.action: The bot should avoid engaging multiple fire giants and attempt to retreat or find a safe location to fight them one at a time.

facts.fact: Eating a fire giant corpse or tin has a 30% chance of granting fire resistance and a 50% chance of increasing strength.
facts.detect: The bot should detect fire giant corpses or tins.
facts.action: The bot should eat fire giant corpses or tins to potentially gain fire resistance and increase strength.

facts.fact: Fire giants are the second quest monster for Valkyries and make up about 13.71% of randomly generated monsters on the Valkyrie quest.
facts.detect: The bot should detect fire giants on the Valkyrie quest levels.
facts.action: The bot should be prepared to encounter and deal with fire giants on the Valkyrie quest levels, using their corpses for fire resistance and strength.

facts.fact: A fire vortex has an engulfing attack that deals fire damage and can destroy scrolls, spellbooks, and potions in the target's inventory if the attack hits the hero during the grace period where they were expelled and cannot be re-engulfed.
facts.detect: You are burning to a crisp!
facts.action: Equip fire resistant items or use a source of fire resistance before engaging with a fire vortex. Avoid having important scrolls, spellbooks, or potions in open inventory when facing a fire vortex.

facts.fact: Fire vortices possess fire resistance, sleep resistance, poison resistance, and stoning resistance.
facts.detect: Monster attributes or resistances
facts.action: Carry wands of cold or other cold-based attacks to deal damage to a fire vortex effectively.

facts.fact: Randomly generated fire vortices are always created hostile and are only created in Gehennom.
facts.detect: Appearance of a fire vortex in Gehennom
facts.action: Avoid unnecessary exploration in Gehennom until you have fire resistance and other necessary protections.

facts.fact: Six fire vortices are generated on the Plane of Fire at level creation.
facts.detect: Entering the Plane of Fire
facts.action: Ensure you have fire resistance and other protections before entering the Plane of Fire.

facts.fact: Fire vortices do not leave a corpse upon death.
facts.detect: Killing a fire vortex
facts.action: Do not rely on corpses for experience or items after defeating a fire vortex.

facts.fact: A flaming sphere has a fire explosion attack that causes them to self-destruct and cover a 3x3 square radius centered on their position, dealing 4-24 base damage.
facts.detect: A flaming sphere approaches or is adjacent to the bot.
facts.action: Move away from the flaming sphere to avoid the explosion.

facts.fact: Flaming spheres can burn through webs while moving.
facts.detect: The bot is in a web-covered area with a flaming sphere nearby.
facts.action: Find a path that avoids webs or clear a path through webs.

facts.fact: Flaming spheres possess fire resistance.
facts.detect: The bot is near a flaming sphere.
facts.action: Avoid using fire-based attacks or items near a flaming sphere.

facts.fact: A flaming sphere does not leave a corpse upon death.
facts.detect: The bot kills a flaming sphere.
facts.action: No action needed, as there is no corpse to loot.

facts.fact: Flaming spheres can destroy scrolls, spellbooks, potions, and globs of green slime on the floor and in the inventory of anyone caught in the blast.
facts.detect: The bot has flammable items in inventory or on the floor near a flaming sphere.
facts.action: Stash or drop flammable items before the flaming sphere can explode.

facts.fact: A flesh golem has two claw attacks, each dealing 2d8 physical damage.
facts.detect: Encounter a flesh golem on the map or receive a message indicating a flesh golem's attack.
facts.action: Prepare for a strong physical attack and consider using ranged attacks or spells to keep distance.

facts.fact: Flesh golems have fire resistance, cold resistance, shock resistance, sleep resistance, and poison resistance.
facts.detect: Receive a message indicating that a flesh golem is unaffected by fire, cold, or shock damage.
facts.action: Avoid using fire, cold, or shock-based attacks on flesh golems and use other elemental attacks or physical/melee attacks.

facts.fact: Flesh golems heal up to 1/6 of the shock damage that would have been inflicted, with a minimum of 1 HP.
facts.detect: Attempt to shock a flesh golem and observe it healing instead of taking damage.
facts.action: Avoid using shock-based attacks on flesh golems and use other elemental attacks.

facts.fact: Eating a flesh golem corpse has a 3/5 chance of granting one of the resistances possessed by the flesh golem.
facts.detect: Observe a flesh golem corpse on the ground or in inventory.
facts.action: Eat the flesh golem corpse to potentially gain valuable resistances.

facts.fact: Flesh golems are always generated with 40 HP.
facts.detect: Encounter a flesh golem and observe its HP.
facts.action: Plan your strategy based on the knowledge that the flesh golem has 40 HP.

facts.fact: A floating eye has a passive gaze attack that has a 2/3 chance of triggering when hit with a melee attack that does not kill them.
facts.detect: You are frozen by gaze!
facts.action: Use ranged attacks or items to avoid melee combat with floating eyes.

facts.fact: Sources of reflection and free action prevent paralysis from a floating eye's gaze.
facts.detect: You are frozen by gaze! / You momentarily stiffen under gaze!
facts.action: Equip items that provide reflection or free action before engaging floating eyes.

facts.fact: Blinding the floating eye or yourself can prevent its gaze attack.
facts.detect: You are frozen by gaze! / The blind cannot defend itself.
facts.action: Use items to blind the floating eye or yourself before melee combat.

facts.fact: Pets have a 1/10 chance of attacking a floating eye in melee and becoming paralyzed.
facts.detect: Your pet [name] is frozen by gaze!
facts.action: Avoid letting pets engage floating eyes in melee.

facts.fact: A floating eye's corpse grants intrinsic telepathy.
facts.detect: You gain intrinsic telepathy.
facts.action: Eat floating eye corpses to gain intrinsic telepathy.

facts.fact: Fog clouds have an engulfing attack that deals 1d6 moisture damage.
facts.detect: You are laden with moisture and can barely breathe!
facts.action: Avoid being engulfed by fog clouds if you are not amphibious or unbreathing and not fiery.

facts.fact: Fog clouds are amorphous and can pass through closed doors and iron bars.
facts.detect: Fog cloud passing through a closed door or iron bar.
facts.action: Be cautious when fog clouds are near closed doors or iron bars as they can move through them.

facts.fact: Fog clouds have sleep resistance, poison resistance, and stoning resistance.
facts.detect: Fog cloud is not affected by sleep, poison, or stoning attacks.
facts.action: Avoid using sleep, poison, or stoning attacks against fog clouds.

facts.fact: Fog clouds do not leave a corpse upon death.
facts.detect: No corpse left after fog cloud is killed.
facts.action: Do not expect to find a corpse after killing a fog cloud.

facts.fact: Fog clouds can extend the lifetime of temporary clouds to about 20 turns.
facts.detect: Fog cloud moving within a temporary cloud.
facts.action: Be aware of extended temporary clouds when fog clouds are present.

facts.fact: Forest centaurs have a 2/7 chance of being generated with a bow and 3-14 arrows.
facts.detect: Bow and arrows in inventory after encountering a forest centaur
facts.action: Use ranged attacks to deal with the forest centaur from a distance if it has a bow.

facts.fact: Forest centaurs are genocidable.
facts.detect: Encountering a forest centaur in the game
facts.action: Genocide forest centaurs if they pose a significant threat or if you have a peaceful relationship with them and do not need their corpses.

facts.fact: Forest centaurs have a speed of 18 and can generate with dangerous wands, including a potential wand of death.
facts.detect: Encountering a forest centaur with a wand in its inventory
facts.action: Avoid close combat and use ranged attacks or magic to deal with the centaur if it has a wand.

facts.fact: Forest centaurs are the first quest monster for Rangers and make up 96/175 of the monsters generated on the Ranger quest.
facts.detect: Entering the Ranger quest and encountering forest centaurs
facts.action: Prepare for multiple encounters with forest centaurs on the Ranger quest by gathering elemental resistances and a source of magic resistance.

facts.fact: Forest centaur corpses provide 600 nutrition.
facts.detect: Killing a forest centaur and obtaining its corpse
facts.action: Eat the corpse to gain nutrition, especially if you are a meat-eating pet or character.

facts.fact: A fox is a hostile monster with a bite attack that deals 1d3 physical damage.
facts.detect: A small, carnivorous canine appears on the map.
facts.action: Avoid or attack the fox if necessary, considering its speed and potential to overwhelm a weak character.

facts.fact: Foxes can be generated by werejackals with a 21/25 chance per summoned monster.
facts.detect: A werejackal appears and summons a fox.
facts.action: Be cautious around werejackals and prepare for the possibility of foxes being summoned.

facts.fact: Foxes are part of the random monster generation for Samurai quests, making up 24/175 of the monsters.
facts.detect: Entering a Samurai quest level.
facts.action: Expect to encounter foxes on Samurai quest levels and prepare accordingly.

facts.fact: Eating a fox corpse is considered cannibalism for a hero with lycanthropy from a werejackal.
facts.detect: Attempting to eat a fox corpse while having werejackal lycanthropy.
facts.action: Avoid eating fox corpses if you have werejackal lycanthropy to prevent cannibalism.

facts.fact: A freezing sphere has an explosion attack that deals 4-24 base damage and can freeze moats or pools in the explosion's radius.
facts.detect: Freezing sphere moves towards player or pet
facts.action: Avoid standing in a 3x3 radius around a freezing sphere to prevent damage and item destruction.

facts.fact: A freezing sphere has a 20% chance of shattering potions caught in the explosion's radius, with cold resistance reducing this to 1%.
facts.detect: Potions in inventory or on the ground near a freezing sphere
facts.action: Equip cold resistance or use a dwarvish cloak to protect potions from freezing.

facts.fact: Freezing spheres are generated hostile and do not leave a corpse upon death.
facts.detect: Freezing sphere appears on the map
facts.action: Avoid direct confrontation unless prepared to deal with its explosion.

facts.fact: Freezing spheres can be immobilized by poison damage or a wand of sleep.
facts.detect: Freezing sphere's movement
facts.action: Use poison or wand of sleep to immobilize and kill the freezing sphere before it can explode.

facts.fact: Freezing spheres do not naturally generate in Gehennom.
facts.detect: Exploring Gehennom
facts.action: No special action needed as freezing spheres are not a concern in Gehennom.

facts.fact: Frost giants have a 50% chance of being generated with a boulder or a club, and an independent chance of being generated with gems.
facts.detect: Boulder, club, or gem in the vicinity of a frost giant
facts.action: Pick up the boulder or club if available, and collect gems if needed for the quest or for selling.

facts.fact: Frost giants have cold resistance.
facts.detect: Frost giant attacking in cold environments or using cold-based attacks
facts.action: Avoid using cold-based attacks or spells against frost giants.

facts.fact: Eating a frost giant corpse or tin has a 33% chance of granting cold resistance and a 50% chance of increasing strength.
facts.detect: Frost giant corpse or tin in inventory
facts.action: Eat the corpse or tin to potentially gain cold resistance and strength.

facts.fact: Frost giants may generate in small groups of two to four.
facts.detect: Multiple frost giants appearing together
facts.action: Be cautious and prepare for a group fight, possibly using ranged attacks or summoning pets.

facts.fact: Frost giants will not be randomly generated in Gehennom.
facts.detect: Exploring Gehennom
facts.action: Do not expect to encounter frost giants in Gehennom.

facts.fact: Gargoyles have stoning resistance.
facts.detect: Monster name: Gargoyle
facts.action: Eat gargoyle corpses to gain temporary stoning resistance.

facts.fact: Gargoyles are hostile and have a natural AC of -4.
facts.detect: Monster name: Gargoyle
facts.action: Equip high AC armor and magical items before engaging.

facts.fact: Gargoyles have two claw attacks and a bite attack.
facts.detect: Monster name: Gargoyle
facts.action: Use ranged attacks or spells to avoid close combat.

facts.fact: Gargoyles are slow with a speed of 10.
facts.detect: Monster name: Gargoyle
facts.action: Use speed to your advantage by moving and attacking quickly.

facts.fact: Gargoyles have no magic resistance.
facts.detect: Monster name: Gargoyle
facts.action: Use magical items and spells effectively against them.

facts.fact: Garter snakes have a single bite attack that deals 1d2 damage.
facts.detect: Garter snake symbol (a small snake icon) or the message 'A garter snake bites you!'
facts.action: Attack garter snakes if they are alone or in small groups, but be cautious of larger groups.

facts.fact: Garter snakes can appear in large groups of 2-11 each.
facts.detect: Multiple garter snake symbols or the message 'A group of garter snakes appears!'
facts.action: Avoid or retreat from large groups of garter snakes to prevent being overwhelmed.

facts.fact: Garter snakes can hide under objects and may generate as peaceful towards neutral player characters.
facts.detect: A peaceful garter snake symbol or the message 'A peaceful garter snake is hiding under a [object]!'
facts.action: Approach with caution and be prepared to attack if the snake becomes hostile.

facts.fact: Garter snakes are part of the second quest monster class for Archeologists and may generate on Medusa's Island.
facts.detect: Garter snakes in specific areas like the Archeologist quest or Medusa's Island.
facts.action: Be prepared for garter snakes in these areas and handle them as needed.

facts.fact: Garter snakes generate with a random item to hide under.
facts.detect: A garter snake hiding under an object.
facts.action: Approach with caution and be prepared to deal with the hidden item.

facts.fact: A gas spore has an on-death explosion attack that deals 4-24 damage to any hero or other monsters caught in the blast.
facts.detect: Explosion sound and visual effect when a gas spore dies.
facts.action: Avoid melee combat with gas spores and use ranged attacks or step back to avoid the explosion.

facts.fact: If a hero is caught in the explosion while being held by another monster, that monster takes doubled damage.
facts.detect: Being held by a monster and the explosion sound.
facts.action: Avoid being held by a monster when near a gas spore.

facts.fact: Monsters will not attack a gas spore unless they are capable of surviving the explosion.
facts.detect: Monsters approaching a gas spore and not attacking it.
facts.action: Be cautious when pets or other monsters are near gas spores.

facts.fact: Pets killed by the gas spore explosion are treated as if you had killed them directly.
facts.detect: Pet death message.
facts.action: Avoid attacking gas spores near pets.

facts.fact: Peaceful monsters become angry if killed by a gas spore explosion.
facts.detect: Anger message from peaceful monsters.
facts.action: Avoid attacking gas spores in peaceful-populated areas.

facts.fact: Geckos are randomly generated hostile.
facts.detect: Encountering a gecko on the level.
facts.action: Attack or prepare to defend against the gecko.

facts.fact: Geckos have a bite attack dealing 1d3 damage.
facts.detect: Taking damage from a gecko bite.
facts.action: Wear armor and use weapons to mitigate damage.

facts.fact: Chatting to a gecko while hallucinating gives YAFM.
facts.detect: Message: '15 minutes could save you 15 .' when hallucinating.
facts.action: Avoid chatting to geckos when hallucinating.

facts.fact: Geckos are slow with a speed of 6.
facts.detect: Observing the gecko's movement on the level.
facts.action: Use speed to outmaneuver the gecko.

facts.fact: Gelatinous cubes have paralysis-inducing attacks that can be blocked by magic cancellation or free action ring.
facts.detect: The message 'You are frozen by the gelatinous cube!' or 'is frozen by the gelatinous cube.'
facts.action: Equip magic cancellation or a ring of free action to avoid paralysis.

facts.fact: Gelatinous cubes can engulf and eat items, including organic containers and their contents.
facts.detect: The message 'The gelatinous cube engulfs .', 'The gelatinous cube engulfs several objects.', or 'The gelatinous cube eats !'.
facts.action: Avoid having valuable items in the same square as a gelatinous cube.

facts.fact: Gelatinous cubes have resistance to various forms of damage and status effects.
facts.detect: The cube survives attacks that would normally cause these effects.
facts.action: Use non-elemental damage to defeat the cube.

facts.fact: Pets will avoid attacking a gelatinous cube in melee 9/10 of the time.
facts.detect: The pet does not attack the cube when it is in melee range.
facts.action: Do not rely on pets to fight gelatinous cubes.

facts.fact: Eating a gelatinous cube corpse or tin can cure stoning and grant resistances.
facts.detect: The message 'You feel less stony.' or 'You feel less sleepy.'
facts.action: Eat the corpse or tin if you are stoned or need resistances.

facts.fact: Geryon is a Unique monster with difficulty 36 and level 33.
facts.detect: Geryon (Geryon symbol)
facts.action: Prepare for a high-level encounter. Ensure you have high-level equipment and spells.

facts.fact: Geryon starts peaceful and asks for payment.
facts.detect: Geryon asks for payment
facts.action: Offer payment to avoid immediate combat. Payment can be a holy symbol or a valuable item.

facts.fact: Geryon has resistances to fire and poison.
facts.detect: Geryon is immune to fire and poison attacks
facts.action: Avoid using fire and poison attacks. Use other elemental attacks or physical damage.

facts.fact: Geryon has attributes that include flying, invisibility detection, poison resistance, and slithy (can move through walls).
facts.detect: Geryon flies and moves through walls
facts.action: Be prepared for Geryon's mobility and use of the terrain to your advantage.

facts.fact: Geryon's attacks include two claws (3d6 each) and a poisonous sting (2d4).
facts.detect: Geryon's claw and sting attacks
facts.action: Wear high AC and resist poison equipment. Use ranged attacks or spells to avoid close combat.

facts.fact: A ghost is a type of monster with a difficulty of 12, level 10, and 238 experience points.
facts.detect: Encountering a ghost on the map.
facts.action: Use a wand of undead turning or the turn undead spell to avoid combat if possible.

facts.fact: Ghosts have a weak touch attack and possess several resistances, including cold, disintegration, sleep, poison, and stoning resistance.
facts.detect: Observing the ghost's resistance to various attacks.
facts.action: Avoid using poison or sleep attacks on ghosts.

facts.fact: Ghosts are not randomly generated but can appear in abandoned temples or when quaffing a milky potion.
facts.detect: Entering an abandoned temple or drinking a milky potion.
facts.action: Avoid entering abandoned temples and be cautious with unidentified potions.

facts.fact: Ghosts can be generated in graveyards with a 1/5 chance on each square during level creation.
facts.detect: Exploring a graveyard.
facts.action: Be prepared for ghost encounters in graveyards.

facts.fact: Ghosts do not leave a corpse when killed.
facts.detect: Killing a ghost and not finding a corpse.
facts.action: Do not waste time searching for a corpse after killing a ghost.

facts.fact: A ghoul has two claw attacks, the first can paralyze a target for up to 10 turns unless they have free action, while the second does normal physical damage.
facts.detect: A ghoul appears on the map or the bot hears 'You hear an awful gobbling noise!'
facts.action: Avoid ghouls or prepare with free action or high magic cancellation to reduce paralysis risk.

facts.fact: Ghouls possess cold resistance, sleep resistance, poison resistance, death resistance, and drain resistance.
facts.detect: Ghouls are encountered in cold or poison-heavy areas.
facts.action: Be prepared with appropriate resistance or healing items.

facts.fact: Ghouls are omnivores that can only consume tainted non-veggy corpses and rotten eggs, and will only do so while tame.
facts.detect: Ghouls eating corpses or eggs on the map.
facts.action: Avoid leaving tainted non-veggy corpses or rotten eggs in areas where ghouls are present.

facts.fact: Randomly generated ghouls are always created hostile.
facts.detect: Ghouls appear on the map.
facts.action: Avoid or prepare to fight hostile ghouls.

facts.fact: Engraving on a headstone will summon a ghoul adjacent to the hero.
facts.detect: The bot engraves on a headstone.
facts.action: Avoid engraving on headstones in areas with ghouls.

facts.fact: A giant has a single weapon attack with 2d10 damage.
facts.detect: monster name 'giant' or 'giant zombie' or 'giant mummy'
facts.action: Avoid or prepare for high damage from a single attack.

facts.fact: Eating a giant corpse or tin has a 50% chance of increasing a character's strength.
facts.detect: monster name 'giant' or 'giant zombie' or 'giant mummy' and corpse or tin
facts.action: Eat giant corpse or tin to potentially increase strength, but be prepared for food poisoning.

facts.fact: Giants can be generated with a boulder or club (50% chance each) and an assortment of gems.
facts.detect: monster name 'giant' and inventory check for boulder, club, or gems
facts.action: Check inventory for boulder, club, or gems after encountering a giant.

facts.fact: Giants can be generated by zapping a wand of undead turning at a giant corpse that is not left by a zombie or mummy.
facts.detect: wand of undead turning and giant corpse
facts.action: Zap wand of undead turning at giant corpse to potentially generate a giant.

facts.fact: Giants can be generated by wishing for a figurine of a giant and applying it.
facts.detect: figurine of a giant
facts.action: Wish for and apply figurine of a giant to potentially generate a giant.

facts.fact: Giant ants have a speed of 18 and appear in groups of 2-4.
facts.detect: Multiple giant ants appearing on the map or the message 'You are surrounded by giant ants!'
facts.action: Retreat to a corridor or use doors to block pursuing ants. Keep escape items handy and be prepared to use them if necessary.

facts.fact: Giant ants have an AC of 3 and no magic resistance.
facts.detect: Attempting to hit a giant ant with a weapon or spell.
facts.action: Use ranged weapons, offensive spells, or wands to attack from a distance. Consider using wands of sleep or slow monster to control the swarm.

facts.fact: Giant ants can be generated by the summon insects spell.
facts.detect: Message 'A monster casts summon insects!'
facts.action: Be prepared to handle a sudden swarm of giant ants if you encounter this spell.

facts.fact: An anthole has a 1/3 chance of being populated entirely by giant ants.
facts.detect: Approaching an anthole.
facts.action: Be cautious and prepared to handle a potential swarm of giant ants.

facts.fact: Giant ants are a frequent cause of early deaths due to their speed and tendency to appear in groups.
facts.detect: Early game encounters with giant ants.
facts.action: Avoid being under-prepared and burdened. Use ranged attacks and escape items if necessary.

facts.fact: A giant bat has a single bite attack that deals 1d6 physical damage.
facts.detect: Giant bat icon or name
facts.action: Avoid or prepare to fight if necessary, as they are hostile and can deal damage.

facts.fact: Eating a giant bat corpse or tin will stun the hero for up to 30 turns.
facts.detect: Giant bat corpse or tin
facts.action: Avoid eating giant bat corpses or tins to prevent being stunned.

facts.fact: Giant bats are always generated hostile.
facts.detect: Giant bat icon or name
facts.action: Be prepared to fight or avoid them as they will always attack.

facts.fact: Giant bats have a tendency to wander, with a 3/4 chance of moving in a random direction during each of its turns.
facts.detect: Giant bat icon or name
facts.action: Be cautious as their movement is unpredictable.

facts.fact: Giant bats generated in Gehennom have 2 extra points of movement speed.
facts.detect: Giant bat icon or name in Gehennom
facts.action: Be extra cautious as they are faster in Gehennom.

facts.fact: A giant beetle has a single bite attack that deals 3d6 physical damage.
facts.detect: monster name 'Giant beetle'
facts.action: Avoid melee combat with giant beetles if possible due to their high damage output.

facts.fact: Giant beetles are randomly generated hostile.
facts.detect: monster name 'Giant beetle'
facts.action: Be prepared to fight giant beetles upon encountering them.

facts.fact: Giant beetles have poison resistance.
facts.detect: monster name 'Giant beetle'
facts.action: Use poison attacks or items cautiously against giant beetles.

facts.fact: Eating a giant beetle corpse or tin has a 33% chance of granting poison resistance.
facts.detect: corpse of 'Giant beetle'
facts.action: Eat giant beetle corpses or tinned giant beetles if you need poison resistance and have a tinning kit.

facts.fact: Giant beetles can be confused with soldier ants due to similar coloration on some systems.
facts.detect: dark gray or blue creature
facts.action: Be cautious and verify the identity of dark gray or blue creatures before engaging.

facts.fact: Giant eels have a touch attack that causes drowning if the hero is adjacent to a pool or moat and hit by the attack while already wrapped by it.
facts.detect: Adjacent to a pool or moat and hit by a giant eel's touch attack.
facts.action: Avoid melee combat with giant eels near water or use items that prevent them from grabbing you (e.g., non-cursed oilskin cloak, greased outer body armor).

facts.fact: Giant eels are generated in specific watery areas such as moats, rivers, and ponds in quest levels and Fort Ludios.
facts.detect: Entering a moat, river, or pond in quest levels or Fort Ludios.
facts.action: Be cautious and prepared for giant eels when entering these areas.

facts.fact: Giant eels are best dispatched at a distance using wands or spells that immobilize or hinder them.
facts.detect: Seeing a giant eel in a distance.
facts.action: Use wands of cold, sleep, or teleportation to immobilize or remove the giant eel from the area.

facts.fact: Giant eels are especially dangerous on the Plane of Water where you cannot engrave and have less room to maneuver.
facts.detect: Entering the Plane of Water.
facts.action: Use a blessed scroll of genocide to wipe out all giant eels upon entering the level.

facts.fact: Giant eels are amphibious and can hide within water, becoming scared and losing HP while stuck on land.
facts.detect: Giant eel moving out of water onto land.
facts.action: Exploit the eel's vulnerability on land by attacking it.

facts.fact: A giant mimic can disguise itself as an appropriate item or dungeon feature and stick to the hero if they walk into it or it attacks them.
facts.detect: The hero gets stuck to an item or feature that seems out of place or behaves unusually.
facts.action: Use telepathy or warning to detect mimics, throw a gold piece to reveal a mimic in a shop, or engrave Elbereth to scare it away.

facts.fact: A giant mimic has two claw attacks that deal 3d4 and 3d6 damage, respectively, and can stick to the hero.
facts.detect: The hero is attacked by a giant mimic with claw attacks.
facts.action: Use ranged attacks or teleports to avoid getting stuck, or engrave Elbereth to scare it away.

facts.fact: Eating a giant mimic corpse or tin causes the hero to polymorph into a pile of gold for 50 turns.
facts.detect: The hero eats a giant mimic corpse or tin.
facts.action: Avoid eating giant mimic corpses or tins unless the polymorph is desired and the hero is prepared for it.

facts.fact: Giant mimics are generated in shops, Sokoban, and on new dungeon floors with a level difficulty of 9 or higher.
facts.detect: The hero enters a new dungeon floor or a shop and encounters a giant mimic.
facts.action: Be cautious in shops and new dungeon floors, especially those with a level difficulty of 9 or higher.

facts.fact: A giant mimic can be generated on the home floor of the Rogue quest disguised as the down stair.
facts.detect: The hero encounters a down stair that seems suspiciously like a giant mimic.
facts.action: Be cautious when approaching suspicious down stairs and use telepathy or warning to detect mimics.

facts.fact: A giant mummy has two claw attacks and possesses cold resistance, sleep resistance, and poison resistance.
facts.detect: monster name 'giant mummy'
facts.action: Avoid melee combat without cold resistance, sleep resistance, and poison resistance. Use fire or cold-based attacks if available.

facts.fact: Giant mummies are poisonous to consume, which primarily comes up if it is somehow digested by another monster.
facts.detect: monster name 'giant mummy' and digestion by another monster
facts.action: Avoid consuming or digesting a giant mummy corpse unless immune to poison.

facts.fact: Giant mummies have a 6/7 chance of being generated with a mummy wrapping.
facts.detect: monster name 'giant mummy' and item 'mummy wrapping'
facts.action: Loot mummy wrapping if available and needed for quest or inventory.

facts.fact: A giant mummy always leaves behind an aged giant corpse upon death.
facts.detect: monster name 'giant mummy' and corpse 'aged giant'
facts.action: Avoid eating the corpse and consider using it for other purposes.

facts.fact: Giant mummies are part of the second quest monster class for Archeologists and make up 6/175 of the monsters randomly generated on the Archeologist quest.
facts.detect: monster name 'giant mummy' and quest context for Archeologists
facts.action: Be prepared for giant mummies during the Archeologist quest.

facts.fact: Giant rats have a single bite attack that deals 1d3 damage.
facts.detect: Monster name 'giant rat' or encounter message 'A giant rat bites you!'
facts.action: Attack giant rats if they are a threat to your survival or if you need experience points.

facts.fact: Giant rats are always generated hostile and may appear in small groups.
facts.detect: Multiple 'giant rat' encounters or messages like 'A group of giant rats appear!'
facts.action: Be cautious and prepare for combat if you detect multiple giant rats.

facts.fact: Giant rats can be seen via infravision.
facts.detect: Infravision status or map feature indicating heat signatures.
facts.action: Use infravision to detect and avoid or confront giant rats.

facts.fact: Giant rats are the first quest monster for Healers and make up a significant portion of the monsters on the Healer quest.
facts.detect: Quest status or messages indicating you are on the Healer quest.
facts.action: Be prepared for encounters with giant rats if you are on the Healer quest.

facts.fact: Wererats can summon hostile giant rats with a 2/9 chance per adjacent square.
facts.detect: Encounter with a wererat or message indicating a wererat summoning.
facts.action: Be cautious and prepare for potential giant rat summoning if you encounter a wererat.

facts.fact: Giant spiders have a poisonous bite attack that drains strength and possess poison resistance.
facts.detect: When the bot encounters a giant spider, it will see the message 'A giant spider bites you!' and may lose strength points.
facts.action: The bot should prioritize gaining poison resistance, either through eating a giant spider corpse or using a unicorn horn to restore strength.

facts.fact: A giant spider corpse is poisonous to eat, but eating it has a 33% chance of conveying poison resistance.
facts.detect: The bot finds a giant spider corpse on the ground.
facts.action: The bot should eat the corpse if it does not have poison resistance and has a way to handle potential poison.

facts.fact: Giant spiders move faster than an unhasted hero at 15 speed.
facts.detect: The bot notices that a giant spider is closing in quickly.
facts.action: The bot should use ranged attacks or Elbereth to maintain distance from the giant spider.

facts.fact: Giant spiders can spin webs, which can trap the bot and cause movement issues.
facts.detect: The bot gets stuck in a web and cannot move.
facts.action: The bot should use a bladed weapon to cut through the web.

facts.fact: Giant spiders are randomly generated on webs with items on them.
facts.detect: The bot sees a giant spider on a web with an item.
facts.action: The bot should avoid the web or carefully approach to pick up the item.

facts.fact: A giant zombie has two claw attacks that deal 2d8 damage each.
facts.detect: Giant zombie icon or name
facts.action: Avoid melee combat if not well-equipped or prepared with high AC and hit points.

facts.fact: Eating a giant zombie corpse has a 50% chance of increasing strength but may cause food poisoning.
facts.detect: Aged giant corpse
facts.action: Use a tinning kit to preserve the corpse for later consumption or prepare for potential food poisoning.

facts.fact: Giant zombies can follow the player to other levels if adjacent.
facts.detect: Adjacent giant zombie
facts.action: Avoid moving to adjacent levels with giant zombies or use a teleporter to escape.

facts.fact: Giant zombies are part of the Priest quest and appear in Orcus-town.
facts.detect: Entering Priest quest or Orcus-town
facts.action: Be prepared for encounters with giant zombies in these areas.

facts.fact: Giant zombies are one of the strongest zombies but not the strongest monster overall.
facts.detect: Giant zombie icon or name
facts.action: Treat giant zombies as a significant threat and prepare accordingly.

facts.fact: A glass golem has two claw attacks, and possesses acid resistance along with the sleep resistance and poison resistance of all golems.
facts.detect: Encounter with a glass golem or seeing the message 'is getting soft!' when hitting it with a flaming attack.
facts.action: Prepare for its claw attacks and be aware of its resistances, especially acid resistance.

facts.fact: Glass golems are always generated with 60 hit points.
facts.detect: Encounter with a glass golem.
facts.action: Expect a glass golem to have 60 hit points and plan accordingly for its durability.

facts.fact: Glass golems leave behind several pieces of worthless glass in varying colors upon death instead of a corpse.
facts.detect: Death of a glass golem.
facts.action: Collect the worthless glass for type-naming purposes.

facts.fact: A glass piercer can hide itself by clinging to the ceiling and will attempt to drop off the ceiling onto targets below them, inflicting 4d6 damage if it makes contact.
facts.detect: The bot will notice a glass piercer dropping from the ceiling when it is in the same column as the glass piercer.
facts.action: The bot should move away from the column where the glass piercer is hiding or use a ranged attack to kill it before it can drop.

facts.fact: A hero wearing a hard helm will only take 2 HP of damage from the piercer's blow glancing off that helm.
facts.detect: The bot has a hard helm equipped.
facts.action: The bot should ensure it has a hard helm equipped to minimize damage from glass piercer attacks.

facts.fact: If the hero has warning, they will reveal a hiding rock piercer's location when moving adjacent to their square.
facts.detect: The bot has the 'warning' intrinsic or is adjacent to a hiding glass piercer.
facts.action: The bot should move adjacent to the hiding glass piercer to reveal its location.

facts.fact: Tame rock piercers will not attack the hero and harmlessly drop off the ceiling if they walk underneath.
facts.detect: The bot has a tame rock piercer in its inventory or on the level.
facts.action: The bot should use tame rock piercers to reveal hiding glass piercers without danger.

facts.fact: Glass piercers have a fairly strong bite and the same AC of 0 as iron piercers, but still move at the same extremely slow speed of 1 as other piercers do.
facts.detect: The bot encounters a glass piercer on the level.
facts.action: The bot should use ranged attacks or a high-damage melee weapon to quickly dispatch the glass piercer.

facts.fact: Gnomes are generated in small groups and are often found in the Gnomish Mines and Minetown.
facts.detect: Encountering multiple gnomes in the Gnomish Mines or Minetown.
facts.action: Be cautious of groups of gnomes, especially in the Gnomish Mines and Minetown, as they can be dangerous in numbers.

facts.fact: Gnomes have a chance of being generated with offensive items such as darts, crossbows, bows, daggers, or aklys.
facts.detect: Seeing a gnome with a ranged weapon or a stack of darts, crossbow bolts, arrows, or daggers.
facts.action: Avoid engaging gnomes in open areas where they can use their ranged weapons effectively.

facts.fact: Gnomes can collect items such as weapons and armor.
facts.detect: Observing a gnome picking up a weapon or armor.
facts.action: Be wary of gnomes in possession of weapons or armor, as they can become more dangerous.

facts.fact: Gnomes are peaceful towards dwarvish and gnomish heroes but hostile towards other races.
facts.detect: Receiving a message indicating that a gnome is peaceful or hostile.
facts.action: Exploit the peaceful nature of gnomes towards dwarvish and gnomish heroes to avoid unnecessary combat.

facts.fact: Gnomes can read scrolls and zap wands, making them potentially dangerous if they find one.
facts.detect: Observing a gnome using a scroll or wand.
facts.action: Avoid letting gnomes access scrolls or wands, especially cursed ones.

facts.fact: Gnome mummies have a 6/7 chance of being generated with a mummy wrapping.
facts.detect: mummy wrapping
facts.action: Pick up mummy wrapping if found, as it is valuable and can be used for bandages or to wrap up items.

facts.fact: Gnome mummies leave behind an aged gnome corpse upon death.
facts.detect: aged gnome corpse
facts.action: Eat aged gnome corpse if hungry and have no better food, but be cautious as it may be cursed or rotten.

facts.fact: Gnome mummies have a -3 alignment.
facts.detect: gnome mummy
facts.action: Avoid killing gnome mummies if trying to maintain lawful alignment.

facts.fact: Gnome mummies have resistance to cold, sleep, and poison.
facts.detect: gnome mummy
facts.action: Use fire or cold-based attacks cautiously around gnome mummies.

facts.fact: Gnome mummies are part of the second quest monster class for Archeologists.
facts.detect: gnome mummy in a quest level
facts.action: Be prepared for gnome mummies on quest levels if playing as an Archeologist.

facts.fact: Gnome zombies are a type of monster with a single claw attack, AC 10, and MR 0.
facts.detect: gnome zombie
facts.action: Attack with melee or ranged weapons, or use spells with a high chance of hitting due to low AC.

facts.fact: Gnome zombies leave an aged gnome corpse upon death.
facts.detect: aged gnome corpse
facts.action: Eat the corpse for nutrition and experience if hungry or low on experience.

facts.fact: Gnome zombies are part of the first quest monster class for Priests and make up 24/175 of randomly generated monsters on the Priest quest.
facts.detect: Encounter with gnome zombies in the Priest quest branch.
facts.action: Be prepared for encounters with gnome zombies in the Priest quest branch.

facts.fact: Gnome zombies are among the first undead you will encounter and are likely to be one of the first you will encounter.
facts.detect: First encounter with an undead monster.
facts.action: Learn to identify and handle undead monsters early in the game.

facts.fact: Gnome zombies are barely stronger than kobold zombies and noticeably weaker than live gnomes.
facts.detect: Combat with a gnome zombie.
facts.action: Use this opportunity to practice combat skills and gain experience without significant risk.

facts.fact: Gnomish wizards are always peaceful towards gnomish and dwarvish characters.
facts.detect: The bot's character race is dwarvish.
facts.action: Approach gnomish wizards peacefully without fear of combat.

facts.fact: Gnomish wizards have infravision and can be seen with infravision.
facts.detect: The bot has infravision and can see gnomish wizards in dark areas.
facts.action: Use infravision to locate and avoid or approach gnomish wizards as needed.

facts.fact: Gnomish wizards may appear among the hostile G that generate in throne rooms.
facts.detect: The bot enters a throne room and sees hostile gnomes.
facts.action: Be cautious in throne rooms and avoid or prepare for potential gnomish wizard encounters.

facts.fact: Gnomish wizards have a chance of being generated with a single candle.
facts.detect: The bot encounters a gnomish wizard with a candle.
facts.action: Be cautious as the candle may be lit and could be used against the bot.

facts.fact: Gnomish wizards often cast the haste self monster spell the first chance they get.
facts.detect: The bot notices a gnomish wizard casting a spell, possibly haste self.
facts.action: Be prepared for the gnomish wizard to become faster and more dangerous.

facts.fact: Goblins have a 1/2 chance of being generated with an orcish helm and a 1/2 chance of receiving an orcish dagger.
facts.detect: orcish helm, orcish dagger
facts.action: Check for orcish helm and dagger when encountering goblins. If enchanted, these items can be useful early in the game.

facts.fact: Goblins can generate peaceful towards chaotic, non-elven player characters.
facts.detect: Peaceful goblin
facts.action: If chaotic, avoid killing peaceful goblins to maintain alignment for early prayer.

facts.fact: Goblins possess infravision and can be seen via infravision.
facts.detect: Infravision
facts.action: Use infravision to detect goblins in dark areas.

facts.fact: Goblins can pick up items they come across.
facts.detect: Goblin carrying items
facts.action: Be cautious of goblins carrying items that could be used against you, such as wands.

facts.fact: Goblins can be used by orcish characters to convert altars to Moloch in Orcish Town.
facts.detect: Altar to Moloch, goblin corpse
facts.action: Use goblin corpses to convert altars and raise Luck if playing as an orc.

facts.fact: The Goblin King is always generated seated atop his throne in the northeastern corner of the map.
facts.detect: The throne in the northeastern corner of the map.
facts.action: Approach the throne with caution and prepare for combat.

facts.fact: The Goblin King has two weapon attacks dealing 1d8 damage each and a claw attack dealing 1d6 damage.
facts.detect: The Goblin King's attack messages.
facts.action: Equip the best armor and weapons available before engaging.

facts.fact: The Goblin King speaks in rhyme before attacking.
facts.detect: The rhyming messages from the Goblin King.
facts.action: Prepare for combat immediately after hearing the message.

facts.fact: The Goblin King has unique messages if the player character is wielding Orcrist or Glamdring.
facts.detect: The specific rhyming messages related to Orcrist or Glamdring.
facts.action: If wielding Orcrist or Glamdring, be prepared for a stronger fight.

facts.fact: The Goblin King is hostile and will attack on sight.
facts.detect: The Goblin King's hostile stance.
facts.action: Engage in combat or find a way to avoid him.

facts.fact: Gold golems have two claw attacks and possess acid resistance, along with sleep resistance and poison resistance like all golems.
facts.detect: Gold golem
facts.action: Avoid using sleep or poison-based attacks on gold golems and be prepared for acid resistance.

facts.fact: Gold golems drop 200–rnl(101) gold pieces upon death instead of a corpse.
facts.detect: Gold golem corpse or death message
facts.action: Loot the gold pieces dropped by a slain gold golem.

facts.fact: Reading a non-cursed scroll of gold detection will reveal the presence of any gold golems on the level.
facts.detect: Scroll of gold detection
facts.action: Use a scroll of gold detection to locate gold golems before engaging them.

facts.fact: Gold golems are always created hostile.
facts.detect: Gold golem approaching or attacking
facts.action: Be cautious and prepared to fight or flee when encountering a gold golem.

facts.fact: Gold golems can generate as a result of polypiling if there are enough gold objects in a pile of items.
facts.detect: Polypiling with a pile containing gold objects
facts.action: Avoid polypiling with piles containing gold objects to prevent the generation of gold golems.

facts.fact: A golden naga has a bite attack and will attempt to cast one mage spell during each of its turns, and possesses poison resistance.
facts.detect: Encountering a golden naga on the map or seeing its name in the message log.
facts.action: Avoid melee combat and use ranged attacks or spells to keep distance. If possible, use magic resistance or items that provide it to mitigate spell damage.

facts.fact: Eating a golden naga corpse or tin has a 66% chance of conveying poison resistance.
facts.detect: Finding a golden naga corpse or tin in the dungeon.
facts.action: Eat the corpse or tin to gain poison resistance, which can be beneficial in future encounters with poison-resistant or venomous monsters.

facts.fact: Lawful characters are likely to encounter peaceful golden nagas.
facts.detect: Seeing a message like 'You see a peaceful golden naga.'
facts.action: Approach and talk to the peaceful golden naga to possibly gain its aid or receive a gift.

facts.fact: Golden nagas are quick-moving monsters that can outpace an unhasted character.
facts.detect: Observing the golden naga's movement speed or seeing messages indicating it has moved out of sight.
facts.action: Use speed-boosting items or spells to keep up with the golden naga or avoid engaging in combat if unable to match its speed.

facts.fact: Golden naga hatchling has poison resistance and a 20% chance to convey poison resistance upon eating its corpse.
facts.detect: Golden naga hatchling corpse
facts.action: Eat the corpse to gain poison resistance if needed and safe to do so.

facts.fact: Golden naga hatchling can generate as peaceful towards neutral characters.
facts.detect: Peaceful status message when encountering the hatchling
facts.action: Attempt to tame or pacify the hatchling if it is peaceful and you are neutral.

facts.fact: Golden naga hatchling is only randomly generated within levels and branches that are biased towards a particular alignment, such as the Oracle and Sokoban.
facts.detect: Entering alignment-biased levels or branches
facts.action: Be cautious and prepared for potential encounters with golden naga hatchlings in these areas.

facts.fact: Golden naga hatchling has a single bite attack that deals 1d4 damage.
facts.detect: Encountering a golden naga hatchling
facts.action: Fight or avoid as necessary based on your equipment and level.

facts.fact: Golden naga hatchling is a valuable source of poison resistance early in the game.
facts.detect: Checking your resistance status
facts.action: Prioritize finding and eating the corpse if you lack poison resistance.

facts.fact: The Grand Master is a unique monster with a difficulty level of 30 and is generated on the Monastery of Chan-Sune, always peaceful and adjacent to the unaligned altar.
facts.detect: The Grand Master, a peaceful unique monster, adjacent to the unaligned altar in the Monastery of Chan-Sune.
facts.action: Avoid engaging the Grand Master unless necessary, as he is very powerful and can deal significant damage.

facts.fact: The Grand Master has a +6 robe as a standard equipment.
facts.detect: A +6 robe in the vicinity of the Grand Master.
facts.action: Stealthily take the +6 robe if possible, as it is a valuable item.

facts.fact: The Grand Master has fire resistance, shock resistance, sleep resistance, and poison resistance.
facts.detect: The Grand Master's resistance to fire, shock, sleep, and poison.
facts.action: Prepare for combat by ensuring you have items or spells that can bypass his resistances, such as wands of cancellation or spells that cause confusion.

facts.fact: The Grand Master has a claw attack (4d10 physical damage) and a kick attack (2d8 physical damage), and can cast two clerical spells (2d8 damage each) per turn.
facts.detect: The Grand Master's attack messages indicating claw and kick attacks, and spellcasting.
facts.action: Focus on dodging his attacks and using ranged weapons or spells to keep distance.

facts.fact: The Grand Master is generated as peaceful and cannot be genocided.
facts.detect: The Grand Master's peaceful status and inability to be genocided.
facts.action: Avoid provoking the Grand Master into hostility unless you are prepared for a difficult fight.

facts.fact: Gray dragons have a magic missile breath weapon, a strong bite attack, and two claw attacks, and possess magic resistance.
facts.detect: Gray dragon symbol (gray dragon) on the map
facts.action: Avoid engaging in melee combat and use ranged attacks or spells to keep distance from the dragon.

facts.fact: Gray dragons may appear among the hostile D generated in throne rooms at dungeon levels 15 and below.
facts.detect: Entering a throne room at dungeon level 15 or below
facts.action: Be cautious and prepared for a gray dragon encounter when entering throne rooms at these levels.

facts.fact: Gray dragons have a 1/3 chance of dropping a set of uncursed +0 gray dragon scales upon death unless disintegrated.
facts.detect: Killing a gray dragon
facts.action: Loot the corpse for uncursed +0 gray dragon scales.

facts.fact: Gray dragons are often sought out by heroes looking to procure gray dragon scale mail and complement an existing or future source of reflection.
facts.detect: Having a source of reflection
facts.action: Seek out and kill gray dragons to obtain gray dragon scales for crafting gray dragon scale mail.

facts.fact: Gray dragons are one of the few dragons whose scales do not gain an additional extrinsic property.
facts.detect: Obtaining gray dragon scales
facts.action: Craft gray dragon scale mail from the scales without expecting additional properties.

facts.fact: Gray oozes have a bite attack that can rust metallic items the target is wearing.
facts.detect: The bot should notice if it is wearing any iron or metallic items and encounters a gray ooze.
facts.action: The bot should remove all metallic items before engaging with a gray ooze to avoid rusting.

facts.fact: Gray oozes are acidic and eating a glob of gray ooze cures stoning on the first bite and has a roughly 6% chance of granting fire resistance, cold resistance, or poison resistance.
facts.detect: The bot should notice if it is stoned or if it needs resistance to fire, cold, or poison.
facts.action: The bot should eat a glob of gray ooze if it is stoned or needs resistance to fire, cold, or poison, but only if it is safe to do so.

facts.fact: Gray oozes are very slow and move at the minimum speed possible for a non-sessile monster.
facts.detect: The bot should notice the slow movement of the gray ooze on the map.
facts.action: The bot should use ranged attacks or melee combat while avoiding metallic armor to take advantage of the gray ooze's slow speed.

facts.fact: Gray oozes do not leave a corpse upon death, but may leave behind a glob of its body.
facts.detect: The bot should notice the absence of a corpse after defeating a gray ooze.
facts.action: The bot should be prepared to deal with the acidic glob left behind, possibly by avoiding it or using a neutralizing agent like a healing potion.

facts.fact: Gray oozes are always created hostile.
facts.detect: The bot should notice the hostile behavior of the gray ooze upon encounter.
facts.action: The bot should prepare to engage in combat or avoid the gray ooze if it is not ready for a fight.

facts.fact: Green dragons have a poisonous breath weapon that leaves a trail of poison clouds, a strong bite attack, and two claw attacks.
facts.detect: Poison clouds, bite, claw
facts.action: Avoid standing in poison clouds, use reflection or poison resistance to mitigate damage

facts.fact: Green dragons have a 3/1 chance of dropping a set of uncursed +0 green dragon scales upon death unless disintegrated.
facts.detect: Green dragon corpse
