facts.action: Eat green dragon corpse to gain poison resistance

facts.fact: Green dragons can be generated by the summon nasties monster spell.
facts.detect: Summon nasties spell cast
facts.action: Avoid or prepare for green dragon encounter

facts.fact: Green dragons have a 1/6 chance of dropping a set of uncursed +0 green dragon scales upon death unless disintegrated.
facts.detect: Green dragon corpse
facts.action: Eat green dragon corpse to gain poison resistance

facts.fact: Green dragons can inflict knockback with their melee attacks.
facts.detect: Knockback effect
facts.action: Fight green dragons in open areas away from hazards like pools or lava

facts.action: Avoid melee attacks on green molds; use ranged attacks or wands to kill them.

facts.fact: Armor and weapons have a chance of corroding when used to attack a green mold.
facts.detect: Seeing the message 'Your [item] is corroded!' after attacking a green mold.

facts.fact: Eating a green mold corpse or tin immediately cures stoning on the first bite.
facts.detect: Eating a green mold corpse or tin and seeing the message 'You feel a burning sensation, but it passes quickly.'
facts.action: Eat green mold corpses or tins to cure stoning if affected.

facts.fact: Green molds are always generated hostile.

facts.action: Avoid or kill green molds to prevent acid damage and equipment corrosion.

facts.fact: Green molds possess acid resistance and stoning resistance.
facts.detect: Noticing that green molds are unaffected by acid or stoning attacks.
facts.action: Use non-acidic attacks or items to deal with green molds.

facts.fact: Green slimes have a touch attack that causes sliming, which turns the victim into a mindless green slime in nine turns if not stopped.

facts.fact: Green slimes are only randomly generated in Gehennom and are always hostile.

facts.fact: Green slimes do not leave a corpse but may leave behind a glob of their body.

facts.fact: An amulet of unchanging can block sliming from touch attack or eaten glob and abort any current sliming.

facts.fact: High magic cancellation significantly reduces the chance of sliming from a green slime's touch attack.
facts.detect: Having high magic cancellation
facts.action: Use magic cancellation to reduce sliming risk

facts.fact: Green-elves have a 1/3 chance of conferring sleep resistance when eaten.
facts.detect: Green-elf corpse or tin
facts.action: Eat Green-elf corpse or tin to gain sleep resistance if needed.

facts.fact: Green-elves can generate in small groups and are sometimes peaceful towards chaotic characters.
facts.detect: Multiple Green-elves appearing together, or peaceful reaction message.
facts.action: Avoid combat if Green-elves are peaceful and you are chaotic.

facts.fact: Green-elves have a 1/2 chance of generating with an elven mithril-coat or elven cloak.

facts.fact: Green-elves have a 1/2 chance of generating with an elven dagger.

facts.fact: Green-elves can generate with elven bow and set of elven arrows, or elven broadsword.
facts.detect: Elven bow, elven arrows, elven broadsword
facts.action: Pick up and use elven bow, elven arrows, or elven broadsword if generated.

facts.fact: Gremlins can clone themselves in water, splitting into two identical clones with half the original's maximum HP.
facts.detect: Gremlin in water or near water source
facts.action: Avoid water near gremlins or kill them before they can clone.

facts.fact: Gremlins have a 10% chance to steal intrinsics at night, which can cancel monsters and destroy clay golem form.
facts.detect: Night time and gremlin attack

facts.detect: Gremlin in proximity to light sources

facts.fact: Gremlin corpses are poisonous and grant poison resistance with a 33% chance.
facts.detect: Eating a gremlin corpse or tin

facts.fact: Gremlins can be peaceful towards chaotic heroes without the Amulet of Yendor.
facts.detect: Peaceful gremlin near chaotic hero

facts.fact: Grey-elves have a 2/5 chance of conferring sleep resistance when eaten.

facts.fact: Grey-elves can generate in small groups.

facts.action: Be cautious and prepare for combat if encountering a group of Grey-elves.

facts.fact: Grey-elves are sometimes peaceful towards chaotic characters and always peaceful towards player elves.

facts.action: Talk to peaceful Grey-elf if you are chaotic or an elf to potentially gain allies or information.

facts.fact: Grey-elves have a 1/2 chance of generating with an elven mithril-coat or elven cloak.
facts.detect: Grey-elf with mithril-coat or cloak
facts.action: Steal or take elven mithril-coat or cloak if available for better AC.

facts.fact: Grey-elves have a 1/2 chance of generating with an elven dagger.
facts.detect: Grey-elf with elven dagger
facts.action: Take elven dagger if available for better weapon.

facts.fact: Grid bugs move and attack only in non-diagonal directions.

facts.detect: Monster name: grid bug.

facts.fact: Grid bugs leave no corpse upon death.
facts.detect: No corpse appears after killing a grid bug.

facts.fact: Grid bugs deal minimal damage with their bite attack.

facts.fact: Grid bugs are among the weakest monsters in NetHack.
facts.detect: Monster name: grid bug.

facts.fact: The guard is aware of gold in a container within your inventory.

facts.fact: The guard is aware of gold in your open inventory, and warns you to drop it before they lead you from the vault.

facts.fact: The guard saw you try to pick up vault gold that was dropped a second time, and becomes hostile.

facts.fact: Iron piercers have a bite attack dealing 3d6 physical damage.
facts.detect: An iron piercer symbol on the map or a bite attack message.
facts.action: Equip a hard helm or good armor to mitigate damage, or use a weapon with high damage or accuracy to quickly defeat the iron piercer.

facts.fact: Iron piercers have a cling attribute, allowing them to hide on the ceiling.
facts.detect: An iron piercer symbol on the ceiling.
facts.action: Move carefully to avoid being under a ceiling where an iron piercer might be hiding.

facts.fact: Iron piercers have a hide attribute, allowing them to remain hidden until a hero moves adjacent to their square.
facts.detect: A sudden appearance of an iron piercer symbol when moving next to a hidden square.
facts.action: Move carefully and use warning or telepathy to detect hidden iron piercers.

facts.fact: Iron piercers have a noeyes attribute, meaning they do not have eyes and cannot see.
facts.detect: An iron piercer symbol on the map.
facts.action: Use stealth or invisibility to avoid detection.

facts.fact: Ixoth is a unique red dragon that guards the Bell of Opening and the Knight quest artifact, The Magic Mirror of Merlin.
facts.detect: Ixoth, Bell of Opening, The Magic Mirror of Merlin
facts.action: Avoid Ixoth until you have a strategy to deal with him, such as a lance and fast steed or a scroll of scare monster.

facts.fact: Ixoth has a powerful fire breath weapon, a strong bite attack, the ability to cast a mage monster spell during each turn, and two claw attacks, including one that can steal quest artifacts.
facts.detect: Ixoth's attacks
facts.action: Equip fire resistant armor and items, and ensure you have a way to deal with monster spells.

facts.fact: Ixoth will always generate at the same point on the goal level, deep within his dark cavern.
facts.detect: Dark cavern with Ixoth sitting next to the entrance of a small subsection
facts.action: Approach with caution, using light sources and stealth if possible.

facts.fact: Ixoth will not use his fire breath unless he has teleported to the upstair to heal.
facts.detect: Ixoth teleporting to the upstair
facts.action: Be prepared to deal with fire breath if Ixoth teleports to the upstair.

facts.fact: If you are mounted on a fast steed and are at least Skilled in lance, you can use your movement speed to potentially joust Ixoth to death.
facts.detect: Fast steed and lance
facts.action: Use jousting as a strategy to defeat Ixoth if you have a fast steed and lance.

facts.fact: A jabberwock is a hostile monster with two bite attacks and two claw attacks, each dealing 2d10 physical damage.
facts.detect: jabberwock
facts.action: Avoid engaging a jabberwock in melee combat unless well-prepared, as its attacks are very strong.

facts.fact: Jabberwocks have a 50% magic resistance (MR), making many spells and wands unreliable against them.
facts.detect: Attempting to use spells or wands on a jabberwock
facts.action: Avoid using spells or wands that are likely to be ineffective due to the jabberwock's high MR.

facts.fact: Jabberwocks can be generated on the Plane of Air at level creation, and two jabberwocks are always generated there.
facts.detect: Entering the Plane of Air
facts.action: Be prepared to fight jabberwocks upon entering the Plane of Air.

facts.fact: A jabberwock can be saddled for riding while tame, making it a powerful steed.
facts.detect: Taming a jabberwock
facts.action: Tame a jabberwock if possible to use it as a powerful steed.

facts.fact: Hitting a jabberwock with Vorpal Blade will always behead it.
facts.detect: Possession of Vorpal Blade
facts.action: Use Vorpal Blade to easily dispatch any jabberwock encountered.

facts.fact: Jackals are hostile and appear in small groups.
facts.detect: Multiple jackals appearing together on the map.
facts.action: Avoid engaging multiple jackals if under-equipped or at low levels.

facts.fact: Jackals have a speed of 12, which is relatively high.
facts.detect: Jackals moving quickly on the map.
facts.action: Stay alert and avoid being surrounded by jackals.

facts.fact: Eating jackals is considered cannibalism for heroes with werejackal lycanthropy.
facts.detect: Message indicating cannibalism when eating a jackal corpse.
facts.action: Avoid eating jackal corpses if you have werejackal lycanthropy.

facts.fact: Werejackals have a 6/7 chance of summoning a jackal when calling for help.
facts.detect: Message indicating a werejackal summoning a jackal.
facts.action: Prioritize killing the werejackal to prevent further summoning.

facts.fact: Jackals are part of the first quest monster class for Samurai, appearing 24/175 of the time.
facts.detect: Jackals appearing in the Samurai quest.
facts.action: Be prepared for jackals during the Samurai quest.

facts.fact: A jaguar has two claw attacks and a bite attack.
facts.detect: monster name 'jaguar' or 'jag'
facts.action: Equip the best armor and weapons available, especially those that are effective against physical damage.

facts.fact: Jaguars are randomly generated hostile.
facts.detect: monster name 'jaguar' or 'jag'
facts.action: Avoid provoking jaguars if possible, especially in low-light conditions where infravision is necessary.

facts.fact: Jaguars can be seen via infravision like all felines.
facts.detect: message 'You see a jaguar.'
facts.action: Ensure infravision is available, either through a magic lamp or a ring of see invisible.

facts.fact: Jaguars have a speed of 15.
facts.detect: monster name 'jaguar' or 'jag'
facts.action: Be prepared to move quickly to avoid attacks or to attack the jaguar before it can move.

facts.fact: Jaguars have an AC of 6.
facts.detect: monster name 'jaguar' or 'jag'
facts.action: Choose weapons and tactics that can penetrate an AC of 6 effectively.

facts.fact: Jellyfish have a poisonous sting attack that can drain strength.
facts.detect: When the bot encounters a jellyfish, the message 'A jellyfish stings you!' or similar will appear.
facts.action: Avoid melee combat with jellyfish unless the bot has poison resistance or high poison resistance from potions or rings. Use ranged attacks or spells if available.

facts.fact: Jellyfish are generated hostile and are found in specific locations on Medusa's Island and Juiblex's swamp.
facts.detect: The bot will encounter jellyfish in specific areas of Medusa's Island and Juiblex's swamp.
facts.action: Be cautious and prepared for combat when entering these areas. Have healing items and poison resistance ready.

facts.fact: Jellyfish are amphibious and can swim and hide in water, but become scared and lose HP while stuck on land.
facts.detect: When the bot is in a water-filled area, jellyfish will be present and move normally. On land, they will be visibly scared and lose health.
facts.action: If possible, lure jellyfish onto land to weaken them before engaging in combat.

facts.fact: Eating a jellyfish corpse or tin has a 1/5 chance of granting intrinsic poison resistance.
facts.detect: The bot finds a jellyfish corpse or tin.
facts.action: Eat the jellyfish corpse or tin to potentially gain poison resistance, but be prepared for the possibility of poisoning.

facts.fact: Jellyfish are the only monster form to not produce a message when a monster polymorphs into one.
facts.detect: The bot polymorphs into a jellyfish or sees another monster polymorph into a jellyfish.
facts.action: If polymorphed into a jellyfish, the bot should try to revert to its original form as soon as possible due to the lack of a message.

facts.fact: Juiblex is a unique monster with an AC of -7 and MR of 65, making him difficult to hit and damage.
facts.detect: Encountering a large, amorphous, amphibious demon lord named Juiblex with the symbol 'J'.
facts.action: Prepare a blessed unicorn horn or a potion of full healing before engaging Juiblex to cure sickness.

facts.fact: Juiblex can engulf and spit acid, inducing sickness and dealing damage.
facts.detect: Being engulfed by Juiblex and feeling sick.
facts.action: Immediately use a blessed unicorn horn or a potion of full healing to cure sickness.

facts.fact: Juiblex can teleport to the up staircase with the player inside, allowing easy traversal of his swamp lair.
facts.detect: Being engulfed by Juiblex and seeing the message 'Juiblex warps to the up staircase with you inside.'
facts.action: Allow Juiblex to teleport to the up staircase to escape his lair.

facts.fact: Juiblex is covetous and desires the Amulet of Yendor, making him a significant threat if the player has it.
facts.detect: Having the Amulet of Yendor and encountering Juiblex.
facts.action: Ensure you have a reliable sickness cure and a wand of digging before engaging Juiblex.

facts.fact: Juiblex does not leave a corpse upon death, making standard revival methods impossible.
facts.detect: Killing Juiblex and not finding a corpse.
facts.action: Use an amulet of life saving and a wand of slow monster to force Juiblex to put on the amulet and be revived.

facts.fact: Keystone Kops are generated when the hero steals from a shop and are hostile.
facts.detect: Stealing items from a shop and seeing Keystone Kops appear around the shopkeeper or near the shop.
facts.action: Avoid stealing from shops to prevent Keystone Kops from appearing.

facts.fact: Each Keystone Kop has a 1/3 chance of being generated with a club or rubber hose, and a 1/4 chance of generating with 3 to 4 cream pies.
facts.detect: Encountering a Keystone Kop with a club, rubber hose, or cream pies.
facts.action: Be cautious around Keystone Kops as they may have offensive items.

facts.fact: Keystone Kops can grow up into Kop Sergeants.
facts.detect: Seeing a Keystone Kop level up into a Kop Sergeant.
facts.action: Avoid prolonged combat with Keystone Kops to prevent them from leveling up.

facts.fact: Keystone Kops are valid targets for genocide.
facts.detect: Checking the genocide list and seeing Keystone Kops listed.
facts.action: Genocide Keystone Kops to prevent them from appearing.

facts.fact: Keystone Kops can blind the hero with cream pies, making them a threat in large numbers.
facts.detect: Being blinded by cream pies thrown by Keystone Kops.
facts.action: Carry towels to clean the face and avoid blindness.

facts.fact: A ki-rin has an AC of -5 and MR of 90, making it highly resistant to attacks and spells.
facts.detect: Encountering a ki-rin in the game.
facts.action: Equip high-enchantment missile weapons or high-damage attack spells like magic missile. Ensure you have magic resistance and a well-enchanted weapon.

facts.fact: Ki-rin can cast mage monster spells and have a speed of 18, making them dangerous and hard to catch.
facts.detect: Observing a ki-rin casting spells or moving quickly.
facts.action: Use ranged attacks or spells to weaken the ki-rin from a distance before it can get into casting range.

facts.fact: Ki-rin do not respect sanctuary or Elbereth.
facts.detect: A ki-rin entering a sanctuary or Elbereth-protected area.
facts.action: Avoid fighting ki-rin in sanctuaries or Elbereth-protected areas.

facts.fact: A ki-rin can be generated as the minion of an angry lawful god.
facts.detect: Receiving a message indicating an angry lawful god has summoned a ki-rin.
facts.action: Attempt to appease the god or avoid areas where the god's influence is strong.

facts.fact: Ki-rin are highly sought-after pets but are difficult to tame due to their MR of 90.
facts.detect: Attempting to tame a ki-rin.
facts.action: Avoid taming ki-rin unless you are a Knight or have a specific need for their abilities.

facts.fact: Killer bees have a single sting attack that can inflict strength-draining poison and possess poison resistance.
facts.detect: Monster name: Killer bee, attack message: You feel weak.
facts.action: Equip poison resistance or high magic cancellation armor, or use escape items if low level or burdened.

facts.fact: Killer bees are generated in large groups and can be summoned by kicking trees or using the summon insects spell.
facts.detect: Message: You've attracted the tree's former occupants!, or spell message: You summon insects.
facts.action: Avoid kicking trees or using summon insects spell until you have poison resistance or a way to handle them.

facts.fact: Killer bees can be found in beehives, which are guaranteed in the Wizard's Tower.
facts.detect: Map feature: Beehive room.
facts.action: Approach with caution and ensure you have poison resistance or a way to handle them.

facts.fact: Eating a killer bee corpse or tin has a 3/10 chance of granting poison resistance.
facts.detect: Item: Killer bee corpse or tin.
facts.action: Eat if you have a tinning kit and need poison resistance.

facts.fact: Killer bees can be generated among the 'a' (a) that are part of the first quest monster class for Valkyries.
facts.detect: Monster name: Killer bee, during Valkyrie quest.
facts.action: Be prepared with poison resistance or a way to handle them during the quest.

facts.fact: King Arthur is a unique monster with difficulty 24, level 20, and 588 experience points.
facts.detect: King Arthur
facts.action: Avoid or prepare for a high-level encounter if King Arthur is detected.

facts.fact: King Arthur is always generated as peaceful and is located in Camelot Castle, specifically on the throne in the central-west room.
facts.detect: Camelot Castle, throne in the central-west room
facts.action: Approach with caution and be prepared for a sudden change in hostility.

facts.fact: King Arthur is always generated with +4 plate mail and a blessed +4 long sword, which turns into Excalibur if it hasn't been generated yet.
facts.detect: +4 plate mail, blessed +4 long sword, Excalibur
facts.action: Steal or destroy his equipment before he becomes hostile to prevent him from gaining Excalibur.

facts.fact: King Arthur has two weapon attacks dealing 4d10 physical damage each.
facts.detect: King Arthur's attack messages
facts.action: Use ranged attacks or magic to avoid close combat.

facts.fact: King Arthur is infravision-capable and omnivorous.
facts.detect: Infravision, omnivorous
facts.action: Avoid being in the dark or leaving edible items around him.

facts.fact: A hero eating a kitten corpse or tin will gain the aggravate monster intrinsic.
facts.detect: Eating a kitten corpse or tin.
facts.action: Avoid eating kitten corpses or tins unless necessary.

facts.fact: Veggy food such as lichen corpses will reliably pacify a hostile kitten.
facts.detect: Encountering a hostile kitten.
facts.action: Use veggy food to pacify hostile kittens.

facts.fact: A tame kitten can be created via the spell of create familiar.
facts.detect: Having the spell of create familiar.
facts.action: Use the spell of create familiar to create a tame kitten.

facts.fact: Kittens are not smart enough to avoid monsters with passive attacks.
facts.detect: Having a tame kitten in the vicinity of passive attack monsters.
facts.action: Keep tame kittens away from passive attack monsters.

facts.fact: Chatting with a tamed kitten can provide an idea of how it is feeling.
facts.detect: Chatting with a tame kitten.
facts.action: Chat with tame kittens to check their tameness and condition.

facts.fact: A knight is a lawful player monster corresponding to a Knight hero and will have the role's appropriate rank title for their monster level.
facts.detect: The bot is playing as a lawful dwarvish Valkyrie.
facts.action: The bot should be aware that as a lawful character, it can encounter peaceful knights in certain situations.

facts.fact: A peaceful knight is generated in each of the four 'watchtower' rooms on the Knight quest home level during level creation.
facts.detect: The bot is on the Knight quest home level and encounters a peaceful knight in a watchtower room.
facts.action: The bot should avoid attacking peaceful knights unless necessary for survival or if the knight poses an immediate threat.

facts.fact: Knight corpses can generate in graveyards and within the Valley of the Dead.
facts.detect: The bot is in a graveyard or the Valley of the Dead and sees a corpse labeled as a knight.
facts.action: The bot should be cautious around knight corpses as they may be dangerous or valuable.

facts.fact: A knight is always generated with 1-3 random offensive items, 1-3 random defensive items, and 1-3 random miscellaneous items.
facts.detect: The bot encounters a knight and observes its inventory.
facts.action: The bot should loot the knight's inventory if the knight is defeated, as it may contain valuable items.

facts.fact: Knights generated on the Astral Plane will have a chance of generating with a long sword that is turned into Vorpal Blade.
facts.detect: The bot is on the Astral Plane and encounters a knight with a long sword.
facts.action: The bot should be extremely cautious around knights on the Astral Plane, especially if they have a long sword, as it could be Vorpal Blade.

facts.fact: A kobold has a 1/4 chance of generating with a stack of darts.
facts.detect: Stack of darts in inventory or on the ground near a kobold
facts.action: Be cautious when approaching a kobold, especially if it has darts. If you have a ranged weapon, try to lure the kobold into a position where you can safely attack it from a distance.

facts.fact: A kobold corpse is poisonous to eat.
facts.detect: Corpse of a kobold on the ground
facts.action: Avoid eating a kobold corpse unless you are certain you have poison resistance or are willing to risk the poison effect.

facts.fact: Kobolds may appear among the hostile 'k' that generate in throne rooms.
facts.detect: Entering a throne room and seeing hostile 'k' on the map
facts.action: Be prepared for combat when entering throne rooms, as kobolds may be present and are hostile.

facts.fact: Kobolds can grow up into large kobolds.
facts.detect: Seeing a kobold that is larger than usual
facts.action: Treat larger kobolds with extra caution as they may be more dangerous.

facts.fact: Kobolds are among the earliest monsters that can wear armor, wield weapons and use items.
facts.detect: Kobold wielding a weapon or wearing armor
facts.action: Be prepared for kobolds to be more dangerous than expected due to their ability to use equipment.

facts.fact: A kobold lord has a 1/4 chance of generating with a stack of darts.
facts.detect: stack of darts in inventory or on the ground near a kobold lord
facts.action: Be cautious and prepare to dodge or block darts if a kobold lord is found with darts.

facts.fact: A kobold lord corpse is poisonous to eat.
facts.detect: corpse of a kobold lord
facts.action: Do not eat the corpse of a kobold lord to avoid poisoning.

facts.fact: Kobold lords are always hostile and can appear among hostile kobolds in throne rooms.
facts.detect: Encountering hostile kobolds in throne rooms
facts.action: Be prepared for a fight if entering a throne room with hostile kobolds.

facts.fact: Kobold lords possess poison resistance.
facts.detect: Kobold lord attacking with poison or surviving poison attacks
facts.action: Use non-poison damage types or weapons to defeat kobold lords.

facts.fact: Kobold mummies have a 6/7 chance of being generated with a mummy wrapping.
facts.detect: mummy wrapping
facts.action: Pick up mummy wrapping if found, as it is valuable for protection against magic.

facts.fact: A kobold mummy leaves behind an aged kobold corpse upon death.
facts.detect: aged kobold corpse
facts.action: Eat aged kobold corpse to gain nutrition and experience points if hungry and not poisoned.

facts.fact: Kobold shamans have a 4/1 chance of generating with a stack of darts.
facts.detect: stack of darts in inventory or on the ground near a kobold shaman
facts.action: Pick up the darts if they are not cursed and can be used effectively as ranged weapons.

facts.fact: Kobold shamans are likely one of the first spellcasting monsters encountered.
facts.detect: Kobold shaman casting a spell (e.g., 'A kobold shaman casts a spell.')
facts.action: Avoid melee combat and use ranged attacks or magic if available to deal with the shaman.

facts.fact: Kobold shamans have poison resistance.
facts.detect: Kobold shaman is not affected by poison attacks or items.
facts.action: Use non-poisonous weapons or spells against the shaman.

facts.fact: Kobold shaman corpse is poisonous to eat.
facts.detect: Corpse of a kobold shaman
facts.action: Do not eat the corpse.

facts.fact: Kobold shamans are always hostile and randomly generated in certain areas.
facts.detect: Appearance of a hostile kobold shaman in a throne room or mine town.
facts.action: Be prepared to fight or avoid them in these areas.

facts.fact: Kobold zombies are the weakest monster in the zombie monster class and have a single claw attack that deals 1d4 damage.
facts.detect: Encounter with a kobold zombie on the map.
facts.action: Attack the kobold zombie as it poses minimal threat and can be easily dispatched.

facts.fact: Kobold zombies leave an aged kobold corpse upon death.
facts.detect: Upon killing a kobold zombie, the corpse will be identified as an aged kobold corpse.
facts.action: Eat the aged kobold corpse to gain 50 nutrition points.

facts.fact: Kobold zombies are part of the first quest monster class for Priests and make up 24/175 of the monsters randomly generated on the Priest quest.
facts.detect: Encounter with kobold zombies in the Priest quest branch.
facts.action: Proceed with caution as kobold zombies may be part of a larger group of undead monsters.

facts.fact: Killing kobold zombies boosts alignment record for neutral protection racketeers.
facts.detect: Player is a neutral protection racketeer and encounters a kobold zombie.
facts.action: Kill the kobold zombie to boost alignment record and enable safe prayer.

facts.fact: Kobold zombies are always hostile and can follow the player to other levels if adjacent.
facts.detect: Kobold zombie is adjacent to the player and follows to another level.
facts.action: Deal with the kobold zombie immediately to prevent it from following to other levels.

facts.fact: Kop Kaptains are generated if you steal from a shop and step outside near the shop or teleport a long distance away or leave the level.
facts.detect: Messages like 'A swarm of Kops appears around you!' or 'A swarm of Kops appears around the shopkeeper!'
facts.action: Avoid stealing from shops to prevent Kop Kaptain generation.

facts.fact: Each swarm of Kops includes DL + d5 Kop Kaptains (rounded down).
facts.detect: Number of Kop Kaptains in a swarm.
facts.action: Be prepared for a large number of enemies if you trigger Kop Kaptain generation.

facts.fact: A Kop Kaptain has a 3/7 chance of generating with either a club or rubber hose, and a 4/7 chance of generating with 3 to 4 cream pies.
facts.detect: Kop Kaptain carrying a club, rubber hose, or cream pies.
facts.action: Be cautious of Kop Kaptains carrying offensive items like clubs or rubber hoses.

facts.fact: Kop Kaptains never generate with an offensive item, defensive item, miscellaneous item, or gold, and never leave death drops.
facts.detect: Kop Kaptain death without dropping items.
facts.action: Do not expect to find useful items or gold from dead Kop Kaptains.

facts.fact: Kop Kaptains are valid forms for polymorph, which is generally the only other means to encounter any of them outside of bones.
facts.detect: Polymorphing into or encountering a Kop Kaptain.
facts.action: Be prepared for a hostile encounter if polymorphing into a Kop Kaptain.

facts.fact: Kop Lieutenants are generated when you steal from a shop and step outside near the shop or teleport far away.
facts.detect: Messages like 'A swarm of Kops appears!' or finding Kops around the shopkeeper and down stairs.
facts.action: Avoid stealing from shops to prevent Kop Lieutenant generation.

facts.fact: Each swarm of Kops includes 1 to 2 Kop Lieutenants (rounded down) based on dungeon level.
facts.detect: Seeing multiple Kops together, especially around the shopkeeper or down stairs.
facts.action: Stealthily leave the shop area without stealing to avoid attracting Kops.

facts.fact: Kop Lieutenants have a 3/7 chance of generating with a club or rubber hose, and a 4/7 chance of generating with 3 to 4 cream pies.
facts.detect: Finding a Kop Lieutenant with a club, rubber hose, or cream pies.
facts.action: Be cautious around Kop Lieutenants as they may have offensive items.

facts.fact: Kop Lieutenants are hostile and can grow up from Kop Sergeants.
facts.detect: Seeing a Kop Sergeant or a message like 'A Kop Sergeant grows up into a Kop Lieutenant.'
facts.action: Avoid or deal with Kop Sergeants before they can grow.

facts.fact: Kop Lieutenants are valid forms for polymorph and can be genocided but not rendered extinct.
facts.detect: Finding a polymorphed Kop Lieutenant or seeing it on bones levels.
facts.action: Genocide Kop Lieutenants if possible to reduce encounters.

facts.fact: Kop Sergeants are generated when you steal from a shop and step outside near the shop or teleport far away.
facts.detect: Appearance of multiple Kop Sergeants around the shopkeeper or down stairs after stealing.
facts.action: Avoid stealing from shops to prevent Kop Sergeant spawns.

facts.fact: Each swarm of Kops consists of (DL + d5) / 3 + 1 Kop Sergeants (rounded down).
facts.detect: Number of Kop Sergeants appearing in a swarm.
facts.action: Be prepared for multiple Kop Sergeants if you trigger their generation.

facts.fact: A Kop Sergeant has a 3/7 chance of generating with a club or rubber hose, and a 4/7 chance of generating with 3 to 4 cream pies.
facts.detect: Appearance of Kop Sergeants with clubs, rubber hoses, or cream pies.
facts.action: Be cautious of cream pies as they can cause blindness.

facts.fact: Kop Sergeants never generate with offensive, defensive, miscellaneous items, or gold.
facts.detect: Lack of items or gold when Kop Sergeants are generated.
facts.action: Do not expect to find useful items or gold from Kop Sergeants.

facts.fact: Kop Sergeants are valid targets for genocide but cannot be rendered extinct.
facts.detect: Option to genocide Kop Sergeants.
facts.action: Consider genociding Kop Sergeants to avoid future encounters.

facts.fact: Kraken difficulty is 22, level 20, and experience is 1574.
facts.detect: Kraken appears on the map or in the level.
facts.action: Avoid or prepare for a kraken if you are not at a high enough level.

facts.fact: Kraken attacks include Claw 2d4, Claw 2d4, Hug 2d6 drowning, and bite 5d4.
facts.detect: Kraken attacks player.
facts.action: Use wands of cold or sleep to immobilize the kraken before it can hug and drown the player.

facts.fact: Kraken is generated in specific locations such as the Tourist quest, Medusa's Island, and Fake Wizard's Tower moats.
facts.detect: Entering specific levels or locations.
facts.action: Be prepared for a kraken if you are in these locations.

facts.fact: Kraken can be handled using wands, spells, and scaring tools due to no MR score.
facts.detect: Kraken is in the vicinity.
facts.action: Use wands of cold or sleep to immobilize the kraken.

facts.fact: Stranded kraken outside of water becomes scared and may still attack if cornered.
facts.detect: Kraken is outside of water and trying to flee.
facts.action: Avoid cornering a scared kraken.

facts.fact: A large cat has a single bite attack that deals 2d4 physical damage.
facts.detect: A large cat appears on the map.
facts.action: Avoid or pacify large cats to prevent damage.

facts.fact: A hero eating a large cat corpse or tin will gain the aggravate monster intrinsic.
facts.detect: Eating a large cat corpse or tin.
facts.action: Avoid eating large cat corpses or tins unless necessary.

facts.fact: Large cats can be tamed by throwing meat or rations at them.
facts.detect: A large cat on the map.
facts.action: Tame large cats by throwing meat or rations to avoid combat.

facts.fact: Veggy food such as lichen corpses will reliably pacify a hostile large cat.
facts.detect: A hostile large cat on the map.
facts.action: Pacify hostile large cats with veggy food to avoid combat.

facts.fact: Chatting to a large cat can provide information about its tameness and condition.
facts.detect: A tame or peaceful large cat on the map.
facts.action: Chat with tame or peaceful large cats to gather information.

facts.fact: A large dog has a single bite attack that deals 2d4 physical damage.
facts.detect: The bot encounters a large dog with the symbol 'D'.
facts.action: Avoid combat with large dogs if possible, especially early in the game when the bot's hit points and defensive capabilities are low.

facts.fact: Large dogs can be tamed by throwing meat or rations at them.
facts.detect: The bot encounters a large dog and has meat or rations in inventory.
facts.action: Throw meat or rations at the large dog to tame it and avoid combat.

facts.fact: Eating a large dog corpse or tin grants the 'aggravate monster' intrinsic.
facts.detect: The bot eats a large dog corpse or tin.
facts.action: Avoid eating large dog corpses or tins unless the bot is an orc or a Cave Dweller.

facts.fact: During a full moon, large dogs have a 5/6 chance of becoming peaceful instead of tame when thrown acceptable food.
facts.detect: The bot encounters a large dog during a full moon.
facts.action: Throw food at the large dog to pacify it during a full moon.

facts.fact: Large dogs can be generated as peaceful towards neutral heroes.
facts.detect: The bot encounters a peaceful large dog.
facts.action: Approach the peaceful large dog to tame it and potentially use it as a pet.

facts.fact: A large kobold corpse is poisonous to eat.
facts.detect: Message: 'You are poisoned!' after eating a large kobold corpse
facts.action: Avoid eating large kobold corpses

facts.fact: A large kobold has a 1/4 chance of generating with a stack of darts.
facts.detect: A stack of darts appears next to a large kobold
facts.action: Be cautious when approaching large kobolds, especially if they have darts

facts.fact: A large mimic can disguise itself as an appropriate item or dungeon feature and can stick to the hero if they walk into it or it attacks them.
facts.detect: The mimic will appear as a disguised item or feature on the map, or the hero will be stuck to the mimic with a message like 'You are stuck to a large mimic!'.
facts.action: Use ranged attacks or telepathy to detect and avoid mimics. If stuck, engrave Elbereth or use a scare tool to make the mimic let go.

facts.fact: Eating a large mimic corpse or tin causes the hero to polymorph into a pile of gold for 40 turns, breaking the polyselfless conduct.
facts.detect: The hero will see a message like 'You feel like a pile of gold.'
facts.action: Avoid eating large mimic corpses or tins unless necessary for a specific strategy.

facts.fact: Large mimics are generated in shops at level creation with a chance of appearing as a strange object.
facts.detect: A strange object in a shop that behaves unusually or is not normally sold there.
facts.action: Be cautious when entering shops and use ranged attacks or telepathy to detect and avoid mimics.

facts.fact: When entering a new dungeon floor, a small mimic disguised as a closed door may be generated in a doorway if the level difficulty is 9 or higher.
facts.detect: A closed door that behaves unusually or is not a real door.
facts.action: Be cautious when opening doors and use telepathy or warning to detect mimics.

facts.fact: A large mimic is generated on the home floor of the Rogue quest disguised as the down stair.
facts.detect: A down stair that behaves unusually or is not a real down stair.
facts.action: Be cautious when descending stairs and use telepathy or warning to detect mimics.

facts.fact: Leather golems have two claw attacks, and possess sleep resistance and poison resistance like all golems.
facts.detect: Leather golem
facts.action: Avoid using sleep or poison-based attacks on leather golems.

facts.fact: A leather golem that is subjected to stoning will become a stone golem.
facts.detect: Leather golem subjected to stoning
facts.action: Avoid stoning attacks or items near leather golems.

facts.fact: A leather golem that is hit by a decay attack (i.e. from a brown pudding) will instantly rot away and be destroyed.
facts.detect: Message: 'falls to pieces!'
facts.action: Use brown puddings or similar decay attacks to destroy leather golems.

facts.fact: Leather golems are always generated with 40 HP.
facts.detect: Leather golem
facts.action: Prepare for a leather golem with 40 HP when encountering one.

facts.fact: Instead of a corpse, leather golems death drop 2-8 items, with 3/4 chance of a leather armor, a 1/6 chance of a leather cloak, and a 1/12 chance of a saddle.
facts.detect: Leather golem death
facts.action: Loot the items dropped by a dead leather golem.

facts.fact: A lemure is a type of monster with infravision, regeneration, and is always hostile.
facts.detect: Infravision and regeneration attributes, hostile behavior
facts.action: Avoid close combat and use ranged attacks or spells to keep distance.

facts.fact: Lemures are poisonous to eat and eating one grants sleep resistance.
facts.detect: Poisonous corpse message
facts.action: Do not eat lemure corpses.

facts.fact: Lemures never leave a corpse upon death.
facts.detect: No corpse left after killing a lemure
facts.action: Do not rely on lemure corpses for any purpose.

facts.fact: Lemures are generated in Gehennom and can appear in large groups.
facts.detect: Appearance in Gehennom and group formation
facts.action: Be prepared for multiple lemures and have sufficient supplies.

facts.fact: Lemures are generated on the skull-shaped island of Juiblex's swamp at level creation.
facts.detect: Skull-shaped island in Juiblex's swamp
facts.action: Be cautious when exploring this area.

facts.fact: Leocrotta difficulty is 8, level is 6, and experience is 76.
facts.detect: Leocrotta monster appearance
facts.action: Avoid or prepare for combat if low level or unprepared for melee.

facts.fact: Leocrotta has a speed of 18 and hits hard with claw and bite attacks.
facts.detect: Leocrotta monster appearance
facts.action: Use ranged attacks or wands of cold, fire, lightning, sleep, or slow monster to immobilize or kill it.

facts.fact: Leocrotta has no resistances and a minimal MR score of 10.
facts.detect: Leocrotta monster appearance
facts.action: Use wands or spells to immobilize or kill it.

facts.fact: Leocrotta can be generated by the summon nasties monster spell.
facts.detect: Summon nasties spell cast
facts.action: Prepare escape items or ranged attacks.

facts.fact: Leocrotta imitates the hero when chatted to.
facts.detect: The leocrotta imitates you.
facts.action: Avoid chatting to it.

facts.fact: A leprechaun has a 7/8 chance of dodging melee attacks unless the hero force-fights.
facts.detect: You miss wildly and stumble forward.
facts.action: Use ranged attacks or force-fight if necessary to ensure hits.

facts.fact: Leprechauns can steal gold from the hero's inventory or from under their feet.
facts.detect: Leprechaun steals gold from you.
facts.action: Drop or stash gold before engaging leprechauns, or use ranged attacks.

facts.fact: Leprechauns have a 50% chance of causing teleportitis when eaten.
facts.detect: Eating a leprechaun corpse.
facts.action: Avoid eating leprechaun corpses unless teleportitis is desired.

facts.fact: Leprechauns are generated asleep and can be found in leprechaun halls with piles of gold.
facts.detect: Entering a room filled with sleeping leprechauns.
facts.action: Be cautious and avoid waking them if not prepared to fight.

facts.fact: Leprechauns can bury stolen gold in non-shop rooms out of the hero's sight.
facts.detect: Leprechaun steals gold and teleports away.
facts.action: Track leprechauns and search areas they teleport to.

facts.fact: Liches have a touch attack that deals cold damage and can shatter potions in the target's open inventory.
facts.detect: Message: 'The lich touches you!' or 'Your potion shatters!'
facts.action: Avoid having open potions and use cold resistance or protection from cold to mitigate damage.

facts.fact: Liches possess cold resistance, sleep resistance, poison resistance, drain resistance, and death resistance.
facts.detect: Monster attributes or resistance checks
facts.action: Prepare for a tough fight with magic resistance and items that provide cold resistance.

facts.fact: Liches are poisonous to consume, primarily if digested by another monster.
facts.detect: Message: 'You feel poisoned.'
facts.action: Avoid eating liches or being digested by other monsters.

facts.fact: Liches never leave a corpse when killed, and their body crumbles to dust.
facts.detect: Message: 'The lich crumbles to dust.'
facts.action: No action needed, but be aware that you won't find a corpse.

facts.fact: Liches have a low movement speed of 6, which can be boosted to 8 with haste.
facts.detect: Monster speed or movement speed of 6 or 8
facts.action: Outrun liches if possible or use ranged attacks to weaken them.

facts.fact: A lichen has a sticky touch attack that deals no damage, but holds the hero in place for a short amount of time.
facts.detect: The bot encounters a lichen and receives the message 'A lichen sticks to you.'
facts.action: The bot should move away from the lichen to avoid being stuck, or attack it to kill it quickly.

facts.fact: Lichen corpses do not become tainted or rot away from age.
facts.detect: The bot finds a lichen corpse.
facts.action: The bot should pick up the lichen corpse as it can be safely eaten later.

facts.fact: Lichen corpses provide 200 nutrition.
facts.detect: The bot has a lichen corpse in its inventory and is hungry.
facts.action: The bot should eat the lichen corpse to regain nutrition.

facts.fact: Lichen corpses can be used to tame domestic herbivores such as ponies.
facts.detect: The bot encounters a domestic herbivore such as a pony.
facts.action: The bot should use a lichen corpse to tame the herbivore.

facts.fact: Lichen are extremely slow, moving at the minimum speed of 1.
facts.detect: The bot notices that lichens move very slowly on the map.
facts.action: The bot should prioritize killing lichens to gain experience and items.

facts.fact: Lieutenants are strong and omnivorous, can be seen via infravision, will pick up any weapons, armor, food, and other items that they come across, and can follow a hero to other levels if they are adjacent.
facts.detect: Adjacent to a lieutenant, the bot notices the lieutenant picking up items or following it.
facts.action: Avoid letting lieutenants follow or pick up items, especially weapons and armor. If necessary, use a corridor to isolate them.

facts.fact: Applying a bugle will cause lieutenants that hear it to awaken from any sleep, end any paralysis or scaring, and turn hostile if they are currently not.
facts.detect: The bot hears a bugle sound or notices a bugle in the vicinity.
facts.action: Avoid using bugles or dropping them near lieutenants.

facts.fact: A lieutenant has a {{frac|2|3}} chance of being pacified by a bribe, with the lieutenant having a base value of 500zm for acceptable bribes.
facts.detect: The bot has 500zm or more and encounters a lieutenant.
facts.action: Consider using a bribe to pacify a lieutenant if there is a strategic advantage, such as blocking a hallway.

facts.fact: Lieutenants have a {{frac|3}} chance of generating with a K-ration, a separate {{frac|2}} chance of generating with a C-ration, and a separate {{frac|3}} chance of generating with a bugle.
facts.detect: The bot finds a lieutenant with a bugle, K-ration, or C-ration.
facts.action: Be cautious around lieutenants with bugles and ration items.

facts.fact: Lieutenants possess the same movement speed of 10 as the rest of the Yendor military and have a low MR score of 15, so while poisoned weapons, poison attacks and various forms of magic remain effective against them, they may occasionally resist such effects.
facts.detect: The bot uses poisoned weapons or magic against a lieutenant.
facts.action: Be prepared for resistance and have backup strategies.

facts.fact: A little dog can be tamed by throwing meat or rations at it, and pacified by throwing veggy food.
facts.detect: The bot can detect a little dog on the map and have food items in inventory.
facts.action: Throw meat or rations to tame, or veggy food to pacify a hostile little dog.

facts.fact: Eating a little dog corpse or tin grants the aggravate monster intrinsic.
facts.detect: The bot can detect eating a little dog corpse or tin.
facts.action: Avoid eating a little dog corpse or tin unless the bot is an orc or a Cave Dweller.

facts.fact: During a full moon, little dogs have a 5/6 chance of becoming peaceful instead of tame when throwing acceptable food to them.
facts.detect: The bot can detect a full moon in the game.
facts.action: Throw food to little dogs during a full moon to pacify them.

facts.fact: Chatting to a little dog will give various responses depending on its tameness and condition.
facts.detect: The bot can detect a tame or peaceful little dog on the map.
facts.action: Chat with a tame or peaceful little dog to check its condition.

facts.fact: Little dogs can appear among the random d that are part of the first quest monster class for Samurai.
facts.detect: The bot can detect little dogs among the random d on the map.
facts.action: Tame or polymorph little dogs encountered during the Samurai quest.

facts.fact: A lizard has a single bite attack and possesses stoning resistance.
facts.detect: Encounter with a lizard or seeing the message 'You feel limber!'
facts.action: Eat the lizard corpse to cure stoning and reduce confusion and stunning duration.

facts.fact: Lizard corpses do not rot away or become tainted from aging, though they can become too old for sacrifice.
facts.detect: Carrying a lizard corpse in inventory.
facts.action: Keep at least one lizard corpse in open inventory to prevent gradual stoning.

facts.fact: Eating a lizard's corpse or tin immediately cures gradual stoning and reduces the duration of any confusion and stunning to two turns.
facts.detect: Feeling gradual stoning or being confused or stunned.
facts.action: Eat a lizard corpse or tin to cure the status effects.

facts.fact: Lizard corpses do not prevent instantaneously turning to stone from contact with a stoning corpse.
facts.detect: Contact with a cockatrice or chickatrice corpse.
facts.action: Avoid contact with stoning corpses.

facts.fact: Lizard meat does not restore any intrinsic speed lost from turning to stone.
facts.detect: Losing intrinsic speed after eating a lizard corpse.
facts.action: Be aware that eating a lizard corpse will not restore lost intrinsic speed.

facts.fact: A long worm's body and head can occupy several squares simultaneously, and its maximum HP is governed by its body length.
facts.detect: Seeing multiple tildes (~) of the same color on the map.
facts.action: Avoid attacking the middle segments to prevent the worm from dividing into two. Attack the head or the last segment to ensure the worm does not split.

facts.fact: Attacking any part of a long worm that is not its head or the last segment can cause it to divide into two long worms with a 5/7 chance if a slashing weapon is used.
facts.detect: Attacking a segment other than the head or the last segment.
facts.action: Target the head or the last segment to avoid splitting the worm.

facts.fact: Long worms have a speed of 3, making them relatively slow and easy to avoid or attack.
facts.detect: Observing the movement speed of the long worm.
facts.action: Use ranged attacks or spells to damage multiple segments at once.

facts.fact: Long worms leave behind a worm tooth upon death, which can be used to craft crysknives.
facts.detect: Finding a worm tooth on the square where the head of the long worm was.
facts.action: Collect the worm tooth for crafting.

facts.fact: Long worms are generated hostile and can be asleep 4/5 of the time unless the Amulet of Yendor is in the hero's inventory.
facts.detect: Encountering a sleeping long worm or seeing a hostile long worm.
facts.action: Avoid waking up sleeping long worms if possible and be prepared to fight hostile ones.

facts.fact: Lord Carnarvon is a unique monster with difficulty 24, level 20, and 583 experience points.
facts.detect: Lord Carnarvon
facts.action: Avoid or prepare for a high-level, powerful encounter if you see Lord Carnarvon.

facts.fact: Lord Carnarvon is always generated as peaceful and is located on the throne in the center-most room of the College of Archeology on the Archeologist quest's home level.
facts.detect: College of Archeology, throne in the center-most room
facts.action: Be cautious and prepared when entering the College of Archeology, especially near the throne.

facts.fact: Lord Carnarvon has a weapon attack of 4d10 physical damage and can cast a mage monster spell for 4d8 damage.
facts.detect: Weapon attack or spellcasting
facts.action: Equip high AC and resistances, and be ready to use defensive spells or items.

facts.fact: Lord Carnarvon is always generated with a +5 fedora and a +4 bullwhip.
facts.detect: Lord Carnarvon with +5 fedora and +4 bullwhip
facts.action: Steal or destroy these items if possible to reduce his combat effectiveness.

facts.fact: Lord Carnarvon can tunnel through walls with a digging tool like an Archeologist hero.
facts.detect: Tunneling through walls
facts.action: Be prepared for unexpected movement and block off areas if necessary.

facts.fact: Lord Sato is always generated as peaceful and is not a valid polymorph form or genocide target.
facts.detect: The bot will encounter Lord Sato in the Castle of the Taro Clan, and he will be peaceful.
facts.action: The bot should not attack Lord Sato unless it is necessary for survival or quest completion.

facts.fact: Lord Sato is always generated with +5 splint mail and a +4 katana, both of which are non-cursed and rustproof.
facts.detect: The bot will see Lord Sato wearing +5 splint mail and wielding a +4 katana.
facts.action: The bot should consider taking the +5 splint mail and +4 katana from Lord Sato if it can do so without angering him.

facts.fact: Lord Surtur is a unique fire giant that guards the Bell of Opening and the Valkyrie quest artifact, The Orb of Fate.
facts.detect: Lord Surtur, Bell of Opening, The Orb of Fate
facts.action: Avoid taking the quest artifact until prepared to fight Lord Surtur.

facts.fact: Lord Surtur can steal back the quest artifact if you have taken it from him with his claw attack.
facts.detect: Taking the quest artifact and engaging Lord Surtur
facts.action: Ensure you have a backup plan if the artifact is stolen back.

facts.fact: Lord Surtur is fire resistant but not cold resistant, taking extra damage from cold attacks.
facts.detect: Wand of cold, cold-based attacks
facts.action: Use cold-based attacks to damage Lord Surtur more effectively.

facts.fact: Lord Surtur respects Elbereth and the scroll of scare monster.
facts.detect: Elbereth engraving, scroll of scare monster
facts.action: Use Elbereth or scare monster to avoid direct combat.

facts.fact: Lord Surtur can knock you backwards with his melee attacks, potentially into lava.
facts.detect: Engaging in melee combat with Lord Surtur
facts.action: Use levitation or flying to avoid being knocked into lava.

facts.fact: A lurker above is a hostile monster with a digestion attack that can instantly kill small pets.
facts.detect: Telepathy warning or seeing a lurker above symbol on the ceiling
facts.action: Use telepathy to detect and avoid lurkers above, or prepare to fight if one is detected.

facts.fact: Lurkers above have a very low speed of 3, making them nonthreatening if you are decently equipped.
facts.detect: Seeing a lurker above on the ceiling with low speed
facts.action: Engage in combat if necessary, but do not panic due to its low speed.

facts.fact: Lurkers above can be generated randomly and are always hostile.
facts.detect: Encountering a lurker above in a random dungeon level
facts.action: Be prepared to fight or avoid the lurker above.

facts.fact: Lurkers above are the only flying monster that cannot be generated on the Plane of Air.
facts.detect: Noticing a lurker above on a non-air plane
facts.action: No specific action needed, but useful for identifying the monster.

facts.fact: Lurkers above can be detected via telepathy or warning, and their digestion attack can instantly kill small pets.
facts.detect: Telepathy warning or seeing a pet die instantly near a lurker above
facts.action: Keep pets away from areas where lurkers above are detected.

facts.fact: A lynx has two claw attacks and a bite attack.
facts.detect: Lynx
facts.action: Avoid engaging lynxes in melee combat without proper armor and weapons.

facts.fact: Lynxes are randomly generated hostile.
facts.detect: Lynx
facts.action: Use ranged attacks or summon pets to fight lynxes from a distance.

facts.fact: Lynxes have infravision.
facts.detect: Infravision
facts.action: Use items or spells that provide infravision to see lynxes in dark areas.

facts.fact: Lynxes have a difficulty level of 7.
facts.detect: Lynx
facts.action: Prepare for encounters with lynxes by ensuring high hit points, good armor, and effective weapons.

facts.fact: Lynxes have a speed of 15.
facts.detect: Lynx
facts.action: Be cautious of lynxes' speed and try to avoid being cornered or surrounded.

facts.fact: A mail daemon will deliver a scroll of mail when the player receives an email on multi-user systems with the MAIL compile-time option defined.
facts.detect: The messages 'Gangway! Look out! Pardon me!', 'Excuse me.', 'This place's too crowded. I'm outta here.', ', ! I have some mail for you.', 'Catch!', 'I'm late!' indicate the presence and actions of a mail daemon.
facts.action: Do not attack the mail daemon as it is peaceful and harmless. If you receive a scroll of mail, read it to launch your preferred mail reader.

facts.fact: Mail daemons can see invisible, fly, and swim, and are immune to elemental attacks and poison.
facts.detect: The mail daemon's attributes and resistances listed in the wiki.
facts.action: Avoid attacking the mail daemon as it is highly resistant and can move through any environment.

facts.fact: The only way to kill a mail daemon is to stone to flesh a statue of a mail daemon and attack it quickly.
facts.detect: A statue of a mail daemon in the inventory or on the ground.
facts.action: Do not attempt to kill a mail daemon unless you are specifically seeking bragging rights, as it will genocide them and prevent further mail delivery.

facts.fact: Mail daemons can be used to generate scrolls of mail for niche purposes, such as propelling yourself while levitating.
facts.detect: A mail daemon delivering a scroll of mail.
facts.action: If levitating, catch the scroll of mail and use it to propel yourself.

facts.fact: Mail daemons will not appear if the MAIL compile-time option is undefined or if the mail option is set to false.
facts.detect: The absence of mail daemon activity in the game.
facts.action: Do not expect mail delivery if you are playing on a system where MAIL is undefined or the mail option is disabled.

facts.fact: Manes are always hostile and frequently appear in large groups.
facts.detect: Multiple manes appearing together or following the player.
facts.action: Avoid engaging large groups of manes and try to isolate and kill them one by one.

facts.fact: Manes have infravision and can be seen via infravision.
facts.detect: Infravision indicator in the status bar or map.
facts.action: Use infravision or items that grant infravision to detect manes in dark areas.

facts.fact: Manes have two claw attacks and a bite attack, and can deal up to 10 damage per round.
facts.detect: Manes attacking the player.
facts.action: Equip armor and weapons with high AC and damage, respectively, to handle manes more effectively.

facts.fact: Manes are poisonous to eat and never leave a corpse upon death.
facts.detect: Eating a manes corpse.
facts.action: Avoid eating manes corpses to prevent poisoning.

facts.fact: Manes are part of the first quest monster class for Knights and appear in the Wizard quest.
facts.detect: Manes appearing in the Knight or Wizard quest.
facts.action: Be prepared for manes in these quests and use tactics to handle them efficiently.

facts.fact: Mariliths have an AC of -6 and MR of 80, making them very difficult to hit and avoid.
facts.detect: Encountering a marilith in Gehennom or through polymorph traps.
facts.action: Avoid engaging a marilith unless well-prepared with high AC and MR resistance, and equipped with a blessed, silver, and/or well-enchanted weapon.

facts.fact: Mariliths can see invisible, which means they can detect invisible players.
facts.detect: Being in Gehennom and noticing a marilith approaches while invisible.
facts.action: Avoid becoming invisible near mariliths or ensure you are well-prepared to fight one if you must.

facts.fact: Mariliths are generated in Gehennom and can be summoned by chaotic gods and Moloch.
facts.detect: Entering Gehennom or encountering chaotic priests or Moloch's minions.
facts.action: Be prepared for a marilith encounter in Gehennom and avoid summoning them by chaotic entities.

facts.fact: Mariliths are dangerous before Gehennom due to their high speed and multiple attacks.
facts.detect: Encountering a marilith in earlier levels of the dungeon.
facts.action: Avoid or flee from mariliths in non-Gehennom areas unless you are well-prepared.

facts.fact: Mariliths are excellent pets due to their six attacks and natural AC, but they are weak to silver and do not leave a corpse.
facts.detect: Attempting to tame a marilith or finding a tame marilith as a pet.
facts.action: Be cautious with marilith pets due to their silver weakness and lack of corpse.

facts.fact: The Master Assassin is a unique monster that guards the Bell of Opening and the Rogue's quest artifact, The Master Key of Thievery.
facts.detect: Bell of Opening, The Master Key of Thievery
facts.action: Avoid taking the Bell of Opening and The Master Key of Thievery unless necessary to complete the Rogue quest.

facts.fact: The Master Assassin has a weapon attack that can poison and drain strength, a second weapon attack that deals physical damage, and a claw attack that can steal the quest artifact.
facts.detect: Master Assassin's attacks
facts.action: Equip poison resistance and carry the quest artifact to reduce damage and prevent artifact theft.

facts.fact: The Master Assassin is always generated hostile and can be awakened from a meditating state using a cursed potion of invisibility, a drum of earthquake, a shrieker, or a mind flayer's psychic blast.
facts.detect: Cursed potion of invisibility, drum of earthquake, shrieker, mind flayer
facts.action: Avoid awakening the Master Assassin unless necessary to complete the Rogue quest.

facts.fact: The Master Assassin can be rendered helpless with a wand of death, wand of sleep, potion of sleeping, or a poisoned weapon.
facts.detect: Wand of death, wand of sleep, potion of sleeping, poisoned weapon
facts.action: Use these items to incapacitate the Master Assassin before engaging in combat.

facts.fact: The level containing the Master Assassin is no-teleport and designed to isolate the hero, but can be entered via level teleportation or dropping through a hole/trap door.
facts.detect: No-teleport level, isolated section
facts.action: Use level teleportation or dropping through a hole/trap door to enter the level safely.

facts.fact: Master Kaen is a unique monster with difficulty 31, level 25, and 1095 experience points.
facts.detect: Encountering a strong human monk named Master Kaen on the Monk's quest level.
facts.action: Avoid direct combat and use ranged attacks or spells to defeat him.

facts.fact: Master Kaen has poison resistance and stoning resistance, but lacks sleep resistance, drain resistance, and disintegration resistance.
facts.detect: Observing that Master Kaen does not react to sleep spells or drain life attacks.
facts.action: Use sleep spells, wands of sleep, or potions of sleeping to immobilize him.

facts.fact: Master Kaen can steal the quest artifact, The Eyes of the Overworld, if obtained without killing him.
facts.detect: Seeing Master Kaen pick up the Eyes of the Overworld.
facts.action: Ensure the Eyes of the Overworld are safely in inventory before engaging Master Kaen.

facts.fact: Master Kaen can teleport and ignore Elbereth, making him unpredictable and dangerous.
facts.detect: Observing Master Kaen teleporting or moving despite Elbereth symbols.
facts.action: Use a scroll of scare monster to immobilize him or create a boulder fort to restrict his movement.

facts.fact: Master Kaen can be polymorphed, but the quest artifact has a 19/20 chance of resisting polymorph.
facts.detect: Using a wand of polymorph on Master Kaen.
facts.action: Have a backup plan if the artifact resists polymorph or if Master Kaen turns into a dangerous monster.

facts.fact: Master liches have a cold touch attack and can cast mage monster spells.
facts.detect: Monster name 'master lich' and its attack messages
facts.action: Avoid melee combat and keep distance to prevent spellcasting. Use magic resistance if available.

facts.fact: Master liches are covetous and seek out the Book of the Dead.
facts.detect: Monster name 'master lich' and its movement towards the Book of the Dead
facts.action: Steal the Book of the Dead before encountering a master lich or avoid areas where it is likely to be found.

facts.fact: Master liches are generated in Gehennom and can be generated in the Castle with a 1/3 chance from a cursed Book of the Dead.
facts.detect: Monster name 'master lich' and its generation location
facts.action: Avoid reading cursed Books of the Dead and be cautious in Gehennom and Castle areas.

facts.fact: Master liches have a 1/3 chance of being generated with an athame or a wand of nothing.
facts.detect: Monster name 'master lich' and its inventory
facts.action: Steal or disarm the athame or wand of nothing if encountered.

facts.fact: Master liches leave no corpse upon death.
facts.detect: Message 'its body crumbles to dust' after killing a master lich
facts.action: No action required, but note that there will be no corpse to loot.

facts.fact: Master mind flayers have a high monster magic resistance (MR) of 90.
facts.detect: Monster magic resistance of 90
facts.action: Avoid using magic-based attacks or spells against master mind flayers.

facts.fact: Master mind flayers can cause intelligence drain and instadeath if intelligence drops too low.
facts.detect: Message 'Your brain is eaten!'
facts.action: Wear a greased helm or use a ring of sustain ability to prevent intelligence drain.

facts.fact: Master mind flayers can be generated in the Gnomish Mines and Gehennom, often unexpectedly.
facts.detect: Encountering a master mind flayer in the Gnomish Mines or Gehennom
facts.action: Be cautious and prepared for their presence in these areas.

facts.fact: Master mind flayers can cause amnesia, making it difficult to identify items and remember floor layouts.
facts.detect: Message 'Your brain is eaten!' followed by difficulty identifying items or remembering floors
facts.action: Carry a means to re-identify items and have a map of the level before encountering them.

facts.fact: Master mind flayers can be generated by the summon nasties spell, even if genocided.
facts.detect: Message indicating a master mind flayer has been summoned
facts.action: Avoid using the summon nasties spell if master mind flayers are genocided.

facts.fact: A master mind flayer's brain-sucking attack can kill a monster instantly and cause the message 'X's last thought fades away...'.
facts.detect: X's last thought fades away...
facts.action: If a master mind flayer is encountered, be cautious and prepare for its brain-sucking attack which can instantly kill other monsters.

facts.fact: Eating a master mind flayer's brain while in master mind flayer form is fatal and abuses wisdom if revived by an amulet of life saving.
facts.detect: Ingesting that is fatal.
facts.action: Avoid eating the brain of a master mind flayer, especially if transformed into one.

facts.fact: Eating a master mind flayer's corpse can increase intelligence.
facts.detect: Yum! That was real brain food!
facts.action: If you have the opportunity and need to increase intelligence, eating a master mind flayer's corpse can be beneficial.

facts.fact: Tame master mind flayers can be turned to stone from attempting to eat a monster's brain.
facts.detect: You have a sad thought for a moment, then it passes.
facts.action: Avoid allowing tame master mind flayers to eat monster brains to prevent them from turning to stone.

facts.fact: Master of Thieves is a unique monster with a difficulty level of 24 and generates with specific equipment for both Rogue and Tourist quests.
facts.detect: Master of Thieves, +5 leather armor, +4 silver dagger, 2-8 non-cursed +2 daggers
facts.action: Prepare for a strong melee combatant with specific equipment and be cautious of artifact-stealing abilities.

facts.fact: Master of Thieves can steal quest artifacts, including the Platinum Yendorian Express Card, and gains magic resistance upon picking it up.
facts.detect: Platinum Yendorian Express Card missing from inventory
facts.action: Avoid awakening the Master of Thieves until you have the Platinum Yendorian Express Card or ensure it is safe from theft.

facts.fact: Master of Thieves is generated peaceful for Rogues and hostile for Tourists, guarding specific quest items.
facts.detect: Peaceful or hostile monster status, specific quest items (Bell of Opening, Platinum Yendorian Express Card)
facts.action: Approach cautiously and be prepared for combat if hostile.

facts.fact: Master of Thieves can be defeated with poisoned projectiles if the player has sufficient skill level.
facts.detect: Potion of sickness, darts or other poison-compatible projectiles
facts.action: Dip darts into potion of sickness and use them to defeat the Master of Thieves.

facts.fact: Master of Thieves can still steal quest artifacts from Rogues, posing a unique threat.
facts.detect: Master Key of Thievery or other quest artifacts missing from inventory
facts.action: Be cautious of artifact theft if you are a Rogue.

facts.fact: A mastodon has two strong headbutt attacks, each dealing 4d8 physical damage.
facts.detect: Encounter a mastodon on the level.
facts.action: Avoid melee combat with mastodons if possible, use ranged attacks or summon pets to fight it.

facts.fact: Mastodons are always generated hostile.
facts.detect: Encounter a mastodon on the level.
facts.action: Be prepared to fight or avoid mastodons as they are always hostile.

facts.fact: Tame mastodons can make decently strong steeds but their herbivorous diet and lack of defenses can make long-term maintenance very difficult.
facts.detect: Tame a mastodon.
facts.action: Use a mastodon as a temporary steed but be prepared to find alternative pets due to dietary and defense issues.

facts.fact: Medusa has a gaze attack that can turn victims to stone.
facts.detect: Medusa's gaze attack message
facts.action: Use a mirror or reflection property to reflect her gaze back at her.

facts.fact: Medusa is always generated asleep and on her special level within the Dungeons of Doom.
facts.detect: Arriving on Medusa's special level or seeing Medusa asleep
facts.action: Prepare to blind or reflect her gaze before she wakes up.

facts.fact: Medusa's level is always between the Castle and the level with the magic portal to the hero's Quest.
facts.detect: Reaching the Castle or the level with the magic portal
facts.action: Be prepared to encounter Medusa's level soon after.

facts.fact: Medusa is poisonous to eat and can turn the eater to stone.
facts.detect: Eating Medusa's corpse
facts.action: Avoid eating Medusa's corpse unless you have stoning resistance.

facts.fact: Medusa can escape via stairs if scared.
facts.detect: Medusa attempting to flee via stairs
facts.action: Block the stairs or follow her to prevent escape.

facts.fact: Mind flayers have a tentacle attack that causes intelligence drain and can cause an instadeath if intelligence is too low.
facts.detect: Message: 's tentacles suck you! or Your brain is eaten!
facts.action: Equip a non-greased helm or use a greased helm to prevent tentacle attacks. Have a blessed unicorn horn or potion of restore ability ready to reverse stat loss.

facts.fact: Mind flayers can generate in the Gnomish Mines and Gehennom, making them a common threat.
facts.detect: Encountering a magenta-colored monster or sensing waves of psychic energy.
facts.action: Avoid melee combat and use ranged attacks or polymorph traps to deal with them.

facts.fact: Mind flayers have a high monster magic resistance (MR) of 90, making them hard to scare or affect with magic.
facts.detect: Attempting to scare or affect a mind flayer with magic fails.
facts.action: Use physical means to deal with them, such as ranged attacks or polymorph traps.

facts.fact: Tame mind flayers can attract covetous monsters, which can be dangerous.
facts.detect: Seeing covetous monsters warping to the level.
facts.action: Temporarily leave tame mind flayers on another floor or be prepared to deal with covetous monsters.

facts.fact: Mind flayers can turn into a headless monster form to avoid intelligence drain attacks.
facts.detect: Polymorphing into a headless monster form.
facts.action: Polymorph into a headless monster form to avoid intelligence drain attacks.

facts.fact: Eating a mind flayer's corpse increases intelligence.
facts.detect: Yum! That was real brain food!
facts.action: Eat the mind flayer's corpse to increase intelligence if below maximum.

facts.fact: A tame mind flayer can be turned to stone from eating a monster's brain.
facts.detect: A tame mind flayer was turned to stone from an attempt to eat a monster's brain.
facts.action: Avoid letting a tame mind flayer eat monster brains to prevent pet loss.

facts.fact: The Minion of Huhetotl is a unique major demon that guards the Bell of Opening and the Archeologist quest artifact, The Orb of Detection.
facts.detect: Encounter the Minion of Huhetotl in the southeastern room of the crypt on the goal level of the Archeologist quest.
facts.action: Avoid engaging the Minion of Huhetotl until you have a reliable strategy to defeat it, such as a blessed silver saber or dwarvish mattock.

facts.fact: The Minion of Huhetotl has a high MR score of 75, making it difficult to put to sleep or polymorph.
facts.detect: Attempting to put the Minion of Huhetotl to sleep or polymorph it.
facts.action: Use offensive spells, wands, or melee attacks instead of sleep or polymorph.

facts.fact: The Minion of Huhetotl can inflict very large amounts of damage with their two weapon attacks and spellcasting.
facts.detect: Engaging in combat with the Minion of Huhetotl.
facts.action: Ensure you have high defensive and offensive capabilities before engaging.

facts.fact: Killing the Minion of Huhetotl will create a stinking cloud centered on its location.
facts.detect: Killing the Minion of Huhetotl.
facts.action: Prepare with magical breathing, healing, or sufficient HP to withstand the stinking cloud.

facts.fact: The Minion of Huhetotl is covetous and capable of warping, will pick up any items they come across, and desires the Archeologist's quest artifact.
facts.detect: Observing the Minion of Huhetotl picking up items or attempting to steal the quest artifact.
facts.action: Keep the quest artifact secure and avoid letting the Minion of Huhetotl pick up valuable items.

facts.fact: Minotaurs are among the small handful of monsters that can ignore Elbereth.
facts.detect: Minotaur appears on the map or in the field of vision.
facts.action: Avoid fighting a minotaur on Elbereth-protected squares.

facts.fact: Minotaurs have a 3/1 chance of generating with a wand of digging.
facts.detect: Minotaur with a wand of digging in inventory or on the ground near a minotaur.
facts.action: Use the wand of digging to escape or dig a pit trap.

facts.fact: Minotaurs are not intelligent and cannot make use of weapons, armor or various other items.
facts.detect: Minotaur in the field of vision.
facts.action: Use magic or items to weaken the minotaur.

facts.fact: Minotaurs are extremely susceptible to conflict, which can turn their fearsome strength on other hostile monsters.
facts.detect: Multiple hostile monsters in the vicinity of a minotaur.
facts.action: Use a scroll of taming or similar item to cause conflict.

facts.fact: Minotaurs are very vulnerable to magic and other effects due to lack of MR score and intrinsic resistances.
facts.detect: Minotaur in the field of vision.
facts.action: Use wands of sleep, slow monster, or other magic items to weaken the minotaur.

facts.fact: A monkey can perform item theft with its claw attack, dealing no damage but potentially stealing items.
facts.detect: The bot notices a message like 'A monkey steals your <item>!' or sees a monkey with an item in its inventory.
facts.action: The bot should prioritize killing monkeys before they can steal items, especially important items like wands, scrolls, or potions.

facts.fact: Monkeys can be tamed with bananas.
facts.detect: The bot finds bananas in its inventory or on the ground.
facts.action: The bot should use bananas to tame monkeys, especially if it needs to pass through an area with many monkeys.

facts.fact: Monkeys appear in the Bazaar Town map of Minetown at level creation, with five monkeys generated.
facts.detect: The bot enters the Bazaar Town map of Minetown.
facts.action: The bot should be cautious and prepared to deal with multiple monkeys in this area.

facts.fact: Monkeys are part of the second quest monster class for Healers, making up 6/175 of the monsters randomly generated on the Healer quest.
facts.detect: The bot starts the Healer quest.
facts.action: The bot should be aware of the increased likelihood of encountering monkeys during the Healer quest.

facts.fact: Monkeys will not teleport after stealing and cannot steal cursed items.
facts.detect: The bot sees a message like 'A monkey tries to steal your <cursed item> but fails.'
facts.action: The bot can relax slightly if a monkey attempts to steal a cursed item, as it will not succeed.

facts.fact: Mordor orc difficulty level is 5 and has poison resistance.
facts.detect: Encounter with Mordor orc or seeing poison resistance in monster info.
facts.action: Be cautious and avoid poison attacks if possible.

facts.fact: Mordor orc has a 1/3 chance of generating with a scimitar, orcish shield, knife, and orcish chain mail.
facts.detect: Mordor orc carrying one of these items.
facts.action: Steal or take these items if needed for equipment.

facts.fact: Mordor orc hordes are more difficult due to wider variety of starting equipment.
facts.detect: Encounter with multiple Mordor orcs.
facts.action: Be better-armored and slightly more cautious.

facts.fact: Mordor orc corpses can be a decent source of nutrition.
facts.detect: Killing a Mordor orc.
facts.action: Eat the corpse for nutrition.

facts.fact: Mordor orcs may appear in large groups in throne rooms and Gnomish Mines.
facts.detect: Entering a throne room or Gnomish Mines.
facts.action: Prepare for a potential large-scale battle.

facts.fact: Mountain centaurs have a weapon attack and two kick attacks, with a difficulty of 9 and a level of 6.
facts.detect: Encountering a mountain centaur in the dungeon.
facts.action: Avoid melee combat if possible, use ranged attacks or spells to weaken it before engaging.

facts.fact: Mountain centaurs have a 50% chance of generating with a crossbow and 3-14 crossbow bolts.
facts.detect: Seeing a mountain centaur with a crossbow and bolts.
facts.action: Prioritize ranged attacks to neutralize the crossbow threat.

facts.fact: Mountain centaurs generate with gold.
facts.detect: Finding gold near a mountain centaur.
facts.action: Steal the gold if possible, but be cautious of the centaur's attacks.

facts.fact: Mountain centaurs have a low magic resistance (MR) score of 10.
facts.detect: Using a wand or spell against a mountain centaur.
facts.action: Exploit their low MR with magical attacks.

facts.fact: Mountain centaurs are the fastest among centaurs at 20 speed.
facts.detect: Observing the mountain centaur's movement speed.
facts.action: Use speed-boosting items or spells to match or exceed its speed.

facts.fact: Mountain nymphs have a 30% chance of granting teleportitis when eaten.
facts.detect: Eating a mountain nymph corpse or tin
facts.action: Avoid eating mountain nymph corpses or tins to prevent teleportitis.

facts.fact: Mountain nymphs can steal items and use them against the player.
facts.detect: Player notices items missing or being used against them by a mountain nymph
facts.action: Avoid engaging mountain nymphs without defensive items or prepare to fight from a distance.

facts.fact: Mountain nymphs can be generated with a mirror, which can break when attacked with force bolts or wands of striking.
facts.detect: Player sees a mountain nymph with a mirror
facts.action: Avoid using force bolts or wands of striking against mountain nymphs with mirrors.

facts.fact: Mountain nymphs are generated hostile and have a 80% chance of being asleep.
facts.detect: Player encounters a sleeping mountain nymph
facts.action: Silently pass by sleeping mountain nymphs or prepare to fight if necessary.

facts.fact: Mountain nymphs can be generated with a potion of object detection.
facts.detect: Player sees a mountain nymph with a potion of object detection
facts.action: Be cautious as the potion can reveal hidden items or traps.

facts.fact: A mumak has a difficulty of 7, level 5, and experience of 68. It has a powerful butt attack of 4d12 physical damage and a bite attack of 2d6 physical damage.
facts.detect: Upon encountering a mumak on the map, the bot will see a large, elephant-like quadruped.
facts.action: The bot should avoid melee combat and use ranged weapons, polearms, wands, spells, or hit and run tactics. It should also consider using sleep or poison spells to immobilize the mumak.

facts.fact: Mumakil have an AC of 0 and no MR score, making them vulnerable to sleep and poison spells.
