facts.detect: The bot will notice the mumak's AC and MR scores when checking its stats.
facts.action: The bot should prioritize using sleep or poison spells to immobilize the mumak before engaging in combat.

facts.fact: Mumakil are hostile and can deal large amounts of damage, especially with their headbutt attack.
facts.detect: The bot will encounter a hostile mumak on the map.
facts.action: The bot should avoid melee combat and use ranged weapons or spells to attack the mumak from a distance.

facts.fact: Mumakil are the only quadruped to be chaotic and are herbivorous, thick-skinned, and strong.
facts.detect: The bot will see the mumak's chaotic alignment and herbivorous nature when checking its stats.
facts.action: The bot should not attempt to use food or plants as weapons against the mumak.

facts.fact: Mumakil take no damage from kicking or bullwhips.
facts.detect: The bot will notice that its kicking or bullwhip attacks do no damage to the mumak.
facts.action: The bot should avoid using kicking or bullwhip attacks against the mumak and use other weapons or spells instead.

facts.fact: A nalfeshnee has a difficulty level of 15 and is generated in Gehennom and Moloch's Sanctum.
facts.detect: Encountering a nalfeshnee in Gehennom or Moloch's Sanctum.
facts.action: Avoid or prepare for a fight with a nalfeshnee if in Gehennom or Moloch's Sanctum.

facts.fact: Nalfeshnees have fire resistance, poison resistance, and drain resistance.
facts.detect: Attempting to use fire, poison, or drain attacks on a nalfeshnee.
facts.action: Use other forms of attack such as physical or magical attacks that are not fire, poison, or drain.

facts.fact: Nalfeshnees can cast monster spells and summon nasties, curse items, and aggravate other monsters.
facts.detect: Observing a nalfeshnee casting a spell or noticing other monsters becoming hostile.
facts.action: Be prepared for unexpected monster attacks and try to avoid or neutralize the nalfeshnee's spellcasting.

facts.fact: Nalfeshnees are always generated hostile and can be generated in small groups.
facts.detect: Encountering multiple nalfeshnees at once.
facts.action: Retreat or prepare for a difficult fight if multiple nalfeshnees are encountered.

facts.fact: A nalfeshnee never leaves a corpse upon death.
facts.detect: Killing a nalfeshnee and not finding a corpse.
facts.action: Do not expect to gain a corpse or any items from a nalfeshnee upon defeating it.

facts.fact: Nalzok is a unique major demon who guards the Bell of Opening and the Priest quest artifact, The Mitre of Holiness.
facts.detect: Nalzok, Bell of Opening, The Mitre of Holiness
facts.action: Avoid taking the Mitre of Holiness until you are ready to fight Nalzok.

facts.fact: Nalzok is covetous and capable of warping, will pick up any items he comes across, and desires the Priest's quest artifact.
facts.detect: Nalzok picks up items, especially the Mitre of Holiness
facts.action: Keep the Mitre of Holiness away from Nalzok until you are ready to fight him.

facts.fact: Nalzok has two strong weapon attacks, the ability to cast mage monster spells, and a claw attack that can steal back the quest artifact if the hero has taken it.
facts.detect: Nalzok's weapon and spell attacks, claw attack
facts.action: Be prepared with high AC and magic resistance, and have a blessed and enchanted artifact weapon or silver weapon.

facts.fact: Nalzok is generated on one of two squares within his lair in the center of the Priest quest goal level, with The Mitre of Holiness underneath.
facts.detect: Lair in the center of the Priest quest goal level
facts.action: Find and prepare for Nalzok in his lair before taking the Mitre of Holiness.

facts.fact: An AC of around -15 with a source of magic resistance is advisable, as is the usual strategy of standing on/blocking/teleporting to the upstair, then awakening and engaging Nalzok there.
facts.detect: Nalzok's lair, upstair
facts.action: Prepare for battle with high AC and magic resistance, and use the upstair to your advantage.

facts.fact: Nazgul have a breath attack that causes sleep (2d25).
facts.detect: The Nazgul uses its breath attack, and the bot feels very sleepy.
facts.action: Ensure the bot has resistance to sleep before encountering Nazgul.

facts.fact: Nazgul are generated with cursed rings of invisibility.
facts.detect: The bot finds a cursed ring of invisibility on the ground.
facts.action: Disarm the cursed ring of invisibility to avoid being stuck invisible.

facts.fact: Nazgul are generated with a knife and long sword.
facts.detect: The bot sees a Nazgul wielding a knife and long sword.
facts.action: Be prepared to fight with weapons that can parry or block.

facts.fact: Nazgul are undead and have a life-draining weapon attack.
facts.detect: The bot notices the Nazgul attacking with a draining weapon.
facts.action: Equip items that resist draining attacks.

facts.fact: Only nine Nazgul will be generated in any given game.
facts.detect: The bot encounters the ninth Nazgul.
facts.action: Be cautious as no more Nazgul will appear after the ninth.

facts.fact: Neanderthals are always generated peaceful and with a club and leather armor.
facts.detect: A peaceful neanderthal with a club and leather armor
facts.action: Avoid attacking peaceful neanderthals to prevent alignment and luck penalties, as well as angering your god.

facts.fact: Killing a peaceful quest guardian (like a neanderthal) will cause a -4 luck penalty and anger the hero's god.
facts.detect: Killing a peaceful neanderthal
facts.action: Avoid killing peaceful neanderthals to maintain luck and alignment.

facts.fact: Neanderthals are quest guardians and are generated in the college of the Archeologist quest home level.
facts.detect: Entering the college of the Archeologist quest home level
facts.action: Be cautious around neanderthals in this area as they are quest guardians.

facts.fact: Neanderthals have a single weapon attack that is slightly stronger than those of most quest guardians.
facts.detect: Neanderthal attacking with a club
facts.action: Be prepared for a slightly stronger attack when fighting neanderthals.

facts.fact: Neanderthals are not randomly generated and are not a valid genocide target.
facts.detect: Attempting to genocide neanderthals
facts.action: Do not attempt to genocide neanderthals as it is not possible.

facts.fact: Neferet the Green is a unique monster generated as peaceful within the Lonely Tower, placed on a throne in the largest room.
facts.detect: Upon entering the Lonely Tower, the bot will see Neferet the Green on a throne in the largest room.
facts.action: Avoid engaging Neferet the Green until the bot is prepared for a strong fight, as she is peaceful and can be negotiated with or bypassed.

facts.fact: Neferet the Green is always generated with a +5 quarterstaff and a +5 elven cloak.
facts.detect: Upon engaging Neferet the Green, the bot will see her wielding a +5 quarterstaff and wearing a +5 elven cloak.
facts.action: Stealthily take the +5 quarterstaff and +5 elven cloak if possible, as they are powerful items.

facts.fact: Neferet the Green has a strong weapon attack and will attempt to cast two mage monster spells during each of her turns.
facts.detect: During combat, the bot will see Neferet the Green attacking with a weapon and casting spells.
facts.action: Focus on dodging her attacks and spells, and use ranged attacks or magic to keep distance.

facts.fact: Neferet the Green's monster spells use 8-sided dice rather than the 6-sided one used with most other spellcasting attacks.
facts.detect: During combat, the bot will notice unusually strong spell damage.
facts.action: Prioritize using magic resistance or protection from magic to mitigate the stronger spell damage.

facts.fact: Eating a newt's corpse or tin has a 2/3 chance of raising your current power by 1d3 points, and will always do so if it is less than or equal to 2/3 of your maximum power - if this increase would raise you above your total maximum power, there is a 3/10 chance of increasing your maximum and current power by 1.
facts.detect: Newt corpse or tin
facts.action: Eat newt corpse or tin to boost energy if needed, especially if your current power is less than or equal to 2/3 of your maximum power.

facts.fact: Newts are primarily a minor nuisance for a starting character unless you are especially weak.
facts.detect: Encountering newts early in the game
facts.action: Kill newts to gain experience and items, but prioritize other threats if you are well-armed and armored.

facts.fact: Non-neutral players should kill newts themselves to raise their alignment record early on for the protection racket or conducts that require frequent prayer.
facts.detect: Being a non-neutral player
facts.action: Kill newts yourself to raise alignment if you are a non-neutral player and need to avoid killing co-aligned monsters.

facts.fact: Newts are amphibious and can swim.
facts.detect: Encountering newts in water
facts.action: Be prepared to fight newts in water if you are not a swimmer.

facts.fact: Newt corpses and tins provide a means of boosting your maximum energy early.
facts.detect: Finding newt corpses or tins
facts.action: Use newt corpses or tins to boost your energy early in the game.

facts.fact: Ninjas are generated exclusively on the Samurai quest floors and are not randomly generated elsewhere.
facts.detect: Encountering ninjas only on specific quest levels.
facts.action: Be cautious and prepared for ninjas when entering the Samurai quest levels.

facts.fact: Ninjas are always generated with a melee weapon and a set of projectiles, with a 3/4 chance of being a short sword and shuriken respectively.
facts.detect: Finding a ninja with a short sword and shuriken.
facts.action: Steal or disarm the ninja's weapons if possible to reduce its combat effectiveness.

facts.fact: Ninjas are strong humans that can be seen via infravision.
facts.detect: Using infravision to spot ninjas in dark areas.
facts.action: Equip infravision items or spells to detect ninjas in dark environments.

facts.fact: Ninjas are hostile and generated on specific quest levels.
facts.detect: Encountering ninjas on the Samurai quest levels.
facts.action: Avoid or prepare for combat with ninjas when entering these levels.

facts.fact: Ninjas are an excellent source of shuriken for Samurai.
facts.detect: Finding a ninja carrying shuriken.
facts.action: Steal or take shuriken from ninjas for use as a weapon or for trading.

facts.fact: The Norn is a unique monster generated as peaceful in the Shrine of Destiny, the Valkyrie quest home level.
facts.detect: The Norn is a huge, strong, female humanoid with cold resistance, located in the center of the Shrine of Destiny with a chest east of her.
facts.action: Approach the Norn to start the Valkyrie quest and gain entrance to the Shrine of Destiny.

facts.fact: The Norn is always generated with +5 banded mail and a +4 long sword.
facts.detect: Upon encountering the Norn, the bot will see her wearing +5 banded mail and wielding a +4 long sword.
facts.action: Do not attack the Norn as she is peaceful and valuable as a quest guardian. If the bot is underprepared, avoid combat and retreat.

facts.fact: If the hero reaches a square adjacent to the Norn with very fast speed and chats to her, but they have not yet gained entrance to the Quest, then she will begin moving around the quest level and run the risk of stepping on a fire trap hidden in the ice.
facts.detect: The bot approaches the Norn and initiates a chat.
facts.action: Avoid initiating a chat with the Norn until the bot is ready to start the quest and has explored the level to avoid fire traps.

facts.fact: A nurse's claw attack can heal the hero if the hero is unarmored, empty-handed, and not generating conflict.
facts.detect: The message 'Relax, this won't hurt a bit.' or 'The nurse hits! (I hope you don't mind.)'
facts.action: Disrobe and disarm to allow the nurse to heal instead of damaging.

facts.fact: Eating a nurse corpse or tin has a 73% chance of granting poison resistance and will always fully restore HP while curing blindness.
facts.detect: Finding a nurse corpse or tin.
facts.action: Eat the nurse corpse or tin to restore HP and gain poison resistance.

facts.fact: If you are a Healer, the nurse's attacks will not damage you regardless of if you are wielding a weapon.
facts.detect: Being a Healer and seeing a nurse attack.
facts.action: Allow the nurse to attack to be healed.

facts.fact: A nurse has a 1/3 chance of teleporting away after healing, or becoming scared on non-teleport levels.
facts.detect: A nurse healing and then disappearing.
facts.action: Continue exploring as the nurse may reappear later.

facts.fact: Tinning a nurse corpse is a good idea for late game and ascension runs as tins of nurse meat are comparable major sources of healing.
facts.detect: Finding a nurse corpse and having a tinning kit.
facts.action: Tin the nurse corpse for later use.

facts.fact: Ochre jellies have an engulfing attack that covers the target in acidic slime and a passive acid attack that has a 1/2 chance of triggering when attacked in melee.
facts.detect: The bot will notice the engulfing attack when the message 'You feel slimy!' appears, and the passive acid attack when the message 'You feel a burning sensation!' appears.
facts.action: The bot should avoid melee combat with ochre jellies and use ranged attacks or disposable projectiles to defeat them. If melee combat is unavoidable, the bot should ensure it has acid resistance (e.g., yellow dragon scales or scale mail) and erosion-proofed weapons.

facts.fact: Being splashed by the passive acid can corrode the bot's armor and weapons, with a 1/30 chance for armor and a 1/6 chance for certain weapons.
facts.detect: The bot will detect this when the message 'Your [armor or weapon] corrodes!' appears.
facts.action: The bot should avoid melee combat with ochre jellies and ensure it has acid resistance and erosion-proofed weapons and armor.

facts.fact: Eating an ochre jelly corpse or tin cures stoning on the first bite.
facts.detect: The bot will detect this when the message 'You feel less stony.' appears after eating an ochre jelly corpse or tin.
facts.action: The bot should eat an ochre jelly corpse or tin if it is stoned or at risk of stoning.

facts.fact: A wand of digging or the dig spell can free the bot from an engulfing ochre jelly and reduce its HP to 1.
facts.detect: The bot will detect this when the message 'You dig out of the slime!' appears.
facts.action: The bot should use a wand of digging or cast the dig spell if it is engulfed by an ochre jelly.

facts.fact: Ochre jellies are randomly generated hostile and can be created by a hostile monster casting the summon nasties spell.
facts.detect: The bot will detect this when it encounters an ochre jelly or receives the message 'A nasty monster appears!'
facts.action: The bot should avoid or prepare for encounters with ochre jellies, especially if it is in an area where hostile monsters might cast summon nasties.

facts.fact: An ogre has a single weapon attack and can be generated with a club (11/12 chance) or a battle-axe (1/12 chance).
facts.detect: Upon encountering an ogre, the bot can notice if the ogre is wielding a club or battle-axe.
facts.action: If the ogre is wielding a club, the bot should prioritize attacking it from a distance with projectiles or wands, as clubs are less dangerous than battle-axes.

facts.fact: Ogres can generate with gold and offensive, defensive, and miscellaneous items.
facts.detect: Upon killing an ogre, the bot can check the inventory for gold and items.
facts.action: The bot should loot any gold and useful items from the ogre's corpse.

facts.fact: Ogres have infravision and can be seen via infravision.
facts.detect: The bot can detect infravision in its status or inventory.
facts.action: If the bot has infravision, it can use it to detect and avoid or confront ogres.

facts.fact: Ogres are generated in small groups of two to four and can grow up into ogre lords.
facts.detect: The bot can detect multiple ogres appearing together or a single ogre growing larger.
facts.action: The bot should be cautious and prepare for multiple ogres or a stronger ogre lord.

facts.fact: Ogres are a good source of loot for Barbarians on their quest, including wands.
facts.detect: The bot can detect wands in the inventory after killing an ogre.
facts.action: The bot should prioritize looting wands and other useful items from ogres, especially on the Barbarian quest.

facts.fact: An ogre king has a single weapon attack and can move faster than a hero without speed, with a weapon attack of 3d5 physical damage and an MR score of 60.
facts.detect: Encountering an ogre king on the map or in a throne room on dungeon level 9 or deeper.
facts.action: Avoid direct confrontation if possible, especially if the bot is not well-equipped or has not yet reached the mid-game stage. Use ranged attacks or spells if available to weaken the ogre king before engaging.

facts.fact: Ogre kings can be generated with gold, a club (2/3 chance) or a battle-axe (1/3 chance), and can generate with offensive, defensive, and miscellaneous items, with weapons at least +1.
facts.detect: Finding an ogre king with a club or battle-axe, or with other items.
facts.action: If the bot is well-equipped and prepared, attempt to steal or take the +1 weapon from the ogre king if it is a battle-axe, as it can be very useful.

facts.fact: Hostile ogre kings can occupy the throne of a throne room generated at dungeon level 9 or deeper.
facts.detect: Entering a throne room on dungeon level 9 or deeper and finding an ogre king there.
facts.action: Be cautious and prepare for a tough fight if an ogre king is encountered in a throne room, especially if the bot is not well-equipped.

facts.fact: Ogre kings can be generated by the summon nasties monster spell.
facts.detect: Encountering a group of nasties that includes an ogre king.
facts.action: Avoid or prepare for a group fight if an ogre king is part of a summoned group of nasties, as it can be dangerous.

facts.fact: Ogre kings can appear among the random O that are part of the first quest monster class for Barbarians.
facts.detect: Encountering an ogre king during the Barbarian quest.
facts.action: Treat the encounter with caution, especially if the bot is not well-equipped or prepared for a tough fight.

facts.fact: Ogre lords have a single weapon attack dealing 2d6 physical damage.
facts.detect: Ogre lord symbol on the map
facts.action: Prepare for a melee combat with a weapon or spell that can deal physical damage.

facts.fact: Ogre lords can be generated with a club (5/6 chance) or a battle-axe (1/6 chance).
facts.detect: Picking up a club or battle-axe from an ogre lord's corpse
facts.action: Equip the weapon if it is better than the current one and you have the strength to wield it.

facts.fact: Ogre lords can generate with gold and have a small chance of generating with a wand of death.
facts.detect: Finding gold or a wand of death on an ogre lord's corpse
facts.action: Collect the gold and be cautious with the wand of death, as it can be dangerous if used improperly.

facts.fact: Ogre lords can appear among a group of ogres if one of them generates with a potion of gain level.
facts.detect: Encountering a group of ogres with an ogre lord
facts.action: Be prepared for a larger battle and possibly retreat if outnumbered.

facts.fact: Ogre lords have an MR score of 30, which can potentially resist effects from spells and wands.
facts.detect: Using a spell or wand on an ogre lord without effect
facts.action: Switch to melee combat or use a different spell or wand that is not resisted.

facts.fact: Olog-hai have an AC of -4 and hit just as hard as rock trolls, but move just as fast.
facts.detect: Encounter with an Olog-hai on the map
facts.action: Use ranged attacks, spells, or pets to avoid close combat due to their high AC and fast movement.

facts.fact: Olog-hai have a 2/175 chance of generating with a polearm (ranseur, partisan, glaive, or spetum).
facts.detect: Olog-hai carrying one of the mentioned polearms
facts.action: Steal or disarm the polearm if possible, as it can be a powerful weapon.

facts.fact: Olog-hai can regenerate from their corpses like other trolls.
facts.detect: Killing an Olog-hai and seeing its corpse
facts.action: Dispose of the corpse by stoning, feeding it to a carnivorous pet, or locking it in a chest to prevent regeneration.

facts.fact: Olog-hai can be generated in throne rooms and by looting a throne while confused.
facts.detect: Entering a throne room or looting a throne while confused
facts.action: Be cautious and prepared for Olog-hai encounters in these areas.

facts.fact: Olog-hai have no elemental resistances and no MR score.
facts.detect: Encounter with an Olog-hai
facts.action: Use magic spells like sleep or slow to weaken them before engaging in combat.

facts.fact: The Oracle is a unique human that can be seen via infravision and is completely sessile.
facts.detect: The Oracle is a peaceful, female, humanoid monster with the symbol 'O' and can only be seen with infravision.
facts.action: Approach the Oracle with gold in inventory to consult her for game information and experience points.

facts.fact: The Oracle offers two types of consultations: minor and major, which can be bought with gold.
facts.detect: The player has gold in inventory and encounters the Oracle on her special level.
facts.action: Buy consultations from the Oracle to gain experience points and learn game information.

facts.fact: Angering the Oracle will prevent a character from buying consultations until she is pacified.
facts.detect: The Oracle is hostile and the player tries to talk to her.
facts.action: Avoid angering the Oracle and keep pets away from her to prevent her from becoming hostile.

facts.fact: If the Oracle is killed, consultations become inaccessible for the rest of the game unless she is brought back to life.
facts.detect: The Oracle is killed by any means.
facts.action: Avoid killing the Oracle unless absolutely necessary, as it will prevent future consultations.

facts.fact: The Oracle has a passive magic missile attack that only triggers if the player character attacks her in melee.
facts.detect: The player attacks the Oracle in melee and receives a magic missile attack.
facts.action: Avoid melee combat with the Oracle to prevent taking damage from her passive attack.

facts.fact: Orange dragons have a breath weapon that puts affected monsters to sleep for 4-100 turns.
facts.detect: The bot will see the message 'You feel drowsy.' or 'The orange dragon breathes sleep gas.'
facts.action: If the bot encounters an orange dragon, it should prioritize obtaining sleep resistance (e.g., by eating an orange dragon corpse or tin) before engaging the dragon.

facts.fact: Orange dragons have a 3/1 chance of dropping a set of uncursed +0 orange dragon scales upon death.
facts.detect: The bot will see the message 'You find a set of uncursed +0 orange dragon scales.'
facts.action: The bot should pick up the orange dragon scales as they provide sleep resistance and can be used to make scale mail.

facts.fact: Orange dragons are generated in throne rooms at dungeon levels 15 and below.
facts.detect: The bot will encounter an orange dragon in a throne room at level 15 or below.
facts.action: The bot should be cautious and prepared for an orange dragon encounter in such areas, especially if it lacks sleep resistance.

facts.fact: Orange dragons are hostile and can be generated by the summon nasties monster spell.
facts.detect: The bot will see the message 'A nasty monster appears!' followed by the appearance of an orange dragon.
facts.action: The bot should avoid using the summon nasties spell and be prepared to deal with hostile orange dragons.

facts.fact: Orange dragons have a 20/1 chance of dropping a set of uncursed +0 orange dragon scales if the dragon was revived.
facts.detect: The bot will see the message 'You find a set of uncursed +0 orange dragon scales.' after reviving an orange dragon.
facts.action: The bot should prioritize picking up the scales if it has the opportunity to revive an orange dragon.

facts.fact: Orcs have a 1/2 chance of generating with an orcish helm.
facts.detect: orcish helm
facts.action: Pick up orcish helm if found, as it can be useful for protection.

facts.fact: Orcs have a 1/2 chance of being given an orcish dagger or a scimitar.
facts.detect: orcish dagger or scimitar
facts.action: Pick up orcish dagger or scimitar if found, as they can be better weapons than default ones.

facts.fact: Orcs can grow up to become orc-captains.
facts.detect: orc-captain
facts.action: Be more cautious when encountering orc-captains as they are stronger than regular orcs.

facts.fact: An orc zombie or orc mummy will leave an aged orc corpse behind upon death.
facts.detect: aged orc corpse
facts.action: Avoid orc zombies and mummies to prevent getting aged orc corpses which may not be useful.

facts.fact: Pursuing any orcs you encounter during a game with Orcish Town is generally a good idea in order to nab the candles and gloves they may be carrying.
facts.detect: Orcish Town
facts.action: Explore Orcish Town and pursue orcs to find candles and gloves.

facts.fact: An orc mummy has a single claw attack that deals 1d6 damage.
facts.detect: orc mummy
facts.action: Avoid or prepare to fight orc mummies, as they can deal significant damage.

facts.fact: Orc mummies have a 6/7 chance of being generated with a mummy wrapping.
facts.detect: mummy wrapping
facts.action: If you find a mummy wrapping, it likely came from an orc mummy. Be cautious as you may encounter one nearby.

facts.fact: An orc mummy leaves behind an aged orc corpse upon death.
facts.detect: aged orc corpse
facts.action: Eat aged orc corpses for nutrition if you are hungry and have no better food options.

facts.fact: Orc mummies are always hostile and randomly generated.
facts.detect: orc mummy
facts.action: Be prepared to fight orc mummies when you encounter them.

facts.fact: Orc mummies are part of the second quest monster class for Archeologists and make up 6/175 of randomly generated monsters on the Archeologist quest.
facts.detect: orc mummy in a quest level
facts.action: Be extra cautious when exploring levels related to the Archeologist quest, as orc mummies may be present.

facts.fact: Orc shamans have poison resistance.
facts.detect: Poison resistance
facts.action: Be cautious of poison attacks or items when fighting orc shamans.

facts.fact: Orc shamans can cast spells such as psi bolt, cure self, haste self, and sometimes stun.
facts.detect: Spells being cast
facts.action: Avoid getting stunned and be ready to counteract haste self.

facts.fact: Orc shamans have a 50% chance of generating with an orcish helm.
facts.detect: Orcish helm
facts.action: Loot orcish helm if available and useful.

facts.fact: Orc shamans are generated near the desecrated temple in Orcish Town.
facts.detect: Desecrated temple
facts.action: Be cautious when exploring areas near desecrated temples.

facts.fact: Orc shaman corpses are a good source of nutrition.
facts.detect: Orc shaman corpse
facts.action: Eat orc shaman corpse to gain nutrition.

facts.fact: Orc zombies have a single claw attack that deals 1d6 damage.
facts.detect: Orc zombie icon or name
facts.action: Attack orc zombies with weapons or spells that deal damage effectively.

facts.fact: Orc zombies are always hostile and may appear in groups of 2 to 4.
facts.detect: Multiple orc zombie icons or names
facts.action: Be prepared for multiple orc zombies and have a strategy to handle them, such as using ranged attacks or spells.

facts.fact: Orc zombies leave an aged orc corpse upon death.
facts.detect: Aged orc corpse
facts.action: Convert aged orc corpses on cross-aligned altars or use them to summon demons on co-aligned altars.

facts.fact: Orc zombies cannot use items of any kind.
facts.detect: Orc zombie attempting to pick up an item
facts.action: Exploit orc zombies' inability to use items by dropping useful items in their path.

facts.fact: Orc zombies have resistances to cold, sleep, and poison.
facts.detect: Orc zombie resisting cold, sleep, or poison effects
facts.action: Use fire-based attacks or other non-cold, non-sleep, non-poison attacks against orc zombies.

facts.fact: An orc-captain has two weapon attacks and possesses poison resistance.
facts.detect: Encounter with an orc-captain or seeing the message 'You see an orc-captain.'
facts.action: Ensure you have poison resistance before engaging, either through potions, scrolls, or by wearing a ring of resistance.

facts.fact: Orc-captains have a roughly 1/2 chance of being generated with an orcish helm and may have Mordor orc or Uruk-hai equipment.
facts.detect: Upon encountering an orc-captain, check if it is wearing an orcish helm or carrying Mordor orc or Uruk-hai equipment.
facts.action: Be cautious if the orc-captain has a helm or equipment, as it may indicate better armor and weapons.

facts.fact: Orc-captains may appear among the hostile 'o' that generate in throne rooms.
facts.detect: Entering a throne room and seeing hostile orcs.
facts.action: Be prepared for the possibility of encountering an orc-captain in throne rooms.

facts.fact: Orc-captains have a roughly 1/2 chance of being generated with an orcish helm and may have Mordor orc or Uruk-hai equipment.
facts.detect: Upon encountering an orc-captain, check if it is wearing an orcish helm or carrying Mordor orc or Uruk-hai equipment.
facts.action: If the orc-captain has orcish arrows, be cautious of poison attacks.

facts.fact: Orc-captains may be best engaged at a distance unless their inventory contains an orcish bow and poisoned arrows.
facts.detect: Seeing an orc-captain with an orcish bow and poisoned arrows.
facts.action: Engage from a distance if possible, or ensure you have poison resistance.

facts.fact: Orcus is a unique monster with a difficulty of 36 and generates meditating on the down stair of his lair in Gehennom at level creation.
facts.detect: Orcus meditating on the down stair in Orcus-town
facts.action: Avoid fighting Orcus directly if not prepared, or block the up stair to prevent his escape

facts.fact: Orcus has a wand of death and can cast the touch of death spell, both of which can instadeath heroes without magic resistance.
facts.detect: Orcus using wand of death or casting touch of death
facts.action: Gain magic resistance before confronting Orcus

facts.fact: Orcus can summon major demons, including Demogorgon, which is often a reason to kill Orcus quickly.
facts.detect: Orcus summoning major demons
facts.action: Kill Orcus before he can summon Demogorgon

facts.fact: Orcus is covetous and will pick up weapons, food, and other items he comes across.
facts.detect: Orcus picking up items
facts.action: Avoid letting Orcus pick up important items

facts.fact: Orcus never leaves a corpse upon death, making it impossible to gain experience or items from him.
facts.detect: Orcus dying without leaving a corpse
facts.action: Ensure Orcus is killed to prevent him from summoning demons or using his wand

facts.fact: Orion is a unique monster with a difficulty level of 24, generated as peaceful on the Ranger quest home level.
facts.detect: Orion is always generated as peaceful and is located in the central square of the grove section of the Ranger quest home level.
facts.action: Avoid combat with Orion if not ready for a high-level fight. If necessary, prepare for a tough battle with high-level equipment and spells.

facts.fact: Orion is equipped with +5 leather armor, a +4 yumi, and 50 +4 ya.
facts.detect: Upon encountering Orion, the bot should notice his equipped items.
facts.action: Steal or destroy Orion's equipment if possible to weaken him before or during combat.

facts.fact: Orion has a weapon attack of 4d10 physical damage and can cast one mage monster spell per turn.
facts.detect: During combat, the bot should observe Orion's attack patterns.
facts.action: Use defensive tactics and magic resistance to mitigate Orion's spellcasting and physical attacks.

facts.fact: Orion has infravision and can see invisible, making him a formidable opponent.
facts.detect: Orion's ability to see invisible is noted in his attributes.
facts.action: Avoid using隐形效果，因为奥里昂可以看到隐形。在与奥里昂战斗时，使用防御性策略和魔法抗性来减轻他的施法和物理攻击。

facts.fact: An owlbear has two claw attacks and a grabbing attack that holds you in place and crushes you each turn.
facts.detect: The owlbear's grabbing attack is indicated by the message 'The owlbear grabs you!' or similar.
facts.action: Equip greased outer body armor or a non-cursed oilskin cloak to prevent the owlbear from grabbing you.

facts.fact: Owlbears can move at the same speed as an unburdened character without a speed boost.
facts.detect: The owlbear moves in the same turn you do.
facts.action: Use ranged attacks, such as spells or wands, to weaken the owlbear from a distance before engaging in melee.

facts.fact: Owlbears can be scared into letting go of you, or teleportation can free you from their grasp.
facts.detect: You are grabbed by an owlbear.
facts.action: Use a tool to scare the owlbear or teleport yourself free.

facts.fact: Owlbears are generated hostile and can be found randomly in the dungeon.
facts.detect: An owlbear appears on the map.
facts.action: Avoid or prepare for combat with owlbears, especially early in the game.

facts.fact: Owlbear corpses are filling and can be left for meat-eating pets.
facts.detect: You kill an owlbear and see its corpse.
facts.action: Eat the corpse yourself or leave it for your pets.

facts.fact: Pages are quest guardians for the Knight quest and are always peaceful when generated.
facts.detect: Encountering a peaceful humanoid with the name 'Page' in King Arthur's main room.
facts.action: Avoid attacking the page unless necessary, as doing so will anger the hero's god and cause a -4 luck penalty.

facts.fact: Pages have two weapon attacks and are strong and omnivorous.
facts.detect: Seeing a page in combat with weapon attacks.
facts.action: Prepare for a stronger combat encounter with a page, as it can deal significant damage.

facts.fact: Pages are generated with a melee weapon, armor, and possibly boots, cloak, and bow.
facts.detect: Finding a page equipped with a long sword, chain mail, and other items.
facts.action: Steal or pick up the page's equipment if possible to improve the bot's gear.

facts.fact: Pages can grow up into player monster knights.
facts.detect: Noticing a page in the game.
facts.action: Do not kill the page unless necessary, as it can potentially grow into a stronger enemy.

facts.fact: Killing a peaceful quest guardian like a page will anger the quest leader and other quest guardians.
facts.detect: Killing a page and seeing other quest guardians become angry.
facts.action: Avoid killing the page to prevent angering other quest guardians and the quest leader.

facts.fact: Panther has two claw attacks and a bite attack, dealing 1d4, 1d4, and 1d10 physical damage respectively.
facts.detect: Panther symbol on the map
facts.action: Avoid engaging panthers if not well-equipped or at low health.

facts.fact: Panthers are hostile and have infravision, allowing them to see in the dark.
facts.detect: Panther symbol on the map in dark areas
facts.action: Use light sources or avoid dark areas to prevent encounters with panthers.

facts.fact: Panthers have a speed of 15, which is relatively high.
facts.detect: Panther symbol moving quickly on the map
facts.action: Be cautious of panthers' speed and plan escape routes or combat strategies accordingly.

facts.fact: Panthers have an AC of 6, making them moderately tough to hit.
facts.detect: Panther symbol on the map
facts.action: Equip weapons and armor that can effectively damage and protect against panthers.

facts.fact: Panthers are large and weigh 600 units, providing 300 nutrition when eaten.
facts.detect: Panther corpse on the map
facts.action: Eat panther corpses for nutrition if starving and no better food is available.

facts.fact: Paper golems have 20 HP and are always generated hostile.
facts.detect: Hostile paper golem appears on the map with the symbol ' (white).
facts.action: Use fire-based attacks to instantly destroy paper golems if encountered.

facts.fact: Paper golems leave behind 1-4 scrolls of blank paper upon death, unless burnt up completely by fire damage.
facts.detect: Upon killing a paper golem, the bot should check for scrolls of blank paper on the ground.
facts.action: Collect scrolls of blank paper for later use in writing other scrolls with a magic marker.

facts.fact: Fire damage can completely destroy a paper golem.
facts.detect: Message ' burns completely!' or 'You smell burning paper.' when a paper golem is hit by fire.
facts.action: Use fire-based attacks to destroy paper golems instantly.

facts.fact: A hero polymorphed into a paper golem can burn up and return to normal form if hit by fire damage.
facts.detect: Message ' burns completely!' or 'You smell burning paper.' when polymorphed into a paper golem and hit by fire.
facts.action: Avoid fire damage if polymorphed into a paper golem.

facts.fact: Paper golems can generate as a result of polypiling if there are enough paper objects in a pile of items.
facts.detect: Polypiling a pile of items with enough paper objects.
facts.action: Be cautious when polypiling as paper golems can be generated.

facts.fact: Pelias is a unique monster with difficulty 24, level 20, and 583 experience points.
facts.detect: Pelias
facts.action: Avoid engaging Pelias directly unless at a significantly higher level or with powerful equipment.

facts.fact: Pelias is always generated as peaceful and is located on the throne in the left half of the Barbarian quest's home level.
facts.detect: A peaceful Pelias on a throne in the Barbarian quest level.
facts.action: Explore the Barbarian quest level carefully to locate Pelias and avoid accidental combat.

facts.fact: Pelias is generated with +5 chain mail and a +5 runesword.
facts.detect: A peaceful Pelias with +5 chain mail and a +5 runesword.
facts.action: Stealthily approach Pelias to loot his +5 chain mail and +5 runesword if possible.

facts.fact: Pelias has intrinsic poison resistance.
facts.detect: Pelias
facts.action: Be prepared for Pelias's attacks if combat is unavoidable.

facts.fact: Pelias cannot be genocided or polymorphed.
facts.detect: Pelias
facts.action: Do not waste time or resources trying to genocide or polymorph Pelias.

facts.fact: Pestilence is a unique monster with teleport control and can revive from its corpse after being destroyed with a 1/3 chance each turn.
facts.detect: Message 'A monster tried to digest Pestilence and immediately died.' or seeing Pestilence revive after its corpse is destroyed.
facts.action: Avoid eating Pestilence's corpse and ensure its corpse is destroyed permanently (e.g., by applying a tinning kit or pushing a boulder onto it).

facts.fact: Pestilence's touch attacks deal damage and inflict disease, and a second successful hit will stun the hero.
facts.detect: Being hit by Pestilence's touch attack and feeling sick or being stunned.
facts.action: Use ranged attacks or spells to avoid melee combat and carry a cure for disease.

facts.fact: Pestilence is generated on the Astral Plane with potions of sickness and is always hostile.
facts.detect: Entering the Astral Plane and seeing Pestilence in the center of a round room.
facts.action: Quickly deal with Pestilence using high-damage ranged attacks or wands of death.

facts.fact: Pestilence has many resistances and is healed by potions of sickness and damaged by potions of healing.
facts.detect: Pestilence drinking a potion of sickness or being hit by a potion of healing.
facts.action: Avoid using healing potions on Pestilence and carry potions of sickness to weaken it.

facts.fact: Eating Pestilence's corpse is instantly fatal and will revive Pestilence.
facts.detect: Seeing Pestilence's corpse and considering eating it.
facts.action: Destroy Pestilence's corpse immediately and avoid eating it.

facts.fact: Piranha difficulty is 7 and has a bite attack dealing 2d6 damage twice.
facts.detect: Piranha (symbol: 'P')
facts.action: Avoid or kill piranha if in water, especially in moats or rivers.

facts.fact: Piranha are generated in pools of swamps, rivers, and moats surrounding the Wizard of Yendor's dwelling.
facts.detect: Swamp pool, river, moat surrounding Wizard of Yendor's dwelling
facts.action: Be cautious when entering these areas, especially if not prepared for water combat.

facts.fact: Piranha are not randomly generated but are always hostile when created.
facts.detect: Piranha appearing in water bodies
facts.action: Prepare for combat or avoid water bodies if not ready to fight piranha.

facts.fact: Piranha have a swimming speed of 18 and are amphibious.
facts.detect: Piranha moving quickly in water
facts.action: Use ranged attacks or magic if possible to avoid close combat.

facts.fact: Piranha are generated in specific numbers in certain areas (e.g., 2 in Tourist quest home level river, 2 in Wizard's Tower moat, 4 on Plane of Water).
facts.detect: Entering these specific levels or areas
facts.action: Prepare for multiple piranha encounters in these areas.

facts.fact: Pit fiends generate YAFM (You Are F***ed Moment) when falling into pits or spiked pits.
facts.detect: How pitiful. Isn't that the pits?
facts.action: Avoid falling into pits or spiked pits to prevent YAFM.

facts.fact: Pit fiends are only randomly generated in Gehennom and are always created hostile.
facts.detect: Encounter in Gehennom
facts.action: Be prepared for hostile encounters in Gehennom.

facts.fact: Pit fiends have natural -3 AC and can make escaping difficult if they grab you.
facts.detect: Being grabbed by a pit fiend
facts.action: Use Elbereth to drive them off or teleport to escape.

facts.fact: Pit fiends are slow at 6 speed, allowing for kiting and teleportation tactics.
facts.detect: Pit fiend movement speed
facts.action: Kite the pit fiend or teleport to escape.

facts.fact: In Gehennom, pit fiends are less of a threat due to player's better equipment and AC.
facts.detect: Location in Gehennom
facts.action: Prepare silver weapons or cold damage methods before encountering pit fiends in Gehennom.

facts.fact: A pit viper has two poisonous bite attacks and poison resistance.
facts.detect: Encounter with a pit viper or seeing the message 'How pitiful. Isn't that the pits?'
facts.action: Avoid close combat with pit vipers until you have poison resistance. Use ranged weapons or magic to deal with them from a distance.

facts.fact: Eating a pit viper corpse or tin has a 2/5 chance of conveying poison resistance.
facts.detect: Finding a pit viper corpse or tin
facts.action: Eat a pit viper corpse or tin to potentially gain poison resistance, but be prepared for the possibility of poisoning.

facts.fact: Pit vipers generate YAFM when falling into pits or spiked pits.
facts.detect: Seeing a pit viper fall into a pit or spiked pit
facts.action: Be cautious around pits and spiked pits, especially in areas where pit vipers are likely to be found.

facts.fact: Pit vipers are part of the first quest monster class for Archeologists and make up 24/35 of the monsters on the Archeologist quest.
facts.detect: Playing as an Archeologist and encountering pit vipers on the quest
facts.action: Be prepared for pit vipers on the Archeologist quest and try to gain poison resistance early.

facts.fact: Pit vipers may generate among the random snakes on Medusa's Island and the Plane of Earth.
facts.detect: Exploring Medusa's Island or the Plane of Earth
facts.action: Be cautious and prepared for pit vipers in these areas, especially if you lack poison resistance.

facts.fact: A plains centaur has a weapon attack and a kick attack.
facts.detect: Encountering a plains centaur on the map
facts.action: Avoid melee combat if possible, use ranged attacks or spells to keep distance

facts.fact: Plains centaurs have a 2 chance of being generated with a crossbow and 3–14 crossbow bolts.
facts.detect: A plains centaur with a crossbow and bolts
facts.action: Prioritize ranged attacks to neutralize the crossbow threat

facts.fact: Four statues of plains centaurs are featured on the Oracle level.
facts.detect: Entering the Oracle level and seeing statues of plains centaurs
facts.action: Be cautious and prepared for potential hostile plains centaurs

facts.fact: Plains centaurs are the weakest among centaurs but still quite vicious due to their speed and ranged weapon likelihood.
facts.detect: Encountering a plains centaur
facts.action: Use ranged attacks or spells to avoid melee combat

facts.fact: Tame plains centaurs can be used as mounts and can equip weapons and wear limited armor.
facts.detect: Taming a plains centaur
facts.action: Equip the centaur with a crossbow and bolts for ranged attacks

facts.fact: Ponies have a 100% chance of generating with a worn saddle.
facts.detect: A pony with a saddle icon next to it.
facts.action: Steal or take the saddle from the pony if it is peaceful or tame it and ride it.

facts.fact: Ponies can be tamed with veggy food such as pears or lichen corpses.
facts.detect: A pony in the vicinity.
facts.action: Use veggy food to tame the pony and potentially ride it.

facts.fact: Pony corpses do not penalize characters for eating them.
facts.detect: A pony corpse on the ground.
facts.action: Eat the pony corpse for nutrition.

facts.fact: Ponies move fairly fast at 16 speed and attack twice during each of their turns.
facts.detect: A pony moving quickly on the map or attacking twice in combat.
facts.action: Avoid or pacify/tame the pony to prevent combat.

facts.fact: Knights start each game with a saddled pony.
facts.detect: Starting as a Knight character.
facts.action: Ride the starting pony to move faster and explore more efficiently.

facts.fact: A prisoner is a type of monster that appears in NetHack, found within jail cells at certain locations.
facts.detect: Encountering a jail cell with a prisoner inside.
facts.action: Free the prisoner to gain a +3 bonus to alignment record and potentially pacify them.

facts.fact: Freeing a prisoner from their cell pacifies them and grants a +3 bonus to the hero's alignment record.
facts.detect: Speaking to a freed prisoner who says 'I'm finally free!'
facts.action: Free prisoners to improve alignment record.

facts.fact: Prisoners are not normally seen in the dungeon and are only found within jail cells at specific locations.
facts.detect: Finding a jail cell in the dungeon.
facts.action: Explore jail cells to find and free prisoners.

facts.fact: There is generally no risk to freeing any prisoners encountered by a hero under normal circumstances.
facts.detect: Encountering a peaceful prisoner in a jail cell.
facts.action: Free the prisoner to gain alignment bonus.

facts.fact: Prisoners are generated meditating at level creation of specific quest floors, such as the Tourist quest goal level and the Wizard quest goal level.
facts.detect: Reaching the quest goal level for Tourist or Wizard.
facts.action: Free any prisoners found in jail cells to improve alignment record.

facts.fact: Purple worms have a bite attack and an engulfing attack that can potentially digest its target, leading to a delayed instadeath for the hero and instantly killing monsters that are large or below in physical size.
facts.detect: Seeing a purple worm on the map or receiving a message like 'You are engulfed by a purple worm!' or 'You feel a sudden urge to digest something.'
facts.action: Use ranged attacks to weaken or kill the purple worm before it can engulf you. If engulfed, zap a wand of digging to escape and kill the worm easily.

facts.fact: A shrieker has a 1/3 chance of summoning a purple worm with each shriek, regardless of the current difficulty level.
facts.detect: Seeing a shrieker on the map or receiving a message like 'A shrieker shrieks!' followed by 'A purple worm appears!'
facts.action: Avoid or destroy shriekers to prevent the summoning of purple worms.

facts.fact: Wearing a ring of slow digestion will prevent a purple worm from engulfing you in the first place.
facts.detect: Equipping a ring of slow digestion.
facts.action: Equip a ring of slow digestion to prevent engulfing.

facts.fact: A purple worm's MR score is 20, which can make some magic-based approaches less reliable.
facts.detect: Attempting to use magic-based attacks on a purple worm and noticing reduced effectiveness.
facts.action: Use physical attacks or ranged attacks instead of magic-based attacks.

facts.fact: Polymorphing into a purple worm allows you to dispatch elusive and powerful enemies such as the arch-lich in a single turn, but you must not swallow deadly prey such as cockatrices.
facts.detect: Polymorphing into a purple worm and encountering a powerful enemy or deadly prey.
facts.action: Use the digestion attack to dispatch powerful enemies but avoid swallowing deadly prey.

facts.fact: A pyrolisk has a gaze attack that damages any foe who makes eye contact unless the pyrolisk or the target cannot see the other party, the pyrolisk is cancelled, or the target has fire resistance.
facts.detect: The pyrolisk attacks you with a fiery gaze!
facts.action: Blind yourself or the pyrolisk to avoid the gaze attack. If you have fire resistance, approach the pyrolisk to avoid its gaze attack and then attack it.

facts.fact: The pyrolisk's gaze can burn away sliming, erode the target's worn cloth or leather armor by burning it, and can also destroy potions, scrolls and spellbooks in the target's open inventory.
facts.detect: The pyrolisk attacks you with a fiery gaze!
facts.action: Stash your potions, scrolls, and spellbooks in a container before engaging with a pyrolisk.

facts.fact: Iron golems are healed by the fiery gaze of a pyrolisk.
facts.detect: The pyrolisk attacks you with a fiery gaze!
facts.action: If polymorphed into an iron golem, the gaze attack will heal you.

facts.fact: Eating a pyrolisk corpse or tin has a 20% chance of granting fire resistance or poison resistance.
facts.detect: Eating a pyrolisk corpse or tin.
facts.action: Eat a pyrolisk corpse or tin to potentially gain fire resistance or poison resistance.

facts.fact: Pyrolisk eggs are explosive and will explode for 3d6 fire damage when eaten, thrown or otherwise broken.
facts.detect: Eating a pyrolisk egg.
facts.action: Avoid eating pyrolisk eggs.

facts.fact: A python has a bite attack, a touch attack, a holding attack that doubles as a drowning attack, and a second holding attack.
facts.detect: grabs you!
facts.action: Avoid getting grabbed by a python near water or wear greased armor/oilskin cloak to protect from holding attacks.

facts.fact: Pythons generate among the random S that are part of the first quest monster class for Archeologists and make up 24/35 of the monsters that randomly generate on the Archeologist quest.
facts.detect: S (symbol for python generation)
facts.action: Be cautious when encountering S symbols, especially if playing as an Archeologist.

facts.fact: Pythons are randomly generated hostile.
facts.detect: Hostile python appears
facts.action: Prepare to fight or avoid hostile pythons.

facts.fact: Pythons can drown heroes if they are caught near water.
facts.detect: grabs you!
facts.action: Avoid getting grabbed by a python near water.

facts.fact: Pythons use a different message for their holding attack than other drowning monsters.
facts.detect: grabs you!
facts.action: Set a MSGTYPE rule for the python's message to be reminded of the danger.

facts.fact: A quantum mechanic has a 1/5 chance of being generated with a large box.
facts.detect: Large box
facts.action: Be cautious when opening a large box, as it may contain a dangerous housecat named 'Schroedinger's Cat'.

facts.fact: Quantum mechanics can teleport the player, which can be dangerous.
facts.detect: Your position suddenly seems very uncertain!
facts.action: If you have teleport control, use it to control your destination after being teleported.

facts.fact: Eating a quantum mechanic corpse toggles intrinsic speed.
facts.detect: Your velocity suddenly seems very uncertain!
facts.action: If you need speed, eat a quantum mechanic corpse or tin to toggle intrinsic speed.

facts.fact: Quantum mechanics are hostile and can teleport you away from the stairs or into dangerous situations.
facts.detect: Being teleported by a quantum mechanic
facts.action: Avoid engaging with quantum mechanics unless necessary, especially in large open areas or near dangerous monsters.

facts.fact: Quantum mechanics can teleport pets, potentially teleporting a shopkeeper out of their shop and angering them.
facts.detect: Your pet quantum mechanic attacks a shopkeeper and teleports them out of their shop.
facts.action: Avoid sending pets to areas with shopkeepers unless you have established credit or can handle the consequences.

facts.fact: A quasit has two poisonous claw attacks that drain dexterity and a bite attack that deals physical damage.
facts.detect: Quasit, Claw attack message
facts.action: Avoid or prepare antidotes before engaging quasits to prevent dexterity drain.

facts.fact: Eating a quasit corpse or tin has a 5/7 chance of granting poison resistance.
facts.detect: Quasit corpse or tin
facts.action: Eat quasit corpse or tin to gain poison resistance.

facts.fact: Quasits have poison resistance.
facts.detect: Quasit
facts.action: Use non-poisonous attacks or items against quasits.

facts.fact: Quasits can regenerate and are infravision-capable.
facts.detect: Quasit, Infravision message
facts.action: Use weapons or spells that deal instant death or high damage to quasits.

facts.fact: Quasits are generated frequently in Knight and Wizard quests.
facts.detect: Knight or Wizard quest level
facts.action: Be cautious and prepared for quasits in these quests.

facts.fact: Queen bee has a sting attack that can inflict strength-draining poison
facts.detect: The buzzes angrily.
facts.action: Avoid or prepare antidotes and resistances before engaging

facts.fact: Queen bee corpse is poisonous to eat
facts.detect: Eating a queen bee corpse
facts.action: Do not eat queen bee corpses

facts.fact: Queen bees are found in beehives, including the guaranteed one within the Wizard's Tower
facts.detect: Entering a beehive or the Wizard's Tower
facts.action: Be cautious and prepared for a queen bee encounter

facts.fact: Queen bees have a speed of 24, the third-highest among monsters
facts.detect: Observing the speed of the queen bee
facts.action: Use fast movement or teleport to avoid or outmaneuver

facts.fact: Queen bees are accompanied by killer bees in their hive
facts.detect: Seeing killer bees in a beehive
facts.action: Use crowd control tactics to isolate and deal with the queen bee

facts.fact: A quivering blob has a single touch attack and possesses poison resistance and sleep resistance.
facts.detect: quivering blob
facts.action: Eat the corpse of a quivering blob to gain poison resistance (33% chance).

facts.fact: A quivering blob corpse is vegan-compatible and eating it has a 1/3 chance of granting poison resistance.
facts.detect: quivering blob corpse
facts.action: Eat the corpse to potentially gain poison resistance.

facts.fact: Randomly generated quivering blobs are always created hostile.
facts.detect: quivering blob
facts.action: Attack or avoid the quivering blob as necessary.

facts.fact: Quivering blobs are extremely slow-moving at 1 speed, cause fairly minor damage with their infrequent touch attacks, and lack any form of passive attack.
facts.detect: quivering blob
facts.action: Ignore or easily defeat quivering blobs.

facts.fact: In NetHack brass, the quivering blob's speed is increased to 8.
facts.detect: NetHack version
facts.action: Adjust strategy if playing NetHack brass, as quivering blobs are faster.

facts.fact: A rabid rat has a single bite attack that is poisonous and drains constitution.
facts.detect: Rabid rat
facts.action: Avoid melee combat with rabid rats unless constitution is high and a means of restoring constitution is available (e.g., unicorn horn).

facts.fact: Rabid rats are randomly generated hostile.
facts.detect: Hostile rabid rats on the map.
facts.action: Use ranged attacks or magic to kill them from a distance.

facts.fact: Rabid rats are part of the first quest monster class for Healers and appear frequently in the Healer quest.
facts.detect: Entering the Healer quest levels.
facts.action: Be cautious and prepared for multiple rabid rats.

facts.fact: Rabid rats have poison resistance.
facts.detect: Rabid rat
facts.action: Do not rely on poison attacks or weapons against them.

facts.fact: A rabid rat corpse is poisonous to eat.
facts.detect: Corpse of a rabid rat
facts.action: Do not eat the corpse.

facts.fact: Rangers are chaotic player monsters corresponding to a Ranger hero and will have the role's appropriate rank title for their monster level.
facts.detect: Encounter a ranger with a chaotic alignment and a rank title.
facts.action: Avoid or prepare for combat with rangers, as they are powerful and may have high-level equipment.

facts.fact: Rangers are generated with 1-3 random offensive items, 1-3 random defensive items, and 1-3 random miscellaneous items.
facts.detect: Find a ranger with a variety of items in its inventory.
facts.action: Stealthily approach and loot the ranger's inventory if possible, as it may contain valuable items.

facts.fact: Rangers generated on the Astral Plane have a chance of having a weapon that is turned into Vorpal Blade.
facts.detect: Encounter a ranger on the Astral Plane with a long sword.
facts.action: Be extremely cautious around rangers on the Astral Plane, as their weapons may be Vorpal Blade.

facts.fact: Rangers on the Astral Plane are given a cheap plastic imitation of the Amulet of Yendor, 0-999 gold pieces, and some valuable gems.
facts.detect: Find a ranger on the Astral Plane with a cheap plastic imitation of the Amulet of Yendor.
facts.action: Stealthily approach and loot the ranger's inventory for the Amulet of Yendor imitation and other valuable items.

facts.fact: Rangers on the Astral Plane have a chance of generating with erosion-proofed and greased weapons.
facts.detect: Find a ranger on the Astral Plane with a weapon that is erosion-proofed or greased.
facts.action: Be cautious when dealing with rangers on the Astral Plane, as their weapons may be difficult to destroy or disarm.

facts.fact: A raven has a bite attack that deals 1d6 physical damage and a claw attack that can blind targets for up to 6 turns.
facts.detect: A raven approaches or the message 'Nevermore!' when chatting to a raven.
facts.action: Wear a pair of lenses or a visored helmet to protect against the blinding claw attack. If none are available, blind yourself with a blindfold or towel to avoid being blinded by the raven's claw.

facts.fact: If the player is wielding a bec de corbin when a raven is generated, it will be peaceful instead of hostile.
facts.detect: Wielding a bec de corbin when a raven is generated.
facts.action: Wield a bec de corbin to make ravens peaceful.

facts.fact: Ravens are quite fast at 20 speed and can prove annoying to an early character, especially if you lack telepathy to detect other monsters.
facts.detect: A raven approaches or the player is blinded.
facts.action: Use telepathy or warning to detect and avoid ravens, or use ranged attacks to pick them off from a distance.

facts.fact: Thirty ravens are generated on the third version of Medusa's Island at level creation.
facts.detect: Entering Medusa's Island and seeing multiple ravens.
facts.action: Be cautious and prepared for multiple ravens, especially if lacking telepathy or warning.

facts.fact: Eating a floating eye corpse or tin while in the form of a raven prints a unique message.
facts.detect: The message 'You peck the eyeball with delight.'
facts.action: Avoid eating floating eye corpses or tins while polymorphed into a raven to prevent the unique message and potential negative effects.

facts.fact: Red dragons have a fire breath weapon dealing 6d6 fire damage.
facts.detect: Red dragon uses fire breath attack
facts.action: Gain fire resistance or reflection before encountering a red dragon.

facts.fact: Red dragons can burn and potentially destroy worn armor, scrolls, potions, and spellbooks in a target's open inventory.
facts.detect: Inventory items burning or disappearing
facts.action: Drop or stash vulnerable inventory before engaging a red dragon.

facts.fact: Red dragons have a 3/5 chance of dropping uncursed +0 red dragon scales upon death.
facts.detect: Red dragon corpse or scales dropped
facts.action: Eat the red dragon corpse to gain fire resistance.

facts.fact: Red dragons can see invisible and have infravision.
facts.detect: Red dragon moving in darkness
facts.action: Avoid fighting red dragons in dark areas.

facts.fact: Red dragons are generated hostile and can be summoned by the summon nasties spell.
facts.detect: Hostile red dragon appearing or summoned
facts.action: Avoid or prepare for encounters with red dragons.

facts.fact: A red mold has a passive attack that can trigger when it is attacked in melee and not killed, dealing fire damage against attackers without fire resistance dependent on their level.
facts.detect: Attacking a red mold in melee and taking fire damage.
facts.action: Avoid melee combat with red molds if you do not have fire resistance. Use ranged attacks or pets to deal with them.

facts.fact: Eating a red mold corpse or tin has a 3% chance of granting either poison resistance or fire resistance.
facts.detect: Finding a red mold corpse or tin.
facts.action: Eat a red mold corpse or tin to potentially gain fire or poison resistance.

facts.fact: Red molds are always generated hostile.
facts.detect: Seeing a red mold on the level.
facts.action: Be cautious around red molds as they will attack you.

facts.fact: Red molds possess poison resistance and fire resistance.
facts.detect: Noticing that a red mold is unaffected by fire or poison attacks.
facts.action: Use non-fire and non-poison attacks against red molds.

facts.fact: A red naga has a bite attack and a fire breath weapon.
facts.detect: red naga
facts.action: Equip fire-resistant armor and wield a fire-resistant weapon. If possible, use reflection to avoid damage from the breath attack.

facts.fact: Eating a red naga corpse or tin has a 20% chance of conveying fire resistance or poison resistance.
facts.detect: red naga corpse or tin
facts.action: Eat the corpse or tin to potentially gain fire resistance or poison resistance.

facts.fact: A red naga is the slowest of the adult nagas, with its speed matching that of an unhasted and unburdened hero.
facts.detect: red naga
facts.action: Use speed-boosting items or spells to outmaneuver the red naga.

facts.fact: A red naga has fire resistance and poison resistance.
facts.detect: red naga
facts.action: Carry fire-resistant items and be cautious with poison attacks.

facts.fact: Randomly generated red nagas may generate as peaceful towards chaotic characters.
facts.detect: red naga
facts.action: If chaotic, approach cautiously and attempt to make the red naga peaceful to avoid combat.

facts.fact: Red naga hatchling has fire resistance and poison resistance
facts.detect: Monster name: Red naga hatchling
facts.action: Avoid attacking if fire or poison attacks are intended

facts.fact: Eating a red naga hatchling corpse or tin has a 10% chance of conveying poison resistance
facts.detect: Monster name: Red naga hatchling and player has a poison resistance need
facts.action: Eat corpse or tin if player lacks poison resistance

facts.fact: Red naga hatchling can grow up into a red naga
facts.detect: Monster name: Red naga hatchling
facts.action: Avoid letting it grow into a more dangerous form

facts.fact: Red naga hatchlings are only randomly generated within levels and branches that are biased towards monsters of a particular alignment
facts.detect: Monster name: Red naga hatchling
facts.action: Be cautious in alignment-biased levels and branches

facts.fact: Red naga hatchlings are somewhat slower than a player character
facts.detect: Monster name: Red naga hatchling
facts.action: Engage in combat if necessary, but prioritize escape if in danger

facts.fact: A rock mole can tunnel through the dungeon and pick up gold and gems.
facts.detect: Seeing a rock mole carrying gold or gems.
facts.action: Kill the rock mole before it can eat or move metal items.

facts.fact: Rock moles have a bite attack that deals 1d6 physical damage.
facts.detect: Being attacked by a rock mole.
facts.action: Use a weapon or spell to kill the rock mole quickly.

facts.fact: Rock moles have an AC of 0 and MR of 20.
facts.detect: Attempting to hit a rock mole with a weapon or spell.
facts.action: Use a weapon or spell with high accuracy or power to hit the rock mole.

facts.fact: Rock moles are metallivorous and can eat metallic jewelry.
facts.detect: Polymorphing into a rock mole or seeing a rock mole eating jewelry.
facts.action: Eat metallic jewelry as a rock mole if necessary, but prefer polymorphing into a xorn.

facts.fact: Rock moles can end punishment by eating the heavy iron ball.
facts.detect: Being in punishment mode and seeing a rock mole.
facts.action: Allow the rock mole to eat the iron ball to end punishment.

facts.fact: A rock piercer can hide itself by clinging to the ceiling and will attempt to drop off the ceiling onto targets below them, inflicting 4d6 damage if it makes contact.
facts.detect: A rock piercer is on the ceiling above the bot's position.
facts.action: Avoid moving directly under a rock piercer or use a high AC to mitigate damage.

facts.fact: If the hero has warning, they will reveal a hiding rock piercer's location when moving adjacent to their square.
facts.detect: Moving adjacent to a square where a rock piercer is hiding.
facts.action: Be cautious when moving next to a rock piercer's hiding spot to avoid being attacked.

facts.fact: Tame rock piercers will not attack the hero and harmlessly drop off the ceiling if they walk underneath.
facts.detect: A tame rock piercer is on the ceiling.
facts.action: Walk directly under a tame rock piercer to make it drop harmlessly.

facts.fact: A rock piercer has a single bite attack.
facts.detect: A rock piercer is in the same square as the bot.
facts.action: Engage in combat or use ranged attacks to avoid being bitten.

facts.fact: Rock piercers are extremely slow with a movement speed of 1.
facts.detect: Rock piercer's movement speed is 1.
facts.action: Use the rock piercer's slow speed to your advantage by attacking from a distance or using hit-and-run tactics.

facts.fact: Rock trolls have a 2 chance of being generated with a ranseur, partisan, glaive, or spetum.
facts.detect: Upon encountering a rock troll, check if it is wielding one of the polearms mentioned.
facts.action: If the rock troll is wielding a polearm, disarm it or take the polearm before engaging in combat.

facts.fact: Rock trolls can often revive from their corpse when killed.
facts.detect: After killing a rock troll, observe if it revives from its corpse.
facts.action: Ensure to properly dispose of the rock troll corpse by eating it, applying a tinning kit, locking it in a large box, throwing it into pools or lava, turning it to stone, or luring it to the Rogue level.

facts.fact: Rock trolls have stronger attacks and move as fast as an unhasted unburdened player.
facts.detect: Notice the combat messages indicating the rock troll's high damage output and fast movement.
facts.action: Avoid prolonged combat with rock trolls and use ranged attacks or magic to keep distance.

facts.fact: Rock trolls generate among the hostile T that appear in throne rooms and when looting a throne while confused.
facts.detect: Encounter rock trolls in throne rooms or after looting a throne while confused.
facts.action: Be cautious in throne rooms and avoid looting thrones while confused.

facts.fact: Several rock trolls appear on the Barbarian quest at level creation.
facts.detect: Encounter rock trolls on the Barbarian quest levels.
facts.action: Lure rock trolls to the oasis on the locate level to ensure they drown upon revival.

facts.fact: A rogue is a chaotic player monster corresponding to a Rogue hero, and will have the role's appropriate rank title for their monster level.
facts.detect: Encounter a monster named with a rank title corresponding to a Rogue hero (e.g., 'Pug')
facts.action: Be cautious, as this monster is likely to be well-equipped and may pose a significant threat.

facts.fact: Rogues are not generated randomly, and are normally created as peaceful towards lawful heroes before specific adjustments are made.
facts.detect: A peaceful rogue approaches or is mentioned in the game messages.
facts.action: Approach cautiously and attempt to negotiate or pacify the rogue before it becomes hostile.

facts.fact: A rogue is always generated with 1-3 random offensive items, 1-3 random defensive items, and 1-3 random miscellaneous items.
facts.detect: A rogue is encountered with a variety of items in its inventory.
facts.action: Be prepared to fight or negotiate for the items, as they may be valuable.

facts.fact: Rogues generated on the Astral Plane will have a random color of dragon scale mail, a random cloak, a random helm, a random shield, and a random pair of boots, each with a 7/8 chance.
facts.detect: Encounter a rogue on the Astral Plane with a variety of armor and equipment.
facts.action: Be wary of the rogue's potential for high-level equipment and prepare accordingly.

facts.fact: Like other player monsters on the Astral Plane, rogues have a chance of generating with a long sword that is turned into Vorpal Blade if it has not yet generated.
facts.detect: A rogue is encountered with a Vorpal Blade or a long sword.
facts.action: Avoid or neutralize the rogue immediately to prevent the potential generation of Vorpal Blade.

facts.fact: Rope golems have a Holding 6d1 grab attack that chokes the target unless they are headless or otherwise cannot be strangled.
facts.detect: The bot encounters a rope golem and receives a message indicating it is choking or being grabbed.
facts.action: The bot should engrave Elbereth, use a bugle or tooled horn to scare the rope golem, or wear an oilskin cloak or greased outer armor to prevent the grabbing attack.

facts.fact: Rope golems are always generated with 30 HP.
facts.detect: The bot sees a rope golem with full health.
facts.action: The bot should prepare for a sustained fight as rope golems have a fixed amount of health.

facts.fact: Rope golems are not a valid genocide target.
facts.detect: The bot tries to genocide rope golems and receives a message indicating it cannot be done.
facts.action: The bot should avoid wasting time or resources trying to genocide rope golems.

facts.fact: Rope golems do not leave behind a corpse but may drop up to 2 items as a special death drop.
facts.detect: The bot sees a rope golem die and does not see a corpse but finds items such as a leash, bullwhip, or grappling hook.
facts.action: The bot should check for dropped items when a rope golem dies.

facts.fact: Rope golems can generate as a result of polypiling if there are enough cloth objects in a pile of items.
facts.detect: The bot sees a pile of items with cloth objects and later encounters a rope golem.
facts.action: The bot should be cautious around piles of items with cloth objects as they can generate rope golems.

facts.fact: Roshi are a strong and lawful human with two weapon attacks, each dealing 1d8 physical damage.
facts.detect: Encounter a roshi in the Samurai quest level or throne room of Lord Sato.
facts.action: Avoid combat with roshi unless necessary, as they are strong and have two weapon attacks.

facts.fact: Killing a peaceful roshi will cause a -4 luck penalty and anger the hero's god.
facts.detect: Hero's luck decreases and god becomes angry after killing a peaceful roshi.
facts.action: Avoid killing peaceful roshi to maintain luck and favor with the god.

facts.fact: Roshi are not randomly generated and are always peaceful.
facts.detect: Encounter a roshi in the Samurai quest level or throne room of Lord Sato.
facts.action: Treat roshi as peaceful until they attack or become hostile.

facts.fact: Roshi have infravision.
facts.detect: Roshi can see the player in dark areas.
facts.action: Avoid dark areas where roshi can see the player.

facts.fact: Roshi are generated with a melee weapon, armor, and possibly boots, cloak, bow, and arrows.
facts.detect: Roshi equipped with a long sword, short sword, chain mail, leather armor, boots, cloak, bow, and arrows.
facts.action: Steal or avoid roshi's equipment to prevent them from becoming stronger.

facts.fact: Rothes are generated hostile in groups of 2-4.
facts.detect: Multiple rothes appearing on the map together.
facts.action: Avoid or prepare for combat with multiple rothes, possibly by equipping better armor or weapons.

facts.fact: Rothes have a claw attack and two bite attacks, with the second bite being stronger.
facts.detect: Rothe attacking with 'claw' or 'bite' messages.
facts.action: Prioritize dodging or blocking the second bite attack.

facts.fact: Rothes are slow at speed 9 and respect Elbereth.
facts.detect: Rothes stopping at Elbereth symbols.
facts.action: Use Elbereth to control rothes' movement and avoid combat.

facts.fact: Rothe corpses provide decent food sources.
facts.detect: Killing a rothe and seeing its corpse.
facts.action: Eat rothe corpses to regain nutrition and HP.

facts.fact: A bovine smell indicates a shapeshifter has turned into a rothe.
facts.detect: Message 'You notice a bovine smell.'
facts.action: Be cautious as a shapeshifter may be nearby.

facts.fact: A rust monster has two touch attacks and a passive attack that deal no direct damage: the former rusts worn metallic armor, and the latter rusts metallic weapons and other items used to hit them.
facts.detect: The bot notices its metallic armor or weapons rusting when a rust monster is nearby.
facts.action: Equip non-metallic armor and weapons or rustproof existing metal items before encountering rust monsters.

facts.fact: Rust monsters will always avoid eating any non-rustable metal, an amulet of strangulation, or a ring of slow digestion if that ring's randomized appearance is made of iron.
facts.detect: The bot sees a rust monster avoid eating a non-rustable metal item or a ring of slow digestion.
facts.action: Ensure important metal items are non-rustable or use a ring of slow digestion to protect metal items.

facts.fact: Wearing non-metal armor or rustproofing whatever metal armor and weapons you have will render rust monster attacks completely harmless.
facts.detect: The bot notices it is wearing non-metal armor or has rustproofed its metal items.
facts.action: Equip non-metal armor or rustproof metal items to avoid rust damage.

facts.fact: Rust monsters can be used to deal with punishment in some cases by having them eat the iron ball and chain attached to you, though they will usually try to rust your armor afterward unless you use one that is not hostile, or else polymorph into one yourself.
facts.detect: The bot is punished and sees a rust monster nearby.
facts.action: Polymorph into a rust monster or use a tame rust monster to eat the iron ball and chain if punished.

facts.fact: Tame rust monsters consider rust-prone, iron-based items to be treats.
facts.detect: The bot sees a tame rust monster eating metallic items.
facts.action: Use tame rust monsters to eat metallic items to keep them from rusting.

facts.fact: Salamanders are generated in Gehennom and on the Plane of Fire, and are always hostile.
facts.detect: Encountering a hostile salamander in Gehennom or on the Plane of Fire.
facts.action: Avoid or prepare for combat with fire resistance and appropriate weapons.

facts.fact: Salamanders have fire resistance and inflict fire damage with their touch and bearhug attacks.
facts.detect: Taking fire damage from a salamander's touch or bearhug.
facts.action: Equip fire resistant armor and use water-based items to mitigate fire damage.

facts.fact: Eating a salamander corpse or tin has an 8/15 chance of granting fire resistance.
facts.detect: Finding a salamander corpse or tin.
facts.action: Eat the corpse or tin to potentially gain fire resistance.

facts.fact: Salamanders can be scared and released from bearhug with wands and spells.
facts.detect: Being bearhugged by a salamander.
facts.action: Use wands or spells to scare the salamander and break free from the bearhug.

facts.fact: Salamanders are immune to sliming and can eat green slime globs.
facts.detect: Encountering a salamander in an area with green slime.
facts.action: Avoid sliming and consider polymorphing into a salamander to eat green slime globs.

facts.fact: A samurai is a lawful player monster corresponding to a Samurai hero, and will have the role's appropriate rank title for their monster level.
facts.detect: Encounter a samurai with a rank title such as 'Captain', 'Lieutenant', etc.
facts.action: Be cautious as samurais are lawful and may be well-equipped.

facts.fact: Samurai are generated with 1-3 random offensive items, 1-3 random defensive items, and 1-3 random miscellaneous items.
facts.detect: Upon encountering a samurai, notice it carrying a variety of items such as weapons, armor, and other equipment.

facts.fact: Samurai generated on the Astral Plane are given a cheap plastic imitation of the Amulet of Yendor, 0-999 gold pieces, and some valuable gems.
facts.detect: Encounter a samurai on the Astral Plane with an imitation Amulet of Yendor and a large amount of gold.
facts.action: Steal the imitation Amulet of Yendor and gold if possible, as these can be valuable.

facts.fact: Samurai always generate with a weapon, which can be a katana, a long sword, or a randomly chosen melee weapon.
facts.detect: Upon encountering a samurai, notice it carrying a katana, long sword, or other melee weapon.

facts.fact: Samurai on the Astral Plane have a chance of generating with a long sword that is turned into Vorpal Blade if it has not yet generated.
facts.detect: Encounter a samurai on the Astral Plane carrying a long sword.
facts.action: Be extremely cautious as the long sword may turn into Vorpal Blade, which can be deadly.

facts.fact: A sandestin has a 6/7 chance of changing into a summonable nasty monster form.

facts.fact: A sandestin does not leave a corpse upon death.
facts.detect: Noticing a monster that disappears without leaving a corpse.
facts.action: Collect any items dropped by the sandestin before it disappears.

facts.fact: A sandestin has stoning resistance.
facts.detect: Attacking a sandestin with a stone-throwing weapon or spell.

facts.fact: A sandestin can follow the player to other levels if adjacent.
facts.detect: Noticing a sandestin following the player to another level.

facts.fact: A ring of protection from shape changers will reveal a sandestin.
facts.detect: Equipping a ring of protection from shape changers.
facts.action: Use the ring to identify and target sandestins.

facts.fact: Sasquatch difficulty level is 9 and has 15 speed, making it a challenging opponent.
facts.detect: Encounter with a sasquatch on the map.

facts.fact: Sasquatches can see invisible and have infravision.
facts.detect: Sasquatch detects the player even when invisible.
