facts.fact: Sasquatches can generate as peaceful towards lawful characters.
facts.detect: Sasquatch appears on the map without hostility.
facts.action: Approach cautiously and attempt to tame or pacify the sasquatch.

facts.fact: Sasquatches are part of the second quest monster class for Healers and make up 6/175 of randomly generated monsters on the Healer quest.
facts.detect: Entering the Healer quest level.
facts.action: Be prepared for potential encounters with sasquatches on these levels.

facts.fact: A hero polymorphed into a sasquatch gains bonuses to kicking.
facts.detect: Polymorphing into a sasquatch.
facts.action: Use the enhanced kicking ability to deal damage in melee combat.

facts.fact: A scorpion has a poison resistance of 50% and can drain strength with its sting attack.
facts.detect: Encounter a scorpion or see the message 'A scorpion stings you!'
facts.action: Equip poison resistance before engaging scorpions or use ranged attacks to avoid melee.

facts.fact: Eating a scorpion corpse has a 50% chance of conveying poison resistance.
facts.detect: Eat a scorpion corpse.
facts.action: Eat a scorpion corpse if you need poison resistance.

facts.fact: Scorpions are randomly generated with an item to hide under.
facts.detect: A scorpion appears with an item under it.
facts.action: Be cautious when approaching scorpions as they may have items under them.

facts.fact: Scorpions are the second quest monster for Rangers and appear frequently on the Ranger quest.
facts.detect: Enter the Ranger quest.
facts.action: Be prepared for multiple scorpions on the Ranger quest.

facts.fact: Scorpions have a difficulty level of 8 and a speed of 15, making them fast and dangerous.
facts.detect: Encounter a scorpion.
facts.action: Use ranged attacks or Elbereth to avoid melee with scorpions.

facts.fact: Scorpius is a unique scorpion that guards the Bell of Opening and the Ranger quest artifact, the Longbow of Diana.
facts.detect: Scorpius, Bell of Opening, Longbow of Diana
facts.action: Avoid taking the Longbow of Diana without killing Scorpius to prevent it from being stolen back.

facts.fact: Scorpius has a sting attack that can induce sickness.
facts.detect: Sickness status effect
facts.action: Carry blessed unicorn horn, eucalyptus leaves, or potions of extra healing/full healing to cure sickness.

facts.fact: Scorpius's corpse is poisonous to eat, but eating it or tin is guaranteed to grant poison resistance.
facts.detect: Scorpius's corpse
facts.action: Eat Scorpius's corpse or tin to gain poison resistance.

facts.fact: Scorpius moves at the same base speed of 12 as the hero.
facts.detect: Scorpius's movement speed
facts.action: Use fast speed or better to attack Scorpius before he can teleport away.

facts.fact: A scroll of scare monster or boulder fort on the up stair is an excellent defensive measure against Scorpius.
facts.detect: Scroll of scare monster, boulder fort, up stair
facts.action: Use a scroll of scare monster or create a boulder fort on the up stair to defend against Scorpius.

facts.fact: Sergeants are always generated hostile and frequently in groups of 2-4.
facts.detect: Multiple sergeants appearing together on the map or in a barracks.
facts.action: Avoid or prepare for combat with multiple sergeants, especially in barracks.

facts.fact: Sergeants can pick up weapons, armor, food, and other items and follow the hero to other levels.
facts.detect: Sergeant picking up items or following the hero.
facts.action: Avoid leaving valuable items near sergeants and be cautious when moving to new levels.

facts.fact: Applying a bugle will cause sergeants to awaken from sleep, end paralysis, and turn hostile.
facts.detect: Sergeant sleeping or paralyzed, and the presence of a bugle.
facts.action: Avoid using bugles near sergeants or in barracks.

facts.fact: Sergeants have a 2/3 chance of being pacified by a bribe, but require 250zm.
facts.detect: Sergeant nearby and sufficient gold.
facts.action: Consider bribery to pacify sergeants for crowd control or blocking hallways.

facts.fact: Sergeants can be a valuable source of wands and rations.
facts.detect: Sergeant corpse or dropped items.
facts.action: Collect dropped items and consider polyfodder from sergeant corpses.

facts.fact: Sewer rats have a Bite attack that deals 1d3 damage.
facts.detect: Eek! There's a sewer rat in the sink!
facts.action: Attack or kill the sewer rat to avoid damage.

facts.fact: Quaffing from a sink has a 1/20 chance of generating a sewer rat.
facts.detect: Eek! There's a sewer rat in the sink!
facts.action: Be cautious when drinking from sinks, especially in early levels.

facts.fact: Sewer rats can grow up into giant rats.
facts.detect: Eek! There's a sewer rat in the sink!
facts.action: Kill sewer rats to prevent them from growing into more dangerous giant rats.

facts.fact: Wererats can summon hostile sewer rats with a 2/3 chance on each adjacent square.
facts.detect: A wererat is nearby and hostile sewer rats appear.
facts.action: Avoid or kill wererats to prevent summoning of sewer rats.

facts.fact: Sewer rats are part of the first quest monster class for Healers, making up 24/175 of randomly generated monsters on the Healer quest.
facts.detect: Encounter sewer rats during the Healer quest.
facts.action: Be prepared to deal with sewer rats during the Healer quest.

facts.fact: Shades can only be harmed with blessed weapons, silver objects, certain artifact weapons and items, and magic.
facts.detect: Encounter with a shade and attempt to attack it with a non-blessed, non-silver weapon.
facts.action: Find or create a blessed weapon or obtain a silver object to attack the shade.

facts.fact: Shades are generated in Orcus-town at level creation outside of bones.
facts.detect: Entering Orcus-town and encountering shades.
facts.action: Avoid unnecessary exploration in Orcus-town or prepare to fight shades with appropriate weapons.

facts.fact: Shades have a paralysis attack and a slowing attack that removes both intrinsic and temporary speed.
facts.detect: Being paralyzed or noticing a significant decrease in movement speed after an attack.
facts.action: Carry a backup source of speed such as a tin of quantum mechanic meat or a wand of speed monster.

facts.fact: Silver weapons and Sunsword are the only weapons that will do their full damage to shades.
facts.detect: Attacking a shade with a non-silver weapon and noticing reduced damage.
facts.action: Switch to a silver weapon or Sunsword if available.

facts.fact: Shades are among the undead that can be created by reading the cursed Book of the Dead.
facts.detect: Reading the cursed Book of the Dead and encountering newly created shades.
facts.action: Avoid reading the cursed Book of the Dead or be prepared to deal with shades.

facts.fact: Shaman Karnov is a unique monster with a difficulty level of 24, generated as peaceful and located in the co-aligned temple in the Caveman quest's home level.
facts.detect: Shaman Karnov, +5 leather armor, +5 club
facts.action: Avoid combat if not prepared, as he is peaceful and can be negotiated with or bribed.

facts.fact: Shaman Karnov has a weapon attack of 4d10 physical damage and can cast one clerical monster spell per turn.
facts.detect: Shaman Karnov attacking
facts.action: Prepare for combat with high defensive and offensive capabilities, as his attacks are strong and unpredictable.

facts.fact: Shaman Karnov is generated with +5 leather armor and a +5 club.
facts.detect: Shaman Karnov with +5 leather armor and +5 club
facts.action: Stealthily approach to loot his items if not in immediate danger, as his equipment is valuable.

facts.fact: Shaman Karnov is always generated as peaceful and cannot be genocide or polymorphed.
facts.detect: Shaman Karnov not changing state
facts.action: Attempt to negotiate or bribe him to avoid combat, as he cannot be genocide or polymorphed.

facts.fact: Shaman Karnov is a strong, omnivorous human that can be seen via infravision.
facts.detect: Infravision revealing Shaman Karnov
facts.action: Use infravision to locate and approach Shaman Karnov cautiously, as he is unique and valuable.

facts.fact: Sharks have a Bite attack dealing 5d6 physical damage.
facts.detect: Shark appears on the map or in the vicinity.
facts.action: Avoid close combat with sharks, especially if you have low hit points or no armor.

facts.fact: Sharks are generated in specific locations such as the Castle moat corners and the Plane of Water.
facts.detect: Entering the Castle moat or the Plane of Water.
facts.action: Be cautious and prepared for shark encounters in these areas.

facts.fact: Sharks are amphibious but become scared and lose HP while on land.
facts.detect: Shark moves onto land.
facts.action: Exploit this weakness by luring sharks onto land to weaken or kill them.

facts.fact: Sharks are not randomly generated outside of specific level creation placements.
facts.detect: Exploring levels other than the specified locations.
facts.action: No special action needed, but be aware of the rarity of shark encounters.

facts.fact: Wands of cold can force sharks out of the water.
facts.detect: Possession of a wand of cold near water.
facts.action: Use wands of cold to drive sharks away from you or to escape from them.

facts.fact: Shimmering dragons have a difficulty level of 20 and a level of 15, making them a high-level monster with a strong magic missile breath weapon, bite, and claw attacks.
facts.detect: Shimmering dragon (monster name)
facts.action: Avoid or prepare for high-level combat if a shimmering dragon is encountered. Ensure the bot has high magic resistance and defensive items.

facts.fact: Shimmering dragons are generated hostile in throne rooms at dungeon levels 15 and below, and when looting a throne while confused and carrying gold.
facts.detect: Throne room (map feature) or confused state while carrying gold and near a throne
facts.action: Avoid throne rooms at high dungeon levels or be cautious when confused near thrones with gold.

facts.fact: Shimmering dragons have a 3/1 chance of dropping uncursed +0 shimmering dragon scales upon death unless disintegrated.
facts.detect: Shimmering dragon death (monster death message)
facts.action: Attempt to loot the corpse of a fallen shimmering dragon for potential dragon scales.

facts.fact: Shimmering dragons possess magic resistance.
facts.detect: Shimmering dragon (monster name)
facts.action: Ensure the bot has high magic resistance or items that can grant magic resistance before engaging in combat.

facts.fact: Shimmering dragons are part of the dragon monster class and are capable of flight, thick-skinned, and can see invisible.
facts.detect: Shimmering dragon (monster name)
facts.action: Prepare for a challenging fight with a monster that can fly and has thick skin, and may have invisibility detection.

facts.fact: A shocking sphere has an explosion attack that deals 4-24 base damage and can destroy rings and wands in the inventory of anyone caught in the blast, with the amount of items affected being equal to 5/24 of the shock damage dealt.
facts.detect: When a shocking sphere moves closer or is in the same level.
facts.action: Avoid getting too close to shocking spheres and prioritize obtaining shock resistance items such as the ring of shock resistance or blue dragon scale mail.

facts.fact: Shocking spheres are generated hostile and have a movement speed of 13, making them faster than an unhasted hero.
facts.detect: When a shocking sphere is generated on the same level.
facts.action: Move away from shocking spheres and prioritize gaining speed or using ranged attacks to avoid direct confrontation.

facts.fact: Pets that attack shocking spheres will likely trigger the explosion and catch you or other pets and monsters in the crossfire.
facts.detect: When a pet approaches a shocking sphere.
facts.action: Prevent pets from attacking shocking spheres or keep them away from areas where shocking spheres are present.

facts.fact: Sources of extrinsic shock resistance are somewhat rarer compared to fire resistance and cold resistance.
facts.detect: When searching for items that provide shock resistance.
facts.action: Prioritize finding and equipping items that provide shock resistance, such as the ring of shock resistance or blue dragon scale mail.

facts.fact: Shocking spheres are vulnerable to poisoned weapon damage and most forms of magic, such as a zapped wand of sleep.
facts.detect: When a shocking sphere is present and you have items or spells that can poison weapons or put monsters to sleep.
facts.action: Use poisoned weapons or zapped wands of sleep to immobilize and disable shocking spheres.

facts.fact: Shopkeepers are always peaceful and will block the entrance if you are invisible, riding, or carrying digging tools.
facts.detect: Will you please leave your pick-axe(s)/mattock(s)/digging tools outside?
facts.action: Remove digging tools from inventory or dismount before entering.

facts.fact: Killing a shopkeeper counts as murder for non-chaotic heroes.
facts.detect: The shopkeeper is present and you attack it.
facts.action: Avoid attacking or killing shopkeepers unless you are chaotic.

facts.fact: Shopkeepers will anger if you damage the shop's door or walls and refuse to pay for them.
facts.detect: The shopkeeper blocks the entrance and demands payment for damage.
facts.action: Pay for any damage done to the shop's door or walls.

facts.fact: Shopkeepers will call the Keystone Kops if you steal items.
facts.detect: The shopkeeper calls the Keystone Kops.
facts.action: Avoid stealing from shops.

facts.fact: Shopkeepers can be pacified by paying them 1000zm, which has a 2/3 chance of success.
facts.detect: The shopkeeper is angry and you have 1000zm.
facts.action: Pay 1000zm to pacify an angry shopkeeper.

facts.fact: You chatted to the shopkeeper, and they had nothing else to talk about.
facts.detect: You chatted to the shopkeeper
facts.action: Chat with the shopkeeper to get more dialogue options or unique lines from Izchak

facts.fact: You left a shop without paying.
facts.detect: You left a shop without paying
facts.action: Pay the shopkeeper or throw gold to them to avoid angering them

facts.fact: You attacked the shopkeeper or damaged the shop walls or doors.
facts.detect: You attacked the shopkeeper or damaged the shop walls or doors
facts.action: Pay 1000 zorkmids for a 2/3 chance of pacifying the shopkeeper

facts.fact: You died in a shop while the shopkeeper is peaceful - nothing was stolen, and nothing was owed.
facts.detect: You died in a shop while the shopkeeper is peaceful
facts.action: No action needed, the shopkeeper inherits all your possessions

facts.fact: You owed the shopkeeper money but you were outside of the shop (you robbed the shopkeeper), but your purse contained enough gold pieces to compensate the shopkeeper.
facts.detect: You owed the shopkeeper money but you were outside of the shop
facts.action: Compensate the shopkeeper with the owed money

facts.fact: A shrieker will shriek intermittently when adjacent to the hero or to a monster attacking them, which can aggravate and wake up monsters and also interrupts any occupation.
facts.detect: shrieks.
facts.action: Avoid or quickly eliminate shriekers to prevent waking up dangerous monsters.

facts.fact: Shrieking has a 1/3 chance of summoning a purple worm, which is very dangerous.
facts.detect: shrieks.
facts.action: Eliminate shriekers immediately to avoid the risk of summoning a purple worm.

facts.fact: Eating a shrieker corpse or tin has a 20% chance of granting poison resistance.
facts.detect: shrieker corpse or tin
facts.action: Eat shrieker corpses or tins to gain poison resistance if needed.

facts.fact: Three shriekers are generated on the goal level of the Caveman quest at level creation.
facts.detect: Caveman quest level
facts.action: Be cautious and eliminate shriekers quickly to avoid unwanted disturbances.

facts.fact: Shriekers are generated hostile and are weak but can summon dangerous monsters.
facts.detect: shrieker
facts.action: Prioritize eliminating shriekers to prevent potential hazards.

facts.fact: Silver dragons have a cold breath weapon, a strong bite attack, and two claw attacks.
facts.detect: Silver dragon symbol or name
facts.action: Avoid melee combat and use ranged attacks or spells that are not affected by cold resistance.

facts.fact: Silver dragons have a 3/1 chance of dropping a set of uncursed +0 silver dragon scales upon death unless disintegrated.
facts.detect: Silver dragon death message
facts.action: Search the corpse for silver dragon scales.

facts.fact: Silver dragons are immune to rays and reflect them back at attackers.
facts.detect: Ray-based attack failure message
facts.action: Avoid using ray-based attacks or wands against silver dragons.

facts.fact: Silver dragons can inflict knockback with their melee attacks, making them exceedingly dangerous to fight near pools or lava.
facts.detect: Knockback message
facts.action: Fight silver dragons on solid ground away from hazards like pools or lava.

facts.fact: Silver dragons have cold resistance but no other resistances, making poison an effective means of dealing with them.
facts.detect: Poison weapon or potion
facts.action: Use poison weapons or potions against silver dragons.

facts.fact: Skeletons have a 1/4 chance of generating with leather armor and a 1/4 chance of generating with a knife (2/3 chance) or a short sword (1/3 chance).
facts.detect: Leather armor, knife, short sword
facts.action: If a skeleton generates with armor or a weapon, the bot should consider equipping it if it's better than its current gear.

facts.fact: Chatting to a skeleton will freeze the hero in place for a few turns.
facts.detect: The skeleton rattles noisily.
facts.action: Avoid chatting to skeletons to prevent being frozen.

facts.fact: Skeletons have cold resistance, sleep resistance, poison resistance, death resistance, drain resistance, and stoning resistance.
facts.detect: Skeletons are not affected by cold, sleep, poison, death, drain, or stoning attacks.
facts.action: Avoid using attacks that are resisted by skeletons.

facts.fact: Skeletons can wield footrice corpses.
facts.detect: Skeleton wielding a footrice corpse.
facts.action: Avoid leaving footrice corpses near skeletons.

facts.fact: Skeletons do not leave a corpse upon death.
facts.detect: No corpse after killing a skeleton.
facts.action: Do not rely on skeletons for nutrition or bones.

facts.fact: A small mimic can hide by disguising itself as an appropriate item or dungeon feature.
facts.detect: The bot should notice items or features that seem out of place or unusually still.
facts.action: The bot should use telepathy or warning to detect mimics, or throw a single gold piece near suspicious items to reveal them.

facts.fact: A small mimic has a single claw attack and possesses acid resistance.
facts.detect: The bot should notice the mimic's claw attack and acid resistance when it attacks.
facts.action: The bot should avoid melee combat and use ranged attacks or acid resistance to counter the mimic's attacks.

facts.fact: Randomly generated small mimics are always created hostile.
facts.detect: The bot should notice hostile mimics in shops or on new dungeon floors.
facts.action: The bot should avoid or safely uncloak hostile mimics before engaging them.

facts.fact: A small mimic disguised as a closed door may appear in a doorway on new dungeon floors with level difficulty 9 or higher.
facts.detect: The bot should notice a closed door that seems out of place or unusually still.
facts.action: The bot should use telepathy or warning to detect the mimic, or throw a single gold piece near the door to reveal it.

facts.fact: Eating a small mimic corpse or tin causes the hero to mimic a pile of gold for 20 turns.
facts.detect: The bot should notice if it has polymorphed into a pile of gold.
facts.action: The bot should avoid eating small mimic corpses or tins to prevent unwanted polymorphing.

facts.fact: A snake has a single bite attack that inflicts strength-draining poison.
facts.detect: Snake symbol (snake) or bite attack message
facts.action: Avoid or kill snakes before they bite, especially if lacking poison resistance.

facts.fact: A snake corpse is poisonous to eat, and eating a snake corpse or tin has a 26% chance of conveying poison resistance.
facts.detect: Snake corpse or tin
facts.action: Eat snake corpse or tin if you have poison resistance or are prepared to gain it.

facts.fact: Snakes are faster than unhasted heroes.
facts.detect: Snake movement speed or relative speed comparison
facts.action: Hasten yourself or avoid direct combat with snakes.

facts.fact: Snakes can hide under objects, making them an unwelcome surprise.
facts.detect: Snake hiding under objects or telepathy
facts.action: Use telepathy or detect hidden objects to avoid surprise attacks.

facts.fact: Snakes generate among the random 'S' that are part of the first quest monster class for Archeologists and make up 24/35 of the monsters on the Archeologist quest.
facts.detect: Random 'S' on Archeologist quest levels
facts.action: Be extra cautious on Archeologist quest levels due to high snake presence.

facts.fact: Soldiers are always generated hostile and frequently in groups of 2-4.
facts.detect: Seeing multiple soldiers together or in barracks.
facts.action: Avoid or prepare for combat with multiple soldiers.

facts.fact: Soldiers can pick up and use bugles to awaken other soldiers and end paralysis.
facts.detect: Seeing a soldier pick up a bugle.
facts.action: Avoid bugles and keep distance from soldiers with bugles.

facts.fact: Soldiers have a 2/3 chance of being pacified by a bribe of 100zm.
facts.detect: Having 100zm and encountering a soldier.
facts.action: Bribe soldiers to block hallways or use as a shield.

facts.fact: Soldiers can grow up into sergeants.
facts.detect: Seeing a soldier level up.
facts.action: Avoid or prepare for combat with stronger soldiers.

facts.fact: Soldiers have a 1/3 chance of generating with K-ration or C-ration.
facts.detect: Soldier corpse or inventory.
facts.action: Eat soldier rations for nutrition.

facts.fact: Soldier ants have a bite attack that deals 2d4 physical damage and a sting attack that deals 3d4 poison damage and can drain strength.
facts.detect: Soldier ant, Bite, Sting
facts.action: Avoid being hit by soldier ants, especially their sting attack. Use poison resistance or antidotes if available.

facts.fact: Soldier ants are generated hostile and can appear in groups of 2-4.
facts.detect: Multiple soldier ants appearing together
facts.action: Retreat to a safe location or use Elbereth to avoid combat if possible.

facts.fact: Soldier ants have poison resistance.
facts.detect: Soldier ant
facts.action: Use weapons or spells that bypass poison resistance.

facts.fact: Eating a soldier ant corpse or tin has a 1/5 chance of granting poison resistance.
facts.detect: Soldier ant corpse or tin
facts.action: Eat soldier ant corpse or tin if you lack poison resistance and have a tinning kit.

facts.fact: Soldier ants can be generated by the summon insects spell.
facts.detect: Summon insects spell being cast
facts.action: Avoid areas where summon insects is likely to be cast.

facts.fact: A spotted jelly has a passive attack that triggers if attacked directly in melee and deals acid damage dependent on the attacker's level, with a separate 30% chance of corroding worn armor, and a separate 6% chance of corroding any weapons and/or armor used to hit the spotted jelly.
facts.detect: Attacking a spotted jelly in melee
facts.action: Avoid melee attacks on spotted jellies; use ranged attacks or wands to destroy them.

facts.fact: Spotted jellies possess acid resistance and stoning resistance.
facts.detect: Spotted jelly corpse
facts.action: Eat a spotted jelly corpse or tin to cure stoning if you are a vegan or vegetarian hero.

facts.fact: Spotted jellies can corrode weapons and armor even if attacked at a distance.
facts.detect: Using a metallic weapon or armor to attack a spotted jelly
facts.action: Use rustproofed weapons and armor when attacking spotted jellies.

facts.fact: Spotted jellies are part of the second quest monster class for Knights and make up 6/175 of the monsters randomly generated on the Knight quest.
facts.detect: Encountering a spotted jelly during the Knight quest
facts.action: Be prepared for spotted jellies during the Knight quest, especially if you are a Knight.

facts.fact: Spotted jellies can be nasty obstacles for pets and polyforms with multiple attacks.
facts.detect: Pets or polyforms attacking spotted jellies
facts.action: Keep pets out of range of spotted jellies if possible.

facts.fact: A stalker is always invisible and has a single claw attack that deals 4d4 physical damage.
facts.detect: The bot will notice a stalker through its invisibility or by seeing its claw attack damage.
facts.action: The bot should avoid engaging with stalkers directly and try to detect them using see invisible or telepathy.

facts.fact: Eating a stalker corpse or tin will stun the hero and turn them invisible for 50-149 turns if they are not already invisible.
facts.detect: The bot will notice eating a stalker corpse or tin.
facts.action: The bot should avoid eating stalker corpses or tins unless it is in a safe location and has a way to quickly cure stun.

facts.fact: Eating a stalker corpse when already invisible will turn the hero permanently invisible and grant the see invisible intrinsic.
facts.detect: The bot will notice eating a stalker corpse while invisible.
facts.action: The bot should eat stalker corpses while invisible to gain permanent invisibility and see invisible intrinsic, but only if it has a way to manage permanent invisibility effectively.

facts.fact: Wearing a mummy wrapping counts as being visible for the purpose of eating a stalker corpse.
facts.detect: The bot will notice wearing a mummy wrapping.
facts.action: The bot should remove mummy wrapping before eating a stalker corpse to avoid being stunned and turned invisible.

facts.fact: Stalkers are generated in the Samurai and Monk quests and can be summoned by a monster casting the summon nasties spell.
facts.detect: The bot will encounter stalkers in the Samurai and Monk quests or notice a monster casting the summon nasties spell.
facts.action: The bot should be cautious in these areas and prepare for the presence of stalkers.

facts.fact: A steam vortex has an engulfing attack that deals fire damage and can destroy scrolls, spellbooks and potions in the target's inventory if the attack hits the hero during the grace period where they were expelled and cannot be re-engulfed.
facts.detect: You are burning to a crisp!
facts.action: Avoid being engulfed by a steam vortex, especially if you have valuable scrolls, spellbooks, or potions in your inventory. If you are engulfed, quickly use a water-based item or spell to extinguish the fire.

facts.fact: Steam vortices possess fire resistance, sleep resistance, poison resistance, and stoning resistance.
facts.detect: The steam vortex is immune to fire, sleep, poison, and stoning attacks.
facts.action: Do not attempt to attack a steam vortex with fire, sleep, poison, or stoning spells or items.

facts.fact: Steam vortices are only generated in Gehennom and on the Plane of Air and Plane of Fire.
facts.detect: The map features indicating Gehennom, Plane of Air, or Plane of Fire.
facts.action: Be cautious when entering these areas, as steam vortices are present and can be dangerous.

facts.fact: Steam vortices do not leave a corpse upon death.
facts.detect: No corpse is left after a steam vortex is killed.
facts.action: Do not expect to find a corpse after killing a steam vortex.

facts.fact: Most heroes will have obtained fire resistance by the time they encounter a steam vortex normally.
facts.detect: You feel mildly hot.
facts.action: If you have fire resistance, you can handle the steam vortex's attack without significant danger.

facts.fact: A stone giant has a 50% chance of being generated with either a boulder or a club.
facts.detect: Upon encountering a stone giant, the bot should check if the stone giant is carrying a boulder or a club.
facts.action: If the stone giant is carrying a boulder, the bot should be cautious as the boulder can be thrown. If the stone giant is carrying a club, the bot should attempt to disarm it or steal the club.

facts.fact: A stone giant has a 50% chance of being generated with a small assortment of gems.
facts.detect: Upon encountering a stone giant, the bot should check if the stone giant is carrying gems.
facts.action: If the stone giant is carrying gems, the bot should attempt to steal them as they can be valuable.

facts.fact: A stone giant has a natural AC of 0, which is the best among giants and second-best among giant humanoids.
facts.detect: Upon encountering a stone giant, the bot should note its AC value.
facts.action: The bot should prepare for a tough fight as the stone giant's low AC means it is well-armored.

facts.fact: A stone giant has a 50% chance of being peaceful towards lawful characters.
facts.detect: Upon encountering a stone giant, the bot should observe if the stone giant is peaceful.
facts.action: If the stone giant is peaceful, the bot should attempt to negotiate or avoid combat.

facts.fact: A stone giant can generate in small groups of two to four.
facts.detect: Upon encountering a stone giant, the bot should check if there are other stone giants nearby.
facts.action: If there are multiple stone giants, the bot should be cautious and prepare for a difficult fight.

facts.fact: A stone golem has stoning resistance.
facts.detect: The bot encounters a stone golem.
facts.action: Avoid using stoning attacks or items on the stone golem.

facts.fact: A stone golem leaves behind a statue of itself containing its inventory upon death.
facts.detect: The bot kills a stone golem and sees a statue.
facts.action: Search the statue for any useful items or equipment.

facts.fact: Casting stone to flesh on a stone golem will turn it into a flesh golem.
facts.detect: The bot encounters a stone golem and has the spell stone to flesh.
facts.action: Consider casting stone to flesh to turn the stone golem into a flesh golem.

facts.fact: Stone golems are always generated with 60 HP.
facts.detect: The bot encounters a stone golem.
facts.action: Prepare for a fight with a stone golem knowing it has 60 HP.

facts.fact: Stone golems are generated on Medusa's Island and the Plane of Earth.
facts.detect: The bot is on Medusa's Island or the Plane of Earth.
facts.action: Be prepared to encounter stone golems in these areas.

facts.fact: A storm giant has a single weapon attack and possesses shock resistance.
facts.detect: Encounter with a storm giant
facts.action: Equip shock resistant armor or wield a shock resistant weapon if available.

facts.fact: Eating a storm giant corpse or tin has a 50% chance of granting shock resistance and an independent 50% chance of increasing a character's strength.
facts.detect: Obtain a storm giant corpse or tin
facts.action: Eat the storm giant corpse or tin to potentially gain shock resistance and strength.

facts.fact: Storm giants may generate as peaceful towards chaotic characters.
facts.detect: Encounter with a storm giant as a chaotic character
facts.action: Attempt to tame or negotiate with the storm giant if possible.

facts.fact: Storm giants may appear among the random H that are part of the second quest monster class for Valkyries.
facts.detect: Entering the Valkyrie quest branch at a high experience level
facts.action: Be prepared for storm giants in the Valkyrie quest branch.

facts.fact: Storm giants have a 50% chance of being generated with either a boulder or a club with equal probability.
facts.detect: Storm giant generation
facts.action: Loot any boulders or clubs dropped by storm giants.

facts.fact: A straw golem can be destroyed instantly with fire damage.
facts.detect: burns completely!
facts.action: Use a wand of fire or a lit potion of oil to destroy the straw golem.

facts.fact: Straw golems have sleep resistance and poison resistance.
facts.detect: Straw golem
facts.action: Avoid using sleep or poison-based attacks on straw golems.

facts.fact: Straw golems are always generated with 20 HP.
facts.detect: Straw golem
facts.action: Straw golems have a fixed amount of HP, making them easier to plan for in terms of damage output.

facts.fact: Straw golems do not leave behind a corpse upon death.
facts.detect: Straw golem dies
facts.action: Do not expect to find a corpse or items dropped by a straw golem.

facts.fact: Fire damage can cause a straw golem to lose up to half its maximum HP plus one.
facts.detect: burns completely!
facts.action: Be cautious when using fire-based attacks, as they can severely weaken or destroy straw golems.

facts.fact: Students are peaceful and cannot be genocided.
facts.detect: Peaceful student monster
facts.action: Avoid attacking peaceful students to prevent alignment and luck penalties.

facts.fact: Killing a peaceful quest guardian (student) causes a -4 luck penalty and anger from the hero's god.
facts.detect: Message: You feel a sudden chill.
facts.action: Avoid killing peaceful quest guardians to maintain luck and alignment.

facts.fact: Students can grow up into player monster archeologists.
facts.detect: Message: The student grows up into an archeologist.
facts.action: If a student grows up, treat it as a more dangerous archeologist.

facts.fact: Students are generated with a 2/3 chance of carrying a potion of healing.
facts.detect: Student drops potion of healing when killed.
facts.action: Collect potion of healing from killed students.

facts.fact: Students can tunnel if they have a digging tool.
facts.detect: Student tunnels through walls.

facts.action: Wear poison resistance gear or use a unicorn horn to neutralize poison before engaging.

facts.fact: Thoth Amon is a unique monster with a difficulty level of 22 and is always generated hostile on the Barbarian quest goal level.

facts.detect: Seeing Thoth Amon with The Heart of Ahriman in his inventory.

facts.action: Use magic resistance and wands of cancellation to counter his spellcasting.

facts.fact: Thoth Amon does not respect Elbereth and may attempt to escape by using the up stair.
facts.detect: Seeing Thoth Amon move towards the up stair.
facts.action: Block off the up stair to prevent his escape.

facts.fact: Thugs are always created peaceful and are not randomly generated.
facts.detect: Encountering a peaceful thug in the Rogue quest home level.

facts.fact: Thugs have two weapon attacks, unlike most quest guardians.
facts.detect: Seeing a thug attack with two weapons.
facts.action: Be prepared for a thug to attack with two weapons, which can be more dangerous than a single weapon attack.

facts.fact: Thugs are generated with a club, a secondary weapon (dagger or knife), and may have leather gloves and armor (leather jacket or leather armor).
facts.detect: Finding a thug equipped with these items.
facts.action: Steal or take these items from thug corpses if possible to improve your equipment.

facts.fact: A tiger has two claw attacks and a bite attack.

facts.fact: Tigers are always created hostile.

facts.fact: Tigers lack a magic resistance score, rendering them vulnerable to magic.

facts.detect: message 'This is gr-r-reat!' when polymorphed into a tiger and eating meat

facts.fact: A titan has a 1/2 chance of being generated with a boulder.
facts.detect: The bot detects a boulder next to a titan.
facts.action: The bot should be cautious and avoid getting hit by the boulder if the titan throws it.

facts.detect: The bot notices the titan's high speed and good AC.

facts.fact: Titans can cast spells such as haste self and summon nasties.
facts.detect: The bot sees the titan casting a spell or notices the presence of summoned nasties.
facts.action: The bot should use magic resistance or Elbereth to protect against spells and be prepared to deal with summoned nasties.

facts.detect: The bot encounters a titan in the Castle or levels above it.
facts.action: The bot should be prepared to handle or avoid the titan based on its current level and equipment.

facts.fact: Titans are among the best monsters that pets can be polymorphed into.
facts.detect: The bot notices a polymorphed pet titan.
facts.action: The bot should ensure the pet titan is well-equipped with a shield of reflection and a unicorn horn.

facts.fact: Titanothere has mediocre AC and no magic resistance.
facts.detect: Titanothere (symbol: T)
facts.action: Use magic missiles or wands of sleep to debilitate it.

facts.fact: A trapper has a speed of 3, making it nonthreatening if you are decently equipped.
facts.detect: Telepathy or warning, or seeing a trapper on the map.
facts.action: Approach cautiously but do not flee unless you are underprepared.

facts.detect: Seeing a pet near a trapper or receiving a message about a pet being killed.

facts.detect: Seeing a hostile trapper on the map.

facts.detect: Receiving a message about the Wizard of Yendor creating a clone.

facts.detect: Weapon name ranseur, partisan, glaive, or spetum in troll's inventory
facts.action: Disarm the troll or avoid engaging it in melee if it has a polearm.

facts.detect: Troll attacking player

facts.detect: Entering Barbarian quest level
facts.action: Be prepared for multiple trolls and have a strategy to deal with their regeneration and revival.

facts.fact: Twoflower is a unique, peaceful monster with a difficulty level of 22 and 4d10 physical weapon attack.
facts.detect: Twoflower (monster name)

facts.fact: Umber hulks have a gaze attack that can confuse anything, including itself if a mirror is used.

facts.detect: Observing an umber hulk wearing armor.

facts.fact: Uruk-hai have a 1/3 chance of being generated with poisoned orcish arrows and a stack of 3 to 14 poisoned orcish arrows.

facts.action: Avoid melee with Uruk-hai if not poison resistant. Pick up arrows if poison resistant and plan to use them against other Uruk-hai.

facts.fact: Uruk-hai have a 1/2 chance of being generated with an orcish helm.
facts.detect: Orcish helm in inventory or on the ground
facts.action: Pick up orcish helm if it is useful and does not conflict with your equipment strategy.

facts.fact: Uruk-hai are faster than Mordor orcs but slower than hill orcs.
facts.detect: Uruk-hai moving on the map

facts.fact: Uruk-hai have poison resistance.
facts.detect: Uruk-hai not affected by poison attacks
facts.action: Avoid using poison attacks or items against Uruk-hai.

facts.fact: A valkyrie has cold resistance like Valkyrie heroes do.

facts.detect: Water moccasin hiding under items
facts.action: Be cautious when moving items in water-filled areas.

facts.fact: Water nymphs have a 30% chance of granting teleportitis when eaten.
facts.detect: Eating a water nymph corpse or tin
facts.action: Avoid eating water nymph corpses or tins unless teleportitis is desired or managed.

facts.fact: Water nymphs can steal items, including weapons and armor, and can seduce to steal multiple items.
facts.detect: Monster name 'water nymph' and item theft attempts
facts.action: Carry important items in the inventory and avoid melee combat with water nymphs.

facts.fact: Water nymphs can be generated by dipping items into fountains or quaffing from them.
facts.detect: Message 'You attract a water nymph!' or 'You hear a seductive voice.'
facts.action: Avoid dipping items into fountains or quaffing from them unless necessary.

facts.fact: Water nymphs can steal levitation, water walking, or flying items, leaving the hero at risk of drowning.
facts.detect: Crossing large bodies of water
facts.action: Avoid crossing large bodies of water when water nymphs are nearby or suspected.

facts.fact: Using force bolts or wands of striking against a water nymph can break her mirror and incur a -2 luck penalty.
facts.detect: Using force bolts or wands of striking against a water nymph
facts.action: Avoid using force bolts or wands of striking against water nymphs unless necessary.

facts.fact: Water trolls have a 50% chance of being generated with a polearm (ranseur, partisan, glaive, or spetum).
facts.detect: Upon encountering a water troll, the bot should notice if the troll is wielding one of these polearms.
facts.action: If the water troll is wielding a polearm, the bot should avoid melee combat and try to lure it into a position where it cannot use its weapon effectively, such as a narrow corridor or a corner.

facts.fact: Water trolls can revive from their corpse when killed.
facts.detect: Upon killing a water troll, the bot should notice if the corpse remains on the ground.
facts.action: The bot should immediately dispose of the water troll corpse using a tinning kit, feeding it to a carnivorous pet, or stoning it to prevent revival.

facts.fact: Water trolls have a speed of 14, making them faster than other trolls and unhasted, unburdened characters.
facts.detect: The bot should notice the speed of the water troll during combat.
facts.action: The bot should avoid prolonged melee combat and try to use ranged attacks or magic to defeat the water troll.

facts.fact: Water trolls have a magic resistance (MR) of 40, making magical attacks unreliable.
facts.detect: The bot should notice if its magical attacks are failing against the water troll.
facts.action: The bot should switch to physical attacks or other reliable combat methods.

facts.fact: Water trolls can swim and breathe in water, making disposal by throwing into a pool ineffective.
facts.detect: The bot should notice if the water troll is in a pool of water.
facts.action: The bot should avoid disposing of the water troll corpse in water and use other methods such as tinning, feeding to a pet, or stoning.

facts.fact: A werejackal can shift between human and canine form, and their shifting to canine form is signified by howling that can wake up sleeping monsters.
facts.detect: You hear a howling at the moon.
facts.action: Avoid engaging the werejackal in combat until it shifts back to human form, as the canine form can cause lycanthropy.

facts.fact: A werejackal in human form that is not subjected to protection from shape changers will transform into their animal form with a chance dependent on whether it is night and if the full moon is out.
facts.detect: Nighttime or full moon conditions.
facts.action: Equip protection from shape changers or avoid werejackals during nighttime or full moon.

facts.fact: A werejackal in animal form has a bite attack that can cause lycanthropy in the hero.
facts.detect: Engaging a werejackal in animal form.
facts.action: Avoid being bitten by a werejackal in animal form or use holy water, sprigs of wolfsbane, or pray to cure lycanthropy.

facts.fact: A werejackal can summon other jackals and canines on nearby squares when in melee range of the hero.
facts.detect: Additional monsters appearing nearby.
facts.action: Engage werejackals quickly to prevent them from summoning additional monsters.

facts.fact: A werejackal corpse is poisonous to eat and can cause lycanthropy.
facts.detect: Eating a werejackal corpse or tin.
facts.action: Avoid eating werejackal corpses or tins.

facts.fact: Wererats in human form have a weapon attack and can pick up weapons, food, armor, and other items.
facts.detect: A human-like figure with a weapon or holding items.
facts.action: Avoid engaging wererats in human form in melee combat and try to use ranged attacks or spells.

facts.fact: Wererats in rodent form have a bite attack that can cause lycanthropy.
facts.detect: A small rodent-like creature with the symbol 'r'.
facts.action: Use ranged attacks, silver weapons, or pets to avoid close combat with rodent-form wererats.

facts.fact: Wererats can summon other rats when in melee range of a hero.
facts.detect: Additional rats appearing nearby when fighting a wererat.
facts.action: Pull the wererat into a hallway to limit the number of rats it can summon.

facts.fact: Eating a wererat corpse or tin gives lycanthropy to the hero.
facts.detect: A wererat corpse or tin in inventory.
facts.action: Avoid eating wererat corpses or tins.

facts.fact: A silver weapon is effective against wererats.
facts.detect: A silver weapon in inventory.
facts.action: Use a silver weapon to quickly dispatch wererats.

facts.fact: Werewolves have a 30% chance to transform into their animal form each turn during nighttime or full moon, and a 3% chance if both conditions are met.
facts.detect: Message: You hear a howling at the moon.
facts.action: Avoid or prepare to fight werewolves during nighttime or full moon.

facts.fact: Werewolves can summon up to 5 hostile monsters, including wolves, wargs, and winter wolves, when in melee range of the hero.
facts.detect: Presence of multiple hostile wolves, wargs, or winter wolves near the hero.
facts.action: Engage in combat with werewolves from a distance or use Elbereth to prevent summoning.

facts.fact: Eating a werewolf corpse or tin causes lycanthropy, and eating other werewolves or wolves is considered cannibalism for lycanthropes.
facts.detect: Message: You eat a werewolf corpse or tin.
facts.action: Avoid eating werewolf corpses or tins.

facts.fact: Werewolves have poison resistance and drain resistance.
facts.detect: Werewolf attacks without effect due to poison resistance or drain resistance.
facts.action: Use silver weapons or other means to bypass resistance.

facts.fact: Contracting lycanthropy from a werewolf causes the hero to shift to wolf form, destroying certain items and forcing the hero to drop armor and inventory.
facts.detect: Message: You feel a strange transformation coming over you.
facts.action: Avoid contact with werewolves to prevent lycanthropy.

facts.fact: White dragons have a cold breath weapon that can destroy potions in a target's open inventory.
facts.detect: Potion destruction message when in open inventory
facts.action: Keep potions in the main inventory or use protection to avoid open inventory

facts.fact: White dragons have a 3/5 chance of dropping uncursed +0 white dragon scales upon death.
facts.detect: Message upon killing a white dragon
facts.action: Collect uncursed +0 white dragon scales for cold resistance and slow digestion

facts.fact: White dragons can freeze moats and pools with their breath, allowing makeshift bridges to be created.
facts.detect: Freezing of moats or pools
facts.action: Use this to cross water safely

facts.fact: White dragons are hostile and appear in throne rooms at dungeon levels 15 and below.
facts.detect: Appearance of white dragon in throne room
facts.action: Be cautious and prepared for combat

facts.fact: Eating a white dragon corpse or tin grants cold resistance.
facts.detect: Message upon eating a white dragon corpse or tin
facts.action: Eat corpse or tin for cold resistance

facts.fact: Winged gargoyle has stoning resistance
facts.detect: Monster name: Winged gargoyle
facts.action: Eat the winged gargoyle to gain temporary stoning resistance

facts.fact: Winged gargoyle has two claw attacks and a bite attack
facts.detect: Monster attacks: Claw 3d6 physical, claw 3d6 physical, bite 3d4 physical
facts.action: Equip high AC and damage resistance gear before engaging

facts.fact: Winged gargoyle is hostile and appears around double-digit dungeon depth
facts.detect: Dungeon level: Around 10 or higher
facts.action: Be prepared for winged gargoyle encounters

facts.fact: Winged gargoyle is generated by hostile spellcasters in Gehennom
facts.detect: Location: Gehennom
facts.action: Be cautious and prepared for winged gargoyle encounters in Gehennom

facts.fact: Winged gargoyle is faster than standard gargoyles
facts.detect: Monster speed: 15
facts.action: Use speed-affecting items or spells to counteract

facts.fact: Winter wolves have a MR score of 20, making wands and spells somewhat less reliable against them.
facts.detect: Winter wolf encounters or messages indicating difficulty in casting spells or using wands.
facts.action: Carry a wand of fire or other fire-based weapons to combat winter wolves effectively.

facts.fact: Winter wolves have a breath weapon that can freeze and destroy potions in the open inventory.
facts.detect: Message indicating a winter wolf's breath weapon hit or destroyed potions.
facts.action: Carry potions in a container to protect them from freezing.

facts.fact: Winter wolves can be summoned by werewolves, which can occur early in the game.
facts.detect: Message indicating a werewolf has summoned winter wolves.
facts.action: Avoid melee combat with werewolves to prevent summoning winter wolves.

facts.fact: Eating a winter wolf corpse grants cold resistance with a ~46% chance.
facts.detect: Message indicating the consumption of a winter wolf corpse.
facts.action: Eat winter wolf corpses to gain cold resistance if not observing vegetarian or foodless conducts.

facts.fact: Winter wolves respect Elbereth but will use their breath attacks while fleeing.
facts.detect: Winter wolf fleeing from Elbereth.
facts.action: Use Elbereth to slow down winter wolves but be prepared for their breath attacks.

facts.fact: Winter wolf cubs have a frost breath weapon that can freeze and destroy potions in the open inventory of those hit by the blast depending on the damage sustained.
facts.detect: Message: You feel a chill in the air as a frost breath hits you.
facts.action: Carry potions in containers or wear a dwarvish cloak to protect them from frost breath.

facts.fact: Winter wolf cubs are randomly generated hostile and can appear in small groups.
facts.detect: Multiple winter wolf cubs appear on the map.
facts.action: Avoid or prepare for combat with multiple winter wolf cubs, especially in dark areas where infravision is not useful.

facts.fact: Winter wolf cubs can be scared off with ease and respect Elbereth like other canines.
facts.detect: Message: The winter wolf cub runs away.
facts.action: Mark Elbereth signs to scare off winter wolf cubs and avoid combat.

facts.fact: Eating a winter wolf cub corpse or tin has a 1/3 chance of granting cold resistance.
facts.detect: Message: You feel less cold.
facts.action: Eat winter wolf cub corpses or tins to potentially gain intrinsic cold resistance.

facts.fact: Winter wolf cubs lack any MR score, so wands and spells that can slow them down or immobilize them will help to close the distance.
facts.detect: Message: The winter wolf cub is slowed down by the wand of slowing.
facts.action: Use wands of slowing or other spells to immobilize winter wolf cubs and close the distance for melee combat.

facts.fact: A wizard is a type of monster that appears in NetHack, corresponding to a Wizard hero with a rank title based on their monster level.
facts.detect: Encounter a named wizard monster with a rank title such as 'Sorcerer', 'Archmage', etc.
facts.action: Be cautious as a wizard can be well-equipped and dangerous, especially if encountered on the Astral Plane.

facts.fact: Wizards are not generated randomly and are normally peaceful towards neutral heroes.
facts.detect: A peaceful wizard named Newt is generated asleep on the Wizard quest goal level.
facts.action: Avoid conflict with peaceful wizards unless necessary, as they may be carrying valuable items.

facts.fact: A wizard is always generated with 1-3 random offensive items, 1-3 random defensive items, and 1-3 random miscellaneous items.
facts.detect: Upon encountering a wizard, notice they are carrying a variety of items such as weapons, armor, and other equipment.
facts.action: Carefully loot the wizard's inventory if defeated, as it may contain useful items.

facts.fact: Wizards generated on the Astral Plane have a chance of being given a cheap plastic imitation of the Amulet of Yendor, gold pieces, and valuable gems.
facts.detect: Upon encountering a wizard on the Astral Plane, notice they are carrying an imitation Amulet of Yendor, gold pieces, and gems.
facts.action: Prioritize taking the imitation Amulet of Yendor and any valuable items from the wizard's inventory.

facts.fact: Wizards generated on the Astral Plane have a chance of being given a long sword that can turn into Vorpal Blade if it has not yet generated.
facts.detect: Upon encountering a wizard on the Astral Plane, notice they are carrying a long sword.
facts.action: Be extremely cautious if the wizard has a long sword, as it may turn into Vorpal Blade.

facts.fact: The Wizard of Yendor is a unique monster with a difficulty level of 34 and level 30, and he is the guardian of the Book of the Dead.
facts.detect: The presence of the Wizard of Yendor in his tower in Gehennom, or the message 'You notice a black glow surrounding you.' when harassed.
facts.action: Prepare for a challenging fight and ensure you have magic resistance and a means to quickly defeat him, such as a wand of death or finger of death.

facts.fact: The Wizard of Yendor can steal the Amulet of Yendor, any invocation items, or quest artifacts with a 20% chance on his claw attack.
facts.detect: The message 'The Wizard of Yendor steals your [item]' when attacked.
facts.action: Avoid fighting the Wizard until you have backup magic resistance and reflection, and keep your quest artifact(s) in a container.

facts.fact: The Wizard of Yendor can cast spells and use the Double Trouble spell to create a clone of himself.
facts.detect: The message 'A clone of the Wizard of Yendor appears!' when he uses Double Trouble.
facts.action: Be prepared to deal with multiple Wizard clones and ensure you have a strategy to defeat them quickly.

facts.fact: The Wizard of Yendor will harass the player with negative effects after being killed or after the invocation is performed.
facts.detect: The message 'You feel vaguely nervous.' or other harassment messages.
facts.action: Maintain magic resistance and be prepared to quickly deal with the Wizard if he reappears.

facts.fact: The Wizard of Yendor can be driven off the dungeon by luring him to the first dungeon level and dealing enough damage to scare him while he is near an up staircase.
facts.detect: The message 'The Wizard of Yendor flees the dungeon!' when he escapes.
facts.action: Lure the Wizard to the first dungeon level and deal damage to scare him near an up staircase.

facts.fact: The Wizard of Yendor can steal items such as the cloak and the Eyes of the Overworld.
facts.detect: The Wizard of Yendor is nearby and the bot notices a decrease in inventory or a message indicating an item has been stolen.
facts.action: Temporarily switch to a cloak of magic resistance and store the Eyes of the Overworld in a bag when the Wizard is near.

facts.fact: The Wizard of Yendor will flee to the top floor if the player leads him there.
facts.detect: The Wizard of Yendor is present and the bot moves towards the stairs to the upper level.
facts.action: Lead the Wizard to the top floor to force him to flee.

facts.fact: The Wizard of Yendor will speak messages indicating his health status and the player's fate.
facts.detect: Messages such as 'Savor thy breath, , it be thy last!' when the player is at 5 HP or lower.
facts.action: Be cautious and prepare to defend against the Wizard when health is low.

facts.fact: The Wizard of Yendor can cast 'summon nasties' to summon monsters.
facts.detect: Message 'Destroy the thief, my pets!' when the Wizard is near.
facts.action: Be prepared to fight summoned monsters or retreat to a safe location.

facts.fact: Wolves are considered 'children of the night' for the purpose of chatting to vampires in their humanoid form.
facts.detect: Chatting to a vampire in humanoid form.
facts.action: Use the 'children of the night' phrase to chat with vampires.

facts.fact: Wolves have a single bite attack that deals 2d4 physical damage.
facts.detect: Encountering a wolf in the dungeon.
facts.action: Be prepared for the bite attack and consider using ranged attacks or spells to avoid melee.

facts.fact: Wolves are randomly generated hostile and may appear in small groups.
facts.detect: Multiple wolves appearing in the same area.
facts.action: Avoid engaging multiple wolves at once and try to pull them into a hallway for safer combat.

facts.fact: Werewolves have a 4/5 chance of summoning a wolf when calling for help.
facts.detect: Encountering a werewolf.
facts.action: Prioritize killing werewolves to prevent them from summoning additional wolves.

facts.fact: Vlad the Impaler can shift into wolf form when outside of the hero's line of sight, except on the Rogue level or over hazardous terrain.
facts.detect: Vlad the Impaler entering wolf form.
facts.action: Be cautious when approaching Vlad the Impaler and avoid hazardous terrain to prevent him from shifting.

facts.fact: Wood golems are resistant to poison and sleep.
facts.detect: Monster name: Wood golem
facts.action: Avoid using poison attacks or sleep spells on wood golems.

facts.fact: Wood golems have a +d4 bonus damage when hit with weapons that use the axe skill.
facts.detect: Weapon skill: Axe
facts.action: Use axes or other axe-based weapons to deal extra damage to wood golems.

facts.fact: Wood golems can lose up to 1/4 of their maximum HP from fire traps and decay attacks.
facts.detect: Message: falls to pieces!
facts.action: Avoid fire traps and be cautious around brown puddings when near wood golems.

facts.fact: Wood golems leave behind 2-8 quarterstaves upon death.
facts.detect: Monster death: Wood golem
facts.action: Collect quarterstaves as they can be useful weapons or for crafting.

facts.fact: Wood golems are always generated hostile and with 40 HP.
facts.detect: Monster name: Wood golem
facts.action: Be prepared to fight wood golems as they are always hostile.

facts.fact: A wood nymph has a 2/5 chance of being generated asleep unless the hero has the Amulet of Yendor.
facts.detect: Message: Wood nymph wakes up.
facts.action: Avoid waking up sleeping wood nymphs if possible, especially if you do not have the Amulet of Yendor.

facts.fact: A wood nymph has a 1/5 chance of being generated with a mirror.
facts.detect: Message: Wood nymph picks up a mirror.
facts.action: Be cautious when attacking a wood nymph with a wand or bolt that could break a mirror, as this will incur a -2 luck penalty.

facts.fact: A wood nymph can steal items and use them against the player, including offensive wands and weapons.
facts.detect: Message: Wood nymph steals [item name].
facts.action: Keep important items like offensive wands and weapons in your inventory and avoid letting wood nymphs get close enough to steal them.

facts.fact: Eating a wood nymph corpse or tin has a 30% chance of granting teleportitis.
facts.detect: Message: You feel a bit dizzy.
facts.action: Avoid eating wood nymph corpses or tins unless you have a way to cure teleportitis.

facts.fact: Wood nymphs can teleport at random.
facts.detect: Message: A wood nymph teleports away.
facts.action: Be prepared for wood nymphs to teleport away after stealing items or when attacking them.

facts.fact: Woodchucks are not randomly generated, though they are a valid form for polymorph, and figurines and statues of them can be wished for.
facts.detect: Wishing for a figurine or statue of a woodchuck
facts.action: Wishing for a figurine or statue of a woodchuck can be a novelty or strategic choice, but it is not necessary for survival or advancement.

facts.fact: A woodchuck has a single bite attack of 1d6 damage.
facts.detect: Encountering a woodchuck in the dungeon
facts.action: Prepare to fight or avoid a woodchuck if encountered, considering its bite attack.

facts.fact: Woodchucks can tunnel through walls and trees, similar to rock moles.
facts.detect: Seeing a woodchuck near a wall or tree
facts.action: Be cautious as woodchucks can escape by tunneling through walls or trees.

facts.fact: Woodchucks can swim.
facts.detect: Encountering a woodchuck in a water-filled area
facts.action: Be prepared to fight or avoid a woodchuck in water, as it can swim.

facts.fact: Woodchucks are not especially notable to most players except for extinctionist play.
facts.detect: Considering the need to generate woodchucks for extinctionist play
facts.action: Focus on regular gameplay objectives rather than generating woodchucks unless playing as an extinctionist.

facts.fact: Woodland-elves have a single weapon attack and possess sleep resistance.
facts.detect: Encountering a Woodland-elf or seeing the message 'A woodland-elf is here.'
facts.action: Avoid melee combat if possible, especially if you do not have sleep resistance.

facts.fact: Eating a Woodland-elf corpse or tin has a 26% chance of granting sleep resistance.
facts.detect: Finding a Woodland-elf corpse or tin.
facts.action: Eat the corpse or tin to gain sleep resistance if you do not already have it.

facts.fact: Woodland-elves can generate in small groups.
facts.detect: Seeing multiple Woodland-elves on the map.
facts.action: Be cautious and prepare for multiple enemies.

facts.fact: Woodland-elves are generated with elven equipment.
facts.detect: Finding an elven mithril-coat, elven cloak, elven leather helm, elven boots, elven dagger, elven bow, elven arrows, elven short sword, elven broadsword, or elven spear.
facts.action: Loot any dropped equipment, especially if you need sleep resistance or elven items.

facts.fact: Woodland-elves are sometimes peaceful towards chaotic characters and always peaceful towards player elves.
facts.detect: Seeing a message like 'A woodland-elf approaches you.'
facts.action: If you are chaotic or an elf, try to make peace with them to avoid combat.

facts.fact: Wraiths have a life-draining touch attack and possess cold resistance, sleep resistance, poison resistance, and stoning resistance.
facts.detect: Monster name 'wraith' and attack message 'A wraith touches you!'
facts.action: Avoid melee combat with wraiths and use ranged attacks or magic if possible. Gain magic cancellation (MC3) to reduce the chance of level drain.

facts.fact: A wraith corpse has no weight and cannot be tinned, but eating it grants a level and has a 1/7 chance of being rotten.
facts.detect: Item name 'wraith corpse'
facts.action: Eat wraith corpses to gain levels, but be cautious of the 1/7 chance of it being rotten and causing instant death.

facts.fact: Wraiths are quite common in graveyards and are generated with a 20% chance on each monster placement.
facts.detect: Map feature 'graveyard' and monster name 'wraith'
facts.action: Be cautious in graveyards as wraiths are common and can drain levels.

facts.fact: Wraiths can be generated with random offensive, miscellaneous, and defensive items.
facts.detect: Monster name 'wraith' and item names such as 'wand', 'ring', 'amulet', etc.
facts.action: Be prepared for wraiths to carry items that can be dangerous or useful.

facts.fact: Wraiths leave a corpse only 2/3 of the time upon death and are less likely to leave a corpse in graveyards.
facts.detect: Monster name 'wraith' and map feature 'graveyard'
facts.action: Lure wraiths to non-graveyard levels to increase the chance of obtaining their corpses.

facts.fact: A wumpus has a single bite attack that deals 3d6 physical damage.
facts.detect: Wumpus symbol or name on the map
facts.action: Avoid melee combat with the wumpus and use ranged attacks or kiting tactics to defeat it.

facts.fact: A wumpus can cling to ceilings and move over moats without drowning.
facts.detect: Wumpus symbol or name on the map
facts.action: Be cautious when exploring areas with moats or high ceilings, as the wumpus can move freely in these areas.

facts.fact: A wumpus is generated on the Ranger quest locate level at level creation.
facts.detect: Exploring the Ranger quest locate level
facts.action: Be prepared for a wumpus encounter when exploring this level.

facts.fact: A wumpus is always generated hostile unless the hero has the Amulet of Yendor.
facts.detect: Wumpus symbol or name on the map
facts.action: Avoid or prepare for combat if you do not have the Amulet of Yendor.

facts.fact: A wumpus is the only eligible steed for riding that can also cling to ceilings.
facts.detect: Wumpus symbol or name on the map
facts.action: Consider taming a wumpus if you need a steed that can also cling to ceilings.

facts.fact: A xan has a unique sting attack that targets one of the hero's legs (or the steed's legs if the hero is riding) with roughly equal probability, and wounds them if the attack hits.
facts.detect: Xan tries to reach your leg!
facts.action: Equip iron shoes or low boots to protect legs from the sting. Use a potion of restore ability to counteract attribute damage if stung.

facts.fact: A xan corpse is poisonous to eat, and eating its corpse or tin has a 7/15 chance (46%) of granting poison resistance.
facts.detect: Xan corpse or tin
facts.action: Eat xan corpse or tin if you need poison resistance, but be prepared to use an extrinsic source like an apron or amulet versus poison or a potion of restore ability to counteract poison.

facts.fact: Xans possess poison resistance.
facts.detect: Xan
facts.action: Be cautious of xan's poison resistance when considering tactics to defeat it.

facts.fact: Randomly generated xans are always created as hostile.
facts.detect: Xan
facts.action: Avoid or prepare to fight hostile xans.

facts.fact: The xan's AC of -4 can make it difficult to hit with immobilizing or slowing items and spells for some mid-game heroes and pets.
facts.detect: Xan
facts.action: Use high to-hit weapons or wands of cancellation to reliably neutralize xans.

facts.fact: Xorns have a solid AC of -2 and an extremely nasty bite, and their phasing can make them difficult to evade.
facts.detect: Encounter a xorn on the map.
facts.action: Use a pick-axe or dwarvish mattock to attack the xorn for a +2 to-hit bonus.

facts.fact: Xorns move at a slow 9 speed and respect Elbereth, so they can be dispatched with sufficient caution.
facts.detect: See a xorn moving slowly on the map.
facts.action: Lay Elbereth symbols to stop the xorn in its tracks.

facts.fact: Xorns are likely to be generated in the throne room of the Castle at level creation.
facts.detect: Enter the throne room of the Castle.
facts.action: Be prepared to face a xorn and have a strategy to deal with its phasing ability.

facts.fact: Avoid using non-disposable iron projectiles against xorns if possible.
facts.detect: Have iron projectiles in inventory.
facts.action: Use other types of projectiles or melee weapons against xorns.

facts.fact: Xorns are the second quest monster for Monks and Wizards, and make up a significant portion of randomly generated monsters on their quests.
facts.detect: Start the Monk or Wizard quest.
facts.action: Be prepared to face multiple xorns during the quest.

facts.fact: Yeenoghu is a unique monster with a difficulty level of 31 and appears at level 25.
facts.detect: Encounter with a unique monster named Yeenoghu.
facts.action: Prepare for a high-difficulty encounter and ensure you have high-level equipment and skills.

facts.fact: Yeenoghu has a weapon attack that inflicts confusion and a claw attack that can paralyze.
facts.detect: Receive a message indicating you are getting confused or paralyzed.
facts.action: Use items or spells that protect against confusion and paralysis.

facts.fact: Yeenoghu can teleport to the upstair tile to regenerate when at low health.
facts.detect: See Yeenoghu teleport to the upstair tile.
facts.action: Block the upstair or lure Yeenoghu to a floor with a blocked upstair.

facts.fact: Yeenoghu can summon other major demons and has a high magic resistance.
facts.detect: Encounter with additional major demons or notice Yeenoghu's magic resistance.
facts.action: Prepare for additional threats and ensure you have high magic resistance.

facts.fact: Yeenoghu respects Elbereth but Elbereth does not work in Gehennom.
facts.detect: Attempt to engrave Elbereth and notice it does not work.
facts.action: Avoid fighting Yeenoghu in Gehennom unless prepared, or use alternative strategies.

facts.fact: Yellow dragons have an acid breath weapon that can ruin metal armor and weapons unless they are erosion-proofed.
facts.detect: The bot will encounter a yellow dragon and see its breath weapon icon or message.
facts.action: Equip erosion-proof armor and weapons before engaging a yellow dragon.

facts.fact: Yellow dragons have a 3/5 chance of dropping uncursed +0 yellow dragon scales upon death.
facts.detect: Upon killing a yellow dragon, the bot will see the message 'You find some yellow dragon scales.'
facts.action: Collect yellow dragon scales for their acid and stoning resistance properties.

facts.fact: Yellow dragons are generated hostile and can be found in throne rooms at dungeon levels 15 and below.
facts.detect: The bot will encounter a hostile yellow dragon in a throne room or by looting a throne while confused and carrying gold.
facts.action: Avoid or prepare for combat with yellow dragons in these areas.

facts.fact: Yellow dragons possess acid resistance and stoning resistance.
facts.detect: The bot will see the yellow dragon's resistance to acid and stoning attacks.
facts.action: Use acid resistance or stoning resistance items or spells before engaging a yellow dragon.

facts.fact: Eating a yellow dragon corpse or tin cures stoning.
facts.detect: The bot will find a yellow dragon corpse or tin.
facts.action: Eat the yellow dragon corpse or tin to cure stoning.

facts.fact: A yellow light has an explosion attack that destroys the yellow light, wakes nearby sleeping monsters, and blinds any monster hit for 10d20 turns.
facts.detect: Explosion sound and visual effect when a yellow light moves towards the bot or nearby monsters.
facts.action: Use a blindfold or towel to become blind and avoid the explosion damage. Alternatively, use a unicorn horn or cure blindness spell to remove blindness immediately after being hit.

facts.fact: Yellow lights are amorphous, can fly, and flow under doors.
facts.detect: Yellow light moving through walls or under closed doors.
facts.action: Close doors and avoid areas with open passages to prevent yellow lights from reaching the bot.

facts.fact: Yellow lights possess every resistance property minus magic resistance.
facts.detect: Yellow light taking no damage from various attacks.
facts.action: Use wands of cancellation or other methods to remove resistances before attacking.

facts.fact: If a yellow light is invisible and the hero cannot see invisible, there is an experience level-based chance that its explosion will have no effect.
facts.detect: Invisible yellow light detected by infravision or magic mapping.
facts.action: Use a blindfold or towel to become blind and avoid the explosion damage, or use a unicorn horn or cure blindness spell to remove blindness.

facts.fact: Be careful of dealing with yellow lights in or around rooms such as treasure zoos or throne rooms, as a light that explodes anywhere close to the room will wake many (if not all) of the inhabitants.
facts.detect: Yellow light near a room with sleeping monsters.
facts.action: Avoid or quickly neutralize yellow lights near such rooms to prevent waking additional dangerous monsters.

facts.fact: A yellow mold has a passive attack that stuns the attacker for some turns depending on the attacker's level.
facts.detect: Attacking a yellow mold in melee
facts.action: Use ranged attacks or wands to avoid being stunned

facts.fact: Yellow molds possess poison resistance.
facts.detect: Attempting to kill a yellow mold with poison
facts.action: Use non-poison weapons or spells

facts.fact: A yellow mold corpse is poisonous to eat.
facts.detect: Corpse of yellow mold
facts.action: Do not eat the corpse

facts.fact: Eating a yellow mold corpse or tin has a roughly 7% chance of granting poison resistance.
facts.detect: Corpse of yellow mold
facts.action: Eat corpse if you need poison resistance and are prepared for hallucination

facts.fact: Eating a yellow mold corpse or tin will always cause hallucination when finished.
facts.detect: Corpse of yellow mold
facts.action: Avoid eating if hallucination is undesirable

facts.fact: A yeti has cold resistance.
facts.detect: Monster name 'Yeti'
facts.action: Use fire-based attacks or spells against yetis.

facts.fact: Eating a yeti corpse or tin has a 33% chance of granting cold resistance.
facts.detect: Monster name 'Yeti' and corpse/tin
facts.action: Eat yeti corpse or tin to gain cold resistance.

facts.fact: Yetis have a speed of 15, faster than the largest ape.
facts.detect: Monster name 'Yeti' and player speed comparison
facts.action: Avoid melee combat with yetis if possible.

facts.fact: Yetis are always created hostile.
facts.detect: Monster name 'Yeti'
facts.action: Prepare for combat when encountering yetis.

facts.fact: Yetis appear among the random 'Y' that are part of the second quest monster class for Healers.
facts.detect: Monster name 'Yeti' and quest context
facts.action: Be cautious in Healer quest areas.

facts.fact: A zruty has an AC of 3 and attacks with Claw 3d4, Claw 3d4, Bite 3d6.
facts.detect: The message 'A zruty appears!' or seeing a zruty on the map.
facts.action: Equip the best armor and weapons available, and ensure high AC and HP before engaging.

facts.fact: Zruties are always hostile and lack any magic resistance (MR).
facts.detect: The message 'A zruty appears!' or seeing a zruty on the map.
facts.action: Use wands and spells effectively against zruties, especially if melee combat is not favorable.

facts.fact: Zruties are generated at level 9 and have a difficulty of 11.
facts.detect: The message 'A zruty appears!' or seeing a zruty on the map.
facts.action: Avoid or prepare for zruties if you are below level 9 or have not yet reached a high enough experience level.

facts.fact: Zruties are large and have a weight of 1200, providing 600 nutrition when killed.
facts.detect: Killing a zruty and seeing the nutrition message.
facts.action: Eat the corpse of a zruty to regain nutrition if needed.

facts.fact: An aklys has the same hit dice as a club versus small and large monsters, but has half the weight of a club.
facts.detect: Weapon appearance: thonged club
facts.action: Pick up and wield the aklys if it is lighter than your current weapon and you have the club skill.

facts.fact: The aklys is tethered to the hero while wielded, allowing it to be used as a projectile weapon, and it gains a +2 to-hit bonus when thrown.
facts.detect: Weapon appearance: thonged club
facts.action: Use the aklys for ranged attacks due to its tethering and +2 to-hit bonus when thrown.

facts.fact: A wielded aklys has a maximum thrown range of 4 squares and returns to the hero's hand 99/100 of the time when thrown.
facts.detect: Weapon appearance: thonged club
facts.action: Throw the aklys at enemies within 4 squares, knowing it will likely return to your hand.

facts.fact: A hero will catch a tethered aklys 99/100 of the time if they are not impaired in some manner.
facts.detect: Weapon appearance: thonged club
facts.action: Ensure you are not impaired (e.g., not blind, stunned, confused) before throwing the aklys.

facts.fact: The aklys is often associated with gnomes, who generate in large numbers in the Gnomish Mines.
facts.detect: Encounter with gnomes in the Gnomish Mines
facts.action: Look for aklyses in the Gnomish Mines as they are more likely to be found there.

facts.fact: An alchemy smock grants 1 base AC, acid resistance, poison resistance, and MC1.
facts.detect: When the bot picks up an alchemy smock and reads its description, it will see the benefits.
facts.action: Equip the alchemy smock as soon as it is found to gain poison resistance and acid resistance, which can be crucial for safety and survival.

facts.fact: An alchemy smock reduces the chance of alchemy with random potions causing explosions to 30%.
facts.detect: When the bot reads an alchemy smock, it will see the message indicating the reduced chance of explosions.
facts.action: Keep the alchemy smock equipped when experimenting with alchemy to reduce the risk of explosions.

facts.fact: An alchemy smock is one of the few extrinsic sources of acid resistance.
facts.detect: The bot can check its inventory and see the alchemy smock as a potential source of acid resistance.
facts.action: Equip the alchemy smock if there are no other sources of acid resistance and if the bot expects to encounter acid damage.

facts.fact: An alchemy smock can be given to humanoid pets to provide them with poison resistance.
facts.detect: The bot can identify humanoid pets in its inventory or on the map.
facts.action: Give the alchemy smock to a humanoid pet if the bot has gained poison resistance and does not need the smock for itself.

facts.fact: Reading an alchemy smock breaks illiterate conduct.
facts.detect: When the bot reads an alchemy smock, it will see a message breaking the illiterate conduct.
facts.action: Avoid reading the alchemy smock if the bot is playing under the illiterate conduct.

facts.fact: An amulet of ESP is the most common amulet, making up 12% of all randomly-generated amulets.
facts.detect: Finding an amulet in the game inventory or on the ground.
facts.action: Wear the amulet of ESP to gain extrinsic telepathy, which allows seeing non-mindless monsters within an 8-square radius and helps in navigating and identifying monsters.

facts.fact: Eating the amulet of ESP has a 1/5 chance of giving intrinsic telepathy.
facts.detect: Eating the amulet of ESP and checking for the intrinsic telepathy message.
facts.action: If intrinsic telepathy is gained, the amulet can be discarded as it is no longer needed.

facts.fact: The amulet of ESP is one of the better amulets early on, especially for casting-focused players.
facts.detect: Being a casting-focused player (Lawful Valkyrie can benefit from spellcasting).
facts.action: Prioritize keeping the amulet of ESP early in the game to aid in spellcasting and monster identification.

facts.fact: In the later game, the amulet of ESP is often replaced by the amulet of reflection or amulet of life saving.
facts.detect: Reaching a point in the game where other amulets are available.
facts.action: Consider swapping the amulet of ESP for an amulet of reflection or amulet of life saving if they are found.

facts.fact: The amulet of ESP can be informally identified by using ';' to far look and select a monster that you shouldn't be able to see.
facts.detect: Using ';' to far look and select a monster behind a closed door or out of sight.
facts.action: If the far look reveals the monster's location, it confirms the amulet of ESP is worn.

facts.fact: The Amulet of Yendor is located in Moloch's Sanctum within Gehennom, where it is always generated in the possession of the high priest of Moloch.
facts.detect: High priest of Moloch in Moloch's Sanctum
facts.action: Defeat the high priest of Moloch to obtain the Amulet of Yendor

facts.fact: Carrying the Amulet of Yendor decreases nutrition by 1 every 20 turns, in addition to normal amulet or ring hunger.
facts.detect: Decrease in nutrition while carrying the Amulet
facts.action: Eat food or use potions of fullness to maintain nutrition while carrying the Amulet

facts.fact: Spellcasting while carrying the Amulet will drain a random amount of additional energy up to twice the normal cost of the selected spell.
facts.detect: Message 'You feel the Amulet draining your energy away.'
facts.action: Avoid spellcasting while carrying the Amulet or prepare for high energy costs

facts.fact: The Amulet of Yendor has a {{frac|15}} chance of detecting magic portals within a certain radius.
facts.detect: Messages 'The Amulet of Yendor feels hot!', 'The Amulet of Yendor feels very warm.', 'The Amulet of Yendor feels warm.'
