facts.action: Use the Amulet to detect magic portals and navigate the dungeon

facts.fact: Offering the Amulet of Yendor on a high altar corresponding to your god results in ascension.
facts.detect: High altar of your god
facts.action: Offer the Amulet on the high altar of your god to ascend

facts.fact: The amulet of change generates as cursed 90.5% of the time, blessed 0.5% of the time, and uncursed otherwise (9%).
facts.detect: Cursed status of the amulet when picked up
facts.action: Avoid putting on a cursed amulet of change to prevent gender change and amulet destruction.

facts.fact: Putting on an amulet of change will use up the amulet, instantly change the gender of the hero's base form, and auto-identify the amulet.
facts.detect: Message 'You are suddenly very !' when putting on the amulet
facts.action: If the bot is a lawful dwarf and does not need to change gender, avoid putting on the amulet to prevent wasting an item.

facts.fact: Eating the amulet has a 5% chance of absorbing its magic and changing the hero's gender.
facts.detect: Message 'You don't feel like yourself.' after eating the amulet
facts.action: If the bot is a lawful dwarf and does not need to change gender, avoid eating the amulet to prevent wasting an item.

facts.fact: A male hero can reliably become female to polymorph into a dragon or other oviparous monster to lay eggs.
facts.detect: The bot is a male dwarf
facts.action: If the bot needs to lay eggs, consider using the amulet of change to become female and then polymorph into an oviparous monster.

facts.fact: The amulet can be used to play male Valkyries, which is a role/gender combination that cannot be obtained otherwise.
facts.detect: The bot is a female Valkyrie
facts.action: If the bot needs to become a male Valkyrie, use the amulet of change to change gender.

facts.fact: Amulets of life saving make up 7.5% of all amulets randomly generated on the ground, in general shops or as death drops.
facts.detect: Finding an amulet of life saving in a shop or on the ground.
facts.action: Pick up the amulet of life saving if found, as it can be crucial for survival.

facts.fact: An intelligent monster that is not a Keystone Kop or a nonliving creature has a base 20% chance of being generated with an amulet of life saving.
facts.detect: Observing an intelligent monster wearing an amulet of life saving.
facts.action: Stealthily approach and attempt to steal the amulet from the monster before it puts it on.

facts.fact: An amulet of life saving is generated inside a chest within a niche on the middle floor of Vlad's Tower during normal level creation.
facts.detect: Exploring Vlad's Tower and finding a chest within a niche on the middle floor.
facts.action: Open the chest and take the amulet of life saving if present.

facts.fact: If a hero's life is saved by the amulet, their constitution is reduced by one point.
facts.detect: Noticing a reduction in constitution after being revived.
facts.action: Keep track of constitution points to avoid overusing the amulet.

facts.fact: Monsters will put on the amulet of life saving unless they are nonliving or a shapeshifted vampire.
facts.detect: Observing a monster wearing an amulet of life saving.
facts.action: Stealthily approach and attempt to steal the amulet from the monster before it puts it on.

facts.fact: An amulet of magical breathing makes up 7.5% of all amulets that are randomly generated on the ground, in general shops or as death drops.
facts.detect: Finding an amulet of magical breathing in a random drop or shop inventory.
facts.action: Pick up the amulet of magical breathing if found.

facts.fact: Wearing an amulet of magical breathing grants the breathless property, making the hero amphibious and preventing drowning.
facts.detect: Entering water and not drowning.
facts.action: Wear the amulet of magical breathing when entering water.

facts.fact: Poison clouds will not damage a hero with a worn amulet of magical breathing.
facts.detect: Entering a poison cloud and not taking damage.
facts.action: Wear the amulet of magical breathing when entering poison clouds.

facts.fact: Wearing the amulet of magical breathing increases the dice used for determining the amount of energy the hero recovers by 2.
facts.detect: Noticing increased energy recovery when wearing the amulet.
facts.action: Wear the amulet of magical breathing to increase energy recovery.

facts.fact: Monsters will not wear this amulet.
facts.detect: Observing that monsters do not wear amulets.
facts.action: Loot amulets from monsters without fear of them being worn.

facts.fact: An amulet of reflection makes up 7.5% of all amulets randomly generated on the ground, in general shops or as death drops.
facts.detect: Finding an amulet on the ground, in shops, or as a death drop.
facts.action: Pick up the amulet and test it for reflection properties.

facts.fact: The amulet of reflection has a 90% chance of generating uncursed, a 10% chance of generating blessed, and a 10% of generating cursed.
facts.detect: Checking the amulet's status when picked up.
facts.action: If cursed, remove it immediately to avoid negative effects.

facts.fact: The Sokoban prize on the final floor of the branch has a 50% chance of being an amulet of reflection.
facts.detect: Entering Sokoban and reaching the final floor.
facts.action: Explore Sokoban carefully to find the amulet.

facts.fact: The amulet of reflection auto-identifies if it reflects a ray or gaze attack.
facts.detect: Receiving the message 'But it reflects from your medallion!' or 'The floating eye's gaze is reflected by your medallion.'
facts.action: Use a wand of magic missile or attack a floating eye to test for reflection.

facts.fact: Monsters may wear the amulet of reflection, especially in Sokoban.
facts.detect: Seeing a monster wearing the amulet or finding a Sokoban closet with a scroll of scare monster but no prize.
facts.action: Avoid using reflectable wands or spells until the amulet is retrieved or the monster is dealt with.

facts.fact: There is a 13.5% chance that a randomly-generated amulet will be an amulet of restful sleep.
facts.detect: Picking up or identifying an amulet
facts.action: Avoid wearing unidentified amulets to prevent falling asleep in dangerous situations.

facts.fact: The amulet is generated cursed 90.5% of the time, uncursed 9% of the time, and blessed 0.5% of the time.
facts.detect: Identifying the amulet's status
facts.action: If the amulet is cursed, avoid wearing it to prevent forced sleep.

facts.fact: You will fall asleep sometime within 100 turns of wearing the amulet, awakening within 1 to 20 turns or when disturbed.
facts.detect: The message 'You yawn.'
facts.action: Remove the amulet immediately to avoid falling asleep in dangerous situations.

facts.fact: Sleep resistance will not cure the condition, but prevents you from actually falling asleep.
facts.detect: Having sleep resistance
facts.action: If you have sleep resistance, you can safely wear the amulet without falling asleep.

facts.fact: Eating the amulet can confer intrinsic restful sleep, causing you to randomly fall asleep with the same effects.
facts.detect: Eating an amulet
facts.action: Avoid eating unidentified amulets to prevent gaining intrinsic restful sleep.

facts.fact: An amulet of strangulation generates as cursed 90.5% of the time.
facts.detect: Message: 'You are being strangled.'
facts.action: Immediately remove the amulet if worn and unidentified.

facts.fact: An amulet of strangulation is always generated in a chest on the middle floor of Vlad's Tower.
facts.detect: Location: Middle floor of Vlad's Tower, chest.
facts.action: Avoid opening chests in Vlad's Tower without identifying amulets first.

facts.fact: Eating an amulet of strangulation has a 20% chance of choking the hero to death.
facts.detect: Item: Amulet of strangulation in inventory.
facts.action: Do not eat unidentified amulets.

facts.fact: Prayer can destroy a worn cursed amulet of strangulation and abort strangulation.
facts.detect: Message: 'You are being strangled.'
facts.action: Pray if wearing a cursed amulet of strangulation.

facts.fact: Wand of cancellation can uncurse and allow removal of an amulet of strangulation.
facts.detect: Item: Amulet of strangulation, Wand of cancellation in inventory.
facts.action: Use wand of cancellation on amulet if other methods of uncursing fail.

facts.fact: Amulets of unchanging make up 4.5% of all amulets randomly generated on the ground, in general shops or as death drops.
facts.detect: Finding an amulet on the ground or in a shop.
facts.action: Pick up the amulet and keep it for later identification.

facts.fact: Wearing an amulet of unchanging prevents polymorphing and changing form by any means, including sliming.
facts.detect: Being slimed while wearing the amulet.
facts.action: Notice that the sliming is immediately cured.

facts.fact: If a hero dies while polymorphed and wearing an amulet of unchanging, they will die in their current form.
facts.detect: Dying while polymorphed.
facts.action: Avoid dying while polymorphed and wearing the amulet.

facts.fact: An amulet of unchanging can be identified by wearing it while eating a mimic corpse and not turning into a pile of gold.
facts.detect: Eating a mimic corpse while wearing the amulet.
facts.action: Check if the amulet prevents polymorphing into gold.

facts.fact: An amulet of unchanging can be identified by wearing it while using a polymorph trap and receiving the standard message for a blocked polymorph.
facts.detect: Using a polymorph trap while wearing the amulet.
facts.action: Check if the polymorph trap does not disappear and the standard message is received.

facts.fact: An amulet versus poison provides extrinsic poison resistance when worn.
facts.detect: Wearing the amulet and encountering a poisonous monster or eating a poisonous corpse without taking damage.
facts.action: Wear the amulet versus poison to gain poison resistance, especially before encountering poisonous monsters or eating poisonous corpses.

facts.fact: Eating an amulet versus poison has a 50% chance of granting intrinsic poison resistance.
facts.detect: Eating the amulet and checking for the message 'You feel less hungry.' or 'You gain poison resistance.'
facts.action: Eat the amulet versus poison if you are in a safe environment and need intrinsic poison resistance.

facts.fact: The amulet versus poison is the second-most common type of amulet, making up 16.5% of all randomly generated amulets.
facts.detect: Finding an amulet on the ground or in a shop.
facts.action: Prioritize identifying and using the amulet versus poison if you lack poison resistance.

facts.fact: Once intrinsic poison resistance is gained, the amulet can be removed and stashed as a backup.
facts.detect: Gaining intrinsic poison resistance.
facts.action: Remove the amulet versus poison and store it for later use if intrinsic poison resistance is lost.

facts.fact: Unicorn horns or other methods of restoring lost attributes can be used to test the amulet versus poison safely.
facts.detect: Finding a unicorn horn or a potion of restore ability.
facts.action: Use a unicorn horn or potion of restore ability to test the amulet versus poison without risking intrinsic loss.

facts.fact: Apples grant 50 nutrition and take 1 turn to consume.
facts.detect: Item name: apple
facts.action: Eat apples to maintain nutrition when hungry.

facts.fact: Healers, Monks, and Knights start with 5-10, 5-10, and 10-20 apples respectively.
facts.detect: Starting inventory message
facts.action: Eat starting apples if extra permafood is scarce.

facts.fact: Cursed apples cause sleep for 20-30 turns unless sleep resistance is present.
facts.detect: Message: This smells like it might have been poisoned.
facts.action: Do not eat cursed apples unless sleep resistance is present.

facts.fact: Apples can be thrown to tame domestic herbivorous monsters and pacify domestic carnivores.
facts.detect: Monster name: domestic herbivorous or carnivorous
facts.action: Use apples to tame or pacify pets.

facts.fact: Apples have a 1.5% chance of randomly generating on the ground, in shops, or as death drops.
facts.detect: Randomly generated item: apple
facts.action: Collect apples for nutrition or pet management.

facts.fact: Human Rangers start the game with two separate stacks of +0 and +2 arrows for their bow.
facts.detect: Starting inventory includes +0 and +2 arrows.
facts.action: Use the +2 arrows for ranged attacks and save the +0 arrows for later if needed.

facts.fact: Stacks of arrows make up 5.5% of all weapons randomly generated on the ground, in general shops or as death drops.
facts.detect: Finding arrows in shops or on the ground.
facts.action: Collect arrows to ensure a steady supply for ranged attacks.

facts.fact: Forest centaurs have a 1/2 chance of being generated with a bow and a stack of arrows.
facts.detect: Encountering a forest centaur with a bow and arrows.
facts.action: Steal the bow and arrows from the centaur if possible.

facts.fact: A humanoid monster with a weapon attack, the ability to wield weapons and no other ruleset governing its monster starting inventory has a chance of generating with a stack of arrows accompanying a bow.
facts.detect: Encountering a humanoid monster with a bow and arrows.
facts.action: Steal the bow and arrows from the monster if possible.

facts.fact: An arrow trap will shoot an arrow at any monster or hero that steps on their square until they run out of arrows, and untrapping them produces 50-rnl(50) arrows.
facts.detect: Stepping on an arrow trap.
facts.action: Avoid stepping on arrow traps or disarm them if possible.

facts.fact: An athame is a one-handed weapon with 1d4 small damage, 1d3 large damage, +2 to-hit, and uses the dagger skill.
facts.detect: Weapon name 'athame' in inventory or on the ground
facts.action: Equip the athame if dagger skill is high and no better weapon is available

facts.fact: Athames are not randomly generated but can be wished for or found in bones levels.
facts.detect: Finding an athame in bones levels or wishing for it
facts.action: Pick up and use the athame if no better weapon is available

facts.fact: An arch-lich has a 2/9 chance of generating with an athame, which may be erosion-proofed and enchanted.
facts.detect: Encountering an arch-lich with an athame
facts.action: Steal or take the athame if it is erosion-proofed and enchanted

facts.fact: Athames are designed for engraving and can engrave up to 19 letters per turn unless cursed.
facts.detect: Weapon name 'athame' and checking for curse status
facts.action: Use the athame for engraving Elbereth if not cursed and has high enchantment

facts.fact: Magicbane, an artifact athame, can be generated with a 1/1170 chance from an arch-lich.
facts.detect: Encountering an arch-lich and checking for Magicbane
facts.action: Prioritize obtaining Magicbane if generated

facts.fact: An axe deals 1d6 damage versus small monsters and 1d4 versus large monsters, and it can be thrown without a to-hit penalty.
facts.detect: Weapon name 'axe' in inventory
facts.action: Use axe to throw at distant enemies or to deal damage to small monsters

facts.fact: A hero eating a non-blessed tin while wielding an axe will use the weapon to open it in six turns at most.
facts.detect: Message 'You use your axe to open the can.'
facts.action: Wield an axe when eating non-blessed tins to open them faster

facts.fact: A hero can apply an axe to chop down adjacent trees and break through doors.
facts.detect: Adjacent trees or closed doors
facts.action: Use axe to chop down trees or break through doors

facts.fact: Axes deal +d4 damage versus wood golems.
facts.detect: Encounter with a wood golem
facts.action: Use axe to deal extra damage to wood golems

facts.fact: An axe is very useful for heroes without unlocking tools as a means of breaking through locked doors.
facts.detect: Locked door
facts.action: Use axe to break through locked doors

facts.fact: A bag of holding can be generated as a prize in Sokoban with a 3/4 chance on Level 4a and a 1/4 chance on Level 4b.
facts.detect: Finding a bag of holding in one of the three closets behind the treasure zoo on Sokoban Level 4a or 4b.
facts.action: Pick up the bag of holding and ensure it is not cursed before storing valuable items inside.

facts.fact: A cursed bag of holding doubles the weight of its contents and has a 1/3 chance per stack that items inside will vanish.
facts.detect: Noticing a significant increase in encumbrance or items disappearing when interacting with a bag of holding.
facts.action: Avoid storing valuable items in a cursed bag of holding and try to uncursed it if possible.

facts.fact: Placing certain items inside a bag of holding can cause an explosion, destroying the bag and the item and scattering the contents.
facts.detect: Recognizing items like bags of tricks, wands of cancellation, or other bags of holding.
facts.action: Avoid placing these items inside a bag of holding to prevent accidental explosions.

facts.fact: Nesting bags of holding can reduce the chance of explosion, but the risk increases with more nesting.
facts.detect: Having multiple bags of holding and sacks to nest them.
facts.action: Use nesting carefully, ensuring the number of sacks between bags of holding is sufficient to reduce the risk of explosion.

facts.fact: A bag of holding can protect its contents from breaking but not from water damage unless greased or placed in a non-cursed oilskin sack.
facts.detect: Encountering water or noticing items getting wet inside the bag.
facts.action: Apply grease to the bag or place it in a non-cursed oilskin sack to protect against water damage.

facts.fact: Placing a charged bag of tricks, charged wand of cancellation, or another bag of holding inside a bag of holding causes it to explode, destroying both objects and their contents.
facts.detect: Exact message: 'As you put inside, you are blasted by a magical explosion!'
facts.action: Avoid placing charged bag of tricks, charged wand of cancellation, or another bag of holding inside a bag of holding.

facts.fact: In NetHack 3.6, Sokoban offers a choice between 3 items, with one being a bag of holding.
facts.detect: Sokoban level item choice screen
facts.action: Select the bag of holding if it is one of the three items offered.

facts.fact: In NetHack 3.6, the final floor of Sokoban (Open at the Top) always has a bag of holding as its prize.
facts.detect: Final Sokoban level (Open at the Top)
facts.action: Take the bag of holding as the prize from the final Sokoban level.

facts.fact: A bag of tricks is a tool that appears in NetHack, made of cloth, and appears as an ordinary bag when unidentified.
facts.detect: bag (when unidentified)
facts.action: Do not use until identified to avoid taking damage.

facts.fact: Applying a charged bag of tricks will use up one charge and either create one monster adjacent to them with a 22/23 chance, otherwise creating 2 to 8 monsters adjacent to them.
facts.detect: Applying a bag of tricks
facts.action: Only use in safe areas or when prepared to handle multiple monsters.

facts.fact: Placing a charged bag of tricks into a bag of holding will cause a magical explosion, destroying both bags as well as everything in the bag of holding.
facts.detect: Carrying both a bag of tricks and a bag of holding
facts.action: Avoid carrying both items together to prevent accidental explosions.

facts.fact: A bag of tricks can hold a maximum of 50 charges and can be recharged indefinitely.
facts.detect: Charges remaining on the bag
facts.action: Recharge when necessary to maintain usefulness.

facts.fact: If you only want the bag to polypile with, apply it until it runs out of charges, and make sure you can deal with the generated monsters.
facts.detect: Applying the bag of tricks
facts.action: Use cautiously for polypiling, ensuring readiness to handle generated monsters.

facts.fact: Bananas make up 1% of all comestibles randomly generated on the ground, in general shops or as death drops.
facts.detect: Banana item name
facts.action: Pick up bananas when found as they provide 80 nutrition and are vegan-friendly.

facts.fact: Kicking a tree has a one-time 8/15 chance of dropping 1 to 8 bananas.
facts.detect: Kicking a tree
facts.action: Kick trees to potentially obtain bananas for nutrition.

facts.fact: Cutting down a tree has a 1/5 chance of producing a banana.
facts.detect: Cutting down a tree
facts.action: Cut down trees to potentially obtain bananas for nutrition.

facts.fact: A tree that is tunneled through has a 1/3 chance of leaving behind bananas.
facts.detect: Tunneling through a tree
facts.action: Tunnel through trees to potentially obtain bananas for nutrition.

facts.fact: A hero can throw bananas to tame domestic herbivorous monsters as well as apes and monkeys.
facts.detect: Encountering apes, monkeys, or domestic herbivorous monsters
facts.action: Use bananas to tame these monsters when encountered.

facts.fact: Banded mail is a type of body armor that appears in NetHack with an AC of 6 and costs 90 gold pieces.
facts.detect: Item name: banded mail
facts.action: Equip banded mail if it provides better AC than current armor and does not exceed carrying capacity.

facts.fact: Banded mail makes up 7.2% of all armor randomly generated on the ground, in general shops, or as death drops.
facts.detect: Item name: banded mail in shops or on the ground
facts.action: Prioritize picking up banded mail if it is available and beneficial to AC.

facts.fact: The Valkyrie quest leader, the Norn, is always generated with +5 banded mail.
facts.detect: Encounter with the Norn
facts.action: If the Norn is encountered, prepare to fight or flee based on readiness for combat.

facts.fact: Player monster barbarians, knights, clerics, and valkyries have an effective 11.61% chance of forcing banded mail in place of their initial body armor.
facts.detect: Character role: barbarian, knight, cleric, or valkyrie
facts.action: Expect to start with banded mail if character is one of these roles.

facts.fact: A bardiche is a two-handed polearm that appears as a long poleaxe when unidentified.
facts.detect: long poleaxe
facts.action: Identify the weapon as a bardiche if it appears as a long poleaxe.

facts.fact: The bardiche has some of the best damage among the polearms, though it is also among the heavier polearms at 120 aum.
facts.detect: bardiche weight
facts.action: Consider the weight when deciding whether to wield the bardiche, especially if you have a preference for lighter weapons.

facts.fact: Bardiches have the highest average damage against large monsters.
facts.detect: encountering large monsters
facts.action: Use the bardiche against large monsters to maximize damage output.

facts.fact: Bardiches' average damage against small monsters is also among the best, with only the halberd outperforming it in that regard.
facts.detect: encountering small monsters
facts.action: Use the bardiche against small monsters if you do not have a halberd.

facts.fact: A battle-axe is a two-handed melee weapon that uses the axe skill and appears as a double-headed axe when unidentified.
facts.detect: double-headed axe
facts.action: Identify the weapon as a battle-axe and use it if you have the axe skill and sufficient strength.

facts.fact: Barbarians have a 50% chance of starting the game with a +0 battle-axe as their starting axe weapon.
facts.detect: Starting as a barbarian
facts.action: If you are a barbarian, expect to start with a battle-axe and use it effectively.

facts.fact: Battle-axes make up 1% of all weapons that are randomly generated on the floor, in general shops or as death drops.
facts.detect: Finding a battle-axe in the dungeon
facts.action: Pick up and use a battle-axe if you have the axe skill and sufficient strength.

facts.fact: Ogres, ogre lords, and ogre kings have a chance of generating with battle-axes.
facts.detect: Encountering ogres, ogre lords, or ogre kings
facts.action: Be prepared to fight enemies wielding battle-axes.

facts.fact: Battle-axes can become a nuisance when cursed, making them an unpopular choice to use past the mid-game.
facts.detect: Cursed battle-axe
facts.action: Avoid using a cursed battle-axe and seek curse removal items.

facts.fact: A beartrap appears as a cyan caret glyph (^) upon being revealed.
facts.detect: Cyan caret (^) glyph on the map
facts.action: Avoid walking over it to prevent triggering it

facts.fact: A hero that successfully untraps a live bear trap will generate an uncursed beartrap item on the former trap's square.
facts.detect: Message: You untrap a bear trap.
facts.action: Pick up the uncursed beartrap item

facts.fact: A hero that is not fumbling will avoid a bear trap 5/8 of the time, or 4/5 of the time if they know the trap's location.
facts.detect: Knowing the location of the trap
facts.action: Move carefully around known traps

facts.fact: A hero that digs down on a beartrap's square disarms that beartrap.
facts.detect: Message: You dig down.
facts.action: Use digging to disarm traps

facts.fact: A hero can escape a bear trap by moving diagonally, which is most effective.
facts.detect: Being trapped in a bear trap
facts.action: Move diagonally to escape the trap

facts.fact: A bec de corbin is a two-handed polearm that appears as a beaked polearm when unidentified.
facts.detect: beaked polearm
facts.action: Identify the weapon as a bec de corbin when found.

facts.fact: Ravens generated while the hero is wielding a bec de corbin are created peaceful.
facts.detect: wielding a bec de corbin and encountering a raven
facts.action: Ravens will not attack if you are wielding a bec de corbin.

facts.fact: The bec de corbin offers decent damage against small monsters compared to other polearms.
facts.detect: Encountering small monsters while wielding a bec de corbin
facts.action: Use the bec de corbin effectively against small monsters.

facts.fact: The bec de corbin has the lowest average damage against large monsters alongside the lucern hammer.
facts.detect: Encountering large monsters while wielding a bec de corbin
facts.action: Avoid using the bec de corbin against large monsters.

facts.fact: Elven Priests and Wizards have a 6/35 chance of starting with a bell as their non-magical instrument.
facts.detect: Starting inventory includes a bell
facts.action: If the bot starts with a bell, it should keep it for potential use in deterring covetous thieves or as a backup for the Bell of Opening.

facts.fact: A bell makes noise that wakes nearby sleeping monsters and calls pets when applied.
facts.detect: You ring the bell.
facts.action: Use the bell to call pets or wake up sleeping monsters when needed, but be cautious of potential danger from waking monsters.

facts.fact: A cursed bell has a 25% chance of summoning a random nymph without their starting inventory.
facts.detect: You summon a nymph!
facts.action: If a nymph is summoned, the bot should prepare to fight or avoid it, especially if the bot is not well-equipped.

facts.fact: A cursed bell has a 7% chance of breaking after summoning a nymph.
facts.detect: The bell has shattered!
facts.action: If the bell breaks, the bot should discard it and not attempt to use it again.

facts.fact: A cursed bell has a 3/4 chance of summoning a fast nymph and a 1/3 chance of paralyzing the hero for 2 turns.
facts.detect: You summon a nymph!
facts.action: If a fast nymph is summoned, the bot should be prepared to move quickly or use items to counteract the paralysis.

facts.fact: The Bell of Opening is guarded by the quest nemesis and appears as a silver bell when unidentified.
facts.detect: Encounter with the quest nemesis or seeing a silver bell in inventory.
facts.action: Prepare to fight the quest nemesis and ensure you have the means to protect the bell.

facts.fact: The Bell of Opening can detect secret doors, magic portals, and traps within a radius of 8 squares when applied and has 3 charges initially.
facts.detect: Applying the bell and observing the detection of hidden features.
facts.action: Use the bell to detect hidden features in dungeons to avoid traps and find secret doors.

facts.fact: A blessed Bell of Opening can open nearby objects and dungeon features.
facts.detect: Applying the bell and observing objects or features opening.
facts.action: Use the bell to open chests, doors, and drawbridges to access items or areas.

facts.fact: A cursed Bell of Opening will wake nearby monsters and raise the dead.
facts.detect: Applying the bell and observing monsters waking or corpses rising.
facts.action: Avoid using the bell if it is cursed to prevent unwanted consequences.

facts.fact: The Bell of Opening must be applied second during the Invocation after lighting the Candelabrum of Invocation.
facts.detect: Completing the quest and entering Moloch's Sanctum.
facts.action: Ensure the bell is non-cursed and charged before the invocation ritual.

facts.fact: A bill-guisarme is a two-handed polearm that appears as a hooked polearm when unidentified.
facts.detect: hooked polearm
facts.action: Identify the weapon as a bill-guisarme when found.

facts.fact: Bill-guisarmes can be found in general shops and antique weapons outlets.
facts.detect: Exploring shops and antique weapons outlets
facts.action: Check these locations for bill-guisarmes.

facts.fact: Watchmen and soldiers may be generated with a bill-guisarme.
facts.detect: Encountering watchmen or soldiers
facts.action: Be prepared to fight for the bill-guisarme if they carry one.

facts.fact: The bill-guisarme is tied for the third-heaviest polearm with the bardiche.
facts.detect: Comparing the weight of the bill-guisarme to other polearms
facts.action: Consider the weight when deciding to wield it.

facts.fact: The bill-guisarme offers relatively high damage against small monsters and decent average damage against large monsters.
facts.detect: Evaluating the damage stats of the bill-guisarme
facts.action: Use it effectively against small and large monsters.

facts.fact: A blindfold renders the character blind and unable to see while worn.
facts.detect: You can't see anymore.
facts.action: Use the blindfold to avoid harmful gaze attacks from monsters like floating eyes, lights, and Medusa.

facts.fact: A cursed blindfold cannot be removed normally.
facts.detect: You still cannot see.
facts.action: Find a way to uncursed the blindfold or find another method to remove it.

facts.fact: A blindfold is guaranteed to appear within one of the niches on the first floor of Vlad's Tower.
facts.detect: Finding a blindfold in a niche on the first floor of Vlad's Tower.
facts.action: Pick up the blindfold and keep it for later use.

facts.fact: A blindfold is useful for scanning the level for non-mindless monsters with intrinsic and/or extrinsic telepathy.
facts.detect: Having intrinsic or extrinsic telepathy.
facts.action: Use the blindfold to scan the level for monsters.

facts.fact: A blindfold can help prevent monsters from using an expensive camera against the character.
facts.detect: Encountering a monster with an expensive camera.
facts.action: Wear the blindfold to avoid the camera's effects.

facts.fact: The Book of the Dead is one of the three unique items needed for the invocation in NetHack.
facts.detect: Wizard of Yendor generated with the Book of the Dead on his square in the Wizard's Tower.
facts.action: Retrieve the Book of the Dead from the Wizard's Tower to prepare for the invocation.

facts.fact: The Book of the Dead can be read even if you are blind.
facts.detect: Blind status and presence of the Book of the Dead.
facts.action: Read the Book of the Dead while blind to ensure progress in the zen conduct.

facts.fact: If you read the Book of the Dead while performing the invocation and standing on the vibrating square, and you lack the Bell of Opening or the Candelabrum of Invocation, or else any of the artifacts are cursed, nothing happens.
facts.detect: Messages indicating missing items or cursed artifacts.
facts.action: Ensure you have the Bell of Opening and the Candelabrum of Invocation and that they are not cursed before attempting the invocation.

facts.fact: If you fail to prepare the invocation items, or read a cursed Book of the Dead when not on the vibrating square, you will raise the dead.
facts.detect: Cursed Book of the Dead and not standing on the vibrating square.
facts.action: Avoid reading a cursed Book of the Dead unless you are on the vibrating square and have the necessary artifacts.

facts.fact: Raising the dead is a viable strategy to farm wraith corpses.
facts.detect: Presence of wraith corpses.
facts.action: Use the cursed Book of the Dead to raise the dead and farm wraith corpses.

facts.fact: A boomerang deals 1d9 damage to all monsters that it hits when thrown.
facts.detect: Throwing a boomerang at a monster
facts.action: Use boomerang to deal significant damage to monsters from a distance

facts.fact: Boomerangs do not mulch upon hitting a monster and their flight path can pass through iron bars.
facts.detect: Boomerang passing through iron bars or hitting a monster without stopping
facts.action: Use boomerang to attack through iron bars or to hit multiple monsters in a line

facts.fact: When thrown, a boomerang will travel in a circular path from the direction it was thrown and hit anything in its path.
facts.detect: Observing the boomerang's flight path on the map
facts.action: Throw boomerang in a strategic direction to hit multiple monsters or to avoid obstacles

facts.fact: If a boomerang thrown by the hero makes its way back to them, they have a DEX/20 chance of catching the boomerang safely.
facts.detect: Boomerang returning to the hero
facts.action: Attempt to catch the boomerang if DEX is 20 or higher

facts.fact: Boomerangs can be 'multishot' by throwing them multiple times in one action, which will be aborted if a returning boomerang hits the hero.
facts.detect: Attempting to throw multiple boomerangs in one action
facts.action: Throw boomerangs in rapid succession to hit multiple targets, but be cautious of returning boomerangs

facts.fact: Boulders are too heavy for you to lift normally and block line of sight.
facts.detect: Cannot move to a space occupied by a boulder, boulder blocking line of sight.
facts.action: Push boulders out of the way to move or see around them.

facts.fact: Tunneling monsters leave behind boulders on 8.3% of diggable rock squares.
facts.detect: Boulder appears after a tunneling monster has been in the area.
facts.action: Be cautious when exploring areas where tunneling monsters have been active.

facts.fact: Non-undead giants and titans have a 50% chance of generating with a boulder.
facts.detect: A giant or titan appears with a boulder next to it.
facts.action: Avoid or prepare to fight giants and titans that have boulders.

facts.fact: A rolling boulder trap will roll a boulder to the opposite side if a character or monster steps on the trigger square.
facts.detect: A boulder starts rolling towards you or others in the room.
facts.action: Avoid stepping on squares that might trigger a rolling boulder trap.

facts.fact: Pushing a boulder into a hole, trap door, or pit will usually plug it and turn that square into normal floor.
facts.detect: A boulder is pushed into a hole, trap door, or pit.
facts.action: Use boulders to plug holes, trap doors, or pits to prevent falling or other hazards.

facts.fact: You should determine whether a monster on the other side of a boulder is hostile before deciding how to proceed.
facts.detect: Telepathy or monster detection reveals the monster's hostility.
facts.action: If peaceful, try to squeeze past or use a magic whistle to move pets. If hostile, prepare to fight.

facts.fact: Squeezing onto a boulder to check the other side can be risky and may drop your inventory.
facts.detect: Inventory is dropped when squeezing onto a boulder.
facts.action: Retrieve dropped inventory promptly and consider using autopickup.

facts.fact: Squeezing through boulders in Sokoban incurs a -1 Luck penalty.
facts.detect: Message 'You try to squeeze through the boulder.'
facts.action: Avoid squeezing if possible to maintain Luck.

facts.fact: Two consecutive boulders in a corridor can be managed by squeezing past one to push the other.
facts.detect: Two boulders in a row in a corridor.
facts.action: Squeeze past the first boulder to push the second.

facts.fact: A 2x2 square of boulders or walls is considered stuck and cannot be moved diagonally.
facts.detect: A 2x2 square of boulders or walls.
facts.action: Avoid creating such formations to keep level solvable.

facts.fact: Human Rangers start the game with a +1 bow and two separate stacks of +0 and +2 arrows as ammunition.
facts.detect: Starting inventory as a Human Ranger
facts.action: If the bot is a Human Ranger, it should use the +1 bow and the +2 arrows for better accuracy and damage.

facts.fact: Bows make up 2.4% of all weapons that are randomly generated on the ground, in general shops or as death drops.
facts.detect: Finding a bow in the dungeon or shops
facts.action: The bot should pick up and use bows when found, especially if they are enchanted.

facts.fact: The themed room containing the ghost of an adventurer and their 'bones' pile has an independent 9/20 chance of including a bow and arrows in the pile.
facts.detect: Entering a themed room with a ghost and bones pile
facts.action: The bot should check the bones pile for a bow and arrows.

facts.fact: One of the weapons in the item pile guarded by the ghost on the Rogue level is a +1 bow with an accompanying set of +0 arrows that each have a 3/4 chance of being cursed.
facts.detect: Entering the Rogue level and encountering the ghost
facts.action: The bot should be cautious and identify the +1 bow and +0 arrows before using them.

facts.fact: Several monsters can be generated with bows accompanied by arrows as ammunition.
facts.detect: Encountering monsters like chieftains, pages, roshi, warriors, hunters, forest centaurs, and humanoid monsters with weapon attacks
facts.action: The bot should be prepared to disarm these monsters and take their bows and arrows if they are useful.

facts.fact: Broadswords make up 0.8% of all randomly generated weapons.
facts.detect: Finding a broadsword on the ground or in a shop.
facts.action: Pick up a broadsword if no better weapon is available, but prioritize finding an elven broadsword or other superior weapon.

facts.fact: Lieutenants have a roughly 2/3 chance of being generated with a broadsword.
facts.detect: Encountering a lieutenant.
facts.action: Be prepared for the possibility of a lieutenant wielding a broadsword.

facts.fact: Balrogs are always generated with broadswords.
facts.detect: Encountering a balrog.
facts.action: Expect a balrog to be wielding a broadsword and be prepared to disarm it.

facts.fact: Player monsters have a low 2/291 chance of generating with a broadsword.
facts.detect: Encountering a player monster.
facts.action: Be prepared for the possibility of a player monster wielding a broadsword.

facts.fact: Monsters prefer elven broadswords or better to regular broadswords.
facts.detect: Encountering a monster wielding a broadsword.
facts.action: Assume the monster would prefer a better weapon if available.

facts.fact: Bronze plate mail provides 6 base AC and MC1.
facts.detect: bronze plate mail
facts.action: Wear bronze plate mail for its AC and MC1 if no better armor is available.

facts.fact: Bronze plate mail is immune to erosion by rust but not corrosion.
facts.detect: bronze plate mail
facts.action: Keep bronze plate mail as a backup if rust is a concern but not corrosion.

facts.fact: A dwarvish mithril-coat offers the same AC as bronze plate mail with MC2 for 1/3 the weight.
facts.detect: dwarvish mithril-coat
facts.action: Prefer dwarvish mithril-coat over bronze plate mail if available.

facts.fact: An elven mithril-coat offers 1 less point of AC with MC2 for the same weight as bronze plate mail.
facts.detect: elven mithril-coat
facts.action: Prefer elven mithril-coat over bronze plate mail if available.

facts.fact: Archeologists start each game with a +2 bullwhip.
facts.detect: Starting inventory message mentioning a +2 bullwhip.
facts.action: Keep the bullwhip as it is a powerful starting weapon.

facts.fact: Balrogs are always generated with a bullwhip.
facts.detect: Encountering a balrog.
facts.action: Be cautious when fighting balrogs as they can use the bullwhip effectively.

facts.fact: A bullwhip can be used to pick up items while levitating or riding.
facts.detect: Being in a levitation or riding state and seeing an item on the ground.
facts.action: Use the bullwhip to pick up items without touching the ground.

facts.fact: A bullwhip can be used to disarm monsters.
facts.detect: Seeing a monster wielding a weapon.
facts.action: Use the bullwhip to disarm the monster and take its weapon.

facts.fact: Applying a bullwhip to a steed while riding causes it to gallop.
facts.detect: Being on a steed and needing to move quickly.
facts.action: Use the bullwhip to make the steed gallop.

facts.fact: C-rations are not randomly generated.
facts.detect: The bot will not find C-rations in the dungeon randomly.
facts.action: The bot should focus on other food sources like lembas wafers or K-rations.

facts.fact: Mercenaries that are part of the Yendorian Army have a 1/2 chance of being generated with a C-ration.
facts.detect: Encountering mercenaries in Fort Ludios or the Castle.
facts.action: Killing mercenaries and checking corpses for C-rations.

facts.fact: C-rations grant 300 nutrition and usually take one move to consume.
facts.detect: Eating a C-ration and seeing the nutrition gain.
facts.action: Using C-rations when in desperate need of nutrition.

facts.fact: C-rations can tame domestic canines and felines and pacify domestic equines.
facts.detect: Encountering domestic canines, felines, or equines.
facts.action: Feeding C-rations to tame or pacify these animals.

facts.fact: C-rations are less preferred than K-rations due to lower nutrition-per-turn value.
facts.detect: Comparing C-rations to K-rations in terms of nutrition and weight.
facts.action: Prioritizing K-rations over C-rations when both are available.

facts.fact: A can of grease is a chargeable item that can be used to grease items for various purposes, and it is made of iron.
facts.detect: Item name: can of grease
facts.action: Collect and use can of grease to protect important items from rust, corrosion, water damage, and acid damage.

facts.fact: Cans of grease make up 1.5% of all tools that are randomly generated on the ground, in general shops or as death drops.
facts.detect: Randomly finding or purchasing a can of grease
facts.action: Prioritize finding and using cans of grease to protect equipment.

facts.fact: Greased objects are protected from rust, corrosion, water damage, and acid damage, but have no protection against burning and rotting.
facts.detect: Item description or message: 'You cover your [item] with a thick layer of grease.'
facts.action: Grease important items such as armor, weapons, and bags of holding to protect them from damage.

facts.fact: Greasing your cloak and helmet is standard strategy for most players: it protects against grabbing from owlbears and sea monsters among other monsters, and mind flayers and master mind flayers cannot attach their tentacles to a greased helmet.
facts.detect: Encounter with owlbear, sea monster, mind flayer, or master mind flayer
facts.action: Ensure cloak and helmet are greased to avoid being grabbed or having tentacles attached.

facts.fact: A charged can of grease can be applied to untrap a squeaky board, with a lower chance of success if the can is cursed.
facts.detect: Encounter with a squeaky board
facts.action: Use a charged can of grease to untrap squeaky boards, especially if cursed.

facts.fact: The Candelabrum of Invocation is one of the three items required to perform the invocation ritual.
facts.detect: Candelabrum of Invocation
facts.action: Keep the Candelabrum safe and do not sell it to Izchak before performing the invocation ritual.

facts.fact: Vlad the Impaler holds the Candelabrum at the top level of his tower in Gehennom.
facts.detect: Vlad the Impaler's tower in Gehennom
facts.action: Retrieve the Candelabrum from Vlad's tower, which may involve fighting Vlad.

facts.fact: To use the Candelabrum, you must attach seven candles to it.
facts.detect: Seven candles
facts.action: Find and attach seven candles to the Candelabrum before attempting to light it.

facts.fact: The Candelabrum loses half of its remaining 'lifespan' each time it is lit outside of the vibrating square.
facts.detect: Vibrating square
facts.action: Light the Candelabrum only on the vibrating square to preserve its lifespan.

facts.fact: The Candelabrum provides a light radius slightly larger than an ordinary lamp.
facts.detect: Light radius
facts.action: Use the Candelabrum's light radius to navigate dark areas.

facts.fact: A candy bar is a type of veggy comestible that appears in NetHack, and is suitable for vegetarians (but not vegans).
facts.detect: Item name: Candy bar
facts.action: Eat if vegetarian conduct is not important or save for later if nutrition is needed.

facts.fact: Eating a candy bar grants 100 nutrition and takes one action to consume.
facts.detect: Item name: Candy bar
facts.action: Eat when hungry to gain 100 nutrition quickly.

facts.fact: Candy bars have labels that can be read, which naturally breaks illiterate conduct.
facts.detect: Item name: Candy bar
facts.action: Do not read the label if maintaining illiterate conduct is important.

facts.fact: Candy bars have a decent nutrition/weight ratio at 50, the same as a slime mold.
facts.detect: Item name: Candy bar
facts.action: Eat when hungry or save for later if nutrition is needed.

facts.fact: They can also be used to tame domestic cats and dogs.
facts.detect: Item name: Candy bar and presence of domestic cats or dogs
facts.action: Use to tame domestic cats or dogs.

facts.fact: Eating a carrot grants 50 nutrition and cures all forms of blindness from sources other than cream pies.
facts.detect: carrot item in inventory, blindness status
facts.action: Eat carrot to cure blindness and gain nutrition

facts.fact: Knights start each game with 10-20 carrots.
facts.detect: carrot item in inventory
facts.action: Keep carrots for potential blindness cure or feeding pets

facts.fact: A hero can throw carrots to tame domestic herbivores and pacify domestic carnivores.
facts.detect: domestic herbivore or carnivore on the map
facts.action: Throw carrot to tame or pacify pets

facts.fact: Blinded pets also consider carrots treats and will eat them to cure their own blindness, regardless of diet.
facts.detect: blinded pet on the map
facts.action: Feed carrot to blinded pet

facts.fact: Chain mail provides 5 base AC and MC1.
facts.detect: Checking the armor's AC value and material.
facts.action: Equip chain mail to improve AC, especially early in the game.

facts.fact: Chain mail makes up 6.6% of all randomly generated armor.
facts.detect: Finding chain mail in shops, on the ground, or as death drops.
facts.action: Prioritize picking up chain mail when found to improve AC.

facts.fact: Chieftains, pages, roshi, and warriors have a 2/3 chance of generating with chain mail.
facts.detect: Encountering these monsters.
facts.action: Prepare to fight these monsters knowing they likely wear chain mail.

facts.fact: Pelias, the quest leader for the Barbarian quest, is always generated with +5 chain mail.
facts.detect: Encountering Pelias during the quest.
facts.action: Be prepared for Pelias to wear +5 chain mail, which is a significant threat.

facts.fact: Player monster barbarians, knights, clerics, and valkyries each have an effective 11.5% chance of being given chain mail.
facts.detect: Encountering player monsters of these roles.
facts.action: Expect player monsters of these roles to potentially wear chain mail.

page: Cheap plastic imitation of the Amulet of Yendor

facts.fact: Wishing for the Amulet of Yendor always creates an unidentified cheap plastic imitation of the Amulet of Yendor
facts.detect: Wishing for the Amulet of Yendor and receiving an unidentified amulet
facts.action: Do not use the wish for the Amulet of Yendor unless you have a way to identify it

facts.fact: Offering an unknown fake Amulet on a regular altar will act as though you had offered the real Amulet on that altar
facts.detect: Offering an unidentified amulet on a regular altar
facts.action: Do not offer unidentified amulets on regular altars

facts.fact: Offering a cheap plastic imitation of the Amulet of Yendor on a high altar carries a -1 luck penalty unless it was identified as a fake
facts.detect: Offering an amulet on a high altar and receiving a luck penalty
facts.action: Identify amulets before offering them on high altars

facts.fact: Offering a known fake Amulet on a high altar results in a -3 luck penalty and a -1 alignment penalty
facts.detect: Offering an identified fake amulet on a high altar
facts.action: Avoid offering identified fake amulets on high altars

facts.fact: If the hero attempts to leave the dungeon through the up stair on dungeon level 1 and has only a fake Amulet, they will escape the dungeon and end the game
facts.detect: Attempting to leave the dungeon through the up stair on DL 1 with an amulet
facts.action: Ensure you have the real Amulet of Yendor before attempting to leave DL 1

facts.fact: Chests have a 5/6 chance of being locked and contain useful items like potions of healing, scrolls, wands, and spellbooks.
facts.detect: Locked chest, items like potions of healing, scrolls, wands, or spellbooks
facts.action: Unlock the chest if possible, or leave it for later if unsure about disarming traps.

facts.fact: Chests in throne rooms may contain gold and useful items, and are often locked.
facts.detect: Throne room with a chest
facts.action: Unlock the chest and check its contents.

facts.fact: Chests in graveyards and barracks have a high chance of appearing and may contain useful items.
facts.detect: Graveyard or Barracks with a chest
facts.action: Approach and check the chest for useful items.

facts.fact: Chests in themed rooms like 'buried treasure' or 'storeroom' may contain valuable items but also mimics.
facts.detect: Themed room with a chest or strange object
facts.action: Approach with caution, check for mimics before opening.

facts.fact: Chests can protect items from damage and rot, but cursed chests reduce protection.
facts.detect: Chest with items inside
facts.action: Store valuable items in a chest, especially if going to a dangerous area.

facts.fact: Cleaver has a base 1/20 chance of being generated as a battle-axe on the ground or as a death drop.
facts.detect: Battle-axe with special properties
facts.action: Pick up and use Cleaver if found, as it is a powerful weapon.

facts.fact: Cleaver can hit multiple monsters in an arc with one swing.
facts.detect: Attacking a monster and hitting others around it
facts.action: Use Cleaver in 'one vs. many' scenarios but avoid peaceful-populated areas.

facts.fact: Cleaver's arcing swing prevents it from being used to perform shattering blows or sneak attacks.
facts.detect: Attempting to shatter a door or sneak attack
facts.action: Avoid using Cleaver for shattering blows or sneak attacks.

facts.fact: Cleaver is a two-handed weapon and risks being welded to your hands if it becomes cursed.
facts.detect: Cursed Cleaver
facts.action: Carry curse removal items and holy water to prevent welding.

facts.fact: Cleaver's average damage against small monsters is 10.5 and against large monsters is 12.
facts.detect: Attacking monsters with Cleaver
facts.action: Use Cleaver for high damage output in combat.

facts.fact: A cloak of displacement is a magical cloak that provides 1 base AC, MC1, and displacement.
facts.detect: You feel that monsters have difficulty pinpointing your location.
facts.action: Equip the cloak of displacement to gain the displacement effect, which can help in escaping from monsters and reducing the chance of being hit.

facts.fact: Monsters will not gain displacement from wearing a cloak of displacement.
facts.detect: N/A (automatically known when the cloak is identified)
facts.action: Use the cloak of displacement to misdirect attacks from hostile monsters, as it will not provide displacement to monsters wearing it.

facts.fact: The cloak of displacement is the only source of displacement in the game.
facts.detect: N/A (automatically known when the cloak is identified)
facts.action: Prioritize finding and keeping the cloak of displacement as it is the only item that provides displacement, which is crucial for misdirecting attacks.

facts.fact: Heroes using a lance or any polearm as their main weapon may especially benefit from monsters wasting turns striking at their image while remaining within pounding range.
facts.detect: Equipping a lance or polearm and noticing that monsters are attacking empty squares.
facts.action: Use a lance or polearm while wearing the cloak of displacement to maximize the benefit of displacement by causing monsters to waste turns attacking empty squares.

facts.fact: A cloak of invisibility is a type of magical armor that appears in NetHack and provides 1 base point of AC, invisibility, and MC1 when worn.
facts.detect: Wearing the cloak and noticing the invisibility effect or seeing the AC change.
facts.action: Wear the cloak to gain invisibility and AC benefits, especially useful for avoiding detection by monsters.

facts.fact: Player monsters, excluding monks, have an effective ~14.83% chance of generating with a cloak of invisibility as their initial cloak.
facts.detect: Generated as a player monster and finding a cloak of invisibility in inventory.
facts.action: Keep the cloak if generated with it, as it provides early invisibility and AC benefits.

facts.fact: Cloaks of invisibility make up 1% of all randomly-generated armor.
facts.detect: Finding a cloak of invisibility in a randomly generated pile of armor.
facts.action: Pick up and wear the cloak to gain invisibility and AC benefits.

facts.fact: Avoid wearing random cloaks in shops without at least testing their beatitude - if the cloak is a cursed cloak of invisibility, the character may not be able to leave the shop without some difficulty and possibly even an angered shopkeeper.
facts.detect: Attempting to leave a shop while wearing a cursed cloak of invisibility.
facts.action: Test the beatitude of cloaks before wearing them in shops to avoid being trapped or facing an angered shopkeeper.

facts.fact: All Wizards start the game with a +0 cloak of magic resistance.
facts.detect: Starting equipment message mentioning cloak of magic resistance
facts.action: Wear the cloak of magic resistance if you are a Wizard to gain magic resistance and AC.

facts.fact: Cloaks of magic resistance are quite rare, and make up 0.2% of all armor randomly generated on the ground.
facts.detect: Finding a cloak of magic resistance on the ground
facts.action: Pick up and wear the cloak of magic resistance to gain magic resistance and AC.

facts.fact: Aligned priests, high priests and the Arch Priest have a 1/21 chance of being generated with a cloak of magic resistance.
facts.detect: Encountering an aligned priest, high priest, or Arch Priest
facts.action: Be prepared to fight or avoid these priests if they have a cloak of magic resistance.

facts.fact: Master Kaen, the Monk quest nemesis, has a 1/11 chance of being generated with a cloak of magic resistance.
facts.detect: Encountering Master Kaen
facts.action: Be cautious of Master Kaen if he has a cloak of magic resistance, as it will nullify the wand of death.

facts.fact: The cloak of magic resistance is an important part of the ascension kit and is frequently paired with silver dragon scale mail for combined protection.
facts.detect: Having silver dragon scale mail and a cloak of magic resistance
facts.action: Wear both the cloak of magic resistance and silver dragon scale mail for maximum protection against magical attacks.

facts.fact: A cloak of protection is a type of magical cloak that appears in NetHack with an AC of 3 and MC3.
facts.detect: Wearing the cloak and noticing the AC and MC3 effects.
facts.action: Equip the cloak of protection to gain the AC and MC3 benefits.

facts.fact: Cloaks of protection make up 1.1% of all randomly generated armor.
facts.detect: Finding a cloak of protection on the ground or in shops.
facts.action: Pick up and identify the cloak of protection.

facts.fact: Cloaks of protection are worn by aligned clerics, high priests, and the Arch Priest with a 2/21 chance.
facts.detect: Encountering an aligned cleric, high priest, or Arch Priest wearing a cloak.
facts.action: Prepare to fight or negotiate with these monsters, noting their equipment.

facts.fact: Player monsters on the Astral Plane have a 77/624 chance of generating with a cloak of protection.
facts.detect: Encountering player monsters on the Astral Plane.
facts.action: Check if the player monster is wearing a cloak of protection.

facts.fact: A cloak of protection is auto-identified when worn.
facts.detect: Wearing the cloak and noticing it auto-identifies.
facts.action: Equip the cloak to auto-identify it.

facts.fact: A clove of garlic on a square will prevent any undead monster other than a ghost or shade from entering that square.
facts.detect: Undead monsters (e.g., skeleton, mummy, vampire) attempting to move onto a square with a clove of garlic.
facts.action: Place cloves of garlic on squares to block undead monsters from entering.

facts.fact: Hitting an undead monster with a clove of garlic will scare them for 2-8 turns.
facts.detect: Undead monster (e.g., vampire, mummy) in combat.
facts.action: Use cloves of garlic as a weapon to scare undead monsters.

facts.fact: Cloves of garlic make up 0.7% of all randomly-generated comestibles.
facts.detect: Finding cloves of garlic in a general store, delicatessen, or health food store.
facts.action: Buy cloves of garlic when available to use for warding off undead.

facts.fact: If a hero eats a clove of garlic while polymorphed into an undead monster, they will vomit.
facts.detect: Polymorphing into an undead monster and attempting to eat a clove of garlic.
facts.action: Avoid eating cloves of garlic while polymorphed into an undead monster.

facts.fact: Undead pets will not eat garlic.
facts.detect: Undead pet (e.g., ghost, vampire) in inventory or on the map.
facts.action: Do not feed cloves of garlic to undead pets.

facts.fact: Cave Dwellers start each game with a +1 club.
facts.detect: Starting inventory message mentioning a +1 club
facts.action: Keep the +1 club as it is a good starting weapon for a Cave Dweller.

facts.fact: Clubs make up 1.2% of all randomly generated weapons.
facts.detect: Finding a club on the ground or in a shop
facts.action: Consider picking up a club if you find one, as it can be a decent weapon, especially if you are a Cave Dweller.

facts.fact: Ettins have a roughly 50% chance of generating with clubs.
facts.detect: Encountering ettins
facts.action: Be prepared to fight ettins with clubs, as they are a common enemy with this weapon.

facts.fact: Thugs and neanderthals are always generated with clubs.
facts.detect: Encountering thugs or neanderthals
facts.action: Expect thugs and neanderthals to be armed with clubs, and prepare accordingly.

facts.fact: Shaman Karnov, the quest leader for the Cave Dweller quest, is always generated with a +5 club.
facts.detect: Encountering Shaman Karnov during the Cave Dweller quest
facts.action: Be prepared to face Shaman Karnov with a +5 club, which can be a significant threat.

facts.fact: A cornuthaum provides MC1 and +1 charisma for Wizards, but blocks clairvoyance and -1 charisma for non-Wizards.
facts.detect: Wearing a cornuthaum and noticing changes in charisma or clairvoyance status.
facts.action: If the bot is a Wizard, it should keep the cornuthaum for its benefits. If not, it should discard it.

facts.fact: Cornuthaums are rare, making up 3/1000 of all helms randomly generated.
facts.detect: Finding a conical hat in shops or on the floor.
facts.action: If the bot is a Wizard, it should prioritize identifying and keeping the cornuthaum.

facts.fact: The base cost of a cornuthaum is 80 zorkmids.
facts.detect: Noticing the price tag of 80 zorkmids on a conical hat.
facts.action: If the bot is a Wizard, it should purchase and keep the cornuthaum.

facts.fact: Wizards can safely enchant a cornuthaum to +5 and further.
facts.detect: Having a cornuthaum and the ability to enchant items.
facts.action: If the bot is a Wizard, it should enchant the cornuthaum to +5 or higher.

facts.fact: Wearing a cornuthaum, a Wizard senses a pointy hat on top of their head when casting clairvoyance.
facts.detect: The message 'You sense a pointy hat on top of your head.'
facts.action: If the bot is a Wizard, it should continue using the cornuthaum for its benefits.

facts.fact: Most corpses can be revived with a wand of undead turning or spell of turn undead, and a few revive spontaneously.
facts.detect: Monster name and description
facts.action: Revive corpses with a wand of undead turning or spell of turn undead if needed.

facts.fact: Some corpses are acidic, poisonous or hallucinogenic, while others can give you a property that you may not want, and still others are deadly to eat.
facts.detect: Monster name and description
facts.action: Avoid eating corpses unless you have the appropriate resistance or means of curing the condition that they cause.

facts.fact: Lizard and acidic corpses cure stoning.
facts.detect: Monster name
facts.action: Eat lizard or acidic corpses to cure stoning.

facts.fact: Troll corpses come back to life 75% of the time.
facts.detect: Monster name
facts.action: Avoid eating troll corpses to prevent them from coming back to life.

facts.fact: Corpses are generally most useful and safe when fresh, slowly rotting as the turns pass.
facts.detect: Age of the corpse
facts.action: Eat fresh corpses and avoid eating old ones to prevent food poisoning.

facts.fact: Eating any of the Riders will kill you. Even if you have an amulet of life saving, they will revive before you can finish.
facts.detect: Rider corpse name
facts.action: Do not eat Rider corpses.

facts.fact: All undead corpses along with those generated on top of traps can cause food poisoning.
facts.detect: Undead corpse name or trap under corpse
facts.action: Do not eat undead corpses or those generated on traps.

facts.fact: Tinning undead corpses makes them safe to eat.
facts.detect: Undead corpse name
facts.action: Tin undead corpses before eating.

facts.fact: Acidic corpses and blobs (acid blob, yellow dragon, green mold, ochre jelly) are dangerous.
facts.detect: Acidic corpse name
facts.action: Avoid eating acidic corpses.

facts.fact: Dwarven heroes gain an additional 100 nutrition from eating cram rations.
facts.detect: The bot is a dwarven hero and has a cram ration in inventory.
facts.action: Eat cram rations to gain extra nutrition.

facts.fact: Cram rations make up 2% of all comestibles randomly generated on the ground, in shops or as death drops.
facts.detect: Finding cram rations in shops or on the ground.
facts.action: Prioritize picking up cram rations when found.

facts.fact: Cram rations cannot be rotten food unless they are cursed.
facts.detect: Eating a cram ration and receiving the message 'This cram ration is bland.'
facts.action: Eat cram rations without fear of rotting.

facts.fact: Gnomish and human Rangers start the game with a stack of 4-8 cram rations.
facts.detect: The bot starts as a Ranger and has cram rations in inventory.
facts.action: Use starting cram rations to manage hunger early in the game.

facts.fact: Cram rations are lighter but less filling than the more common food rations.
facts.detect: Comparing the weight and nutrition of cram rations to other food items.
facts.action: Use cram rations for their lighter weight when carrying capacity is low.

facts.fact: Eating a cream pie grants 100 nutrition and takes 1 turn to consume.
facts.detect: Item name: cream pie
facts.action: Eat cream pie to gain nutrition when hungry.

facts.fact: A hero that wields a single cream pie or a stack of cream pies and attacks a monster with them will splatter one of the pies in the defender's face, rendering the monster hostile, waking them from sleep and blinding them for up to 127 total turns.
facts.detect: Message: cream pie splashes over !
facts.action: Use cream pie to blind and weaken hostile monsters.

facts.fact: A hero that applies a cream pie or a stack of cream pies to smash one pie from the stack over their face will blind them for up to 25 turns.
facts.detect: Message: You immerse your in the cream pie(s).
facts.action: Apply cream pie to face to become temporarily blind.

facts.fact: A hero that throws a cream pie straight upward and does not hit the ceiling will have it land on their face, blinding them for up to 25 turns.
facts.detect: Message: You've got it all over your !
facts.action: Avoid throwing cream pie upward to prevent self-blinding.

facts.fact: A hero that is hit by a monster's thrown cream pie will be blinded for up to 25 (more) turns.
facts.detect: Message: Yecch! You've been creamed.
facts.action: Avoid being hit by thrown cream pies from monsters.

facts.fact: All Tourists start the game with an uncursed credit card.
facts.detect: Starting inventory as a Tourist
facts.action: As a non-Tourist, the bot should not expect to start with a credit card and should not rely on it.

facts.fact: Credit cards make up 1.5% of all randomly-generated tools.
facts.detect: Finding a credit card in a general store or hardware store
facts.action: The bot should prioritize purchasing or finding a credit card if it needs an unlocking tool, especially if it is a lawful dwarvish Valkyrie who might not have access to other unlocking tools.

facts.fact: Applying a credit card towards a locked door or container will unlock it with a chance dependent on dexterity and role.
facts.detect: Attempting to unlock a door or container with a credit card
facts.action: The bot should attempt to unlock doors and containers with a credit card if it has no better unlocking tool, but it should be aware of the low success rate and the risk of angering the watch in Minetown.

facts.fact: A hero applying a credit card to a door in Minetown in view of a watch member has a 1/3 chance during each action of being interrupted and warned, causing the door to become trapped.
facts.detect: Being in Minetown and attempting to unlock a door while a watch member is nearby
facts.action: The bot should avoid using a credit card to unlock doors in Minetown if a watch member is nearby to prevent angering the watch and getting trapped.

facts.fact: A hero that applies a credit card on a mimic disguised as a door will uncover the mimic, and the mimic will have a 2/3 chance of absorbing the tool.
facts.detect: Attempting to unlock a door and encountering a mimic
facts.action: The bot should be cautious when using a credit card to unlock doors, especially if it suspects a mimic, as it risks losing the credit card.

facts.fact: Gnomish heroes in roles that start the game with a bow and arrows will instead receive a crossbow and crossbow bolts.
facts.detect: Starting equipment as a gnomish hero
facts.action: Use the crossbow and bolts as primary ranged weapon

facts.fact: Crossbows have a maximum range of 8 squares and do not base their range on strength.
facts.detect: Using the crossbow to shoot
facts.action: Use crossbow to attack enemies up to 8 squares away

facts.fact: Gnomish heroes must have at least 16 strength to obtain full multishot bonuses from firing crossbows.
facts.detect: Hero's strength level
facts.action: Ensure strength is at least 16 to maximize crossbow effectiveness

facts.fact: Crossbows always prioritize crossbow bolts if the autoquiver option is enabled.
facts.detect: Enabling autoquiver option
facts.action: Enable autoquiver to automatically use crossbow bolts

facts.fact: Gnomish Rangers may get additional crossbow bolts in the early game from gnomes.
facts.detect: Interacting with gnomes
facts.action: Collect crossbow bolts from gnomes

facts.fact: Crossbow bolts are stackable projectiles designed for use with a crossbow and are made of iron.
facts.detect: Item name: crossbow bolt
facts.action: Collect and use crossbow bolts if you have a crossbow.

facts.fact: Stacks of crossbow bolts make up 5.5% of all randomly-generated weapons.
facts.detect: Item name: crossbow bolt
facts.action: Prioritize collecting crossbow bolts when found.

facts.fact: Crossbow bolts have a 100% chance of generating as poisoned.
facts.detect: Item name: crossbow bolt
facts.action: Do not dip crossbow bolts in potion of sickness.

facts.fact: Crossbow bolts always fire from a crossbow at their maximum range of 8 squares.
facts.detect: Weapon skill: crossbow
facts.action: Use crossbow bolts at maximum range for optimal damage.

facts.fact: Gnomish heroes must have at least 16 strength to obtain full multishot bonuses.
facts.detect: Race: gnome
facts.action: Ensure strength is at least 16 for full multishot bonuses.

facts.fact: A crysknife deals 1d10 damage to all monsters and has a +3 to-hit bonus.
facts.detect: Weapon name 'crysknife' in inventory or wielded
facts.action: Use crysknife for melee combat due to its consistent damage and to-hit bonus.

facts.fact: A crysknife can revert to a worm tooth if it leaves the hero's inventory and hits the ground.
facts.detect: Message 'A crysknife reverts to a worm tooth.'
facts.action: Avoid dropping or losing crysknives to prevent reverting to worm teeth.

facts.fact: Erosion-proofing a crysknife will reduce the chance of reverting to a worm tooth to 10%.
facts.detect: Message 'You feel the crysknife become more stable.' after erosion-proofing
facts.action: Erosion-proof crysknives to reduce the risk of reverting.

facts.fact: Opening a tin to eat while wielding a crysknife takes 3 actions instead of 1.
facts.detect: Wielding a crysknife and attempting to open a tin
facts.action: Unequip the crysknife before opening tins to save actions.

facts.fact: Throwing a crysknife is risky due to the chance of reverting to a worm tooth after 10 throws.
facts.detect: Wielding a crysknife and considering throwing it
facts.action: Avoid throwing crysknives unless absolutely necessary due to the risk of reverting.

facts.fact: A crystal ball is a magical tool that appears as a glass orb when unidentified and can be found randomly in general shops, hardware stores, and as death drops. It has 3-7 charges and a 1/4 chance of being blessed, 1/2 chance of being uncursed, and 1/4 chance of being cursed.
facts.detect: The item name 'crystal ball' or the appearance 'glass orb' when unidentified.
facts.action: Identify the crystal ball to know its charges and beatitude. Use it wisely, especially if you have low intelligence or are in a dangerous situation.

facts.fact: Using a crystal ball while not blind requires an intelligence check, which can result in various negative effects if failed, such as confusion, blindness, hallucination, or explosion (if not an artifact).
facts.detect: The message 'too much to comprehend!', 'confuses you!', 'damages your vision!', 'zaps your mind!', or 'explodes!' when using the crystal ball.
facts.action: Avoid using a crystal ball if your intelligence is low or if you are in a dangerous situation. Ensure you have a quick cure for impairments like blindness or confusion.

facts.fact: The crystal ball can be used to detect objects, monsters, traps, and dungeon features on the current level, but using it leaves the hero entranced and immobile for up to 10 turns.
facts.detect: The message 'You may look for an object or monster symbol.' when successfully using the crystal ball.
facts.action: Use the crystal ball to detect important items or threats, but be prepared to wait out the entrancement effect.

facts.fact: The crystal ball is the quest artifact for Valkyries (Orb of Fate) and Archeologists (Orb of Detection), which resist item-cursing effects 4/5 of the time and have unique properties.
facts.detect: The item name 'Orb of Fate' or 'Orb of Detection'.
facts.action: Use the quest artifact for its unique properties and resistances, but still be cautious with its use.

facts.fact: Charging a crystal ball with a blessed scroll sets it to 7 charges and blesses it, while cursed charging removes all charges and curses it.
facts.detect: The message 'You feel a surge of positive energy.' for blessing or 'You feel a surge of negative energy.' for cursing.
facts.action: Charge your crystal ball with a blessed scroll to ensure it has maximum charges and is blessed.

facts.fact: Crystal plate mail provides 7 base AC and MC2, and is treated as bulky armor similar to plate mail.
facts.detect: Crystal plate mail
facts.action: Wear crystal plate mail if you have high strength and need high AC, but manage inventory weight carefully.

facts.fact: Crystal plate mail is fragile and can crack from throwing, kicking, dropping from height, or being hit by force bolt or wand of striking.
facts.detect: Cracked crystal plate mail
facts.action: Avoid actions that may crack the armor and keep it erosion-proofed.

facts.fact: Crystal plate mail is the second-highest source of AC in the game that does not inhibit spellcasting after dragon scale mail.
facts.detect: Dragon scale mail
facts.action: Prioritize obtaining dragon scale mail over crystal plate mail if possible.

facts.fact: Crystal plate mail is generated in one of the niches on the middle floor of Vlad's Tower during level creation.
facts.detect: Vlad's Tower middle floor
facts.action: Search the niches on the middle floor of Vlad's Tower for crystal plate mail.

facts.fact: Crystal plate mail has an irregular base price of 820zm.
facts.detect: Price of crystal plate mail
facts.action: Use the price to identify enchantments on armor.

facts.fact: Valkyries start each game with a +0 dagger as their secondary weapon.
facts.detect: Checking inventory upon starting the game.
facts.action: Keep the dagger for its utility in early game combat and as a backup weapon.

facts.fact: A stack of daggers may be automatically quivered if the hero uses the firing command without any other projectiles or ammo quivered.
facts.detect: Using the firing command and noticing the automatic quiver of daggers.
facts.action: Use daggers as a primary projectile weapon, especially in early game when other ammo is scarce.

facts.fact: Rogues gain a +1 multishot bonus when throwing daggers.
facts.detect: Being a Rogue character and throwing daggers.
facts.action: Exploit the multishot bonus by throwing daggers frequently to deal high damage.

facts.fact: A hero that wields a dagger while eating a non-blessed tin will open the tin in 3 turns at most.
facts.detect: Eating a non-blessed tin while wielding a dagger.
facts.action: Use a dagger to speed up the opening of tins, reducing the risk of bad effects.

facts.fact: Daggers are typically cheap and plentiful, and are more durable than arrows, crossbow bolts and darts.
facts.detect: Finding daggers in shops, on the floor, or from monsters.
facts.action: Stockpile daggers for both melee and ranged combat due to their durability and availability.

facts.fact: Tourists start each game with a stack of {{rn1|20|21}} +2 darts.
facts.detect: Starting inventory message upon character generation
facts.action: Use the starting darts as a primary ranged weapon until obtaining a better weapon or until they run out.

facts.fact: Stacks of darts make up {{frac|3|50}} (6%) of all weapons that are randomly generated on the ground, in general shops or as death drops.
facts.detect: Finding darts in shops, on the ground, or as death drops
facts.action: Collect darts to use as a secondary ranged weapon or for disposable projectiles.

facts.fact: A dart trap will shoot a dart at any hero or monster that steps on the floor of the square containing that trap, with a {{frac|6}} of the dart being poisoned.
facts.detect: Stepping on a dart trap
facts.action: Avoid stepping on dart traps or disarm them if possible.

facts.fact: Dipping darts in a potion of sickness will poison them, adding +d6 damage and a {{frac|10}} chance of instadeath per hit against monsters without poison resistance.
facts.detect: Using a potion of sickness on darts
facts.action: Poison darts to increase their damage and effectiveness against non-poison resistant monsters.

facts.fact: With high Luck and enchantment, a stack of darts can last through a significant portion of the game.
facts.detect: Having high Luck and enchantment
facts.action: Continue using darts as a primary or secondary ranged weapon throughout the game if they are enchanted and have high Luck.

facts.fact: Demonbane prevents demon gating while wielded
facts.detect: A demon would have gated in other demons when attacking the hero, but the hero was wielding Demonbane.
facts.action: Wield Demonbane when facing major demons to prevent them from summoning reinforcements.

facts.fact: Demonbane can banish imp monsters and major demons within line of sight
facts.detect: You invoke Demonbane and a nearby demon or imp is banished.
facts.action: Use Demonbane to banish demons and imps to reduce enemy numbers and avoid dangerous encounters.

facts.fact: Demonbane has a +1d5 to-hit bonus and double damage against major demons
facts.detect: The hero is fighting a major demon and notices increased damage and accuracy.
facts.action: Use Demonbane as the primary weapon against major demons for increased effectiveness.

facts.fact: Lawful demon princes will be generated hostile if the hero wields Demonbane
facts.detect: A lawful demon prince approaches hostile or the message 'looks very angry...' appears.
facts.action: Avoid wielding Demonbane when dealing with lawful demon princes to prevent hostility.

facts.fact: Demonbane has a base price of 2500 and a weight of 36
facts.detect: The hero finds a silver mace with a price of 2500 and weight of 36.
facts.action: Identify and keep Demonbane if found, as it is a powerful artifact.

facts.fact: A dented pot is a type of helm that appears in NetHack, providing 1 base AC.
facts.detect: dented pot
facts.action: Pick up and wear the dented pot for immediate AC improvement.

facts.fact: Wearing or removing a dented pot takes only one action, compared to most other helms which have a wear/remove delay of at least one turn.
facts.detect: Wearing or removing a dented pot
facts.action: Use the dented pot for quick AC adjustments in combat situations.

facts.fact: Dented pots make up 0.2% of all helms that are randomly generated on the ground, in general shops or as death drops.
facts.detect: Finding a dented pot in the dungeon or shops
facts.action: Prioritize picking up dented pots when found due to their unique properties.

facts.fact: Mercenaries have an effective 1/6 chance of being generated with a dented pot that counts for 1 point of their target AC.
facts.detect: Encountering a mercenary with a dented pot
facts.action: Consider killing mercenaries to obtain their dented pots if needed.

facts.fact: The dented pot will usually be replaced with an elven leather helm or any viable magical helm in the long term.
facts.detect: Finding better helms like elven leather helm
facts.action: Replace the dented pot with better helms as they are found.

facts.fact: The dilithium crystal is the most valuable gem in NetHack, with a base value of 4500 zorkmids.
