facts.detect: item with the symbol '*' and the name 'dilithium crystal'
facts.action: Collect the dilithium crystal if found, as it is highly valuable.

facts.fact: Dragonbane is an artifact broadsword that deals double damage against dragons and grants reflection when wielded.
facts.detect: Item name 'Dragonbane' in inventory or on the ground
facts.action: Pick up and wield Dragonbane if available, especially when facing dragons or needing reflection.

facts.fact: Dragonbane has a base 1/20 chance of appearing as a randomly generated broadsword or as a death drop.
facts.detect: Randomly generated broadsword or death drop
facts.action: Check if the broadsword is Dragonbane when found.

facts.fact: Dragonbane can be obtained as a sacrifice gift, requiring a sacrifice of at least 5 value.
facts.detect: Message 'You feel a strange presence...' when sacrificing
facts.action: Sacrifice items to obtain Dragonbane if needed.

facts.fact: Dragonbane is useful for dealing with dragons and obtaining dragon scales for dragon scale mail.
facts.detect: Encounter with a dragon
facts.action: Use Dragonbane to defeat dragons and collect their scales.

facts.fact: Dragonbane is more spellcasting-friendly than a shield of reflection.
facts.detect: Spellcasting as a Valkyrie
facts.action: Wield Dragonbane for spellcasting if not using a shield of reflection.

facts.fact: Drums of earthquake make up 0.2% of all tools randomly generated on the ground, in general shops or as death drops.
facts.detect: Finding a drum of earthquake in the inventory or on the ground
facts.action: Avoid using unidentified drums, especially on levels with peaceful monsters or temples.

facts.fact: Applying a charged drum of earthquake will consume one charge and cause an earthquake across a portion of the dungeon level that is dependent on the hero's experience level.
facts.detect: Applying a drum of earthquake
facts.action: Only use charged drums when necessary and in controlled environments to avoid unintended consequences.

facts.fact: Applying a drum of earthquake with no charges will produce noise that has a range dependent on the hero's experience level.
facts.detect: Applying a drum of earthquake with no charges
facts.action: Use drums with no charges cautiously to avoid deafening or angering peaceful monsters.

facts.fact: Drums of earthquake can hold a maximum of 20 charges: uncursed charging adds d4 charges while blessed charging adds 2d4 charges, and cursed charging will strip all charges instead.
facts.detect: Charging a drum of earthquake
facts.action: Charge drums blessedly to maximize charges, but be cautious of cursed charging.

facts.fact: Destroying an altar by applying a drum of earthquake or by any other means will raise the anger of that altar's god to its maximum, and also applies a -20 alignment record penalty if the altar belonged to the hero's god.
facts.detect: Applying a drum of earthquake near an altar
facts.action: Avoid using drums near altars to prevent angering gods and losing alignment.

facts.fact: A dunce cap sets a hero's intelligence and wisdom to 6 each and autocurses.
facts.detect: You feel like sitting in a corner.
facts.action: Do not wear a conical hat without identifying it first.

facts.fact: Shopkeepers will add an additional 3/10 markup to the price of each item when buying and only give 3/10 of the base price in gold when selling items.
facts.detect: Prices in shops are unusually high or low.
facts.action: Avoid wearing a dunce cap when shopping.

facts.fact: Taking off or removing the dunce cap will restore the hero's intelligence and wisdom to their original values.
facts.detect: Your cap constricts briefly, then relaxes again.
facts.action: Remove the dunce cap immediately if worn.

facts.fact: The dunce cap prevents instadeath from a mind flayer's intelligence drain.
facts.detect: Encounter with a mind flayer.
facts.action: Wear the dunce cap if you expect to fight a mind flayer.

facts.fact: The dunce cap can be distinguished by price identification, as the dunce cap has a base cost of only 1 zorkmid.
facts.detect: Picking up a conical hat with a price of 1 zorkmid.
facts.action: Do not wear a conical hat with a price of 1 zorkmid.

facts.fact: Dwarvish cloaks make up 0.8% of all randomly-generated armor created on the floor, in general shops or as death drops.
facts.detect: Finding a hooded cloak in the dungeon or in a shop
facts.action: Pick up and sell dwarvish cloaks for easy money early in the game.

facts.fact: Sergeants have a 50% chance of being generated with a flail.
facts.detect: Encountering a Sergeant.
facts.action: Be prepared for the possibility of fighting a Sergeant with a flail.

facts.fact: Yeenoghu is always generated with a flail.
facts.detect: Encountering Yeenoghu.
facts.action: Be prepared for Yeenoghu's flail attack.

facts.fact: Player monsters on the Astral Plane have a ~6.87% chance of generating with a flail.
facts.detect: Encountering a player monster on the Astral Plane.
facts.action: Be prepared for the possibility of fighting a player monster with a flail.

facts.fact: Valkyries start the game with 1-2 food rations.
facts.detect: Starting inventory check
facts.action: Consume or store food rations as needed for early game nutrition.

facts.fact: Food rations grant 800 nutrition and take roughly five actions to eat.
facts.detect: Eating a food ration
facts.action: Eat food rations when hungry to maintain nutrition levels.

facts.fact: Food rations have a 1/7 chance of being rotten if uncursed and older than 30 turns or blessed and older than 50 turns.
facts.detect: Message 'This food ration looks a bit moldy.'
facts.action: Avoid eating potentially rotten food rations to prevent negative effects.

facts.fact: Food rations can be thrown to tame domestic canines and felines and pacify domestic equines.
facts.detect: Encountering a domestic canine, feline, or equine
facts.action: Use food rations to tame or pacify animals when necessary.

facts.fact: Food rations are common and can be found randomly on the floor, in general shops, or as death drops.
facts.detect: Finding food rations in shops or on the floor
facts.action: Collect food rations to maintain a steady supply of nutrition.

facts.fact: Monks start each game with 3-6 fortune cookies.
facts.detect: Starting inventory as a Monk
facts.action: Eat or read fortune cookies to gain wisdom or nutrition, depending on the situation.

facts.fact: Fortune cookies make up 5.5% of all comestibles randomly generated.
facts.detect: Finding fortune cookies in the dungeon
facts.action: Eat or read fortune cookies to gain wisdom or nutrition, depending on the situation.

facts.fact: Eating a fortune cookie grants 40 nutrition and automatically reads the fortune inside unless the hero is blind.
facts.detect: Eating a fortune cookie
facts.action: Eat fortune cookies to gain nutrition and read fortunes to gain wisdom or abuse it, depending on the fortune's veracity.

facts.fact: Fortune cookies are a lightweight means of taming domestic carnivores.
facts.detect: Seeing domestic carnivores in the dungeon
facts.action: Throw fortune cookies to tame domestic carnivores.

facts.fact: A hero can preserve vegan or foodless conduct by reading the cookie instead of eating it.
facts.detect: Having vegan or foodless conduct
facts.action: Read fortune cookies instead of eating them to preserve conduct.

facts.fact: Frost Brand grants cold resistance to the wielder, preventing the wielder's open inventory from being frozen with a 99/100 chance.
facts.detect: Inventory items do not freeze when hit by cold damage.
facts.action: Wield Frost Brand to protect inventory from freezing.

facts.fact: Frost Brand deals double damage against monsters without cold resistance and has a 1/4 chance of freezing and destroying potions in the target's open inventory.
facts.detect: Target monster does not have cold resistance.
facts.action: Attack cold-resistant monsters with Frost Brand to destroy their potions.

facts.fact: Frost Brand can be invoked to cast an Expert skill cone of cold spell.
facts.detect: Invoke Frost Brand.
facts.action: Use Frost Brand's invocation to cast cone of cold spell.

facts.fact: Frost Brand is more effective than Fire Brand against Gehennom's denizens due to many being fire-resistant.
facts.detect: Encounter Gehennom's denizens.
facts.action: Prefer Frost Brand over Fire Brand in Gehennom.

facts.fact: Frost Brand is considered the best artifact weapon for Gehennom after Grayswandir.
facts.detect: Enter Gehennom.
facts.action: Prioritize obtaining Frost Brand for combat in Gehennom.

facts.fact: Frost horns are generated with 4 to 8 charges and can hold a maximum of 20 charges.
facts.detect: Item description or inventory details
facts.action: Check the number of charges before using to avoid running out

facts.fact: Applying a frost horn with charges will prompt for a cardinal direction and emit a ray of cold in that direction, using up a charge and auto-identifying the item type.
facts.detect: Prompt to choose a cardinal direction
facts.action: Use the frost horn to freeze moats, reinforce ice, destroy doors, and cool lava

facts.fact: A hero that applies the horn at themselves will take 12d6 damage unless they have cold resistance.
facts.detect: Prompt to apply the horn to oneself
facts.action: Avoid applying the horn to oneself unless necessary and with cold resistance

facts.fact: Choosing to improvise on a frost horn with no charges will treat it as an applied tooled horn, which can wake up nearby sleeping monsters and scare any that fail a roll against their MR score.
facts.detect: Prompt to improvise on an empty charge horn
facts.action: Use the horn to scare monsters if no charges are left

facts.fact: Monsters can use this item with the same conditions, and hostile ones will apply it offensively in the hero's direction.
facts.detect: Hostile monster using frost horn
facts.action: Avoid or prepare for potential frost horn attacks from monsters

facts.fact: Fumble boots have a 90% chance of being cursed when randomly generated.
facts.detect: The boots are cursed when worn and a message appears saying 'You feel clumsy.'
facts.action: Avoid wearing unidentified fumble boots to prevent potential fumbling and stoning from cockatrice or chickatrice corpses.

facts.fact: Wearing cursed fumble boots is considered a minor trouble.
facts.detect: The player receives a message indicating a minor trouble when wearing cursed fumble boots.
facts.action: Pray to remove the minor trouble if the boots are cursed.

facts.fact: Fumble boots grant 1 base AC and cause fumbling every 1d20 turns, immobilizing the character for 2 turns.
facts.detect: The character experiences a fumbling event, immobilizing them for 2 turns.
facts.action: Avoid wearing fumble boots in dangerous situations where movement is critical.

facts.fact: Fumbling while wielding the corpse of a cockatrice or chickatrice will result in immediate stoning.
facts.detect: The character is wielding a cockatrice or chickatrice corpse and experiences a fumbling event.
facts.action: Avoid wielding cockatrice or chickatrice corpses while wearing fumble boots.

facts.fact: Fumble boots are generally undesirable to wear and are used as polyfodder if needed.
facts.detect: The boots are identified as fumble boots.
facts.action: Do not wear fumble boots unless absolutely necessary, such as for polymorphing.

facts.fact: Gauntlets of dexterity make up 0.8% of all randomly generated armor.
facts.detect: Finding a pair of gloves with a randomized appearance.
facts.action: Pick up and wear gauntlets of dexterity if found, as they can significantly improve dexterity and AC.

facts.fact: Wearing or taking off gauntlets of dexterity that have a non-zero enchantment will auto-identify them.
facts.detect: Wearing or removing gauntlets of dexterity.
facts.action: Wear or remove gauntlets of dexterity to auto-identify them.

facts.fact: Gauntlets of dexterity grant 1 base AC.
facts.detect: Wearing gauntlets of dexterity.
facts.action: Wear gauntlets of dexterity to gain the AC bonus.

facts.fact: Higher dexterity can improve hit rates for attack spells, attacks, and thrown items.
facts.detect: Having a high dexterity score.
facts.action: Wear highly enchanted gauntlets of dexterity to improve accuracy with attack spells and thrown items.

facts.fact: In NetHack brass, gauntlets of dexterity set the wearer's dexterity to their race or role's maximum.
facts.detect: Playing NetHack brass version.
facts.action: Wear gauntlets of dexterity to maximize dexterity.

facts.fact: Gauntlets of fumbling have a 9/10 chance of generating cursed with a non-positive enchantment.
facts.detect: The bot will notice the cursed status when trying to wear them and receive a message like 'You can't wear cursed items.'
facts.action: Avoid wearing unidentified gauntlets of fumbling to prevent the fumbling effect and -3 to-hit penalty while firing from bows.

facts.fact: Cursed gauntlets of fumbling are considered a minor trouble by the hero's god.
facts.detect: The bot will receive a message from its god like 'You have offended your god.'
facts.action: If the bot receives such a message, it should try to remove the gauntlets and pray to its god to regain favor.

facts.fact: Gauntlets of power set the wearer's strength to 25.
facts.detect: Wearing the gauntlets and observing the strength increase.
facts.action: Wear the gauntlets to increase strength for better carrying capacity, melee damage, and to-hit chance.

facts.fact: Gauntlets of power grant 1 base point of AC.
facts.detect: Wearing the gauntlets and observing the AC change.
facts.action: Wear the gauntlets to gain a small AC bonus.

facts.fact: Gauntlets of power incur a spellcasting penalty.
facts.detect: Attempting to cast a spell while wearing the gauntlets.
facts.action: Remove the gauntlets before casting spells to avoid spell failure.

facts.fact: Mjollnir can only be thrown by a hero with 25 strength.
facts.detect: Finding Mjollnir in the game.
facts.action: Wear the gauntlets to be able to throw Mjollnir.

facts.fact: Monsters wearing gauntlets of power gain 3-6 extra damage with weapon attacks.
facts.detect: Observing a monster wearing gauntlets of power in combat.
facts.action: Be cautious of monsters wearing gauntlets of power as they deal more damage.

facts.fact: Giantslayer has a +1d5 to-hit bonus and deals double damage against giants.
facts.detect: Encountering giants or seeing the message 'You feel steady when wielding Giantslayer.'
facts.action: Prioritize finding and equipping Giantslayer if you encounter giants or if you are in an area known to have giants.

facts.fact: Giantslayer requires a sacrifice of at least 4 value, and will always have +2 added to its enchantment when randomly generated or given as a sacrifice gift.
facts.detect: Checking the sacrifice value required for Giantslayer or seeing the message 'Giantslayer appears.'
facts.action: If you have the resources, consider sacrificing to obtain Giantslayer, especially if you are in an area with giants or if you are early in the game and need a powerful weapon.

facts.fact: Wielding Giantslayer now grants steadfastness, preventing the wielder from being sent flying by attacks.
facts.detect: Being attacked by a giant and not being sent flying.
facts.action: If you are sent flying by an attack while wielding Giantslayer, it means you do not have the steadfastness effect, and you should check if you have the correct weapon or if the game version supports this feature.

facts.fact: Giantslayer has a base 1/20 chance of being generated as an artifact long sword, and a 1/6 chance of being Giantslayer.
facts.detect: Finding a long sword on the ground or as a death drop.
facts.action: If you find a long sword, especially in a dungeon level where giants are common, consider picking it up and identifying it to see if it is Giantslayer.

facts.fact: In DynaHack, Giantslayer grants warning of giants.
facts.detect: Not applicable in vanilla NetHack.
facts.action: Not applicable in vanilla NetHack.

facts.fact: Glaives make up 0.8% of all randomly generated weapons.
facts.detect: Item name 'glaive' when found
facts.action: Pick up and equip if a polearm specialist (Barbarian, Knight, Samurai, Valkyrie) or if no better weapon is available.

facts.fact: Watchmen and soldiers may be generated with a glaive.
facts.detect: Encounter with watchmen or soldiers
facts.action: Be prepared for combat and check if they are wielding a glaive.

facts.fact: Trolls have an effective 1/8 chance of being generated with a glaive.
facts.detect: Encounter with a troll
facts.action: Be cautious and prepared for combat, as trolls may be wielding a glaive.

facts.fact: The glaive is the third-lightest polearm at 75 aum.
facts.detect: Item weight of 75 aum
facts.action: Consider equipping if weight is a concern and no lighter polearm is available.

facts.fact: The glaive has the lowest average damage of all polearms against small monsters.
facts.detect: Combat with small monsters
facts.action: Be aware that the glaive may be less effective against small monsters.

facts.fact: A grappling hook is a one-handed weapon-tool that uses the flail skill and appears as an iron hook when unidentified.
facts.detect: iron hook
facts.action: Identify the item as a grappling hook to understand its properties and potential uses.

facts.fact: Grappling hooks make up 0.5% of all tools that are randomly generated on the ground, in shops or as death drops.
facts.detect: Finding a grappling hook in a hardware store or as a random drop.
facts.action: Pick up the grappling hook if found, as it can be useful in specific situations.

facts.fact: A hero can apply a wielded grappling hook towards a location some distance away, with the distance determined by the hero's flail skill.
facts.detect: Wielding the grappling hook and attempting to apply it.
facts.action: Use the grappling hook to grab items or drag oneself, but only if the flail skill is at least basic.

facts.fact: If the hero is applying a grappling hook at Basic or lower skill, there is an equal chance of hitting an item, hitting a monster, hitting the ground, nothing happening, or the hero hooking themselves for 10-19 damage.
facts.detect: Applying the grappling hook and receiving damage.
facts.action: Train the flail skill to at least Skilled to avoid self-damage.

facts.fact: Using a grappling hook and snagging a wielded footrice corpse will subject the hero to instant stoning if they do not have gloves.
facts.detect: Picking up a footrice corpse with a grappling hook.
facts.action: Ensure gloves are worn before attempting to pick up a footrice corpse with a grappling hook.

facts.fact: Grayswandir is an artifact silver saber with a base damage of 1d8, double damage, and +1d5 to-hit bonus.
facts.detect: Grayswandir
facts.action: Wield Grayswandir for its damage output and to-hit bonus, especially against silver-hating monsters.

facts.fact: Grayswandir grants hallucination resistance while wielded.
facts.detect: Hallucination resistance granted while wielding Grayswandir.
facts.action: Wield Grayswandir to avoid hallucinations, especially in dangerous situations.

facts.fact: Grayswandir has a 1/4 chance of causing 4d4 damage to non-lawful heroes upon touching.
facts.detect: Touching Grayswandir as a non-lawful hero.
facts.action: Avoid touching Grayswandir if not lawful to prevent potential damage.

facts.fact: Grayswandir is most effective when heavily enchanted due to its damage calculation.
facts.detect: Highly enchanted Grayswandir.
facts.action: Enchant Grayswandir to maximize its damage output.

facts.fact: Grayswandir is one of the most sought-after artifact weapons in NetHack, especially in the late game.
facts.detect: Late game with high-quality artifact weapons.
facts.action: Prioritize obtaining Grayswandir if aiming for high damage output in the late game.

facts.fact: Grimtooth is an artifact orcish dagger with +d2 to-hit and +d6 damage bonuses against all monsters, grants poison resistance, and warns of elves.
facts.detect: Wield Grimtooth and notice poison resistance and red glow when elves are present.
facts.action: Wield Grimtooth to gain poison resistance and detect elves, which can be useful for avoiding or preparing for elf encounters.

facts.fact: Grimtooth is permanently poisoned and has a chance to poison targets without resistance, with a 10% chance of immediate death and d6 additional damage.
facts.detect: Notice poison messages when attacking with Grimtooth.
facts.action: Be cautious when using Grimtooth against non-elf enemies, especially those without poison resistance, to avoid poisoning and potential death.

facts.fact: Grimtooth can be invoked to launch venom, with equal chances of acid or blinding variety, consuming 25 energy if possible.
facts.detect: Invoke Grimtooth and observe the effect (acid or blindness).
facts.action: Use Grimtooth's venom ability strategically to blind or acid enemies, but be aware of energy consumption.

facts.fact: Elves cannot wield Grimtooth and will be blasted and evade its grasp.
facts.detect: Attempt to wield Grimtooth as an elf and notice the blast and evasion.
facts.action: Avoid wielding Grimtooth if the bot is polymorphed into an elf or is an elf.

facts.fact: Grimtooth is a major factor in chaotic heroes receiving Stormbringer through sacrifice, as elven heroes will never be gifted Grimtooth.
facts.detect: Check sacrifice gifts and notice the absence of Grimtooth for elven characters.
facts.action: Consider the implications of Grimtooth for chaotic characters aiming to receive Stormbringer through sacrifice.

facts.fact: A guisarme is a two-handed polearm that appears as a pruning hook when unidentified.
facts.detect: pruning hook
facts.action: Identify the weapon as a guisarme to understand its properties and usage.

facts.fact: Guisarmes can be found in general shops and antique weapons outlets.
facts.detect: Exploring shops and antique weapons outlets
facts.action: Check these locations for a guisarme.

facts.fact: Watchmen and soldiers may be generated with a guisarme.
facts.detect: Encountering watchmen or soldiers
facts.action: Be prepared to fight them if they are wielding a guisarme.

facts.fact: The guisarme has high average damage against small monsters among polearms.
facts.detect: Fighting small monsters
facts.action: Use the guisarme effectively against small monsters.

facts.fact: The guisarme has low average damage against large monsters.
facts.detect: Fighting large monsters
facts.action: Avoid using the guisarme against large monsters or find a more suitable weapon.

facts.fact: A halberd is a two-handed polearm with 2d6 damage and +0 to hit.
facts.detect: When the bot picks up or identifies an item as a halberd.
facts.action: Equip the halberd if the bot has the strength to wield two-handed weapons and is not already using a better weapon.

facts.fact: Halberds can be found in general shops and antique weapons outlets.
facts.detect: When the bot is in a shop and sees an item listed as a halberd.
facts.action: Purchase the halberd if the bot has the gold and it is not a cursed item.

facts.fact: Watchmen and soldiers may be generated with a halberd.
facts.detect: When the bot encounters a watchman or soldier.
facts.action: Prepare to fight or avoid the watchman or soldier if the bot is not ready for combat.

facts.fact: The halberd has the highest average damage against small monsters among polearms.
facts.detect: When the bot encounters small monsters.
facts.action: Use the halberd to attack small monsters.

facts.fact: While hallucinating, the hero's perception of their environment will change every time the screen is updated, even when simply far looking or starting and then aborting an action.
facts.detect: Status line shows 'Hallu' and messages like 'Oh wow! Everything so cosmic!' or 'Oh wow! Great stuff!'
facts.action: Avoid eating unidentified tins or quaffing unidentified potions, keep away from peaceful monsters and pets, and wait for the effect to end or use a unicorn horn to cure it.

facts.fact: Hallucination abuses the hero's wisdom every 5 turns for its duration.
facts.detect: Decrease in wisdom attribute.
facts.action: Cure hallucination as soon as possible to prevent further abuse of wisdom.

facts.fact: While hallucinating, the hero has a 3/4 chance of ignoring the effects of gaze attacks.
facts.detect: Being attacked by a monster with a gaze attack but not being affected.
facts.action: Exploit this to safely approach monsters with gaze attacks.

facts.fact: Monsters cannot hallucinate, with a monster that would be subjected to hallucination becoming confused instead.
facts.detect: Monster behavior changes to confused state.
facts.action: Be cautious as confused monsters may attack more unpredictably.

facts.fact: Hallucination can be cured by applying a unicorn horn of non-cursed beatitude, quaffing a potion of sickness, extra healing, or full healing, praying, or waiting for the effect to end.
facts.detect: Status line shows 'Hallu' and hero is hallucinating.
facts.action: Use one of the listed methods to cure hallucination.

facts.fact: Tourists start the game with an uncursed +0 Hawaiian shirt.
facts.detect: Starting inventory check
facts.action: Keep the Hawaiian shirt for later enchantment or trading purposes.

facts.fact: Entering a shop with a visible worn Hawaiian shirt will cause the shopkeeper to charge an extra 1/3 markup and buy things for 1/3 of the base price.
facts.detect: Shopkeeper dialogue mentioning Hawaiian shirt
facts.action: Remove the Hawaiian shirt before entering shops to avoid price penalties.

facts.fact: A Hawaiian shirt may be wished for in order to top off an otherwise-complete ascension kit.
facts.detect: Wishing for ascension kit items
facts.action: Consider wishing for an enchanted Hawaiian shirt if missing a torso slot item.

facts.fact: The Castle's armor storeroom has a 13.13% chance of containing either a Hawaiian shirt or a T-shirt.
facts.detect: Exploring the Castle's armor storeroom
facts.action: Search the storeroom for Hawaiian shirts or T-shirts.

facts.fact: A bones containing a Hawaiian shirt is very likely to belong to a Tourist.
facts.detect: Finding bones with a Hawaiian shirt
facts.action: Loot bones from Tourists for potential Hawaiian shirts.

facts.fact: A heavy iron ball is a type of item that appears in NetHack and is classified under the 'iron balls' object type in the hero's inventory.
facts.detect: heavy iron ball
facts.action: If found, the bot should consider using it as a weapon due to its high damage potential (d25) and +2 to-hit bonus when thrown.

facts.fact: Heavy iron balls are not randomly generated, though they can be wished for or found in bones.
facts.detect: bones level or wish for heavy iron ball
facts.action: If the bot finds itself in a bones level or has the opportunity to wish, it should consider wishing for a heavy iron ball to use as a weapon.

facts.fact: Reading a scroll of punishment that is cursed or uncursed will tether a heavy iron ball to the hero's leg.
facts.detect: message 'You feel a heavy weight on your leg.'
facts.action: If punished, the bot should attempt to remove the heavy iron ball as soon as possible to avoid the weight penalty.

facts.fact: The iron ball deals d25 damage against all monsters when wielded or thrown as a weapon, which is biased towards higher numbers if the ball has been made heavier.
facts.detect: wield or throw heavy iron ball
facts.action: The bot should use the heavy iron ball as a weapon due to its high damage potential, especially if it has been made heavier.

facts.fact: Using the iron ball as a weapon does not break the weaponless conduct.
facts.detect: hero's conduct status
facts.action: If the bot is trying to maintain the weaponless conduct, it can use the heavy iron ball without breaking this conduct.

facts.fact: A helm of brilliance appears as a 'crystal helmet' when unidentified.
facts.detect: crystal helmet
facts.action: Identify the item as a helm of brilliance if found.

facts.fact: The helm of brilliance grants 1 base point of AC and increases intelligence and wisdom by its enchantment.
facts.detect: Wearing the helm and noticing increased intelligence and wisdom stats.
facts.action: Wear the helm to improve spellcasting and AC.

facts.fact: A helm of brilliance has a 20% chance of becoming cracked if thrown, kicked, hit by a force bolt spell, or dropped from a great height.
facts.detect: Cracked helm of brilliance message.
facts.action: Handle the helm with care to avoid cracking it.

facts.fact: A helm of brilliance does not prevent instant death from brainlessness induced by intelligence drain.
facts.detect: Instant death from brainlessness.
facts.action: Avoid intelligence drain while wearing the helm.

facts.fact: A positively-enchanted helm of brilliance slightly improves energy regeneration and may give characters a significant boost to maximum power when gaining experience levels.
facts.detect: Noticing improved energy regeneration and power gain.
facts.action: Enchant the helm to +4 for maximum benefits.

facts.fact: Wearing a helm of opposite alignment will switch the hero's alignment to the opposite one, autocurse and auto-identify the helm, remove any divine protection, and set their alignment record to zero.
facts.detect: Message: Your mind oscillates (or Your mind is wildly oscillating if hallucinating).
facts.action: Avoid wearing the helm unless absolutely necessary, such as for specific alignment-based quests or artifact acquisition.

facts.fact: Wearing the helm incurs 7 points of alignment abuse, confuses the hero for 3-4 turns, and rolls an alignment abuse-based chance of summoning an erinys on an adjacent square.
facts.detect: Confusion effect and potential summoning of an erinys.
facts.action: Do not wear the helm in dangerous areas or when low on health and resources.

facts.fact: Attempting to wear the helm while in the hero's Quest branch will always fail and auto-identify the helm.
facts.detect: Message: You narrowly avoid losing all chance at your goal. or You are suddenly overcome with shame and change your mind.
facts.action: Do not attempt to wear the helm in the Quest branch.

facts.fact: Most helms of opposite alignment will generate cursed and can usually be avoided with relative ease, especially through methods such as pet-testing.
facts.detect: Item name: helm of opposite alignment and its cursed status.
facts.action: Formally identify a suspected helm of opposite alignment as soon as possible.

facts.fact: A chaotic hero may become lawful to safely traverse the Gnomish Mines in the early game, though this runs the risk of a tough fight with an erinys instead.
facts.detect: Hero's alignment and current level.
facts.action: Consider using the helm to change alignment temporarily if necessary, but be prepared for potential erinys encounters.

facts.fact: A helm of telepathy grants 1 base AC and the extrinsic telepathy property.
facts.detect: Wearing the helm and observing the increase in telepathy range or AC.
facts.action: Equip the helm of telepathy to gain telepathy and AC.

facts.fact: The helm of telepathy is one of the magical helms that can be found randomly with a 0.4% chance.
facts.detect: Finding a helm with randomized appearance in shops, on the ground, or as a death drop.
facts.action: Pick up and equip the helm if found.

facts.fact: The helm of telepathy raises spellcasting failure rates and protects from falling objects.
facts.detect: Observing spellcasting failure or noting protection from falling objects.
facts.action: Continue to use the helm for its benefits, but be cautious with spellcasting.

facts.fact: A non-chaotic character can use the helm of telepathy to murder peaceful humans and recover alignment and luck.
facts.detect: Intending to murder peaceful humans or priests.
facts.action: Wear the helm to murder peaceful humans if necessary and recover alignment and luck.

facts.fact: Telepathy can be confirmed by far looking a non-mindless monster.
facts.detect: Far looking a non-mindless monster.
facts.action: Confirm the helm's property by far looking a monster.

facts.fact: Knights start each game with a +0 helmet.
facts.detect: Checking inventory at the start of the game.
facts.action: Keep the +0 helmet as it provides a base AC of 1 and is enchanted.

facts.fact: Helmets make up 1% of all helms that are randomly generated on the ground.
facts.detect: Finding a helmet on the ground.
facts.action: Pick up the helmet if it has a positive enchantment or is a visored helmet.

facts.fact: Helmets hinder spellcasting for the hero while worn.
facts.detect: Trying to cast a spell while wearing a helmet.
facts.action: Remove the helmet if spellcasting is necessary.

facts.fact: Helmets can be distinguished from other randomized helms by their price and weight: they are the only ones to have a base cost of 10 zm and weigh 30 aum.
facts.detect: Checking the price and weight of a helm in a shop.
facts.action: Identify the helmet by its unique price and weight.

facts.fact: A helmet may still prove a viable replacement for the hero's current helm if it has a positive enchantment and/or has the appearance of a visored helmet, which offers eye protection.
facts.detect: Checking the enchantment and appearance of a helmet.
facts.action: Replace the current helm with the new helmet if it offers better protection or enchantment.

facts.fact: High boots grant 2 base AC.
facts.detect: Item name: high boots
facts.action: Equip high boots for additional AC.

facts.fact: High boots protect against xan's leg-wounding sting attack 4/5 of the time.
facts.detect: Monster name: xan
facts.action: Wear high boots when facing xan to mitigate sting damage.

facts.fact: High boots do not interfere with spellcasting.
facts.detect: Item name: high boots
facts.action: Wear high boots while spellcasting to avoid AC penalty from other boots.

facts.fact: High boots are commonly generated for quest guardians and player monsters on the Astral Plane.
facts.detect: Map feature: quest level, Astral Plane
facts.action: Search for high boots in quest levels and on the Astral Plane.

facts.fact: High boots are a suitable choice until finding magical boots like elven boots, speed boots, or jumping boots.
facts.detect: Item name: high boots
facts.action: Use high boots as a temporary AC boost until better boots are found.

facts.fact: A horn of plenty is a type of magical tool that appears in NetHack, made of bone, and appears as a horn when unidentified.
facts.detect: Item name 'horn of plenty' or appearance 'horn' when unidentified
facts.action: Identify the item to confirm it is a horn of plenty

facts.fact: Horns of plenty are very rare, making up 0.2% of all randomly-generated tools.
facts.detect: Not directly detectable, but known from item rarity
facts.action: Explore various shops and dungeon levels to find one

facts.fact: Applying a horn of plenty produces an item from it that is placed in the hero's inventory if possible, using up a charge and auto-identifying the horn.
facts.detect: Applying the horn and receiving an item
facts.action: Use the horn to generate food or potions when needed

facts.fact: A horn of plenty can hold up to 50 charges, and charging a horn of plenty with an uncursed scroll of charging adds 1 to 5 charges, while a blessed scroll adds 1 to 10 charges if the horn has 10 or less and otherwise adds 1 to 5 charges.
facts.detect: Having an uncursed or blessed scroll of charging
facts.action: Charge the horn with scrolls of charging to extend its usefulness

facts.fact: For a Tourist or any neutral hero with the Platinum Yendorian Express Card, a blessed horn of plenty is a great item as it can be recharged an unlimited number of times with little opportunity cost.
facts.detect: Having the Platinum Yendorian Express Card
facts.action: Bless the horn and recharge it as needed

facts.fact: A huge chunk of meat provides the highest nutrition value of any comestible in the game at 2000.
facts.detect: huge chunk of meat
facts.action: Eat the huge chunk of meat to gain a significant amount of nutrition, but be cautious of oversatiation and choking.

facts.fact: The huge chunk of meat is the heaviest non-corpse comestible at 400 aum.
facts.detect: huge chunk of meat
facts.action: Be aware of the weight and its effect on movement and encumbrance.

facts.fact: Eating while oversatiated can lead to choking and death unless the hero is breathless or wearing an amulet of life saving.
facts.detect: feeling: full
facts.action: Avoid eating if oversatiated, or use breathlessness or an amulet of life saving to mitigate choking risk.

facts.fact: The nutrition from a huge chunk of meat can last for several hundred turns, which can abuse dexterity.
facts.detect: feeling: full
facts.action: Engage in exercise or use a potion of restore ability to counteract the dexterity penalty.

facts.fact: Healers can use the spell of stone to flesh to create a huge chunk of meat from boulders.
facts.detect: stone to flesh spell
facts.action: Cast stone to flesh on boulders to create a huge chunk of meat for sustenance.

facts.fact: Ice boxes make up 1/200 of all randomly generated tools.
facts.detect: Finding an ice box on the ground or in a shop.
facts.action: Prioritize picking up an ice box if found, as it is rare and useful for corpse preservation.

facts.fact: Randomly generated ice boxes are always uncursed and may contain up to 20 random corpses.
facts.detect: Opening an ice box and finding uncursed corpses inside.
facts.action: Store valuable corpses in the ice box to prevent aging and spoilage.

facts.fact: Ice boxes prevent items from becoming wet and pause aging timers for corpses and eggs.
facts.detect: Checking the ice box's properties or storing a corpse and checking its age later.
facts.action: Use the ice box to preserve corpses and eggs for later use.

facts.fact: Ice boxes are very heavy (900 aum), making them impractical to carry around.
facts.detect: Feeling the weight of the ice box when picked up.
facts.action: Leave the ice box in a safe location and return to it later when needed.

facts.fact: Gelatinous cubes cannot eat plastic ice boxes, leaving contents unharmed.
facts.detect: Encountering a gelatinous cube while carrying an ice box.
facts.action: Use the ice box to store items and corpses when exploring areas with gelatinous cubes.

facts.fact: Iron chains are not randomly generated, though they can be wished for or found in bones.
facts.detect: Finding bones level or wishing for an item
facts.action: Wish for iron chains if needed for polypiling or leave them be as they are generally useless.

facts.fact: Iron chains are left behind by iron golems as a special death drop in lieu of a corpse.
facts.detect: Killing an iron golem
facts.action: Collect iron chains left by iron golems for polypiling or leave them be.

facts.fact: A wielded iron chain deals 1d4+1 damage on hit, with additional damage to susceptible monsters if blessed.
facts.detect: Equipping an iron chain
facts.action: Use iron chains as a weapon if blessed for additional damage, but generally avoid as they are considered useless.

facts.fact: Iron chains are considered the most useless item in NetHack.
facts.detect: Inventory management
facts.action: Discard iron chains as they serve few purposes and have no value when sold.

facts.fact: Iron chains can be used to lower the chance that something 'good' will be cursed or stolen.
facts.detect: Inventory management
facts.action: Carry iron chains in main inventory to lower the chance of good items being cursed or stolen, but consider using lighter objects instead.

facts.fact: Iron shoes grant 2 base AC.
facts.detect: Item name: iron shoes
facts.action: Equip iron shoes for additional AC.

facts.fact: Iron shoes protect against certain traps and leg-targeting attacks.
facts.detect: Trap types: beartrap, spiked pit, anti-magic trap, polymorph trap, land mine
facts.action: Wear iron shoes when encountering these traps.

facts.fact: Iron shoes interfere with spellcasting.
facts.detect: Spell failure rate increase
facts.action: Avoid wearing iron shoes if relying heavily on spells.

facts.fact: Iron shoes are vulnerable to rusting and corrosion.
facts.detect: Encounter with black puddings or rust monsters
facts.action: Avoid wearing iron shoes in areas with these monsters.

facts.fact: Iron shoes can be found easily in the Gnomish Mines.
facts.detect: Location: Gnomish Mines
facts.action: Look for iron shoes in the Gnomish Mines.

facts.fact: Javelins make up 1% of all randomly generated weapons.
facts.detect: Finding a javelin on the ground, in shops, or as a death drop.
facts.action: Pick up javelins if found, as they are relatively common and useful for ranged attacks.

facts.fact: Player monsters on the Astral Plane have a ~1.72% chance of being generated with up to 4 javelins.
facts.detect: Noticing a stack of up to 4 javelins when starting as a player monster on the Astral Plane.
facts.action: Keep the javelins for ranged attacks or trade them for better weapons if available.

facts.fact: Javelins have a +2 to-hit bonus when thrown and can be multishot.
facts.detect: Using a javelin and noticing the +2 to-hit bonus or the ability to multishot.
facts.action: Use javelins for ranged attacks to take advantage of the to-hit bonus and multishot ability.

facts.fact: Cave Dwellers get a +1 multishot bonus for throwing javelins.
facts.detect: Identifying as a Cave Dweller and throwing a javelin.
facts.action: Use javelins for ranged attacks to take advantage of the multishot bonus.

facts.fact: Monsters using ranged weapons prefer javelins to shuriken and will prefer orcish spears or better to javelins.
facts.detect: Noticing monsters using javelins or orcish spears.
facts.action: Be cautious of monsters using javelins, as they are a sign of a stronger ranged weapon preference.

facts.fact: Jumping boots grant 1 base AC and confer extrinsic jumping.
facts.detect: Wearing jumping boots and attempting to jump.
facts.action: Use jumping boots to escape dangerous situations or move faster through levels.

facts.fact: Player monsters on the Astral Plane have an effective ~8.01% chance of generating with jumping boots.
facts.detect: Encountering player monsters on the Astral Plane.
facts.action: Steal jumping boots from player monsters if they have them.

facts.fact: Jumping boots can be identified by attempting to jump while wearing them.
facts.detect: Wearing boots and attempting to jump.
facts.action: Use #jump command to identify if the boots are jumping boots.

facts.fact: Jumping boots are often part of an ascension kit.
facts.detect: Having a high level character with speed potions and haste self spell.
facts.action: Equip jumping boots to move faster through levels.

facts.fact: Jumping boots can be found in general stores, used armor dealerships, and antique weapons outlets.
facts.detect: Visiting these shops.
facts.action: Purchase jumping boots if available.

facts.fact: K-rations grant 400 nutrition and take one move to consume.
facts.detect: Item name: K-ration
facts.action: Eat K-ration when hungry to quickly gain nutrition.

facts.fact: K-rations can tame domestic canines and felines and pacify domestic equines.
facts.detect: Item name: K-ration, presence of domestic animals
facts.action: Use K-ration to tame or pacify domestic animals encountered.

facts.fact: K-rations are not randomly generated but have a 1/3 chance to be carried by mercenaries in the Yendorian Army.
facts.detect: Encountering mercenaries in Fort Ludios or the Castle
facts.action: Search mercenaries for K-rations.

facts.fact: K-rations are tied with lembas wafers for the highest amount of nutrition per turn for non-elven characters.
facts.detect: Item name: K-ration
facts.action: Carry K-ration in ascension kit for high nutrition value.

facts.fact: Eating a non-cursed K-ration results in the message 'This K-ration is bland.'
facts.detect: Message: This K-ration is bland.
facts.action: Ignore the blandness message as it indicates successful consumption.

facts.fact: All Samurai start the game with a +0 katana.
facts.detect: Starting equipment message mentioning a katana
facts.action: Keep the katana as it is a powerful starting weapon for a Samurai.

facts.fact: The katana deals 1d10 damage to small monsters and 1d12 damage to large monsters.
facts.detect: Attacking a monster and seeing the damage dealt
facts.action: Use the katana effectively against both small and large monsters.

facts.fact: A Samurai hero that attacks with a wielded katana and is not wearing a shield has a base 40% chance of performing a shattering blow that destroys the target's wielded weapon.
facts.detect: Attacking a monster and seeing the message 'shattering blow!'
facts.action: Attack monsters without a shield to maximize the chance of shattering their weapons.

facts.fact: The katana is the most damaging non-artifact weapon to use the long sword weapon skill.
facts.detect: Checking weapon skill and damage output
facts.action: Focus on improving the long sword skill to maximize the katana's effectiveness.

facts.fact: The katana is often sought after as an off-hand weapon for two-weapon combat.
facts.detect: Having a second weapon and seeing the damage output
facts.action: Use the katana as an off-hand weapon with another long sword skill weapon for two-weapon combat.

facts.fact: Kelp fronds are generated in pools and moats with a 1/10 chance for pools and 3/10 chance for moats.
facts.detect: Water squares with or without kelp fronds
facts.action: Use object detection or food detection to locate kelp fronds in water squares

facts.fact: Kelp fronds grant 30 base nutrition and take 1 turn to consume.
facts.detect: Eating a kelp frond
facts.action: Eat kelp fronds when hungry and have no other food available

facts.fact: Kelp fronds can be used to tame herbivorous domestic animals.
facts.detect: Herbivorous pets
facts.action: Use kelp fronds to tame ponies or other herbivorous pets

facts.fact: Kelp fronds are best collected in Juiblex's swamp and Medusa's Island.
facts.detect: Reaching Juiblex's swamp or Medusa's Island
facts.action: Collect kelp fronds in these areas if interested in harvesting them

facts.fact: Bullwhips cannot retrieve underwater items in NetHack 3.7.0.
facts.detect: Attempting to use a bullwhip in water
facts.action: Submerge in water to collect kelp fronds manually

facts.fact: Kicking boots give a +5 bonus to kick attacks against monsters that are not thick-skinned.
facts.detect: The bot notices a +5 bonus to kick attacks when wearing boots and attempting to kick a monster.
facts.action: The bot should use kick attacks more frequently against monsters that are not thick-skinned.

facts.fact: Kicking boots increase the distance that kicked objects travel.
facts.detect: The bot notices that kicked objects travel further than usual.
facts.action: The bot can use kicking boots to kick objects further, potentially to trigger traps or to clear out areas.

facts.fact: Kicking boots guarantee success when kicking down doors.
facts.detect: The bot attempts to kick a door and it opens immediately without any failure message.
facts.action: The bot should use kicking boots to reliably kick down doors.

facts.fact: Kicking boots can be used to reliably reveal secret passages and hidden doors.
facts.detect: The bot notices that kicking reveals secret passages and hidden doors without fail.
facts.action: The bot should use kicking boots to explore and reveal hidden areas.

facts.fact: Kicking boots have a randomized appearance and weigh 50 aum.
facts.detect: The bot identifies boots with a randomized appearance and weight of 50 aum.
facts.action: The bot should identify boots with these characteristics as kicking boots.

facts.fact: Knives make up 2% of all randomly generated weapons.
facts.detect: Finding a knife on the floor or in a shop
facts.action: Collect knives if you are a Healer or plan to use them as projectiles, but prioritize other weapons for melee.

facts.fact: Mordor orcs have a 1/3 chance of being generated with a knife.
facts.detect: Encountering a Mordor orc
facts.action: Be cautious as Mordor orcs may be armed with knives, which can be dangerous in melee.

facts.fact: Skeletons have an effective 1/6 chance of generating with a knife.
facts.detect: Encountering a skeleton
facts.action: Be prepared to fight skeletons that may be armed with knives.

facts.fact: Watchmen and Yendorian army soldiers have a 1/3 chance of generating with a knife as a secondary weapon.
facts.detect: Encountering watchmen or Yendorian army soldiers
facts.action: Be cautious as these enemies may be armed with knives.

facts.fact: Barrow wights and Nazgul are always generated with a knife.
facts.detect: Encountering barrow wights or Nazgul
facts.action: Be extremely cautious as these enemies are always armed with knives.

facts.fact: Knights start each game with a +1 lance.
facts.detect: Starting inventory as a Knight
facts.action: Keep the +1 lance as it is a powerful weapon for jousting.

facts.fact: Lances are quite rare, making up 0.4% of all randomly generated weapons.
facts.detect: Finding a lance in shops or on the ground
facts.action: Prioritize picking up lances when found as they are valuable.

facts.fact: Jousting chance is 1/5 base, increasing by 1/5 for each skill level.
facts.detect: Attacking a monster while riding with a lance
facts.action: Attempt jousting when attacking monsters while riding to deal extra damage and stun them.

facts.fact: Jousting can push monsters back one square if they are medium or smaller and not immobilized.
facts.detect: Seeing a monster pushed back after a joust
facts.action: Use jousting to control monster movement and keep them at a distance.

facts.fact: Lances have a luck-based chance of breaking during jousting.
facts.detect: Lance breaking message after jousting
facts.action: Avoid jousting with low luck to prevent lance breaking.

facts.fact: Land mines are only randomly generated in the form of traps, which are encountered at dungeon level 6 and below, and several land mines are placed in the treasure room of Fort Ludios.
facts.detect: Encountering a dungeon level 6 or below, or entering Fort Ludios
facts.action: Be cautious and prepared to disarm traps, especially in Fort Ludios

facts.fact: Stepping on a square with a land mine trap will set it off, causing d16 damage and wounded legs, and creating a pit.
facts.detect: KAABLAMM!!! You triggered a land mine!
facts.action: Avoid stepping on unexplored squares and be prepared to deal with sudden damage and movement restrictions

facts.fact: Flying or levitating over a land mine square will reveal the trap if it was not already visible, with a much lower chance of setting it off.
facts.detect: You discover a trigger in a pile of soil below you
facts.action: Use flying or levitating to safely explore areas with potential land mines

facts.fact: Land mines can be set off by rolling boulders, which can scatter rocks and potentially detonate land mines.
facts.detect: KAABLAMM!!! The rolling boulder triggers a land mine.
facts.action: Be cautious when dealing with boulder traps near suspected land mine areas

facts.fact: Land mines are very unlikely to be used by a majority of characters due to their weight and risk, and are primarily obstacles.
facts.detect: Encountering a land mine trap
facts.action: Treat land mines as significant hazards and avoid carrying them unless necessary

facts.fact: Large boxes have a 5/6 chance of being locked and contain useful items with a 1/5 chance of being a stack of two healing potions.
facts.detect: Locked large box, message 'You succeed in unlocking the .', 'Klick!', 'You break open the lock!', 'THUD! The lid slams open, then falls shut.'
facts.action: Unlock the box and check its contents for healing potions and other useful items.

facts.fact: Large boxes have a 1/5 chance of generating as a 'supply container' with useful items inside.
facts.detect: Large box in a room, message 'You succeed in unlocking the .', 'Klick!', 'You break open the lock!', 'THUD! The lid slams open, then falls shut.'
facts.action: Unlock and open the box to retrieve useful items.

facts.fact: Large boxes have a 1/10 chance of generating with a container trap, which is always obvious.
facts.detect: Message 'You hear a click as you approach the large box.'
facts.action: Disarm the trap before opening the box.

facts.fact: Large boxes can be used to store troll corpses to prevent them from reviving.
facts.detect: Troll corpse in inventory
facts.action: Lock a large box and store the troll corpse inside.

facts.fact: Large boxes can be used as stash locations, especially when secured with a boulder and/or scroll of scare monster to prevent gelatinous cubes from eating them.
facts.detect: Large box on the map
facts.action: Use large boxes as stash locations and secure them appropriately.

facts.fact: Large shields make up 0.7% of all randomly-generated armor.
facts.detect: Not directly detectable by the bot, but known from the wiki.
facts.action: The bot should not prioritize finding a large shield as it is rare.

facts.fact: Angels and Aleaxes have a 3/4 chance of generating with erodeproof large shields.
facts.detect: Encountering an Aleax or an Angel.
facts.action: If the bot encounters an Aleax or an Angel, it should attempt to pick up the erodeproof large shield they drop.

facts.fact: Mercenaries have an effective 1/6 chance of generating with a large shield that counts for 2 points of their target AC.
facts.detect: Encountering a Mercenary.
facts.action: If the bot encounters a Mercenary, it should attempt to pick up the large shield they drop.

facts.fact: Large shields grant 2 base AC.
facts.detect: Wearing a large shield.
facts.action: The bot should use a large shield for its AC value, but should consider replacing it with a lighter option like an elven shield or a shield of reflection if available.

facts.fact: Spellcasting-focused heroes will prefer small shields over large shields due to weight and casting conduciveness.
facts.detect: The bot's spellcasting ability or preference for lighter equipment.
facts.action: If the bot is a spellcaster or prefers lighter equipment, it should prefer small shields over large shields.

facts.fact: Tourists have a 4% chance of starting each game with a leash.
facts.detect: Starting inventory
facts.action: If the bot starts with a leash, it should keep it for potential pet management.

facts.fact: Leashes are used by applying them to a pet and selecting the direction of an adjacent square.
facts.detect: Applying a leash to a pet
facts.action: When a pet is needed to be controlled, apply the leash to it.

facts.fact: A hero can apply one leash per pet, and up to two such pets can be leashed at a time.
facts.detect: Attempting to leash a third pet
facts.action: Do not attempt to leash a third pet if two are already leashed.

facts.fact: A cursed leash cannot be removed from a pet by applying it.
facts.detect: Trying to remove a cursed leash
facts.action: Avoid removing a cursed leash from a pet to prevent choking and strangling the pet.

facts.fact: A hero that gets more than 3 squares away from a leashed pet while moving will pull on the leash.
facts.detect: Moving more than 3 squares away from a leashed pet
facts.action: Keep pets close to avoid pulling on the leash and causing them to vocalize their displeasure.

facts.fact: Leather armor provides an AC of 2 and MC1.
facts.detect: Leather armor
facts.action: Wear leather armor to improve AC and reduce spell failure rate for early spellcasting characters.

facts.fact: Cavemen start with +0 leather armor and Rogues start with +1 leather armor.
facts.detect: Starting character (Caveman or Rogue)
facts.action: Keep the starting leather armor until finding better armor.

facts.fact: Mercenaries have a chance to generate with leather armor that counts for 2 points of their target generation AC.
facts.detect: Mercenary
facts.action: Check if a Mercenary is wearing leather armor to estimate their AC.

facts.fact: Leather golems leave behind 2-8 sets of leather armor as a special death drop.
facts.detect: Leather golem death
facts.action: Collect the leather armor dropped by a leather golem.

facts.fact: Enchanted leather armor can be found from killing leather golems.
facts.detect: Leather golem death
facts.action: Check for enchanted leather armor dropped by a leather golem.

facts.fact: Leather cloaks make up 0.8% of all armor randomly generated on the ground, in general shops or as death drops.
facts.detect: Finding a leather cloak in a general shop or on the ground.
facts.action: Pick up the leather cloak as it provides 1 base AC and MC1, which can be useful early in the game.

facts.fact: Mercenaries have a 2 chance of generating with a leather cloak.
facts.detect: Encountering a mercenary with a leather cloak.
facts.action: Steal or kill the mercenary to obtain the leather cloak if needed.

facts.fact: Quest guardians commonly have a leather cloak.
facts.detect: Encountering quest guardians such as students, attendants, abbots, acolytes, guides, apprentices, chieftains, pages, roshis, and warriors.
facts.action: Steal or kill quest guardians to obtain the leather cloak if needed.

facts.fact: Leather cloaks grant 1 base AC and MC1.
facts.detect: Wearing a leather cloak.
facts.action: Use the leather cloak as temporary coverage until better magical cloaks are obtained.

facts.fact: A leather drum has a 6/35 chance of being the starting instrument for Elven Priests and Wizards.
facts.detect: Starting inventory includes a leather drum
facts.action: If the bot starts with a leather drum, it should be aware of the potential for deafness and monster awakening when using it.

facts.fact: Leather drums make up 0.4% of all randomly generated tools.
facts.detect: Finding a leather drum on the ground or in a shop
facts.action: The bot should be cautious when using a leather drum due to the risk of deafness and awakening monsters.

facts.fact: Applying a leather drum produces noise with a range dependent on the hero's experience level.
facts.detect: Applying the drum and seeing nearby monsters waking up
facts.action: The bot should avoid using the drum in areas with dangerous monsters or when it needs to remain stealthy.

facts.fact: Using a leather drum renders the hero deaf for 30-49 turns if not already deaf.
facts.detect: Message 'You beat a deafening row!' or 'You pound on the drum.'
facts.action: The bot should avoid using the drum in critical situations where hearing is necessary.

facts.fact: The noise from a leather drum can wake up sleeping monsters and scare them if they fail a roll against their MR score.
facts.detect: Seeing nearby monsters waking up and possibly fleeing
facts.action: The bot should use the drum strategically to scare off monsters but be cautious of unintended consequences.

facts.fact: Leather gloves grant 1 base AC while worn.
facts.detect: Wearing leather gloves
facts.action: Wear leather gloves to improve AC

facts.fact: Leather gloves are sufficient to prevent most footrice-related deaths.
facts.detect: Encountering footrice
facts.action: Wear leather gloves to avoid bare-handed footrice attacks

facts.fact: Leather gloves cannot be destroyed by polymorph and will at worst simply fall off.
facts.detect: Polymorph trap or spell
facts.action: Use leather gloves as a safe enchantment target

facts.fact: Leather gloves are trivial to distinguish via price identification.
facts.detect: Price of leather gloves is 8zm
facts.action: Identify leather gloves by price

facts.fact: Leather gloves are a common drop from soldiers, watchmen, and their higher-ups.
facts.detect: Killing soldiers, watchmen, or their higher-ups
facts.action: Collect leather gloves as backup or for polypiling

facts.fact: A leather jacket is a type of body armor that appears in NetHack, providing 1 base AC.
facts.detect: Leather jacket
facts.action: Equip the leather jacket for its AC bonus until better armor is found.

facts.fact: Archeologists start each game with a +0 leather jacket.
facts.detect: Starting character: Archeologist
facts.action: Keep the leather jacket as it provides initial AC and does not interfere with spellcasting.

facts.fact: Leather jackets make up 1.2% of all randomly-generated armor.
facts.detect: Randomly generated armor
facts.action: Pick up and equip leather jackets when found to improve AC temporarily.

facts.fact: Quest guardians commonly have a chance of being generated with a leather jacket.
facts.detect: Quest guardian names (Student, Attendant, Abbot, Acolyte, Guide, Apprentice, Hunter, Thug)
facts.action: Be prepared to fight quest guardians who may wear leather jackets.

facts.fact: Lembas wafers provide 800 base nutrition, with 200 extra nutrition for elven characters and 200 less nutrition for orcish heroes.
facts.detect: elf or orc character status
facts.action: Stock up on lembas wafers if not an orc, as they provide high nutrition. If an orc, consider other food options due to reduced nutrition.

facts.fact: Lembas wafers have the highest nutrition-to-weight ratio of all comestibles at 800 nutrition to 5 units.
facts.detect: weight and nutrition values of lembas wafers
facts.action: Prioritize lembas wafers for ascension kits due to their high efficiency.

facts.fact: Lembas wafers can be thrown to tame domestic cats and dogs and pacify horses.
facts.detect: presence of domestic cats, dogs, or horses
facts.action: Use lembas wafers to tame or pacify animals when needed.

facts.fact: Lembas wafers are never rotten.
facts.detect: non-cursed lembas wafers
facts.action: Eat non-cursed lembas wafers without checking for rot.

facts.fact: Lembas wafers are generated as 2% of all comestibles in the game.
facts.detect: randomly generated food items
facts.action: Collect lembas wafers when found, as they are valuable for their nutrition.

facts.fact: Randomly generated levitation boots have a 9/10 chance of being cursed.
facts.detect: Message: 'You feel strangely heavy.' or 'You feel strangely light.'
facts.action: Avoid wearing unidentified levitation boots unless you have a way to remove curses.

facts.fact: Cursed levitation boots prevent reaching the floor to grab items or travel down stairs.
facts.detect: Message: 'You feel strangely heavy.'
facts.action: Find a sink to remove cursed levitation boots.

facts.fact: Successful prayer is a viable solution for removing cursed levitation boots.
facts.detect: Message: 'You feel strangely heavy.'
facts.action: Pray to remove the curse if you have the prayer points.

facts.fact: Levitation boots auto-identify when worn if the wearer is not already levitating.
facts.detect: Message: 'You feel strangely light.'
facts.action: Wear to identify if you are not levitating.

facts.fact: Levitation boots cannot be destroyed by shock damage, unlike a ring of levitation.
facts.detect: Message: 'You feel strangely light.'
facts.action: Wear if you expect to encounter electric eels or similar.

facts.fact: Normally-generated loadstones on the dungeon's floor are always generated cursed.

facts.fact: A loadstone will autocurse once it is dropped or leaves the main inventory in any other way.
facts.detect: Attempting to drop a gray stone and being unable to.

facts.fact: A loadstone weighs slightly more than an iron ball at 500 aum.
facts.detect: Feeling unusually heavy when picking up a gray stone.

facts.fact: Loadstones are heavy enough that they cannot be kicked under normal circumstances.

facts.fact: All Rogues start the game with an uncursed lock pick.
facts.detect: Starting inventory as a Rogue

facts.fact: Lock picks make up 6% of all tools that are randomly generated on the ground, in general shops or as death drops.

facts.fact: A lock pick is one of the items generated within the niches around the room with the up stair on the first floor of Vlad's Tower at level creation.

facts.fact: Knights start each game with a +1 long sword.

facts.fact: A long sword is always generated in a niche on the first floor of Vlad's Tower.
facts.detect: Exploring the first floor of Vlad's Tower and finding a niche.
facts.action: Search the niche for a long sword.

facts.fact: Watch captains, Yendorian army captains and lieutenants each have a roughly 50% chance of generating with a long sword.
facts.detect: Encountering these monsters and noting they are wielding a long sword.
facts.action: Steal or take the long sword from these monsters if possible.

facts.fact: The Norn, the quest leader for the Valkyrie quest, is always generated with a +4 long sword.

facts.fact: A lawful hero that is at least experience level 5 and dips a single, non-artifact long sword that is not named into a fountain has a chance of transforming the sword into the blessed and erosion-proofed Excalibur.
facts.detect: Finding a fountain and having a non-artifact long sword.
facts.action: Dip the long sword into the fountain to attempt to transform it into Excalibur.

facts.fact: Low boots provide 1 base AC.

facts.fact: Low boots protect legs from xan stings 2/5 of the time.
facts.detect: Encounter with xan monsters.
facts.action: Wear low boots to reduce risk of leg wounds from xan stings.

facts.fact: Low boots are lighter than iron shoes and resist rust.
facts.detect: Iron shoes in inventory or rust traps/monsters.
facts.action: Prefer low boots over iron shoes to avoid rust damage.

facts.fact: Low boots are commonly found in used armor dealerships and antique weapon outlets.
facts.detect: Visit shops and find low boots.
facts.action: Purchase low boots from shops if available.

facts.fact: Low boots are generated on 2.5% of all randomly-generated armor.
facts.detect: Randomly generated armor in the dungeon.
facts.action: Pick up low boots when found.

facts.fact: A lucern hammer makes up 0.5% of all randomly-generated weapons.
facts.detect: Finding a lucern hammer in a general store, used armor dealership, or antique weapon outlet.
facts.action: If found, consider equipping it as a two-handed weapon if no better option is available, but be aware of its weight and damage limitations.

facts.fact: Watchmen and soldiers may be generated with a lucern hammer.
facts.detect: Encountering watchmen or soldiers carrying a lucern hammer.
facts.action: Be cautious when fighting watchmen or soldiers with a lucern hammer, as they may be stronger than usual.

facts.fact: Strong humanoid monsters with weapon attack and ability to wield weapons have a chance of generating with a lucern hammer.
facts.detect: Encountering a strong humanoid monster wielding a lucern hammer.
facts.action: Treat such monsters with caution due to the potential for increased combat difficulty.

facts.fact: A noncursed luckstone adds 3 Luck, and can exceed the ordinary maximum of 10 in this way; and a cursed luckstone subtracts 3 Luck.
facts.detect: Luck value displayed in inventory or status screen
facts.action: Formally identify the beatitude of the luckstone as soon as possible to avoid negative Luck effects.

facts.fact: A cursed luckstone prevents the timeout of negative Luck, blessed ones prevent the timeout of positive Luck and uncursed ones prevent both.
facts.detect: Luck value displayed in inventory or status screen
facts.action: Keep a backup luckstone in a container or stash in case the primary luckstone becomes cursed.

facts.fact: Luckstones are typically vital to any ascension kit.
facts.detect: Luck value displayed in inventory or status screen
facts.action: Maximize Luck before entering Gehennom, as it is vital for ascension.

facts.fact: Once you have a known luckstone or other similar item to prevent Luck timeout, you want to max out your Luck.
facts.detect: Luck value displayed in inventory or status screen
facts.action: Increase Luck by throwing precious gems to co-aligned unicorns or sacrificing powerful monsters on a co-aligned altar.

facts.fact: An uncursed luckstone in Sokoban may be worth putting away temporarily in order to allow Luck penalties from any 'illegal' moves you make to time out.
facts.detect: Sokoban level
facts.action: Temporarily put away the uncursed luckstone in Sokoban to allow Luck penalties to time out.

facts.fact: A lump of royal jelly grants 200 base nutrition and can heal wounded legs and increase strength by one point if non-cursed.
facts.detect: Eating a lump of royal jelly
facts.action: Eat a lump of royal jelly if wounded or to increase strength

facts.fact: There is a 1/3 chance of each square in a beehive being generated with a lump of royal jelly.
facts.detect: Exploring beehives
facts.action: Search beehives for lumps of royal jelly

facts.fact: Applying a charged horn of plenty has a 5% chance of producing 1-2 lumps of royal jelly.
facts.detect: Using a charged horn of plenty
facts.action: Use a charged horn of plenty to potentially obtain royal jelly

facts.fact: Lumps of royal jelly can be thrown to tame carnivorous domestic animals.
facts.detect: Having carnivorous domestic animals
facts.action: Use lumps of royal jelly to tame carnivorous domestic animals

facts.fact: Cursed royal jelly will lower strength by one point and may decrease the hero's HP by up to 20.
facts.detect: Eating cursed royal jelly
facts.action: Avoid eating cursed royal jelly

facts.fact: Clerics start each game with a blessed +1 mace.
facts.detect: Starting inventory message mentioning a blessed +1 mace.
facts.action: Keep the blessed +1 mace as it is a good early-game weapon.

facts.fact: Maces make up 4% of all randomly generated weapons.
facts.detect: Finding a mace in the dungeon or in shops.
facts.action: Consider picking up maces, especially if they are enchanted.

facts.fact: Aligned clerics, acolytes, high clerics, and the Arch Priest are always generated with maces.
facts.detect: Encountering these monsters in the dungeon.
facts.action: Be prepared to fight these monsters as they will be armed with maces.

facts.fact: The Arch Priest is also generated with a +4 mace.
facts.detect: Encountering the Arch Priest.
facts.action: Be wary of the Arch Priest's +4 mace, as it is a powerful weapon.

facts.fact: Player monsters, including those generated on the Astral Plane, have a ~3.44% chance of generating with a mace.
facts.detect: Encountering player monsters in the Astral Plane or elsewhere.
facts.action: Be prepared to fight player monsters that may be armed with maces.

facts.fact: A magic flute is a type of magical tool that appears in NetHack, made of wood and appears as a flute when unidentified.
facts.detect: Item name: magic flute
facts.action: Identify the item as a magic flute when found.

facts.fact: Magic flutes are rare, making up 0.2% of all tools randomly generated on the ground, in general shops, or as death drops.
facts.detect: Item rarity
facts.action: Prioritize finding and using magic flutes due to their rarity and utility.

facts.fact: Choosing to improvise on a magic flute with charges will exercise dexterity and use up a charge to produce 'soft music' that has a chance of putting all nearby monsters to sleep.
facts.detect: Message: You produce music.
facts.action: Use the magic flute to put nearby monsters to sleep when in danger.

facts.fact: A hero that applies a magic flute while stunned, confused, or hallucinating will automatically improvise with it.
facts.detect: Status: stunned, confused, or hallucinating
facts.action: Avoid using the magic flute when in these states to prevent unintended effects.

facts.fact: A hero cannot apply a magic flute if they are subjected to strangulation, in the form of a sea monster, or in the form of any monster that is tiny, unbreathing, cannot speak, lacks a head, or can only buzz.
facts.detect: Status: strangulation, sea monster form, tiny form, unbreathing form, cannot speak form, lacks a head form, buzz form
facts.action: Avoid using the magic flute in these conditions.

facts.fact: Magic harps are generated with 4 to 8 charges and can hold a maximum of 20 charges.
facts.detect: Item description or 'magic harp' in inventory
facts.action: Check the number of charges when found and recharge if necessary.

facts.fact: Improvising on a magic harp with charges will exercise dexterity and use up a charge to produce 'attractive music' that has a chance of taming nearby monsters.
facts.detect: Message 'The harp produces very attractive music.'
facts.action: Use the magic harp to tame monsters when in danger or need to pacify enemies.

facts.fact: Choosing to improvise on a magic harp with no charges will treat it as an applied wooden harp, which has a chance of pacifying nearby nymphs.
facts.detect: Message 'You extract a strange sound from the magic harp!' when no charges are left
facts.action: Use the magic harp to pacify nymphs when in danger or need to calm enemies.

facts.fact: The hero will be prevented from applying a magic harp while underwater.
facts.detect: Being in water
facts.action: Avoid using the magic harp underwater.

facts.fact: The magic harp can be used to play the passtune to enter the Castle.
facts.detect: Being near the Castle drawbridge
facts.action: Use the magic harp to play the passtune to enter the Castle.

facts.fact: Magic lamps make up 1.5% of all tools randomly generated on the ground, in general shops or as death drops.
facts.detect: Finding a lamp with a price of 50 and weight of 20 in a shop or on the ground.
facts.action: Pick up the lamp and bless it before rubbing it.

facts.fact: Applying a magic lamp is much like applying an oil lamp, but it will never run out of fuel.
facts.detect: Applying the lamp and observing that it does not run out of fuel.
facts.action: Use the lamp as a reliable light source in dark areas.

facts.fact: Each time the hero rubs a magic lamp, there is a 1/3 chance of a puff of smoke, a 1/3 chance that nothing happens, and a 1/3 chance of a djinni appearing.
facts.detect: Rubbing the lamp and observing the outcome (puff of smoke, djinni appearance, or nothing).
facts.action: Rub the lamp to potentially summon a djinni for a wish.

facts.fact: If a djinni appears, the lamp is then identified and turns into an oil lamp of the same beatitude with fuel for 1000-1500 turns.
facts.detect: Observing the lamp turning into an oil lamp after a djinni appears.
facts.action: Use the oil lamp for light and prepare to make a wish if the djinni grants it.

facts.fact: Always make sure a magic lamp is blessed before rubbing it, as an early magic lamp stands a high chance of being wasted if you rub it without knowing its beatitude.
facts.detect: Checking the beatitude of the lamp before rubbing it.
facts.action: Bless the lamp before rubbing it to maximize the chance of a wish.

facts.fact: A magic marker is generated with 30–99 charges.
facts.detect: Upon reading the magic marker, it will display the number of charges.
facts.action: Check the number of charges when you find a magic marker to plan your writing strategy.

facts.fact: Monks and Wizards have a 1/5 chance of starting with a magic marker.
facts.detect: Upon starting the game, check inventory for a magic marker.
facts.action: If you start with a magic marker, prioritize using it to write scrolls and spellbooks.

facts.fact: Writing a scroll or spellbook uses up charges, and the cost is random between half and the full ink cost.
facts.detect: When attempting to write, the game will inform you if your marker is too dry.
facts.action: Be cautious with charges and only write when you are sure you have enough.

facts.fact: Successfully writing an unknown scroll or spellbook depends on luck and whether you are a Wizard.
facts.detect: When attempting to write an unknown item, the game will inform you of success or failure.
facts.action: Maximize luck and attempt to write high-value scrolls or spellbooks.

facts.fact: Engraving Elbereth with a magic marker is generally a waste of charges, but can be necessary in emergencies.
facts.detect: When engraving Elbereth, the game will inform you of the charge cost.
facts.action: Use other methods to engrave Elbereth unless you are in a situation where you need to use the marker.

facts.fact: Your marker dries out while writing, leaving the writing unfinished or the scroll useless and disappearing.
facts.detect: Your marker dries out!
facts.action: Avoid using a magic marker when it is low on ink or when you are unsure of the outcome.

facts.fact: Attempting to write a spellbook or scroll without knowing how results in failure and potential loss.
facts.detect: You don't know how to write that.
facts.action: Only attempt to write spellbooks or scrolls if you are certain of the outcome or have identified the item.

facts.fact: A magic marker can only be recharged once.
facts.detect: Your marker seems permanently dried out.
facts.action: Do not attempt to recharge a magic marker that has already been used.

facts.fact: Writing a scroll by description can fail if the scroll is not formally identified.
facts.detect: You fail to write that.
facts.action: Ensure scrolls are formally identified before attempting to write them by description.

facts.fact: A non-cursed magic whistle produces a 'strange sound' that warps any pets on the current level next to the hero, auto-identifying the whistle if a pet warps.
facts.detect: Message 'You produce a strange whistling sound.' or 'You produce a strange, sharp vibration.'
facts.action: Use the whistle to warp pets to a safer location or to reveal hidden pets like mimics.

facts.fact: A cursed magic whistle has a roughly 50% chance of producing a 'high-pitched humming noise' that awakens all sleeping monsters in a roughly-circular area with a radius less than the square root of (20*XL).
facts.detect: Message 'You produce a high-pitched humming noise.' or 'You produce a high-frequency vibration.'
facts.action: Avoid using cursed whistles unless in a safe area or when pets are needed to protect the hero.

facts.fact: A hero cannot apply a magic whistle if they are subjected to strangulation, if they are in the form of a sea monster, or if they are in the form of any monster that is tiny in size, unbreathing, cannot speak, lacks a head, or can only buzz.
facts.detect: Hero's status or form
facts.action: Do not use the whistle under these conditions.

facts.fact: A hero can apply a magic whistle while underwater.
facts.detect: Underwater status
facts.action: Use the whistle underwater to reveal hidden pets or warp them.

facts.fact: Spare magic whistles may be worth keeping for polypiling fodder to turn into other magical items such as magic markers.
facts.detect: Inventory item 'magic whistle'
facts.action: Keep extra magic whistles for polypiling.

facts.fact: Magicbane grants magic resistance and absorbs and negates 95% of curses when wielded.
facts.detect: The bot notices it has magic resistance and sees messages like 'You feel immune to curses.'
facts.action: Wield Magicbane to gain magic resistance and protection from curses.

facts.fact: Magicbane has a +1d3 to-hit bonus and deals +1d4 damage if the monster fails a magic resistance check.
facts.detect: The bot sees messages like 'You hit the monster for extra damage.'
facts.action: Use Magicbane to attack monsters, especially those with low magic resistance.

facts.fact: Magicbane has a 1-in-12 chance of confusing the target with any magical attack.
facts.detect: The bot sees messages like 'The monster is confused.'
facts.action: Continue attacking with Magicbane to potentially confuse enemies.

facts.fact: Magicbane has a 1-in-20 chance of probing a monster's stats when enchanted to +0.
facts.detect: The bot sees messages like 'You feel a strange probing sensation.'
