facts.action: Wield Magicbane to gain information about monsters.

facts.fact: Magicbane's enchantment affects the probability of stun, scare, and cancel effects.
facts.detect: The bot sees messages like 'The magic-absorbing blade stuns the monster.'
facts.action: Maintain a moderate enchantment level on Magicbane to balance damage and effects.

facts.fact: Meat rings are not randomly generated and can only be created by zapping a stone to flesh spell at a ring with a randomized appearance that is made of mineral or gemstone.
facts.detect: None, as the bot cannot generate these items itself and must find them in the game.
facts.action: If the bot finds a ring with one of the listed appearances (agate, black onyx, clay, coral, diamond, emerald, granite, jade, moonstone, opal, ruby, sapphire, tiger eye, topaz) and has the spell of stone to flesh, it can zap the spell at the ring to create a meat ring.

facts.fact: Meat rings grant 5 base nutrition when eaten.
facts.detect: Meat ring item name.
facts.action: Eat the meat ring to gain nutrition if the bot is hungry and has no better food options.

facts.fact: Meat rings can be worn like normal rings but have no effect and do not incur ring hunger.
facts.detect: Meat ring item name.
facts.action: Wear the meat ring if the bot has no better rings to wear and needs to avoid ring hunger penalties.

facts.fact: Meat rings can be used to tame carnivorous domestic animals or as a treat for carnivorous pets.
facts.detect: Carnivorous pet or domestic animal.
facts.action: Feed the meat ring to a carnivorous pet or domestic animal to tame it.

facts.fact: Dropping a meat ring down a sink prints a message: 'Several flies buzz around the sink.'
facts.detect: Message: 'Several flies buzz around the sink.'
facts.action: Avoid dropping meat rings down sinks to prevent waste.

facts.fact: Meat sticks are not randomly generated and can only be created by zapping a stone to flesh spell at a wand with the 'marble wand' randomized appearance.
facts.detect: Zapping a stone to flesh spell at a wand with the appearance 'marble wand'.
facts.action: If the bot has a wand and the appearance 'marble wand', it should zap the stone to flesh spell at it to create a meat stick.

facts.fact: Meat sticks grant 5 base nutrition.
facts.detect: Eating a meat stick.
facts.action: Use meat sticks to feed carnivorous pets or tame carnivorous domestic animals, or as a last resort for nutrition.

facts.fact: Most meat sticks are junk created from a hero zapping stone to flesh at themselves.
facts.detect: Zapping stone to flesh at oneself.
facts.action: Avoid zapping stone to flesh at oneself to prevent creating junk meat sticks.

facts.fact: A meat stick provides very little nutrition.
facts.detect: Checking the nutrition value of a meat stick.
facts.action: Use meat sticks as a lightweight treat for carnivorous pets or tame carnivorous domestic animals, or as polyfodder.

facts.fact: Meatballs are not randomly generated and can only be created by zapping a stone to flesh spell at rocks, valuable gems, gray stones, or statues that depict tiny-sized or non-fleshy monsters.
facts.detect: Zapping a stone to flesh spell at rocks, valuable gems, gray stones, or statues that depict tiny-sized or non-fleshy monsters.
facts.action: Use the stone to flesh spell to create meatballs.

facts.fact: Meatballs grant 5 base nutrition and take 1 turn to consume.
facts.detect: Eating a meatball.
facts.action: Eat meatballs to gain nutrition.

facts.fact: Meatballs are considered a treat for carnivorous pets and can be thrown to tame carnivorous domestic animals.
facts.detect: Carnivorous pets or domestic animals.
facts.action: Feed meatballs to carnivorous pets or throw them to tame carnivorous domestic animals.

facts.fact: Meatballs are useful for taming hostile domestic carnivores.
facts.detect: Hostile domestic carnivores.
facts.action: Use meatballs to tame hostile domestic carnivores.

facts.fact: Meatballs can be used as polyfodder to obtain lightweight food such as lembas wafers, tins of spinach, tengu meat, and cockatrice eggs.
facts.detect: Cockatrice or its corpse, tengu meat, tins of spinach, lembas wafers.
facts.action: Use meatballs as polyfodder to obtain these items.

facts.fact: Melons make up 1% of all comestibles randomly generated on the ground, in general shops or as death drops.
facts.detect: Finding a melon on the ground, in shops, or as a death drop.
facts.action: Eat the melon to gain 100 nutrition, which is useful for keeping fed.

facts.fact: Eating a melon grants 100 nutrition and takes 1 turn to consume it.
facts.detect: Eating a melon.
facts.action: Consume the melon to gain nutrition and continue playing.

facts.fact: Melons are fragile, and throwing one will cause it to 'splat' and be destroyed.
facts.detect: Throwing a melon.
facts.action: Avoid throwing melons to prevent wasting them.

facts.fact: Melons share the same color glyph as the corpse of Medusa.
facts.detect: Seeing a bright green glyph.
facts.action: Be cautious and verify the identity of the object before interacting with it to avoid confusion with Medusa's corpse.

facts.fact: Mirrors have a 50% chance of being generated with nymphs.
facts.detect: Encountering a nymph
facts.action: Avoid using force bolt or wand of striking on nymphs to prevent luck penalty from breaking the mirror.

facts.fact: Applying a mirror to a floating eye will paralyze it for several turns with a 4/5 chance.
facts.detect: Encountering a floating eye
facts.action: Use a mirror to paralyze a floating eye before engaging it.

facts.fact: Applying a mirror to an umber hulk will confuse it.
facts.detect: Encountering an umber hulk
facts.action: Use a mirror to confuse an umber hulk before engaging it.

facts.fact: Applying a mirror to a nymph or foocubus will cause it to steal the mirror and teleport away.
facts.detect: Encountering a nymph or foocubus
facts.action: Use a mirror to prevent a nymph or foocubus from stealing items.

facts.fact: Applying a mirror to Medusa will reflect her stoning gaze back at her, turning her to stone.
facts.detect: Encountering Medusa
facts.action: Use a mirror to reflect Medusa's gaze back at her.

facts.fact: Mjollnir has a +d5 to-hit bonus and deals +d24 shock damage against non-shock resistant monsters.
facts.detect: The bot can notice the situation when it encounters a monster without shock resistance and observes the damage dealt.
facts.action: The bot should prioritize using Mjollnir against non-shock resistant monsters to maximize damage.

facts.fact: Mjollnir has a 1/5 chance of destroying each wand and ring in the target's inventory on a hit.
facts.detect: The bot can detect this when it observes wands or rings disappearing from a monster's inventory after a hit.
facts.action: The bot should be cautious when using Mjollnir against monsters with valuable wands or rings in their inventory.

facts.fact: Mjollnir is magically heavy and can only be thrown by a hero with 25 strength and is wielding the non-cursed artifact.
facts.detect: The bot can detect this when it tries to throw Mjollnir and fails due to lack of strength or being cursed.
facts.action: The bot should ensure it has gauntlets of power or equivalent strength boost before attempting to throw Mjollnir.

facts.fact: Mjollnir has a 99% chance of returning to the Valkyrie when thrown, and a 99% chance of being caught if not confused, stunned, blind, hallucinating, or fumbling.
facts.detect: The bot can detect this when it throws Mjollnir and observes it returning.
facts.action: The bot should throw Mjollnir only when it is not confused, stunned, blind, hallucinating, or fumbling to avoid losing the weapon.

facts.fact: Mjollnir deals low base damage but high shock damage, making it effective against non-shock resistant monsters.
facts.detect: The bot can detect this when it observes the damage dealt to non-shock resistant monsters.
facts.action: The bot should use Mjollnir primarily against non-shock resistant monsters to maximize its effectiveness.

facts.fact: Morning stars make up 1.2% of all weapons randomly generated on the ground, in general shops or as death drops.
facts.detect: Finding a morning star in a general shop or on the ground.
facts.action: Pick up morning stars if found, as they are relatively rare.

facts.fact: A normally-generated morning star has a base 20% chance of being made into Trollsbane if no artifacts have been generated yet.
facts.detect: Picking up a morning star and checking if it is Trollsbane.
facts.action: If a morning star is found, check if it is Trollsbane and prioritize it if it is.

facts.fact: Player monsters that are not monks and are created on the Astral Plane have an effective 2.06% chance of being generated with a morning star as their initial weapon.
facts.detect: Starting the game as a non-monk character on the Astral Plane.
facts.action: If starting on the Astral Plane, check if the initial weapon is a morning star.

facts.fact: Morning stars are preferred by monsters over elven short swords but less preferred than silver sabers or better.
facts.detect: Encountering monsters wielding morning stars.
facts.action: Be cautious of monsters wielding morning stars as they may be stronger than usual.

facts.fact: Morning stars are heavy at 120 aum and are generally not common enough for most heroes to consider investing skill points in.
facts.detect: Checking the weight of a morning star (120 aum).
facts.action: Avoid investing skill points in morning stars due to their weight and rarity.

facts.fact: Mummy wrappings are not generated randomly, though they can be wished for or found in bones.
facts.detect: Finding bones level with a mummy or wishing for mummy wrapping
facts.action: Wish for or seek bones levels to find mummy wrapping

facts.fact: Mummies have a 6/7 chance of being generated with a mummy wrapping.
facts.detect: Encountering a mummy
facts.action: Check inventory for mummy wrapping after defeating a mummy

facts.fact: Wearing a mummy wrapping negates invisibility.
facts.detect: Becoming visible after putting on mummy wrapping while invisible
facts.action: Use mummy wrapping to negate invisibility effects

facts.fact: Wearing a mummy wrapping prevents the effects of some items from turning the wearer invisible.
facts.detect: Not becoming invisible after using an item that normally causes invisibility
facts.action: Wear mummy wrapping when using items that cause invisibility

facts.fact: Heroes that elect for permanent invisibility will often keep a mummy wrapping on hand to enter shops.
facts.detect: Being unable to enter a shop while invisible
facts.action: Put on mummy wrapping to enter shops

facts.fact: Ogresmasher sets the wielder's constitution to 25.
facts.detect: Wield Ogresmasher and check constitution.
facts.action: Wield Ogresmasher before leveling up to gain more HP.

facts.fact: Ogresmasher has a +d5 to-hit bonus.
facts.detect: Wield Ogresmasher and check to-hit bonus.
facts.action: Use Ogresmasher in combat for improved accuracy.

facts.fact: Ogresmasher does double damage against ogres.
facts.detect: Encounter ogres while wielding Ogresmasher.
facts.action: Target ogres for combat to maximize damage.

facts.fact: Ogresmasher can be obtained as a sacrifice gift.
facts.detect: Sacrifice a monster with a positive non-zero 5 value.
facts.action: Sacrifice a monster to obtain Ogresmasher.

facts.fact: Ogresmasher has +2 enchantment when randomly generated or gifted.
facts.detect: Check the enchantment of Ogresmasher upon obtaining.
facts.action: Use Ogresmasher's inherent +2 enchantment for better stats.

facts.fact: An oil lamp is a light source that appears as a lamp when unidentified and is made of copper.
facts.detect: lamp
facts.action: Identify the lamp as an oil lamp by applying it or by its appearance.

facts.fact: Valkyries have a {{frac|6}} chance of starting the game with an oil lamp.
facts.detect: Starting inventory
facts.action: If starting with an oil lamp, use it to light dark areas and conserve it by turning it off in lit areas.

facts.fact: Applying a cursed oil lamp has a {{frac|2}} chance of lighting and a {{frac|3}} chance of spilling oil on your hands if it fails to light.
facts.detect: Message: The lamp spills and covers your fingers with oil.
facts.action: Avoid lighting cursed oil lamps unless necessary.

facts.fact: Oil lamps can be refilled by reading a scroll of charging, invoking the Platinum Yendorian Express Card, or #dipping the unlit lamp into a potion of oil.
facts.detect: Inventory contains scroll of charging or potion of oil
facts.action: Refill the oil lamp when it is about to go out to continue exploring dark areas.

facts.fact: Oil lamps will remain on for 1000 to 1499 turns and provide light in a radius of three squares.
facts.detect: Lamp flickering messages
facts.action: Turn off the oil lamp when entering a lit room or area to conserve it.

facts.fact: An oilskin cloak grants 1 base AC and MC2, and functions as a permanently greased cloak.
facts.detect: slippery cloak
facts.action: Equip the oilskin cloak to protect against grabbing attacks and water damage.

facts.fact: A non-cursed oilskin cloak protects its wearer from all grabbing attacks, including the drowning attacks commonly associated with sea monsters.
facts.detect: Encounter with sea monsters or water traps
facts.action: Wear the oilskin cloak to avoid drowning and grabbing attacks.

facts.fact: Buying or selling an oilskin cloak in a shop will auto-identify the cloak.
facts.detect: Attempting to buy or sell a slippery cloak in a shop
facts.action: Buy or sell the cloak to identify it.

facts.fact: A cursed oilskin cloak will only stop grabbing and protect armor 2/3 of the time.
facts.detect: Cursed status of the cloak
facts.action: Avoid wearing a cursed oilskin cloak or find a way to uncursed it.

facts.fact: An oilskin sack can protect its contents from water damage if not cursed, and auto-identifies when it prevents water from getting inside.
facts.detect: Some water slides right off your oilskin sack.
facts.action: Store water-sensitive items like potions, scrolls, and rust-prone weapons and armor in an oilskin sack to protect them from water damage.

facts.fact: Oilskin sacks can be auto-identified by dipping them into water.
facts.detect: Dipping an oilskin sack into water.
facts.action: Dip an oilskin sack into water to auto-identify it.

facts.fact: Oilskin sacks can be used to protect a bag of holding from water damage and the curse items monster spell.
facts.detect: Having a bag of holding and an oilskin sack.
facts.action: Place the bag of holding inside an oilskin sack to protect its contents from water damage and potential curses.

facts.fact: Oilskin sacks can protect a wand of cancellation stored outside the main bag of holding.
facts.detect: Possessing a wand of cancellation and an oilskin sack.
facts.action: Store the wand of cancellation in an oilskin sack to protect it.

facts.fact: Oilskin sacks can protect blessed potions of full healing and scrolls of remove curse without needing to be greased.
facts.detect: Possessing blessed potions of full healing or scrolls of remove curse and an oilskin sack.
facts.action: Store blessed potions of full healing and scrolls of remove curse in an oilskin sack for protection.

facts.fact: Monks start each game with 5-10 oranges.
facts.detect: Checking inventory at the start of the game.
facts.action: Eat oranges to gain nutrition and maintain vegan conduct if desired.

facts.fact: Oranges make up 1% of all comestibles randomly generated on the ground.
facts.detect: Finding oranges on the ground or in shops.
facts.action: Eat oranges to gain nutrition and maintain vegan conduct if desired.

facts.fact: Kicking a tree has a one-time 8/15 chance of dropping 8-rnl(7) oranges.
facts.detect: Kicking a tree and seeing oranges drop.
facts.action: Kicking trees to obtain oranges for nutrition and vegan conduct.

facts.fact: Cutting down a tree has a 1/5 chance of producing an orange.
facts.detect: Cutting down a tree and seeing an orange appear.
facts.action: Cutting down trees to obtain oranges for nutrition and vegan conduct.

facts.fact: A tree that is tunneled through has a 1/3 chance of leaving behind oranges.
facts.detect: Tunneling through a tree and seeing oranges appear.
facts.action: Tunneling through trees to obtain oranges for nutrition and vegan conduct.

facts.fact: Orcish arrows have a 100% chance of generating as poisoned.
facts.detect: Poisoned orcish arrow
facts.action: Avoid picking up orcish arrows unless you have poison resistance or a way to neutralize poison.

facts.fact: Orcish arrows are one of the primary reasons that groups of Uruk-hai and orcs are best dealt with via crowd control strategies.
facts.detect: Uruk-hai or orc-captains in a group
facts.action: Use crowd control strategies such as funneling them into hallways to avoid being hit by poisoned arrows.

facts.fact: Orcish arrows make up 2% of all weapons randomly generated on the ground.
facts.detect: Finding orcish arrows on the ground
facts.action: Be cautious when picking up orcish arrows as they are likely poisoned.

facts.fact: Orcish arrows gain a +1 multishot bonus when fired by an orc from an orcish bow.
facts.detect: Orcish hero using orcish bow
facts.action: Be wary of orcish heroes using orcish bows as they can fire multiple poisoned arrows at once.

facts.fact: Orcish arrows are best used by orcish Rangers and other orcish bow-users due to their poison resistance and proficiency in bows.
facts.detect: Identifying yourself as a non-orcish hero
facts.action: Avoid using orcish arrows unless you have poison resistance and proficiency in bows.

facts.fact: Barbarians, Knights, Samurai, Valkyries, and all orcish heroes start the game with knowledge of the orcish bow.
facts.detect: The bot starts the game as a lawful dwarvish Valkyrie and notices the orcish bow in its inventory.
facts.action: The bot should use the orcish bow if it has arrows, as it is a weapon the Valkyrie starts with knowledge of.

facts.fact: Orcish bows make up 1.2% of all weapons randomly generated on the ground, in general shops or as death drops.
facts.detect: The bot finds an orcish bow on the ground or in a shop.
facts.action: The bot should pick up the orcish bow if it has arrows or plans to find arrows, as it is a common weapon.

facts.fact: Uruk-hai have a 1/3 chance of being generated with an orcish bow and a stack of poisoned orcish arrows as ammunition.
facts.detect: The bot encounters a Uruk-hai with an orcish bow and poisoned orcish arrows.
facts.action: The bot should be cautious and avoid or prepare to fight the Uruk-hai, as it is armed with a dangerous weapon and ammunition.

facts.fact: Orc-captains have an effective 1/6 chance of generating with an orcish bow and stack of orcish arrows.
facts.detect: The bot encounters an orc-captain with an orcish bow and orcish arrows.
facts.action: The bot should be prepared to fight the orc-captain, as it is a common enemy with a dangerous weapon.

facts.fact: Orcish chain mail provides 4 base AC and MC1.
facts.detect: Item name: orcish chain mail
facts.action: Equip orcish chain mail if no better armor is available, especially if the bot is a melee character.

facts.fact: Orcish chain mail is less effective than standard chain mail.
facts.detect: Item name: orcish chain mail
facts.action: Do not rely on orcish chain mail for long-term protection; upgrade to better armor as soon as possible.

facts.fact: Mordor orcs have a 1/3 chance of being generated with orcish chain mail.
facts.detect: Monster name: Mordor orc
facts.action: Be cautious when encountering Mordor orcs, as they may be wearing orcish chain mail.

facts.fact: Orc-captains have a 1/2 chance of being generated with Mordor orc armor, giving them a 1/6 chance of generating with orcish chain mail.
facts.detect: Monster name: orc-captain
facts.action: Treat orc-captains as potentially wearing orcish chain mail and be prepared for combat.

facts.fact: An orcish cloak grants MC1 (Magic cancellation 1) and no base AC before enchantment.
facts.detect: Item name: orcish cloak
facts.action: Wear the orcish cloak to protect worn body armor from erosion by direct attacks such as a brown pudding's decay-inducing bite attack.

facts.fact: Orcish cloaks make up 0.8% of all armor that is randomly generated on the ground, in general shops or as death drops.
facts.detect: Item name: orcish cloak
facts.action: Prioritize finding and using an orcish cloak if no better cloak is available, especially for protecting body armor from erosion.

facts.fact: Uruk-hai and orc-captains have a 1/3 chance of being generated with an orcish cloak.
facts.detect: Monster name: Uruk-hai or orc-captain
facts.action: Check for orcish cloaks when encountering Uruk-hai or orc-captains.

facts.fact: Orcish cloaks can be used as a throwaway cloak to catch the scroll of destroy armor when testing unknown scrolls.
facts.detect: Item name: orcish cloak and scroll of destroy armor
facts.action: Wear an orcish cloak before reading unknown scrolls to avoid losing valuable armor.

facts.fact: Orcish dagger is the base item for the artifact Grimtooth.
facts.detect: Finding an orcish dagger with unusual properties or a message about Grimtooth.
facts.action: Keep the orcish dagger if it appears to be special, as it may be the artifact Grimtooth.

facts.fact: Orcish daggers make up 1.2% of all randomly generated weapons.
facts.detect: Noticing the weapon type when randomly generated or found in shops.
facts.action: Evaluate the orcish dagger's usefulness compared to other weapons found, considering its weak damage.

facts.fact: Orcs have a 50% chance of being generated with an orcish dagger.
facts.detect: Encountering orcs with weapons.
facts.action: Be cautious when fighting orcs, as they may be armed with orcish daggers.

facts.fact: Player monsters have a slightly less than 1% chance of generating with an orcish dagger.
facts.detect: Noticing player monsters with weapons.
facts.action: Be prepared for player monsters to potentially wield orcish daggers.

facts.fact: Orcish Rogues have a 25% chance of their initial weapon being an orcish dagger.
facts.detect: Encountering orcish Rogues.
facts.action: Expect orcish Rogues to be armed with orcish daggers.

facts.fact: An orcish helm provides 1 base AC.
facts.detect: iron skull cap
facts.action: Equip the orcish helm to gain 1 AC.

facts.fact: Orcish helms are commonly found on early-game orcish monsters such as goblins.
facts.detect: Encountering goblins or other early-game orcish monsters.
facts.action: Loot orcish helms from these monsters to gain early AC.

facts.fact: Orcish helms can be found in general shops or as death drops, making up 0.6% of all randomly generated armor.
facts.detect: Exploring general shops or finding death drops.
facts.action: Check shops and loot death drops for orcish helms.

facts.fact: Orcs that are not undead have a 50% chance of being generated with an orcish helm.
facts.detect: Encountering living orcs.
facts.action: Loot orcish helms from living orcs.

facts.fact: Orcish helms are typically replaced towards the end of the early game.
facts.detect: Reaching the end of the early game.
facts.action: Consider replacing the orcish helm with better armor as the game progresses.

facts.fact: Orcish ring mail grants 2 base AC and MC1.
facts.detect: Item name: orcish ring mail
facts.action: Equip orcish ring mail for its AC and MC1 properties, but be aware of its weight and consider swapping for lighter armor if available.

facts.fact: Orcish ring mail is as heavy as standard ring mail but provides 1 less point of AC.
facts.detect: Item weight: 250 aum
facts.action: Prioritize finding lighter armor with better AC, especially leather armor, as it is 100 aum lighter and does not interfere with spellcasting.

facts.fact: Orcish Barbarians start the game with orcish ring mail in place of standard ring mail.
facts.detect: Character class: Orcish Barbarian
facts.action: Swap orcish ring mail for better armor as soon as possible, even if it means sacrificing AC temporarily.

facts.fact: General stores and used armor dealerships sell orcish ring mail.
facts.detect: Shop type: General store or used armor dealership
facts.action: Purchase orcish ring mail if it is the best available armor at the time, but plan to upgrade as soon as possible.

facts.fact: An orcish shield is made of iron and appears as a red-eyed shield when unidentified.
facts.detect: red-eyed shield
facts.action: Identify the shield to confirm it is an orcish shield before equipping it.

facts.fact: Orcish shields make up 0.2% of all armor that is randomly generated on the ground, in general shops or as death drops.
facts.detect: Finding an orcish shield in shops or on the ground.
facts.action: Prioritize equipping an orcish shield if no better shield is available, but replace it with a lighter or better shield as soon as possible.

facts.fact: Mordor orcs and orc-captains have a 1/3 chance of being generated with an orcish shield.
facts.detect: Encountering Mordor orcs or orc-captains.
facts.action: Be prepared to fight Mordor orcs or orc-captains who may be carrying orcish shields.

facts.fact: Orcish shields grant 1 base AC.
facts.detect: Checking the AC value of the shield.
facts.action: Use the orcish shield for its AC value, but be aware of its weight and interference with spellcasting.

facts.fact: Orcish shields interfere with spellcasting to a greater extent than smaller shields.
facts.detect: Attempting to cast a spell while wearing the orcish shield.
facts.action: Avoid casting spells while wearing the orcish shield if possible, or replace it with a lighter shield.

facts.fact: Orcish heroes start the game with knowledge of the orcish short sword.
facts.detect: Starting character is an orcish hero
facts.action: If starting as an orcish hero, prioritize learning and using the orcish short sword skill.

facts.fact: Orcish Barbarians have a 1/2 chance of starting the game with a +0 orcish short sword as their one-handed weapon.
facts.detect: Starting character is an orcish Barbarian and has a +0 orcish short sword in inventory
facts.action: If starting as an orcish Barbarian and have a +0 orcish short sword, use it as your primary weapon until you find a better one.

facts.fact: Orcish short swords make up 0.3% of all randomly-generated weapons created on the floor, as death drops or in shops.
facts.detect: Finding an orcish short sword in a shop or on the floor
facts.action: Consider picking up an orcish short sword if you find one, as it may be useful for orcish enemies.

facts.fact: Uruk-hai have a 1/3 chance of being generated with an orcish short sword.
facts.detect: Encountering a Uruk-hai with an orcish short sword
facts.action: Be prepared to fight Uruk-hai with orcish short swords, as they may be more dangerous due to their weapon.

facts.fact: Player monsters, including those on the Astral Plane, have a 1/2000 chance of generating with an orcish short sword as their initial weapon.
facts.detect: Encountering a player monster with an orcish short sword
facts.action: Be cautious when fighting player monsters, as they may have an orcish short sword.

facts.fact: Orcish spears are stackable one-handed weapons that use the spear skill and are made of iron.
facts.detect: crude spear
facts.action: Identify and use orcish spears if they are the only available spear-type weapon, especially against larger monsters.

facts.fact: Orcish spears make up about 1.3% of randomly generated weapons and can be found in weapon shops and general stores.
facts.detect: crude spear in shops or randomly generated in the dungeon
facts.action: Purchase or pick up orcish spears if they are available, as they are useful for dealing damage against larger monsters.

facts.fact: Orcish spears are the weakest among spear weapons against smaller monsters.
facts.detect: Encountering smaller monsters while using an orcish spear
facts.action: Switch to a different weapon or tactic when fighting smaller monsters to avoid inefficiency.

facts.fact: Orcrist has a +d5 to-hit bonus and deals doubled damage to all orcs.
facts.detect: Encounter with orcs, orc mummies, orc zombies, or orcish heroes.
facts.action: Wield Orcrist when fighting orcs to maximize damage.

facts.fact: While wielded, Orcrist glows blue and warns of orcs.
facts.detect: Blue glow of the weapon.
facts.action: Wield Orcrist in orc-infested areas to detect orcs early.

facts.fact: Orcrist requires a sacrifice of at least 4 value to obtain.
facts.detect: Message indicating a sacrifice of at least 4 value is required.
facts.action: Sacrifice items worth at least 4 value to obtain Orcrist.

facts.fact: Orcrist will unconditionally blast any orcish hero or hero polymorphed into an orc.
facts.detect: Polymorphing into an orc or being an orcish hero.
facts.action: Avoid wielding Orcrist if polymorphed into an orc or if the character is an orcish hero.

facts.fact: Naming Orcrist can force an early Stormbringer via sacrifice.
facts.detect: Naming an elven broadsword as Orcrist.
facts.action: Name an elven broadsword as Orcrist to force an early Stormbringer via sacrifice.

facts.fact: A pancake is a type of comestible that appears in NetHack with 200 nutrition and takes 2 turns to consume.
facts.detect: Item name: pancake
facts.action: Eat the pancake to gain nutrition when hungry.

facts.fact: Pancakes make up 40% of all comestibles randomly generated on the ground, in general shops, or as death drops.
facts.detect: Item name: pancake in random locations or shops
facts.action: Collect pancakes for nutrition when found.

facts.fact: Pancakes are considered 'people food' and can be thrown to tame domestic canines and felines.
facts.detect: Monster name: domestic canine or feline
facts.action: Throw a pancake to tame a domestic canine or feline.

facts.fact: Pancakes are vegetarian-friendly but not vegan-friendly.
facts.detect: Item name: pancake
facts.action: Eat pancakes if vegetarian conduct is acceptable.

facts.fact: The pancake has a nutrition/weight ratio of 100, tying it with the lump of royal jelly for the second most weight-efficient food.
facts.detect: Item name: pancake
facts.action: Carry pancakes for efficient nutrition storage.

facts.fact: Barbarians, Knights, Samurai, and Valkyries start the game with knowledge of the partisan.
facts.detect: Starting character is a Valkyrie
facts.action: Use partisan effectively as it is a known weapon for Valkyries

facts.fact: Partisans make up 0.5% of all randomly-generated weapons created on the floor, as death drops or in shops.
facts.detect: Finding a partisan in a shop or on the floor
facts.action: Consider picking up a partisan if it is available, as it is a rare weapon

facts.fact: Watchmen and soldiers may be generated with a partisan.
facts.detect: Encountering watchmen or soldiers
facts.action: Be prepared to fight watchmen or soldiers who may be armed with a partisan

facts.fact: Trolls have an effective 1/8 chance of being generated with a partisan.
facts.detect: Encountering a troll
facts.action: Be cautious when fighting trolls, as they may be armed with a partisan

facts.fact: The partisan has the lowest average damage against small monsters of all polearms.
facts.detect: Using a partisan against small monsters
facts.action: Consider switching to a different weapon with better damage against small monsters

facts.fact: Pears make up 1% of all comestibles randomly generated on the ground, in general shops or as death drops.
facts.detect: Finding a pear on the ground or in a shop
facts.action: Eat the pear to gain 50 nutrition and 1 turn of hunger satisfaction

facts.fact: Kicking a tree has a one-time 8/15 chance of dropping 1 to 8 pears.
facts.detect: Kicking a tree and seeing pears drop
facts.action: Collect the pears and eat them to manage hunger

facts.fact: Cutting down a tree has a 1/5 chance of producing pears.
facts.detect: Cutting down a tree and seeing pears appear
facts.action: Collect the pears and eat them to manage hunger

facts.fact: A tree that is tunneled through has a 1/3 chance of leaving behind pears.
facts.detect: Tunneling through a tree and seeing pears appear
facts.action: Collect the pears and eat them to manage hunger

facts.fact: Applying a charged horn of plenty has a 0.9% chance of generating a pear or two.
facts.detect: Using a horn of plenty and seeing pears appear
facts.action: Collect the pears and eat them to manage hunger

facts.fact: Archeologists start each game with an uncursed +0 pick-axe.
facts.detect: Starting inventory check
facts.action: Keep the pick-axe as it is useful for digging and combat against mimics.

facts.fact: A pick-axe deals 1d6 damage versus small monsters and 1d3 versus large monsters.
facts.detect: Combat with small or large monsters
facts.action: Use the pick-axe in combat against small monsters but switch to a better weapon against large monsters.

facts.fact: A hero can apply a pick-axe to tunnel through solid rock walls, dig downward into the floor to create a pit or turn a pit into a hole, dig through doors to break them open, and smash apart boulders and statues.
facts.detect: Encountering solid rock walls, doors, boulders, or statues
facts.action: Use the pick-axe to dig through obstacles to find vaults or create shortcuts.

facts.fact: Pick-axes have +2 to-hit bonuses against xorns and earth elementals.
facts.detect: Encountering xorns or earth elementals
facts.action: Use the pick-axe in combat against xorns and earth elementals due to the bonus.

facts.fact: A blessed pick-axe has a {{frac|3}} chance of immediately clearing the same area of rock around them when digging on the Plane of Earth.
facts.detect: Entering the Plane of Earth
facts.action: Bless the pick-axe to improve digging efficiency on the Plane of Earth.

facts.fact: Plate mail grants 7 base AC and MC2.
facts.detect: Checking the armor's properties when worn.
facts.action: Wear plate mail to maximize AC early in the game if carrying capacity allows.

facts.fact: Plate mail makes up 4.4% of all randomly generated armor.
facts.detect: Finding plate mail in shops, on the floor, or as death drops.
facts.action: Prioritize picking up plate mail when found due to its high AC.

facts.fact: The 'bones' pile on the Rogue level has a 1/2 chance of containing plate mail with an enchantment ranging from -1 to +3.
facts.detect: Exploring the Rogue level and finding a 'bones' pile.
facts.action: Search for and take plate mail from 'bones' piles on the Rogue level.

facts.fact: Mercenaries with a target AC of -1 or better have a 16/25 chance of being generated with plate mail.
facts.detect: Encountering mercenaries with a target AC of -1 or better.
facts.action: Prepare to fight mercenaries in plate mail to potentially loot it.

facts.fact: King Arthur, the quest leader for the Knight quest, is always generated with +4 plate mail.
facts.detect: Starting the Knight quest and encountering King Arthur.
facts.action: Loot King Arthur's +4 plate mail if possible.

facts.fact: Potions of acid make up 1% of all randomly-generated potions.
facts.detect: Finding a potion of acid in inventory or on the ground
facts.action: Store the potion safely or use it as a stoning cure if needed

facts.fact: Quaffing a potion of acid without acid resistance abuses constitution and deals damage based on the potion's beatitude.
facts.detect: Quaffing a potion and seeing messages like 'This burns a lot!', 'This burns!', or 'This burns a little!'
facts.action: Avoid quaffing unless it's a stoning cure or you have acid resistance

facts.fact: Dipping items into a potion of acid that are vulnerable to corrosion will corrode those items.
facts.detect: Dipping an item into a potion and seeing a message about corrosion
facts.action: Avoid dipping non-corrosion resistant items into unidentified potions

facts.fact: Acid boils on contact with water, causing an explosion and damage.
facts.detect: Walking into water or dipping a potion into water while carrying acid
facts.action: Avoid carrying acid near water sources

facts.fact: Dipping a lichen corpse into a potion of acid will print a unique message without consuming either object.
facts.detect: Dipping a lichen corpse into a potion and seeing a unique message
facts.action: Use this method to identify a potion of acid without risk

facts.fact: A potion of amnesia removes memory of the current map with a 1/3 chance of forgetting level maps, and has additional effects dependent on beatitude. A blessed potion cures lycanthropy and sickness while granting 51-100 nutrition.
facts.detect: Potion of amnesia (sparkling potion)
facts.action: Avoid drinking unless in dire need (e.g., to cure lycanthropy or sickness).

facts.fact: Dipping an item or stack of items into the potion sets its beatitude to uncursed, positively-enchanted items may lose a point of enchantment, rustprone items have a 1/2 chance of rusting, erosion-proof objects have a 1/3 chance of losing their erosion-proof status, and magic markers lose 3-12 charges.
facts.detect: Potion of amnesia (sparkling potion)
facts.action: Avoid dipping items into the potion unless absolutely necessary.

facts.fact: A thrown potion of amnesia that hits the hero causes them to forget some maps, object identities and spells, and has a 9/10 chance of subjecting the worn helm to the effects of dipping.
facts.detect: Thrown potion of amnesia
facts.action: Avoid being hit by thrown potions of amnesia.

facts.fact: Monsters will throw this potion at you, causing amnesia, so it is advisable to pick up any that you find, even if you do not intend to use them.
facts.detect: Monsters throwing a sparkling potion
facts.action: Pick up any found potions of amnesia to prevent monsters from throwing them at you.

facts.fact: When throwing a potion of amnesia, make sure there is at least one empty square between you and your target - otherwise, you will be subjected to the vapors of the potion, potentially forgetting maps and item identities.
facts.detect: Throwing a sparkling potion
facts.action: Ensure there is at least one empty square between you and your target when throwing a potion of amnesia.

facts.fact: A potion of blindness makes the hero blind for 125-324 turns if blessed, 250-449 turns if uncursed, and 375-574 turns if cursed.
facts.detect: A cloud of darkness falls upon you.
facts.action: Avoid drinking unidentified potions, especially if you do not have intrinsic telepathy or other blindness protection.

facts.fact: Monsters hit with a potion of blindness will be blinded for 64-127 turns if they are not already blind.
facts.detect: A monster is hit by a potion of blindness.
facts.action: Use potions of blindness to blind hostile monsters, but be cautious as it requires a successful hit.

facts.fact: Dipping a unicorn horn into a potion of blindness will produce an uncursed potion of water.
facts.detect: You dip a unicorn horn into a potion of blindness.
facts.action: Use a unicorn horn to neutralize potions of blindness and obtain water.

facts.fact: Potions of healing, extra healing, or full healing mixed with a potion of blindness produce uncursed water.
facts.detect: You mix a potion of healing/extra healing/full healing with a potion of blindness.
facts.action: Mix healing potions with blindness potions to obtain water, but be cautious as it wastes healing potions.

facts.fact: Potions of blindness are generated 4% of the time among all randomly generated potions.
facts.detect: Finding a potion of blindness in a general store or liquor emporium.
facts.action: Be cautious when picking up unidentified potions, especially in areas where potions of blindness are common.

facts.fact: A potion of booze grants nutrition and may confuse the player based on its beatitude.
facts.detect: Quaffing a potion of booze
facts.action: Drink a blessed potion of booze for nutrition without confusion, or avoid drinking if confused or unconscious.

facts.fact: Uncursed potions of booze confuse the player for 3d8 turns.
facts.detect: Message 'Ooph! This tastes like liquid fire!' followed by confusion
facts.action: Avoid drinking uncursed potions of booze unless necessary for specific strategies.

facts.fact: Cursed potions of booze grant 10 nutrition, confuse the player for 3d8 turns, and render them unconscious for up to 15 turns.
facts.detect: Message 'You pass out.'
facts.action: Avoid drinking cursed potions of booze unless absolutely necessary.

facts.fact: Mixing a potion of booze with a potion of gain level or gain energy can create a potion of hallucination.
facts.detect: Mixing a potion of booze with a potion of gain level or gain energy
facts.action: Avoid mixing these potions unless hallucination is desired.

facts.fact: Mixing a potion of booze with a potion of enlightenment can create a potion of confusion.
facts.detect: Mixing a potion of booze with a potion of enlightenment
facts.action: Avoid mixing these potions unless confusion is desired.

facts.fact: A potion of clairvoyance grants a single application of clairvoyance, revealing all corridors, walls, and stairs in a 19x11 region around you if uncursed.
facts.detect: Potion of clairvoyance item name
facts.action: Drink the potion to reveal the immediate surroundings, especially useful on non-mappable levels.

facts.fact: A blessed potion of clairvoyance grants 100-149 turns of intrinsic clairvoyance, giving a 50% chance of mapping the surrounding 19x11 area every 15 turns.
facts.detect: Blessed potion of clairvoyance item name
facts.action: Drink the potion to gain intrinsic clairvoyance for exploration and navigation.

facts.fact: A cursed potion of clairvoyance has no effect.
facts.detect: Cursed potion of clairvoyance item name
facts.action: Do not drink the potion.

facts.fact: The potion of clairvoyance reveals the same tiles as magic mapping but only in a small fraction of the map, centered on the player.
facts.detect: Potion of clairvoyance item name
facts.action: Use the potion to map a small area around you, especially useful when magic mapping is not available or would confuse you.

facts.fact: Intrinsic clairvoyance from the blessed potion potentially increases the area that can be mapped if the player is moving constantly to cover new area for the duration of the potion's effects.
facts.detect: Blessed potion of clairvoyance item name
facts.action: Drink the potion and move around to map more areas.

facts.fact: A potion of confusion confused the hero for {{rn1|7|8}} turns (blessed), {{rn1|7|16}} turns (uncursed), and {{rn1|7|24}} turns (cursed).
facts.detect: Quaffing a potion of confusion
facts.action: Avoid quaffing a potion of confusion unless it is needed for a specific strategy, such as reading a scroll while confused.

facts.fact: Dipping a unicorn horn into a potion of confusion will turn it into an uncursed potion of water.
facts.detect: Having a unicorn horn and a potion of confusion
facts.action: Dip the potion of confusion into a unicorn horn to convert it into water and reduce inventory weight.

facts.fact: Monsters will throw the potion of confusion at the hero as an offensive item.
facts.detect: A monster throwing a potion
facts.action: Avoid getting hit by a thrown potion of confusion or use protection to avoid confusion.

facts.fact: Mixing a potion of booze with a potion of enlightenment can create a potion of confusion.
facts.detect: Having a potion of booze and a potion of enlightenment
facts.action: Avoid mixing these potions unless intentionally creating a potion of confusion.

facts.fact: A hero that is hit with the potion or inhales its vapors is confused for up to 5 more turns.
facts.detect: Being hit by a thrown potion of confusion
facts.action: Avoid inhaling the vapors of a thrown potion of confusion or use protection to avoid confusion.

facts.fact: A potion of enlightenment makes up 2% of all randomly-generated potions.
facts.detect: Item name: Potion of enlightenment
facts.action: Save for alchemy or bless if identified to increase mental stats.

facts.fact: Quaffing a non-cursed potion of enlightenment exercises wisdom and provides enlightenment, allowing the player to momentarily see the hero's intrinsics and other attributes.
facts.detect: Message: You feel enlightened.
facts.action: Quaff to see intrinsics and attributes, consider blessing for stat increase.

facts.fact: Quaffing a cursed potion of enlightenment abuses wisdom and prints a message with no other effect.
facts.detect: Message: You have an uneasy feeling...
facts.action: Do not quaff cursed potions.

facts.fact: Mixing a potion of levitation with a potion of enlightenment has a 3/5 chance of producing a potion of gain level.
facts.detect: Item names: Potion of levitation and Potion of enlightenment
facts.action: Mix to potentially create a potion of gain level.

facts.fact: All Tourists start with 2 non-cursed potions of extra healing. All Healers start the game with 4 non-cursed potions of extra healing.
facts.detect: Starting character class is Tourist or Healer
facts.action: Tourists and Healers should prioritize using these potions for healing and HP boost if needed.

facts.fact: Quaffing a potion of extra healing will heal you for more than a standard potion of healing, with the effect's strength dependent on beatitude. A blessed one heals 8d8 HP, an uncursed one 6d8 HP, and a cursed one 4d8 HP.
facts.detect: Potion of extra healing in inventory
facts.action: Prioritize quaffing blessed potions of extra healing for maximum healing effect.

facts.fact: Inhaling vapors from a potion of extra healing of any beatitude will restore 2 HP to the hero (up to your maximum HP), adjust the health of their base form if they are polymorphed, cure blindness and deafness if it was non-cursed, and exercise constitution.
facts.detect: Potion of extra healing in inventory
facts.action: If unable to quaff, consider opening the potion to inhale vapors for minor healing and status effect removal.

facts.fact: Mixing potions of extra healing with potions of gain level or gain energy can produce a potion of full healing.
facts.detect: Potion of extra healing and potion of gain level or gain energy in inventory
facts.action: Mix potions to create a potion of full healing for more effective healing.

facts.fact: Smoky and milky potions can pose an obstacle if either one ends up as the randomized appearance of the potion of extra healing. Smoky extra healing in particular presents a bind, as it often forces a choice between extra HP or the chance for a wish.
facts.detect: Smoky or milky potion of extra healing
facts.action: Avoid using smoky or milky potions of extra healing unless absolutely necessary, as they may not provide the expected benefits.

facts.fact: Potions of fruit juice make up 4.2% of all potions randomly generated on the ground, in general shops or as death drops.
facts.detect: Finding a brown potion or seeing a potion of fruit juice in a shop inventory.
facts.action: Quaff the potion to gain nutrition, especially if foodless conduct is being observed.

facts.fact: Quaffing a potion of fruit juice raises the hero's nutrition: 10 nutrition if cursed, 20 if uncursed, and 30 if blessed, halved if diluted.
facts.detect: Quaffing the potion and observing the nutrition gain.
facts.action: Quaff the potion to gain nutrition, especially if foodless conduct is being observed.

facts.fact: Potions of fruit juice are unaffected by cancellation.
facts.detect: Cancelling a potion and observing that it remains a potion of fruit juice.
facts.action: Use cancellation to identify fruit juice from other potions.

facts.fact: If you become hungry within the last few turns and that status disappears upon quaffing a potion, it is fruit juice.
facts.detect: Becoming hungry and then quaffing a potion.
facts.action: Quaff the potion to gain nutrition.

facts.fact: Dipping a unicorn horn into a potion of sickness produces fruit juice.
facts.detect: Dipping a unicorn horn into a potion of sickness.
facts.action: Dip a unicorn horn into a potion of sickness to create fruit juice.

facts.fact: A potion of full healing can be identified by its default randomized appearance as a 'black potion'.
facts.detect: Black potion
facts.action: Identify and keep this potion for healing purposes.

facts.fact: Potions of full healing make up 1% of all randomly-generated potions.
facts.detect: Finding a potion in a store or randomly generated in the dungeon.
facts.action: Collect and keep potions of full healing for healing purposes.

facts.fact: Quaffing a potion of full healing heals up to 400 HP, cures hallucination and blindness, and exercises constitution and strength.
facts.detect: Drinking a potion and seeing the message 'You feel completely healed.'
facts.action: Use this potion when in need of significant healing.

facts.fact: A blessed potion of full healing can restore one lost experience level but also decreases the maximum experience level by one.
facts.detect: Drinking a blessed potion of full healing and noticing a decrease in maximum experience level.
facts.action: Use this potion cautiously to restore lost levels, but be aware of the trade-off.

facts.fact: Smoky and milky potions of full healing can turn into dangerous items like ghosts or djinn when quaffed.
facts.detect: Potion with smoky or milky appearance.
facts.action: Avoid quaffing these potions unless absolutely necessary and HP is not critically low.

facts.fact: Quaffing an uncursed potion of gain ability increases one attribute at random by one point, unless the attribute is already at its maximum, in which case it will re-select until it finds an attribute that is not at its maximum or it has attempted to select an attribute six times total.
facts.detect: Quaffing a potion of gain ability and noticing if an attribute increases or if the message 'You have a peculiar feeling for a moment, then it passes.' appears.
facts.action: Quaff uncursed potions of gain ability to increase attributes, especially if attributes are below maximum.

facts.fact: Quaffing a blessed potion of gain ability increases all of the hero's attributes by one point.
facts.detect: Quaffing a blessed potion of gain ability and noticing if all attributes increase.
facts.action: Quaff blessed potions of gain ability to increase all attributes.

facts.fact: Quaffing a cursed potion of gain ability has no effect and does not identify the potion.
facts.detect: Quaffing a cursed potion of gain ability and seeing the message 'Ulch! That potion tasted foul!'
facts.action: Avoid quaffing cursed potions of gain ability.

facts.fact: Inhaling vapors from a broken potion of gain ability restores 1 lost point to a random attribute if the potion was uncursed, and restores 1 lost point to all applicable attributes if it was blessed.
facts.detect: Breaking a potion of gain ability and inhaling its vapors.
facts.action: Inhale vapors from a broken potion of gain ability to restore lost attribute points.

facts.fact: A monster hit by a thrown potion of gain ability is restored to full HP and has any blindness cured.
facts.detect: Throwing a potion of gain ability at a monster and seeing the monster's HP restored and blindness cured.
facts.action: Use thrown potions of gain ability to heal and cure blindness in monsters.

facts.fact: Potions of gain energy make up 4.2% of all randomly-generated potions.
facts.detect: Item name: potion of gain energy
facts.action: Collect and use for energy restoration or alchemy.

facts.fact: Quaffing a blessed potion of gain energy increases maximum energy by 3d6 and restores three times that value to current energy.
facts.detect: Message: Magical energies course through your body.
facts.action: Drink when blessed to maximize energy gain.

facts.fact: Quaffing an uncursed potion of gain energy increases maximum energy by 2d6 and restores three times that value to current energy.
facts.detect: No specific message, but can be inferred from potion effects.
facts.action: Drink when uncursed to restore energy.

facts.fact: Quaffing a cursed potion of gain energy decreases maximum energy by 1d6 and subtracts three times that value from current energy.
facts.detect: Message: You feel lackluster.
facts.action: Avoid drinking cursed potions to prevent energy loss.

facts.fact: Mixing a potion of gain energy and a potion of fruit juice produces a potion of see invisible.
facts.detect: Item names: potion of gain energy and potion of fruit juice
facts.action: Mix to create potion of see invisible for alchemy.

facts.fact: Potions of gain level make up 2% of all randomly-generated potions.
facts.detect: Finding a potion of gain level in a randomly generated pile of potions.
facts.action: Identify the potion before drinking it to ensure it is not cursed.

facts.fact: Quaffing a non-cursed potion of gain level will auto-identify the potion and increase the hero's experience level by one.
facts.detect: Message 'You feel more experienced.' after drinking a potion.
facts.action: Drink non-cursed potions of gain level to level up.

facts.fact: Quaffing a cursed potion of gain level causes the hero to gain one dungeon level by pulling them through the ceiling to the floor above.
facts.detect: Message 'You rise up, through the ceiling!' after drinking a potion.
facts.action: Avoid drinking cursed potions of gain level unless necessary for escape.

facts.fact: Intelligent monsters with hands will quaff a potion of gain level in their inventory as soon as the player is within a certain range.
facts.detect: Message ' seems more experienced.' or ' rises up, through the ceiling!' near a monster.
facts.action: Be cautious around monsters carrying potions of gain level.

facts.fact: Witnessing a monster gain experience will auto-identify the potion.
facts.detect: Message ' seems more experienced.' or ' rises up, through the ceiling!' near a monster.
facts.action: Observe the effects of a potion on a monster to identify it.

facts.fact: Potions of hallucination make up 4% of all randomly-generated potions.
facts.detect: Sky blue potion
facts.action: Avoid drinking unless in a situation where hallucination resistance is guaranteed or the potion is needed to survive a touch of death from a high-level spellcaster.

facts.fact: Quaffing a potion of hallucination causes hallucination for a duration dependent on the potion's beatitude.
facts.detect: Message 'Oh wow! Everything so cosmic!' or 'You have a momentary vision.'
facts.action: If hallucinating, avoid dangerous situations such as identifying unknown items or engaging in combat.

facts.fact: Hallucination resistance, which is only granted by wielding Grayswandir, suppresses the effects of the potion of hallucination.
facts.detect: Wielding Grayswandir
facts.action: Wield Grayswandir to suppress the effects of hallucination if a potion of hallucination is consumed.

facts.fact: Mixing a potion of healing with a potion of hallucination will produce uncursed water.
facts.detect: Mixing a potion of healing with a potion of hallucination
facts.action: Avoid mixing these potions to prevent wasting healing potions.

facts.fact: Quaffing a non-cursed potion of hallucination may grant enlightenment, which exercises wisdom.
facts.detect: Message 'Oh wow! Everything so cosmic!' or 'You have a momentary vision.'
facts.action: Consider drinking a non-cursed potion of hallucination to gain enlightenment if wisdom is low and no other source is available.

facts.fact: All Healers start the game with 4 non-cursed potions of healing, and all Monks start the game with 3 non-cursed potions of healing.
facts.detect: Player character class is Healer or Monk
facts.action: Use potions of healing to restore health and exercise constitution, especially in the early game.

facts.fact: Intelligent monsters may generate with a potion of healing as a defensive item.
facts.detect: Encounter with an intelligent monster
facts.action: Steal or take the potion of healing from the monster if possible.

facts.fact: Quaffing a non-cursed potion of healing will heal for 6d4 HP, cure blindness and deafness, and increase maximum HP if healing above maximum.
facts.detect: Player is blind, deaf, or has low health
facts.action: Quaff a potion of healing to restore health and cure status effects.

facts.fact: Dipping a poisoned weapon into a potion of healing will neutralize the poison and use up the potion.
facts.detect: Player has a poisoned weapon
facts.action: Dip the poisoned weapon into a potion of healing to neutralize the poison.

facts.fact: Mixing potions of healing with potions of gain level, gain energy, or speed can produce a potion of extra healing.
facts.detect: Player has potions of healing and gain level, gain energy, or speed
facts.action: Mix potions to create potions of extra healing for more effective healing later in the game.

facts.fact: A blessed potion of invisibility grants permanent invisibility.
facts.detect: Quaffing a potion of invisibility and seeing the message 'You feel a peculiar sensation, then it passes.'
facts.action: Seek out and quaff a blessed potion of invisibility to gain permanent invisibility.

facts.fact: Uncursed potion of invisibility grants temporary invisibility for 31-45 turns.
facts.detect: Quaffing a potion of invisibility and seeing the message 'You feel a peculiar sensation, then it passes.'
facts.action: Use an uncursed potion of invisibility for temporary invisibility when needed.

facts.fact: Cursed potion of invisibility grants temporary invisibility but aggravates monsters.
facts.detect: Quaffing a potion of invisibility and seeing the message 'For some reason, you feel your presence is known.'
facts.action: Avoid quaffing cursed potions of invisibility unless you are prepared to deal with aggravated monsters.

facts.fact: Monsters may seek out and quaff potions of invisibility.
facts.detect: Seeing a monster drink a potion of invisibility and their position being marked with an 'I'.
facts.action: Be cautious around monsters that have become invisible after drinking a potion.

facts.fact: Inhaling vapors from a broken potion of invisibility causes brief invisibility.
facts.detect: Breaking a potion of invisibility and inhaling its vapors.
facts.action: Use the vapors for brief invisibility if needed, but be aware of the brief duration.

facts.fact: A potion of levitation causes the hero to levitate for a number of turns based on its beatitude: blessed for rn1(50,250) + 1 turns, uncursed for rn1(140,10) + 1 turns, and cursed for 1 turn if not already levitating.
facts.detect: Message 'You hit your head on the ceiling.' or 'You have a peculiar feeling for a moment, then it passes.'
facts.action: Identify potions before quaffing to avoid cursed ones, and use blessed potions before entering hazardous areas like the Plane of Air.

facts.fact: Quaffing a cursed potion of levitation while not levitating causes the hero to hit their head on the ceiling and take physical damage, reduced by helm material.
facts.detect: Message 'You hit your head on the ceiling.'
facts.action: Avoid quaffing cursed potions of levitation unless already levitating.

facts.fact: Blessed potions of levitation allow the hero to end levitation at will by using the '>' key.
facts.detect: Message 'You feel lighter.' when using '>' while levitating.
facts.action: Use '>' to control levitation duration, especially in hazardous areas.

facts.fact: Mixing potions of levitation with potions of enlightenment has a 3/5 chance of producing an uncursed and diluted potion of gain level.
facts.detect: Message 'The potion seems to be diluted.'
facts.action: Mix potions of levitation with enlightenment for gain level potions.

facts.fact: Quaffing four blessed potions of levitation in quick succession provides 1001 to 1197 turns of levitation.
facts.detect: Message 'You feel lighter.' after quaffing each potion.
facts.action: Quaff four blessed potions of levitation before entering the Plane of Air for extended levitation control.

facts.fact: A potion of monster detection displays all monsters on the current level when quaffed, exercising wisdom and auto-identifying the potion.
facts.detect: Quaffing a potion of monster detection
facts.action: Quaff the potion to see all monsters on the current level, which can help in navigating and planning your route.

facts.fact: A cursed potion of monster detection aggravates all monsters on the level, waking all sleeping monsters and un-paralyzing all immobile monsters.
facts.detect: Quaffing a cursed potion of monster detection
facts.action: Avoid quaffing cursed potions of monster detection unless you are prepared to deal with all monsters being awake and hostile.

facts.fact: A blessed potion of monster detection grants passive monster detection for 21-60 turns, continually updating the screen with the position of all monsters on the level.
facts.detect: Quaffing a blessed potion of monster detection
facts.action: Bless and quaff the potion to gain passive monster detection, which is very useful for navigating levels and dealing with monsters.

facts.fact: Quaffing a potion of monster detection while hallucinating will display monsters as their hallucinated identities.
facts.detect: Quaffing a potion of monster detection while hallucinating
facts.action: If hallucinating, be prepared for the monsters to appear as their hallucinated forms, which can be confusing.

facts.fact: A potion of monster detection can be used to remotely awaken monsters, which can be useful for avoiding alignment penalties from attacking 'helpless' hostiles.
facts.detect: Quaffing a cursed potion of monster detection
facts.action: Use a cursed potion to remotely awaken monsters if you need to avoid alignment penalties from attacking 'helpless' hostiles.

facts.fact: Potions of object detection make up 4.2% of all potions randomly generated on the floor, in general shops, or as death drops.
facts.detect: Finding a potion of object detection in a general shop or on the floor.
facts.action: Collect and save the potion for later use when needed, especially for detecting important items like wands or gold.

facts.fact: In The Gnome King's Wine Cellar map of Mines' End, a potion of object detection is always generated within the titular wine cellar at level creation.
facts.detect: Entering The Gnome King's Wine Cellar in Mines' End.
facts.action: Ensure to collect the potion of object detection for later use.

facts.fact: Nymphs have a 1/2 chance of being generated with a potion of object detection.
facts.detect: Encountering a nymph.
facts.action: Stealthily approach the nymph to avoid angering it and then steal the potion if it has one.

facts.fact: An uncursed potion of object detection displays the current position of all objects on the level using a blank map.
facts.detect: Quaffing an uncursed potion of object detection.
facts.action: Use the map to prioritize loot collection, especially for wands and gold.

facts.fact: A blessed potion of object detection will display objects as an uncursed one does, but items that are not in a monster's inventory are treated as though the hero handled them up close.
facts.detect: Quaffing a blessed potion of object detection.
facts.action: Use the potion to learn the identities of objects, especially useful for conduct play like zen.

facts.fact: A potion of oil can be used to refuel an oil lamp by dipping the lamp into the potion.
facts.detect: Murky potion or smoky potion (appearance of potion of oil)
facts.action: Refuel oil lamp with potion of oil if lamp is empty.

facts.fact: Applying a potion of oil will light it and auto-identify the potion.
facts.detect: Applying a potion of oil
facts.action: Apply potion of oil to light it and identify it.

facts.fact: Dipping a rusty or corroded weapon into a non-cursed potion of oil will repair one level of erosion.
facts.detect: Rusty or corroded weapon
facts.action: Dip rusty or corroded weapon into potion of oil to repair it.

facts.fact: Quaffing an unlit potion of oil abuses wisdom and identifies the potion.
facts.detect: Quaffing an unlit potion of oil
facts.action: Quaff unlit potion of oil to identify it.

facts.fact: A potion of oil can be used to untrap a squeaky board.
facts.detect: Squeaky board
facts.action: Use potion of oil to untrap squeaky board.

facts.fact: Potions of paralysis make up 4.2% of all randomly-generated potions.
facts.detect: Potion of paralysis appearance (emerald potion)
facts.action: Avoid quaffing unidentified potions to prevent paralysis.

facts.fact: Quaffing a potion of paralysis will paralyze the hero for 13-22 turns if blessed, 25-34 turns if uncursed, and 37-46 turns if cursed.
facts.detect: Message 'You are frozen to the!', 'You are frozen in place!', 'You are motionlessly suspended.', 'Something seems to be holding you.'
facts.action: Do not quaff unidentified potions and avoid getting hit by thrown potions.

facts.fact: Vapors from a thrown or boiled potion of paralysis can paralyze the hero for up to 5 turns.
facts.detect: Message 'Something seems to be holding you.'
facts.action: Avoid throwing potions in enclosed spaces or near yourself.

facts.fact: Monsters may throw potions of paralysis at the hero as an offensive item.
facts.detect: Message 'Something seems to be holding you.'
facts.action: Avoid engaging in combat with monsters that have potions in their inventory.

facts.fact: Potions of paralysis are the only 300zm potion to always have a negative effect when quaffed.
facts.detect: Potion of paralysis appearance (emerald potion)
facts.action: Do not quaff unidentified potions and avoid getting hit by thrown potions.

facts.fact: Potions of polymorph make up 1% of all randomly-generated potions.
facts.detect: Finding a potion of polymorph in a randomly generated potion pool or store.
facts.action: Store or save the potion for later use when needed, such as for item or monster polymorphing.

facts.fact: Randomly generated monsters with a monster difficulty of 5 or less have an effective 5/180 chance of being generated with a potion of polymorph.
facts.detect: Observing a low-difficulty monster drinking a potion and polymorphing.
facts.action: Avoid letting low-difficulty monsters drink potions in your presence to prevent unwanted polymorphing.

facts.fact: Quaffing a potion of polymorph will cause the hero to polymorph unless they have unchanging.
facts.detect: Drinking a potion of polymorph without unchanging.
facts.action: Avoid drinking a potion of polymorph unless you have unchanging or are prepared to polymorph into a form that can survive.

facts.fact: Dipping an item into a potion of polymorph may polymorph that item, with artifacts having a 19/20 chance of resisting.
facts.detect: Dipping an item into a potion of polymorph and observing the item's reaction.
facts.action: Use the potion of polymorph to safely polymorph non-artifact items, especially for testing the potion's identity.

facts.fact: Wielding the potion and hitting a monster can cause the monster to polymorph into a footrice, which can petrify the hero.
facts.detect: Wielding a potion of polymorph and hitting a monster.
facts.action: Avoid wielding a potion of polymorph and hitting a monster to prevent the risk of petrification.

facts.fact: A potion of restore ability can restore lost attributes and experience levels depending on its beatitude (uncursed, blessed, cursed).
facts.detect: Message upon quaffing: 'Wow! This makes you feel !', 'Wow! This makes you feel good!', 'Ulch! This makes you feel mediocre!'
facts.action: Quaff a blessed potion of restore ability to restore all lost attributes and experience levels.

facts.fact: Potions of restore ability are the most reliable means of restoring lost experience levels, especially with the potion blessed.
facts.detect: Lack of drain resistance or presence of level-draining threats like wraiths or Vlad the Impaler.
facts.action: Keep one or two blessed potions safely stored for restoring lost experience levels.

facts.fact: A hero subjected to vapors from a thrown, wielded, or boiled potion of restore ability will have their attributes affected depending on the potion's beatitude.
facts.detect: Vapor message: 'Wow! This makes you feel !', 'Wow! This makes you feel good!', 'Ulch! This potion smells terrible!'
facts.action: Avoid inhaling vapors from cursed potions.

facts.fact: Potions of restore ability are always safe to quaff even if their beatitude is unknown.
facts.detect: Unknown beatitude of a potion of restore ability.
facts.action: Quaff the potion to check its effect.

facts.fact: Attribute restoration from the potion of restore ability ignores any active source of sustain ability.
facts.detect: Active source of sustain ability.
facts.action: Quaff a potion of restore ability to restore lost attributes regardless of sustain ability.

facts.fact: A potion of see invisible grants the see invisible intrinsic for 750-849 turns if uncursed or cursed, and has a chance to grant it permanently if blessed.
facts.detect: Quaffing the potion while blind and having the blindness cured, or seeing previously invisible monsters become visible.
facts.action: Quaff a blessed potion of see invisible to maximize the chance of obtaining the permanent see invisible intrinsic.

facts.fact: A hero quaffing a potion of see invisible while invisible and not blind will auto-identify the potion.
facts.detect: Message: 'You can see through yourself, but you are visible!'
facts.action: If the bot is invisible and receives this message, it should auto-identify the potion as see invisible.

facts.fact: Potions of see invisible and fruit juice share the same quaffing message, making them difficult to distinguish by quaffing alone.
facts.detect: Quaffing message: 'This tastes like fruit juice.'
facts.action: Type-name both potions to differentiate them later.

facts.fact: A blessed potion of see invisible has a higher chance of granting the permanent see invisible intrinsic if the hero already has the temporary see invisible intrinsic.
facts.detect: Having the temporary see invisible intrinsic from a non-cursed potion of see invisible.
facts.action: Quaff a blessed potion of see invisible to increase the chance of obtaining the permanent intrinsic.

facts.fact: Canceling a potion of see invisible turns it into a potion of fruit juice.
facts.detect: Using the 'c' command on a potion of see invisible.
facts.action: Cancel a potion of see invisible to gain nutrition from the resulting fruit juice if the intrinsic is already obtained permanently.

facts.fact: Rogues start the game with an uncursed potion of sickness.
facts.detect: Checking the starting inventory of a Rogue character.
facts.action: Avoid quaffing the potion if found in inventory.

facts.fact: Potions of sickness make up 4.2% of all randomly-generated potions.
facts.detect: Finding a potion with a 'fizzy' appearance.
facts.action: Avoid quaffing unidentified potions with a 'fizzy' appearance.

facts.fact: Quaffing a potion of sickness causes the hero to lose HP, lowers one of their attributes, and abuses their constitution.
facts.detect: Messages such as 'Yecch! This stuff tastes like poison.' or 'You feel very sick.'
facts.action: Do not quaff the potion unless necessary and have means to mitigate the effects.

facts.fact: Dipping a stack of fruit juice potions into a potion of sickness will 'contaminate' the stack, turning them into potions of sickness.
facts.detect: Dipping fruit juice potions into an unidentified potion.
facts.action: Avoid dipping fruit juice potions into unidentified potions.

facts.fact: Dipping darts, arrows, shuriken, or crossbow bolts into a potion of sickness will coat the stack of projectiles in poison.
facts.detect: Dipping a missile weapon into an unidentified potion.
facts.action: Use the potion to poison weapons if needed, but be aware of alignment penalties for lawful characters.

facts.fact: A potion of sleeping will put a hero to sleep for a duration dependent on the beatitude of the potion: blessed (13-23 turns), uncursed (25-35 turns), cursed (37-47 turns).
facts.detect: You suddenly fall asleep!
facts.action: Avoid drinking a potion of sleeping unless it is part of a strategy to sleep a specific monster or if you are in a safe location where you can wake up without danger.

facts.fact: A hero hit by a thrown potion of sleeping or breathing its vapors will be immobilized for up to five turns and abuse dexterity unless they have sleep resistance or free action.
facts.detect: You feel rather tired.
facts.action: Avoid being hit by a thrown potion of sleeping or being near one when it is thrown to avoid immobilization.

facts.fact: A potion of sleeping can be used to immobilize a troublesome monster, but it can be overshadowed by the wand of sleep or the sleep spell.
facts.detect: falls asleep.
facts.action: Use a potion of sleeping to immobilize a troublesome monster if you do not have a wand of sleep or the sleep spell, but be aware that it can be less effective.

facts.fact: Potions of sleeping are generally candidates for dilution or polypiling if not used for strategic purposes.
facts.detect: Potion of sleeping in inventory
facts.action: Dilute or polypile potions of sleeping if you do not plan to use them strategically.

facts.fact: A potion of speed grants very fast speed to a hero temporarily and exercises dexterity.
facts.detect: You are suddenly moving much faster.
facts.action: Drink the potion to gain speed and exercise dexterity, which can help in combat and escaping enemies.

facts.fact: A blessed potion of speed lasts for rn1(10, 160) more turns, an uncursed one for rn1(10, 100) more turns, and a cursed one for rn1(10, 40) more turns.
facts.detect: You are suddenly moving much faster.
facts.action: Drink a blessed potion of speed for the longest duration of speed enhancement.

facts.fact: A non-cursed potion of speed also grants the hero intrinsic speed and heals wounded legs unless the hero is riding.
facts.detect: Your quickness feels very natural.
facts.action: Drink a non-cursed potion of speed to gain intrinsic speed and heal wounded legs if applicable.

facts.fact: A hero inhaling vapors from a broken potion of speed exercises dexterity and gains up to 5 more turns of very fast speed.
facts.detect: Your knees seem more flexible now.
facts.action: Inhale vapors from a broken potion of speed to gain additional speed and exercise dexterity.

facts.fact: Potions of speed can be mixed with potions of healing to create a potion of extra healing.
facts.detect: Mixing a potion of speed with a potion of healing.
facts.action: Mix a potion of speed with a potion of healing to create a potion of extra healing for better healing effects.

facts.fact: A potion of water always appears as a clear potion when unidentified.
facts.detect: Clear potion
facts.action: Identify the potion as water if it appears clear.

facts.fact: Diluting any non-acid potion twice will turn it into uncursed water.
facts.detect: Diluting a potion twice
facts.action: Dilute non-acid potions twice to create uncursed water.

facts.fact: Mixing a potion of healing, extra healing, or full healing with a potion of blindness, confusion, or hallucination will produce uncursed water.
facts.detect: Mixing specific potion combinations
facts.action: Mix healing or full healing potions with blindness, confusion, or hallucination potions to create uncursed water.

facts.fact: Quaffing an uncursed potion of water gains d10 nutrition.
facts.detect: Quaffing a clear potion
facts.action: Quaff clear potions to gain nutrition if food is scarce.

facts.fact: Uncursed water can be distinguished from holy and unholy water by its base cost of 5 zm.
facts.detect: Base cost of 5 zm
facts.action: Do not quaff or dip into potions unless they are clearly uncursed water.

facts.fact: Valkyries start the game with knowledge of the quarterstaff.
facts.detect: Starting game as a Valkyrie
facts.action: Use the quarterstaff if found, as proficiency is already known.

facts.fact: Quarterstaves have a 1.1% chance of randomly appearing on the ground, in shops, or as death drops.
facts.detect: Finding a quarterstaff on the ground or in a shop
facts.action: Pick up and use the quarterstaff if no better weapon is available.

facts.fact: Quarterstaves provide a small bonus to spellcasting while wielded.
facts.detect: Wielding a quarterstaff
facts.action: Use the quarterstaff to cast spells, especially in early game.

facts.fact: Quarterstaves deal 1d6 blunt damage and provide a damage bonus from strength.
facts.detect: Attacking with a quarterstaff
facts.action: Use the quarterstaff for melee combat, especially if strength is high.

facts.fact: Quarterstaves have a chance to perform a shattering blow that destroys the target's weapon and may cause them to flee.
facts.detect: Attacking with a quarterstaff
facts.action: Use the quarterstaff in combat to potentially disarm and scare enemies.

facts.fact: A ranseur is a two-handed polearm that appears as a hilted polearm when unidentified.
facts.detect: hilted polearm
facts.action: Identify the weapon as a ranseur to know its properties and use it effectively.

facts.fact: Watchmen and soldiers may be generated with a ranseur.
facts.detect: Encountering watchmen or soldiers
facts.action: Be prepared to fight for the ranseur if encountered.

facts.fact: Trolls have an effective 8/7 chance of being generated with a ranseur.
facts.detect: Encountering a troll
facts.action: Check if the troll is wielding a ranseur and prepare to fight or avoid it accordingly.

facts.fact: The ranseur is tied for the lightest of the polearms with the spetum at 50 aum.
facts.detect: Weight of the ranseur when picked up
facts.action: Consider the weight when deciding to carry it, especially in long dungeon exploration.

facts.fact: The ranseur has high average damage against small monsters but low average damage against large monsters.
facts.detect: Type of monster encountered
facts.action: Use the ranseur more effectively against small monsters and consider other weapons for large ones.

facts.fact: Ring mail grants 3 base AC and MC1.
facts.detect: Item name: ring mail
facts.action: Wear ring mail for its AC and MC1 properties, especially in the early stages of the game.

facts.fact: Studded leather armor is generally preferred to ring mail due to its lower weight and cost, and it does not interfere with spellcasting.
facts.detect: Item name: studded leather armor
facts.action: Replace ring mail with studded leather armor as soon as it becomes available, especially if the bot is a magic-focused role.

facts.fact: Knights start each game with +1 ring mail.
facts.detect: Role: Knight
facts.action: Utilize the starting +1 ring mail until better armor is found.

facts.fact: Human Barbarians start each game with +0 ring mail.
facts.detect: Role: Human Barbarian
facts.action: Utilize the starting +0 ring mail until better armor is found.

facts.fact: Mercenaries have an 8/15 chance of being generated with ring mail that counts for 3 points of their target AC.
facts.detect: Monster name: Mercenary
facts.action: Check if a mercenary is wearing ring mail and consider its AC value when evaluating combat scenarios.

facts.fact: A hero putting on the ring of adornment gains the adornment property and has their charisma modified by the ring's enchantment while it is worn.
facts.detect: You are adorned.
facts.action: Wear the ring if it has a positive enchantment to improve charisma, which can help with shop prices and foocubi encounters.

facts.fact: A hero eating the ring has a 1/3 chance of successfully absorbing its magic and gaining a temporary bonus or penalty to charisma based on the ring's enchantment.
facts.detect: Eating the ring.
